SYN.: ὁμοίωμα, denoting resemblance, which may however be merely accidental. εἰ. is a derived likeness and like the head on a coin or the parental likeness in a child…
(-λίμ, WH in Re, l.with), ὁ indecl. (Heb. נַפְתָּלִי) Naphtali: " (LXX).
[in LXX for גָּמַל;] camel: in proverbs. κάμιλος, see: κάμηλος, and cf. Thayer; LS, s.v
reflex prop. of first of person(s), used only in genitive, dative and accusative sing., of myself: ἀπ᾽ ἐ, ὑπ᾽ ἐμαυτόν
(θάντω), [in LXX chiefly for קֶבֶר;] 1. a burial. 2. a grave, tomb: " (LXX).

ἐπι-βαίνω [in LXX chiefly for רָכַב;] 1. to get up on, mount: before ἐπί, with accusative, (LXX); to embark in (a boat), go aboard: with dative, before εἰς, (Rec.); absol.. 2. to go up to, go on to, enter: before εἰς, with dative.
adv., in NT, always of time; now, already: νῦν... ἤ., now already, ἤ. ποτέ, now at length, with fut.

(Æolic μάρτυρ), -υρος, ὁ (also ἡ), [in LXX for עֵד;] a witness: (Westc., in l); in forensic sense, with genitive obj., with genitive poss., with dative of person(s), of Christ, of God, of those who have witnessed for Christ by their death (in later Xn. lit., martyr: Swete, Ap., 35).
[in LXX for שֵׁן;] a tooth: pl., ὁ βρυγμὸς τ. ὀδόντων.

1. beauty, (Homer),—; ἐς κάλλος with an eye to beauty, so as to set off her beauty, (Euripides); but, εἰς κ. ζῆν for pleasure, (Xenophon Historicus) 2. of persons, a beauty, (Xenophon Historicus) 3. in plural also rich garments and stuffs, (Aeschulus Tragicus); κάλλεα κηροῦ beautiful works of wax, i. e. honeycombs…

1. of a year, one year old, σῦς (Odyssey by Homer), 2. yearly, annual, year by year, (Herdotus Historicus):—;neuter plural as adverb, (Hesiod) 3. for a year, lasting a year, (Euripides); κἀνιαύσιος βεβώς gone, absent for a year, (Sophocles Tragicus) from ἐνιαυτός
breadth, width, absolute, εὖρος in breadth, (Odyssey by Homer), so, τὸ εὖρος (Xenophon Historicus); εἰς εὖρος (Euripides)
(ἀκάθαρτος), [in LXX chiefly for טֻמְאָה, טָמֵא;] uncleanness, impurity, (a) physical: (b) moral.
a pursuit, business, practice, Lat. studium, (Thucydides) from ἐπιτηδεύω

πάρ-ειμι [in LXX for בּוֹא,] 1. to be by, at hand or present; (a) of persons: παρών (opposite to ἀπών), before ἐπί with genitive, ἐνώπιον, ἐνθάδε, πρός, with accusative of person(s), (b) of things: of time, ὁ καιρός, τ. παρόν, ἡ ἀλήθεια, ταῦτα, τ. παρόντα. 2. to have come or arrived: before εἰς, before ἐπί, with accusative of thing(s).
(ἀφανίζω), [in LXX chiefly for שַׁמָּה, שְׁמָמָה;] vanishing.

[in LXX chiefly for נָטָה;] 1. to make to bend, to bow: τ. κεφαλήν (of one dying), τ. πρόσωτον (of terrified persons). 2. to make to lean, to rest: τ. κεφαλήν (in sleep). 3. As in Hom., of soldiers, to turn (to flight), παρεμβολάς. 4. In late Gk. (as mid, in cl.), to decline: intrans., ἡ ἡμέρα.
κατ-ευθύνω [in LXX for כּוּן ni., hi.,] to make or keep straight, direct, guide: metaphorically, τ. ὁδόν, τ. πόδας εἰς ὁδὸν εἰρήνης, τ. καρδίας εἰς τ. ἀγάπην.
τό (τρέχω), [in LXX chiefly for אוֹפָן;] a wheel.

(ξηρός), [in LXX chiefly for יָבֵשׁ;] to dry up, parch, wither. with accusative, τ. χόρτον, pass., to become or be dry or withered. of plants, of ripened crops, of liquids, of members of the body, to waste away.
(εὐώδης, fragrant; ὄζω) [in LXX for נִיחוֹחַ, (ὀσμὴ εὐωδίας); Sir.20:9,] fragrance: metaphorically, Χριστοῦ εὐ., ὀσμὴ εὐωδίας (a metaphor of sacrifice, most frequently in Pent. and Ez.).

[in LXX chiefly for אָדוֹן, אֲדֹנָי; in Jdth.9:17, δ. τ. οὐρανῶν κ. τ. γῆς]; a master, lord, correlative of δοῦλος, οἰκέτης: as title of God, voc., δέσποτα (so usually in LXX), ὁ δ. = voc. δέσποτα, of Christ, Ju 4, R, txt.. SYN.: κύριος, implying limitation of authority and a more general relation than δ.…

[in LXX: chiefly for שָׁמַע;] to listen, attend, hence, (a) to answer a knock at a door: (b) to attend to, submit to, obey: absol., with inf., with dative of person(s), with dative of thing(s), before εἰς.

[in LXX for לוּן, שָׁבַת,] 1. to destroy, cast down: τ. ναόν, οἰκίαν, opposite to οἰκοδομεῖν. Metaphorical, to overthrow, annul, abrogate: τ. ἔργον τ. θεοῦ, τ. νόμον, (2Ma.2:22). 2. to unloose, unyoke (e.g. horses), hence intrans., of travellers, to take up one's quarters, lodge.
[in LXX for רָחָב;] broad. As subst., ἡ π. (sc. ὁδός), [in LXX chiefly for רָחָב;] a street: " (LXX), WH, mg..
[in LXX for שֵׁנָה, חֲלוֹם,] sleep: metaphorically.
[in LXX chiefly for שֶׁוַע, שִׁבְעָה and cogn. forms;] an oath: p1., (LXX).
[in LXX chiefly for מִרְמָה;] 1. in Hom., a bait. 2. a snare. 3. In the abstract, craft, deceit: " (LXX) (λαλῆσαι δ.).
τό, [in LXX for מַרְאֶה,] 1. that which is seen, appearance, external form: (ICC in l.). 2. form, sort, kind.

indecl., (Heb. שִׁמְעוֹן), Simeon, Symeon, a Heb. name for which the Gk. Σίμων, which see, was also used; 1. the son of Jacob. 2. An ancestor of our Lord: 3. An aged worshipper in the Temple. 4. One surnamed Niger. 5. The apostle Peter: (R, txt., WH, txt., Σίμων).
(Heb. אֱדֹם), [in LXX: a1.; elsewhere, as, Ἐδώμ;] Idumæa.

(ἐλεέω), [in LXX chiefly for חֶסֶד, צְדָקָה;] 1. mercy, pity. 2. almsgiving, alms (like the German Almosen, a corruption of the Greek word ἐ): ποιεῖν ἐ., ἐ. διδόναι, αἰτεῖν, λαβεῖν, πρὸς (in order to ask) ἐ., pl., (Cremer, 711).
1. a he-goat, Lat. caper, = τράγος, (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. also feminine = χίμαιρα, [, variant datesAnthology Palantina

(so sometimes in cl., but most frequently -α, -ον), [in LXX chiefly for חָסִיד, also for טָהוֹר, יָשָׁר, תָּמִים;] religiously right, right­eous, pious, Holy: of men.; by meton., ὁ. χεῖρας, of God, as subst., ὁ ὅ., of the Messiah, " (LXX); τὰ ὅ. Δανεὶδ τ. πιστά (Field, Notes, 121), (LXX). SYN.: see: ἅγιος

(στραός, ἄγω), [in LXX chiefly for סָגָן (always in pl.), שַׂר;] 1. a military commander, a general. 2. A civic commander, a governor, magistrate. 3. The commander of the Levitical guard of the Temple, ὁ σ. τ. ἱεροῦ (EV, captain of the Temple): pl.. SYN.: ἄρχων.
ἀνα-τέλλω [in LXX for צָמַח, פָּרַח, זָרַח,] 1. trans., to cause to rise. 2. Intrans., to rise: φῶς, (=); ὁ ἥλιος, νεφέλη, φωσφόρος, ὁ Κύριος, prob. with ref. to metaphorically of sun or star.

see: μόνος. μόνος, -η, -ον, [in LXX chiefly for לְבַד;] 1. adj., alone, solitary, forsaken: with verb., with pron., with subst., pleonast., οὐκ... εἰ μὴ μ., attrib., only, (ὁ) μ. θεός, Ju 25. 2. As adv., (a) neut., (μόνον, alone, only: referring to verb or predic., οὐ (μὴ) μ., οὐ μ.... ἀλλά, id. before καί, (b) κατὰ μόνας, alone.
genitive, φλογός, [in LXX chiefly for לַהַב, לֶהָבָה;] a flame: φ, πυρός, " (LXX).

εὐ-δοκέω, -ῶ [in LXX chiefly for רָצָה, also for אָבָה, חָפֵץ,] 1. with inf., to be well pleased, to think it good, to give consent (so frequently in π. in legal docu­ments; Milligan, Th., 22 f.): R, mg., μᾶλλον εὐ., with accusative and inf. (Polyb., i, 8, 4), Col, l.with, R, txt. (Lft., in l). 2…
interrog. adv. of time, when?: ἕως π., how long. In indir. questions, = ὁπότε.

[in LXX chiefly for לָמַד;] 1. to learn, esp. by inquiry: absol., with accusative of thing(s), (sc. αὐτά), before quaes. indir., Χριστόν, (ICC, in l); before ἀπό, with genitive of thing(s), ἀπό, with genitive of person(s), παρά, with genitive of person(s), ἐν, with dative of person(s), "point" aorist (M, Pr., 117), to ascertain…
(Heb. זַכַּי); 1. Zacharias, father of John the Baptist. 2. Zechariah, the son of Jehoiada.
(ἄρρην, T, in; Rec. in) -ενος, ὁ, ἡ, ἄρσεν, τό, [in LXX chiefly for זָכָר;] male.
(λύπη), [in LXX for חָרָה,] to distress, grieve, cause pain or grief: with accusative of person(s), pass., λ. καὶ ἀδημονεῖν, opposite to χαίρειν, κατὰ θεόν, τ. πνεῦμα τ. ἅγιον, SYN.: see: θρηνέω

(πλοῦτος), [in LXX chiefly for עָשִׁיר;] rich, wealthy. Substantively, ὁ π., oἱ π., anarth., a rich man. Metaphorical, of God, ἐν ἐλέει (= cl., with genitive, dative), of Christ, of Christians, ἐν πίστει.

(δόκος, opinion, δέκομαι, Ion, form of δέχ-), [in LXX for טוֹב, נָדַב,] 1. to be of opinion, suppose: with inf., with accusative and inf., before ὅτι. 2. to seem, be reputed: with inf., οἱ δοκοῦντες, those of repute. Impers., it seems, with dative of person(s); (a) to think: (b) to please, seem good to: with inf.. SYN…

δια-στελλω [in LXX for בָּדַל hi., זְהַר hi., and 19 other words] 1. to divide, distinguish, define. 2. to command, charge expressly: pass., τὸ διαστελλόμενον. Mid., in late Gk. with same sense; a. dative of person(s), before ἵνα.

[in LXX for חָדָשׁ, exc. (אַחֵר);] of that which is unused or unaccustomed, new in respect to form or quality, fresh, unused, novel: opposite to παλαιός, ἀρχαῖος, πλήρωμα, μνημεῖον, διαθήκη (T, WH, R, txt., omit), " (LXX), οὐρανοί, γῆ, " (LXX) Ἰερουσαλήμ, ἄνθρωπος, πάντα, γέννημα τ. ἀμπέλου, διδαχή, ἐντολή, ὄνομα, (LXX); ᾠδή, (of.)…
(μάταιος), [in LXX for הֶבֶל, and nearly 40 times in Ec; for שָׁוְא, רִיק,] vanity, emptiness, frailty, folly: τ. νοός.
ἐμ-πίπτω [in LXX chiefly for נָפַל;] to fall into: before εἰς, metaphorically, εἰς κρίμα, ὀνειδισμόν; πειρασμόν, εἰς χεῖρας θεοῦ.

ἐπι-πίπτω [in LXX chiefly for נָפַל;] to fall upon (Field, Notes, 25): with dative of person(s), before ἐπὶ τ. τράχηλον. Metaphorical, φόβος, ὀνειδισμοί, (LXX); of the Holy Spirit: before ἐπί, with dative, ἐπί, with accusative, absol..

(ζύμη), [in LXX for מָצָּה; τὰ ἄ. (sc. λάγανα, cakes) = הַמָצָּה;] unleavened: ἡ ἑορτὴ τῶν ἄ. (הַג הַמָצָּה), the paschal feast (also called τὰ ἄ.,), ἡμέρα τῶν ἄ., ἡμέραι. Fig., of Christians, free from corruption: exhorted to keep festival, ἐν ἀζύμοις (sc. ἄρτοις, λάγανοις, or, indefinitely, "unleavened elements"), ib. 8 (Cremer, 724).
τό [in LXX chiefly for מְעָרָה;] a cave, cavern: σ. (EV, den) λῃστῶν.
τό [in LXX chiefly for אֵבֶל;] mourning.

1. as adv. of time, before, formerly (cl.; 3Ma.5:28 3Mac 3Mac) 2. As conic. (cl.), before; (a) after a positive sentence, with accusative and inf.: " (LXX), WH, txt.; πρὶν ἤ, WH, mg., (b) after a negative sentence, πρὶν ἤ: a. subjc. (before ἄν, M, Pr., 169), with optative.
ἐκ-καίω [in LXX chiefly for בָּעַר;] 1. to burn up. 2. to kindle. Pass., to burn: metaphorically, of the passions.

[in LXX chiefly for צֵל, 4 ff., but σ. and σ. θανάτου are also used for צַלְמָוֶת, (1),] 1. shadow, shade, caused by interception of light: metaphorically, σ. θανάτου, of ignorance and error, " (LXX). 2. a shadow, the image or outline cast by an object: figuratively, ὑπόδειγμα καὶ σ., opposite to σῶμα, opposite to εἰκών.

1. a stem, tree, (Odyssey by Homer):—;commonly a plank or beam, (Homer); δόρυ νήϊον a ship's plank, (Homer):—; hence, 2. a ship is called δόρυ, like Lat. trabs, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 3. the shaft of a spear, (Iliad by Homer): then, generally, a spear, pike, (Homer), εἰς δόρυ ἀφικνεῖσθαι to come within a spear's throw…
[in LXX chiefly for יָצַר;] to form, mould: (LXX).
ἐν-ισχύω [in LXX for חָזַק,] to strengthen: in spiritual sense, pass..
(ὄρθρος), [in LXX chiefly for שָׁכַם hi., also for שָׁחַר pi.,] = cl. poët., ὀρθρεύω, to rise early: before πρός, with accusative of person(s).

1. to rub out, πῦρ ἐκτρ. to produce fire by rubbing, (Xenophon Historicus):—; to rub hard, (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. to rub out, i. e. to destroy root and branch, (Herdotus Historicus); βίον ἐκτρ. to bring life to a wretched end, (Sophocles Tragicus):—;Pass., πρόρριζος ἐκτέτριπται (Herdotus Historicus) 3. to rub constantly, wear out…
οὐ, ὁ, [in LXX chiefly for שְׁכֶם, כָּתֵף;] the shoulder.
[in LXX for נָתַן, שׂוּם,] to place or put around: with accusative and dative, of garments, to put on: (Sir.6:31). Metaphorical, like περιβάλλω, to bestow, confer.
τό (δίδωμι), [in LXX for מַתָּנָה,] a gift: " (LXX). SYN.: δόσις, δῶρον, δωρεά, δώρημα
τό [in LXX chiefly for חֶרְפָּה, also for כְּלִמָּה,] 1. reproach, censure, blame. 2. matter of reproach, disgrace.

[in LXX chiefly for סוּר hi.;] to take away that which surrounds, take away, take off: τ. κάλυΜΜα, pass., as nautical term (RV, cast off), ἀγκύρας, absol., to cast loose. Metaphorical, to take away entirely: ἐλπίς, pass., ἁμαρτίας.
[in LXX chiefly for כָּבַס pi.;] to wash (inanimate objects, esp. clothing): τ. δίκτυα. Fig., τ. στολάς. SYN.: see: λούω

(θυμός), [in LXX chiefly for אָוָה pi., hithp.; also for חָמַד,] to set one's heart upon, desire, lust after, covet: absol., " (LXX), (of. 4Ma.2:6); before κατά (against, in opposition to), prop. (as in cl.) with genitive, in late Gk. also with accusative (M, Pr., 65), with inf., with accusative and inf., as in Hebrew…
τό [in LXX chiefly for מוֹפֵת;] a wonder, marvel: in NT always pl., τ. κ. σημεῖα
[in LXX for יָתוֹם;] 1. prop., orphan, fatherless: WH, mg. 2. In a general sense, bereft, friendless, desolate.

παρ-οξύνω [in LXX for נָאַץ, קָצַף, רָגַז,] 1. primarily, but never so in cl., to sharpen (μάχαιραν, שָׁנַן). 2. Metaphorical, as always in cl., (a) to spur on, stimulate; (b) to provoke, rouse to anger: pass..
παρ-οργίζω [in LXX chiefly for כַּעַס hi.;], to provoke to anger: (LXX).
Ἀσάφ, ὁ indecl. (Heb. אָסַף), [H609] Asaph, an obvious error for Ἀσά, found in the best texts, and adopted by LTTr. and WH, R, mg..

[in LXX: (15) (צֹרֶךְ), (חַשְׁחוּת) frequently in Sir.1:1-30 -2 Mac;] 1. need, necessity: πρὸς οἰκοδομὴν τῆς χ., ἕστι χ., χ. ἔχειν, with genitive, before τοῦ, with inf., absol. (sc. genitive), with genitive of person(s), with inf., before ἵνα, absol., οὐδὲν χ. ἔχειν, ἡ χ., with genitive subjc., pl.. 2. matter, business.
[in LXX chiefly for עֶשֶׂב, also for חָצִיר,] 1. an enclosure, a feeding place (Hom.). 2. food, esp. for cattle, grass: " (LXX), χ. χλωρός.
(as LXX, FlJ, who also gives Νώεος, Νῶχος), ὁ, indecl. (Heb. נֹחַ) Noah.
(οἰκέω), [in LXX for עֶבֶד;] a house-servant: pl., (In Plat., Hdt., Sir.4:30, the pl. includes all the inmates of the house, the familia, οἰκετεία.) SYN.. see: διάκονος
[in LXX chiefly for טוֹב;] 1. to please: with dative of person(s), before ἐνώπισν (= Heb. בּעֵנֵי, Bl., § 37, 1; 40, 7), Ac 65. 2. In late Gk., esp. in Inscr., to render service to.

[in LXX for נָשָׂא,] to marvel, wonder, wonder at: absol., with accusative of person(s), with accusative of thing(s), (WH, R, mg. om.), θαῦμα μέγα, πρόσωπον, Ju 16; before διά, with accusative, before ἐν, with dative obj., before ἐπί, with dative of thing(s), περί, ὀπίσω, ὅτι, εἰ. Pass. (Sir.38:3, Wis.8:11): before ἐν…

κατ-έχω [in LXX for אָחַז, חָזַק hi.,] 1. perfective of ἔχω (M, Pr., 116; M, Th., 155), (a) to possess, hold fast: (Lft., Notes, 251), (b) to lay hold of, get possession of. 2. to hold back, detain, restrain (M, Th., 156 f.): with accusative before τοῦ μή with inf., before πρός, with accusative, Phm 13; absol., τὸ κατέχον (ὁ κ.). 3…
(θωή, a penalty), [in LXX chiefly for נקה ni., pi., נָקִי;] 1. unpunished. 2. innocent: (WH, R, mg., δίκαιον).
(ποιμήν), [in LXX chiefly for רָעָה;] to act as shepherd, tend flocks: with accusative, ποιμνην. Metaphorical, to tend, shepherd, govern: with accusative, (LXX), Ju 12. SYN.: βόσκω, q.v

1. a standing place for animals, Lat. stabulum, a stable, fold, (Iliad by Homer): a stye, (Odyssey by Homer): of men, a dwelling, abode, (Hesiod) 2. quarters, lodgings for travellers or soldiers, Lat. statio, (Xenophon Historicus) 3. in Persia, σταθμοί were stations on the royal road, where the king rested…
[frequently in LXX for חָזַק hi., סָמַךְ, etc;] to take instead of or in turn. Mid., with genitive, to take hold of; (a) of persons, to help: (b) of things, to partake of.
[in LXX for מָסַס ni., מָקַק ni., מוּג ni.,] trans., to melt, melt down; pass., to melt, melt away.
[in LXX chiefly for גָּאוֹן and cogn. forms;] haughtiness, arrogance, disdain: (Plat., Xen.).

(γράφω), [in LXX chiefly for כְּתָב;] 1. a drawing, painting. 2. (a) writing; (b) that which is written, a writing: πᾶσα γ., γ. ἅγιαι, προφητικαί, al αἱ γ. τ. προφητῶν, ἡ γ., αἱ γ., the sacred writings, the Scriptures; in pl., when the sacred writings as a whole are meant, e.g., in sing., when a particular passage is referred to, as in…

(τίθημι), [in LXX for אַרְמוֹן, מוֹסָד,] of or for a foundation; as subst., ὁ θ. (sc. λίθος), a foundation stone, foundation: pl., οἰ θ. (cl.), neut., τὸ θ. (Arist., Phys., vi, 6, 10, LXX and later writers), metaphorically.

(ὄνειδος), [in LXX chiefly for חָרַף pi.;] to reproach, upbraid: absol., with accusative of person(s) (in cl. more frequently with dative of person(s); Bl., § 34, 2; WM, 278), WH, mg., " (LXX); τ. πόλεις, pass., WH, mg., with accusative of thing(s), with dupl. accusative.
Ptolemais, a maritime city of Phœnicea.
τό [in LXX chiefly for רֹחַב;] breadth: τ. π. τῆς γῆς (, מֶרְחָב).
ή, -όν (συνίημι), [in LXX for בִּין, חָכָם,] intelligent, sagacious, understanding: " (LXX).

(-ους), τό [in LXX chiefly for עֹז,] 1. strength, esp. as in Hom., of bodily strength. 2. power, might: τὸ κ. τῆς ἰσχύος αὐτοῦ, (, Da TH); τ. δόςης αὐτοῦ, κατὰ κράτος, mightily, a mighty deed, an act of power, in doxologies, Ju 25.

1. the head, top, highest point; hence, 2. the crown or top of the head, (Iliad by Homer), attic 3. the top or peak of a mountain, (Iliad by Homer) 4. metaphorically the highest point, Lat. summa, παντὸς ἔχει κορυφάν is the best of all, (Pindar); κορυφὰ λόγων προτέρων the sum and substance of ancient legends, (Pindar) 5…

[in LXX for נפל, שׂום, ידד,] prop., of a weapon or missile; then generally, of things and persons, lit. and metaphorically, to throw, cast, put, place: with accusative, before εἰς, and frequently ἐπί, κάτω, ἔξω, ἀπό, ἐκ, δρέπανον, μάχαιραν, κλῆρον, of fluids, to pour: pass., to be laid, to lie ill: ἐβλήθη (timeless aor., M, Pr., 134)…
(ἀφίημι), [in LXX for יוֹבֵל, דְּרוֹר,] 1. dismissal, release. 2. Metaphorical, of sins (never in LXX), pardon, remission of penalty: ἁμαρτιῶν, παραπτωμάτων, absol.. SYN.: πάρεσις, which see

(κόπος), [in LXX chiefly for יָגַע;] 1. (as in cl.) to grow weary. 2. Hence, in LXX and NT, to work with effort, to toil: absol., with accusative of thing(s), frequently in Paul. Epp., of ministerial labour: before ἐν, εἰς.

(Epic and old Att..) and κρείττων (later Att..), prop. comparat. of κρατύς, strong, but in sense often as comparat. of ἀγαθός, [in LXX chiefly for טוֹב;] better; (a) as to ad­vantage or usefulness: πολλῷ μᾶλλον κ., κρεῖσσον ποιεῖν, ἐστιν, before inf., (b) as to excellence: κ. ἐστι, before inf..

(στέφω, to encircle), [in LXX chiefly for עֲטָרָה;] 1. that which surrounds or encompasses. 2. a crown, i.e. the wreath, garland or chaplet given as a prize for victory, as a festal ornament, or as a public honour for disting­uished service or personal worth (so to sovereigns, especially on the occasion of a παρουσία, which see; cf…
[in LXX for נוּעַ hi., רָמַשׂ,] 1. to set in motion, move: τ. κεφαλήν, pass.. 2. to remove. 3. to excite, stir up: pass..
[in LXX for סָמַךְ, שׂוּם,] to fix, set fast, make fast: τ. πρόσωτον. Metaphorical, to confirm, establish: with, accusative, id. before ἐν.

(ἄξιος), [in LXX chiefly for בְּעָא, בָּקַשׁ; frequently in Wis.1:1-16, 2 Mac;] (a) to deem worthy: with accusative and inf., id. and genitive of thing(s), pass. with genitive of thing(s), (b) to think fit: with inf..
(εἰρήνη), [in LXX for שָׁלוֹם and cognates;] peaceful.
(πορνεύω), [in LXX for תַּזְנוּת and cogn. forms;] fornication: (Lft., Notes, 53), pl., disting. from μοιχεία, = μοιχεία. Metaphorical (of idolatry:): (Westc., in l), and so perh..
(δέω), [in LXX chiefly for אסר;] a band, bond: metaphorically, ὁ δεσμὸς τ. γλώσσης. Pl., δεσμοί, δεσμά (as also in cl.), genitive, dative, Phm 10, Ju 6; ἐν τοῖς δ. τοῦ εὐαγγελίου Phm 13.

(fern. Pres. pass. ptcp. of οἰκέω; sc. γῆ) [in LXX chiefly for תֵּבֵל, אֶרֶץ;] the inhabited earth; (a) in cl., the countries occupied by Greeks, as disting. from barbarian lands; (b) in later writers, the Roman world: by meton., of its inhabitants: (with) in LXX and NT, also of the whole inhabited world: by meton. (ut supr.)…
(φονεύς), [in LXX chiefly for רָצַח;] to kill, murder. absol., μὴ (οὐ) φονεύσῃς (-εις), (all from); with accusative.
δια-σκορπίζω [in LXX for פּוּץ, זָרָה,] to scatter abroad, disperse: of sheep, = " (LXX); of persons, opposite to συνάγω, of winnowing grain, metaphorically, of property, to squander, waste.
1. a warrior, combatant, (Iliad by Homer), 2. π. ἵππος a war-horse, charger, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus)
(αὐλή), [in LXX chiefly for לוּן;] 1. prop., to lodge in a courtyard. 2. to lodge in the open. 3. to pass the night, lodge.

ὑπο-λαμβάνω [in LXX: and frequently (עָנָה), (דָּמָה pi.), Tob.6:17, Wis.17:2, 3Ma.3:8 3Mac,] 1. to take or bear up (by supporting from beneath): with accusative of person(s). 2. to receive, welcome, entertain (Xen.): III Jn 8. 3. to catch up in speech. 4. Of mental action, to assume, suppose: before ὅτι.
[in LXX chiefly for קָנָא pi.;] 1. to burn with envy or jealousy, to be jealousy: absol.. 2. to seek or desire eagerly: with accusative of thing(s), with accusative of person(s), pass..

1. dew, Lat. ros, (Herdotus Historicus); in plural, (Aeschulus Tragicus), 2. pure water, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 3. of other liquids, δρ. φονία, of blood, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 4. any thing tender, like ἕρση II, the young of animals, (Aeschulus Tragicus)
(στερεός), [in LXX: (רָקַע), (חָזַק pi.),] (a) to make firm or solid; (b) to strengthen, make strong; with accusative of person(s), τ. βάσεις, pass.. Metaphorical: τ. πίστει, pass..

(ἀκούω), [in LXX: for שׁמע, its parts and derivatives, exc. (שׁמר);] 1. hearing, the sense of hearing: "Hebraic dative," ἀκοῇ ακούειν (frequently in LXX; V. M, Pr., 14, 75). 2. organ of hearing, the ear: pl.. 3. a thing heard, i.e., (a) a message, teaching: and " (LXX), R, mg.; λόγος ἀκοῆς, (b) a report, rumour: with genitive…

see: δοῦλος. δοῦλος, -η, -ον, [in LXX, ὁ δ. nearly always for עֶבֶד; ὁ δ. chiefly for שִׁפְחָה,אָמָה;] 1. in bondage to, subject to. 2. As subst., ὁ, ἡ δ., a slave; (a) fem., ἡ δ., a female slave, bondmaid (Cremer, 702; DB, iii, 215): " (LXX); (b) masc., ὁ δ., a slave, bond-man: opposite to ἐλεύθερος, opposite to κύριος, δεσπότης…
(ἀπειθής), [in LXX for מָרָה, סָרַר,] as in cl.; to disobey, be disobedient: absol., with dative, (Cremer, 475).
[in LXX for אַרְגָּמָן, אַרְגְּוָן;] 1. the purple fish. 2. purple dye. 3. Later, = πορφυρίς, a purple gar­ment.
τριχός, ἡ [in LXX chiefly for שֵׂעָר;] hair; (a) of the head: (b) of animals.
a mistake in music, false note: metaphorically a fault, offence, error, (Plato Philosophus) from πλημμελέω
(-οῦς, -ᾶ -οῦν) (σίδηρος), [in LXX chiefly for בַּרְזֶל;] of iron.
ἐξ-ουδενέω (Rec. -όω; T, -θανόω), -ῶ, [in LXX (with vv. ll. -όω, -θενέω, -θενόω) for בּוּז, בָּזָה, מָאַס, בּוּס,] to despise, set at nought.

ἄ-βυσσος, -ον (Ion. βυσσός = βυθός), 1. in cl., boundless, bottomless (e.g. ἄ. πέλαγος, ἄ. πλοῦτος Æsch.). 2. [In LXX and] NT, as subst., ἡ ἄ. (sc. χώρα), the abyss; (a) of the sea; (b) of the underworld, as the abode of the dead: (a paraphrase of LXX); as the abode of demons, (Cremer, 2).
(φυτόν, a plant, φύω), [in LXX chiefly for נָטַע, also for שָׁתַל,] to plant: with accusative, φυτείαν, ἀμπελῶνα, pass., before ἐν.
to have, possess; (n.) possessions; to be, exist to begin; to come into existence; to exist; to be, subsist, Acts; to be in possession, to belong, Acts; goods, possessions, property, to be
τό [in LXX for חלב;] milk. Metaphorical, of elementary Christian teaching: τὸ λογικὸν ἄδολον γ., the rational (spiritual) genuine milk.

poët. and late prose form of πειράω, which see, [in LXX for נָסָה pi.;] 1. to make proof of (Hom.). 2. to try, attempt (Luc., Polyb., with inf.. 3. 1. to tie or bind together, to join together, unite, ς. χέρα, in sign of friendship, (Euripides); ἰδού, ξύναψον (i.e. τὴν χέρα); (Euripides); but, ς. χεῖρά τινος ἐν βρόχοις to bind it fast, (Euripides):—; ς. πόδα or ἴχνος τινί to meet him, (Euripides); ς. κῶλον τάφῳ to approach the grave, (Euripides); so, φόνος ς. τινὰ γᾷ (Euripides):—…
(θύω), [in LXX (with -άζω) chiefly for קָטַר pi., hi.;] to burn incense.
(ἀληθής), [in LXX for אֶמֶת;] true, in the sense of real, ideal, genuine: Jn; = ἀληθής. SYN.: ἀληθής, q.v

(λειτουργέω), [in LXX chiefly for עֲבֹדָה,] 1. in cl. (chiefly of Athens), the discharge of a public office at one's own expense, hence, 2. a service, ministry; in π. (Deiss., BS, 140 f.) and in LXX, of religious service or ministration; and so in NT: of priestly ministrations, figuratively, θυσία καὶ λ. τῆς πίστεως ὑμῶν…

τό (θέλω), [in LXX chiefly for חָפֵץ, also for רָצוֹן,] will, (a) objectively = that which is willed: θ. τ. θεοῦ, τ. κυρίου, pl., of precepts, WH, mg., (LXX); ἐστιν τὸ θ., with genitive of person(s), before ἵνα, with inf., with accusative and inf., (b) subjectively = τὸ θέλειν: ποιεῖν, γίνεσθαι, ἡ εὐδοκία ( βουλὴ) τοῦ θ., ἐν τῷ θ…

adv. (ἔξω opposite to ἔσωθεν), [in LXX for חוּץ;] 1. prop. (in answer to the question, Whence ?), from without: 2. More often, without: τὸ ἔ., οἱ ἔ., (WH, mg.); ὁ ἔ. κόσμος, ἐκβάλλειν ἔ.. As prep. with genitive: 4.

ἐξ-αλείφω [in LXX for טוּחַ, metaphorically, מָחָה, שָׁחַת,] 1. to plaster, wash over (LXX). 2. to wipe off, wipe out: δάκρυον, metaphorically, χειρόγραφον, τ. ὄνομα, before ἐκ, (MM, Exp., xiii); pass., ἀμαρτίαι (ἐξαλιφθῆναι, WH), (cf., Sir.46:20 (ἁμ. ἀπαλ-), 3Ma.2:19).
λιβός, ὁ [in LXX chiefly for נֶגֶב, also for תֵּימָן, מַעֲרָב,] the SW. wind: βλέποντα κατὰ λ..
a hollow, deep valley, [variant datesAnthology Palantina

μάλα adv., [in LXX for אֲבָל, Dan LXX, compar. for מ, (31), μᾶλλον ἠ (מ), superlat., 2Ma.8:7, 4Ma.4:22;] I. Pos., very, very much, exceedingly. II. Compar., μᾶλλον. 1. Of increase, more; with qualifying words: πολλῷ, πόσῳ, τοσούτῳ... ὅσῳ. 2. Of comparison, the more: ἔτι μ. καὶ μ., with compar., πολλῴ μ. κρεῖσον, μ. διαφέρειν…
(μυρίος), [in LXX chiefly for רְבָבָה;] ten thousand, a myriad: pl., hyperb., of vast numbers, Ju 14.
indecl. Zebulun, Jacob's tenth son: the tribe of Z..
(T, -λία), -ας, ἡ (δουλεύω), [in LXX, as, for עֶבֶד and cognates;] slavery, bondage.
εἴσ-οδος, -ου, ὁ (ὁδός) [in LXX chiefly for בּוֹא;] 1. a means of entering, place of entrance. 2. a going in, entrance: with genitive loc., before εἰς, πρός.

A. Compar., πρότερος, -α, -ον, [in LXX for רִאשׁוֹן,לִפָנִים,] before, of time, place, rank, in NT always of Time, before, former. Adverbially, πρότερον, before, aforetime, formerly: opposite to ἔπειτα, τὸ π., αἱ π. ἡμέραι, αἱ π. ἐπιθυμίαι.
1. a compounding, (Plato Philosophus), 2. a comparing, comparison, (Aristotle Philosopher)

συμ-βαίνω [in LXX for עָשָׂה, קָרָא, קָרָה,] 1. to stand with the feet together. 2. to come together, come to terms. 3. Of events, to come to pass, happen: with dative of person(s), absol., τὰ σνμβεβηκότα, with accusative and nf..
(κλίνω), [in LXX chiefly for מִטָּה;] a bed, couch.

impersonal (δέω), [in LXX chiefly for infin. with לְ;] one must, it is necessary: with inf., with accusative and inf., with ellipse of accusative, of accusative, and inf., οὐ (μὴ) δεῖ (non licet), ought not, must not: impf., ἔδει, of necessity or obligation in past time regarding a past event, periphr., δέον ἐστίν, id.…

[in LXX for נִיר,);] a lamp (portable, and usually set on a stand, λυχνία): ἔρχεται ὁ λ., λ. ἅπτειν; φῶς λύχνου, id. opposite to φ.ἡλίου, metaphorically, of the eye, of John the Baptist, of the Lamb, of prophecy, of spiritual readiness, pl., λύχνοι (as always in LXX; frequently in Att.. λύχνα). SYN.: λαμπάς, q.v
(βαίνω), [in LXX (Hex.) for מִזְבֵּחַ, in Proph., chiefly for בָּמָה;] 1. any raised place, a platform. 2. an altar.

(παραβάλλω), [in LXX: (מָשַׁל), Sir.47:17 (חִידָה), mutt. in Sir, Wis.5:3;] 1. a placing beside, juxtaposition. 2. a comparing, comparison. 3. a comparison, illustration, analogy, figure: specif. of the pictures and narratives drawn from nature and human life which are characteristic of the synoptic teaching of our Lord…
in LXX and NT, in FlJ, Ant., see 6, 3 and 4 -ῶνος (Heb. גִּדְעוֹן), Gideon.
[in LXX chiefly for עוֹלֵל, also for פְּתִי,] infant; of children and minors: (LXX). Metaphorical, childish, unskilled, simple: (WH, fox ἤπιοι); opposite to τέλειος, ν. ἐν Χριστῷ.

1. to make different, to change, alter, (Plato Philosophus), 2. Pass. with future middle ἀλλοιώσομαι and passive ἀλλοιωθήσομαι:—; to become different, be changed, (Thucydides) 3. to be changed for the worse, (Xenophon Historicus) Hence
(WH, Ἁναν-), -α, ὁ (Heb. חֲנַנְיָה), Ananias; 1. of Jerusalem. 2. Of Damascus. 3. High Priest.
Demetrius; 1. a silversmith, 38. 2. A Christian disciple, III Jn 12.
a coos, a measurement of liquid
ἐπι-κατ-άρατος, -ον (ἐπικαταράομαι, to imprecate curses on), [in LXX for אָרַר, also Wis.3:12 Ma.2:19;] accursed: (LXX) (LXX κεκαταραμένος) (Cremer, 109).
[in LXX chiefly for שָׁכַר, רָוָה;] to be drunken: metaphorically.
τό (ὁράω), [in LXX for חָזוֹן, מַרְאֶה,] that which is seen; (a) a sight, spectacle: (b) an appearance, vision: (Rec.).
(ἄλλος, γένος), [in LXX chiefly for זוּר, נֵכָר;] of another race, a foreigner.
(ἔργον), [in LXX for מְלָאכָה, עֲבֹדָה,] 1. work, business: δὸς ἐ. (Lat. da operam). 2. working, performance.
ύ, [in LXX chiefly for כָּבֵד;] heavy. Metaphorical, burdensome: ἐντολή, severe (perh. impressive): ἐπιστολή, weighty: τὰ βαρύτερα τ. νόμου, αἰτιώματα, violent, cruel (EV, grievous): λύκος.

[in LXX chiefly for רָחַץ;] to bathe, wash the body: with accusative of person(s), (of a dead body); id. before ἀπό (Deiss., BS, l.with), pass. ptcp. pf., mid., to wash oneself (Mayor, in l; M. Pr., 155 f., 238 f.), metaphorically, Rec., R, mg.. SYN.: νίπτω, used of parts of the body-hands, feet, face; πλύνω, of things, as garments

(τιμή), [in LXX for כָּבַד pi., עָרַךְ hi.,] 1. to fix the value, price: with accusative of person(s), of Christ, (LXX). 2. to honour: with accusative of person(s), (LXX), " (LXX) (LXX), " (LXX), " (LXX), πολλαῖς τιμαῖς.
two thousand, (Herdotus Historicus):—;singular with collective nouns, δισχιλίη ἵππος 2000 horse, (Herdotus Historicus)

[in LXX chiefly for זָמַר pi., also for נָגַן pi.;] 1. to pull, twitch, twang, hence, 2. absol., (a) to play a stringed instrument with the fingers; (b) later, to sing to a harp, sing psalms (LXX); in NT, to sing a hymn, sing praise: with dative of person(s), (LXX), dative instr..
[in LXX for דָּרַךְ, רָמַס, שָׁאַף,] to tread down, trample under foot: pass.. Metaphorical, τ. υἱὸν τ. θεοῦ.
(ἄτιμος) [in LXX for כְּלִמָּה, קָלוֹן,] dishonour, disgrace: εἰς ἀ., ἐν ἀ., κατ᾽ ἀ., πάθη ἀτιμίας, base passions.
τό (ἕρπω, to crawl), [in LXX chiefly for רֶמֶשׂ, שֶׁרֶץ;] a creeping thing, reptile.

[in LXX for עֶצֶב and cogn. forms,] pain of body or mind, grief, sorrow: opposite to χαρά, ἀπὸ τῆς λ., ἐκ λ., ἡ κατὰ θεὸν λ., opposite to ἡ τ. κόσ-μου λ., λ. μοι ἐστιν, λ. ἔχω, id. before ἀπό, λ. ἐπὶ λ. ἔχω, ἐν λ. ἐλθεῖν, (to come sad and cause sadness); pl..

συν-έχω [in LXX for עָצָר, חָבַר,] 1. to hold together (τ. συνέχον τ. πάντα, Wis.1:7): of closing the ears, (τ. στόμα,); to hem in, press on every side. 2. to hold fast; (a) of a prisoner, to hold in charge: (b) to constrain: pass., in pass., of ills, to be seized or afflicted by, suffering from.
[in LXX chiefly for כַּלָּה;] 1. cl., a bride, young wife, young woman: WH, mg.. 2. As frequently in LXX (, for כַּלָּה; (a) bride; (b) daughter-in-law) and in MGr. (νύφφη, νύφη), a daughter-in-law.
the eighth., " (LXX), one of eight, with seven others.

1. a block of stone used as a prop or buttress to a wall, (Iliad by Homer): a block of rockcrystal, in which the Egyptian mummies were cased, (Herdotus Historicus) 2. a block or slab, bearing an inscription; and so, 3. a gravestone, (Homer), attic 4. a block or slab, inscribed with record of victories, dedications, treaties, decrees…
[in LXX chiefly for = רָעֵב;] to hunger, be hungry: " (LXX), metaphorically.

(ὁδηγός) [in LXX chiefly for נוּחַ, also for דֶּרֶךְ hi., הָלַךְ hi.,] to lead on one's way, to guide: with accusative of person(s), id. before ἐπί. Metaphorical, to guide, instruct, teach: before εἰς τ. ἀλήθειαν (ἐν τ. ἀ., WH, mg.).
ή (ἀσχήμων), [in LXX chiefly for עֶרְוָה;] unseemliness: euphemism for ἡ αἰσχύνη, as frequently in LXX, shame, nakedness.
1. a foraging, a foraging expedition, foray, (Xenophon Historicus): in plural, foraging parties, (Xenophon Historicus) 2. an elephant's trunk, (Polybius Historicus) 3. = προ-νομία, (Lucian)
[in LXX chiefly for מָרַד qal., hi., מְרִי, most frequently in Psa and Eze;] to embitter, provoke: absol..
ὑπο-δείκνυμι [in LXX for נָגַד hi.,] 1. to show secretly. 2. to show by tracing out; hence, generally, to teach, make known: with dative of person(s), id. with inf., before, ὅτι.
Attic, genitive (-αος) -ως, dative ᾳ; Ion. and κοινή, -εος (-ους), dative -ει, τό, [in LXX for שֵׂיבָה,] old age: ἐν γήρει.
ὑπ-εναντίος, -α, -ον [in LXX for אָיַב, צַר,] set over against, opposite. Metaphorical, opposed to, contrary to: with dative of person(s), absol., as subst., ὁ ὑ..

[in LXX chiefly for רָצָה;] 1. to receive to oneself, receive favourably, admit, accept: with accusative of person(s), with accusative of thing(s), (R, mg.). 2. to expect, look for, wait for: with accusative of person(s), with accusative of thing(s), Ju 21.
(δάκτυλος), [in LXX chiefly for טַבַּעַת;] a ring.
[in LXX for תּוֹלָע, תּוֹלָע, שָׁנִי,] scarlet: neut., without substantive, of clothing
[in LXX chiefly for גֹּרֶן;] a threshing floor: (here prob. by meton. = the grain on the threshing floor).

ἐπι-σκοπή, -ῆς, ἡ [in LXX chiey for פָּקַד פְּקֻדָּה;] 1. a visiting, visitation (εἰς ἐ. τοῦ παιδός, Lucian, dial. deor., 20, 6); as in LXX (after Heb.), of God's visitation in mercy, or in judgment. 2. office, charge, esp. office of an ἐπίσκοιος: (LXX), (Cremer, 527 f., 864; DCG, ii, 809b).

τό indecl. (Aram. טַּסְחָא), [in LXX for פֶּסַח;] 1. the festival of the Passover.ἡ ἐορτὴ τοῦ π.. 2. By meton., (a) the paschal supper: ἑτοιμάζειν τὸ π., ποιεῖν τό π., (b) the pasohal lamb: θύειν τό π., of Christ, φαγεῖν τὸ π. (lamb or supper).
[in LXX chiefly for אֶצְבַּע;] a finger: metaphorically, δ. θεοῦ.
a glade or grove, Lat. saltus, (Homer); grove, (Odyssey by Homer)
ἐκ-πορνεύω [in LXX chiefly for זָנָה, frequently of spiritual unfaithfulness;] strengthened form of πoρνεύω, implying excessive indulgence; mid, to give oneself up to fornication: Ju 7.

[in LXX chiefly for אֶרֶז, χειμάρρους τῶν Κέδρων, (קִדְרוֹן);] a cedar: χείμαρρος τῶν Κ. (as in 2Sam, 1Ki, ll. with). Κεδρών, ὁ, indecl. (in FlJ, genitive -ῶνος; Heb. קִדְרוֹן), [in LXX:] Cedron (OT, Kidron): χείμαρρος τοῦ Κ..

(χαίρω), [in LXX for שִׂמְחָה, שָׂשׂוֹן,] joy, delight: opposite to κατήφεια, to λύπη, χ. τῆς πίστεως, ἀγαλλιᾶσθαι, χαρᾷ, χ. ἔχειν, Phm 7; πληροῦν (-οῦσθαι) χαρᾶς, ποιεῖν χ. μεγάλην, ἀπὸ τῆς χ., ἐν χ., μετὰ χαρᾶς, id. beforeπνεύματος ἁγίου, χ. ἐν π. ἁ, χ. ἐπί, διά, ὅτι, ἵνα, III Jn 4 By meton., of the cause or occasion of joy: WH, txt.…
[in LXX chiefly for שָׁקַט;] to be still; (a) to rest from labour: (b) to live quietly: (with) to be silent. SYN.: σιγάω, σιωπάω
adv., whence; (a) of direction or source: = ἐκεῖθεν ὅπου, ὅ. γινώσκομεν, (b) of cause, whence, wherefore.
indecl. (Heb. שְׁכֶם), Shechem; 1. the son of Hamor: b, Rec. 2. A city of Samaria (AV, Sychem; in LXX also sometimes Σίκιμα, -ων, as in FlJ): a,b.
(ταπεινόω), [in LXX chiefly for עֳנִי;] abasement, humiliation, low estate: " (LXX), (Plat., Arist., and later writers).
ἀνα-βοάω, -ῶ [in LXX for צָעַק, זָעַק, קָרָא,] to cry out.

(ἵκω, ἱκάνω, to reach, attain), [in LXX for דַּי,] 1. of persons, suffcient, competent, fit: with inf., before πρός, before ἵνα. 2. Of things, in number, quantity or size, sufficient, enough, much, many: absol., ἱκανοί, (WH, R, omit), ὄχλος ἱ., κλαυθμός, ἀργύρια, λαμπάδες, λόγοι, φῶς, ἱ, ἐστιν, τὸ ἱ. ποιεῖν, τὸ ἱ. λαμβάνειν, of time…
indecl. (in FlJ, -έου), ὁ (Heb. קֶרַח) Korah: Ju 11.
[in LXX chiefly for יָרֵחַ, also for לְבָנָה; ((10), ?);] the moon: " (LXX).
[in LXX for כּ'' הָרֹאשׁ,כּ'' הַגָּדוֹל,כּהֵן;] 1. high-priest: of Christ. In pl., chief priests, including ex-high-priests and members of high-priestly families.

(βασιλεύς), [in LXX for מֶלֶךְ and its cognates;] royal, belonging to a king: χώρα, Act; ἐσθής, νόμος β., a supreme law, "a law which governs other laws and so has a specially regal character" (Hort), or because made by a king, τις, one in the service of a king, a courtier, (WH, mg., βασιλίσκος).
τό (βάλλω), [in LXX chiefly for חֵץ;] a missile, a dart.
[in LXX chiefly for נָפַל hi.;] 1. to cast down, prostrate: metaphorically, pass.. 2. to put down, lay down: metaphorically, mid., with accusative, θεμέλιον.

[in LXX chiefly for parts and derivatives of אכל;] 1. eating: β. καὶ πόσις, with genitive obj., metaphorically, corrosion, rust. 2. As also in cl. = βρῶμα, food: a.; metaphorically, of spiritual nourishment.
δι-αιρέω, -ῶ [in LXX for בּתר (as), חלק (as),] 1. to divide into parts, cut asunder. 2. to distribute: with accusative of thing(s), dative of person(s).
ἐπι-συν-άγω [in LXX for אָסַף, קָבַץ, (Cremer, 65);] 1. to gather together: pass.. 2. to gather together against.
adv., as pl. of δεῦρο, 1. (b), which see, [in LXX chiefly for לְכוּ;] come on! come here! come!: with imperat., with subjc., before ὀπίσω, πρός, εἰς.
(genitive pl.), dative -οις, -αις, accusative -ους, -ας, -α (no nom.), recipr. pron. (ἄλλος), of one another, mutually
συν-κλείω (Rec. συγκ-), [in LXX chiefly for סגר;] to shut together, enclose, shut in on all sides: of a catch of fish, metaphorically.

[in LXX chiefly for חֵיק;] 1. prop., the bosom: fig., of close association, ἐν (εἰς τὸν) τοῖς κ. Ἀβραάμ, ὁ ὢν εἰς τὸν κ. τ. πατρός, 2. The bosom or fold of a loose garment falling over a girdle, used as a pocket, hence figuratively, εἰς τὸν κ., 3. A bosom-like hollow, as a bay or gulf.
adv., whence; (a) of place: metaphorically, of condition, (b) of origin: of parentage, (with) of cause.
adv. of place, [in LXX chiefly for אָחוֹר, אַחַר;] behind, after. As prep. with genitive: (WH, mg.).
ἀν-ίημι (ἀνά, ἵημι), [in LXX for רָפָה, נָשָׂא,] 1. to send up, produce, to send back. 2. to let go, leave without support. 3. to relax, loosen: hence, metaphorically, to give up, desist from.

(ἄγω, in sense, to weigh), [in LXX for בֵּן, מָלֵא, שָׁוָה; frequently in Wis, 2Mac;] 1. Part One (a) of weight, worth, before πρός: (b) befitting, meet: with genitive, absol., (with) of persons, worthy; 2. Part Two α in good sense: with genitive of thing(s), with aor. inf.: Act_13:25, before ἵνα: ἅς, absol.…
ἀπο-καθ-ίστημι, [in LXX chiefly for שׁוּב;] 1. to restore, i.e. to a former condition: of health, of social or political affairs. 2. to give back, bring back.
κατ-άρα, -ας, -ἡ [in LXX chiefly for קְלָלָה;] a curse: opposite to εὐλογία, concrete, of Christ.
ἐκ-λύω [in LXX for רָפָה,] 1. to loose, release. 2. to unloose, as a bow-string, to relax, enfeeble; pass., to be faint, grow weary: of mental weariness, " (LXX).

συν-ίστημι [in LXX for צָוָה pi., קָהַל ni., 1Ma.12:43, 2Ma.4:24, 3Ma.1:19 (and frequently in these books);] 1. trans., (a) to commend, recommend: with accusative of person(s), id. with dative, (as frequently at the beginning of a letter; Deiss., LAE, 226), before πρός, pass., before ὑπό, (b) to show, prove, establish: with accusative…
τό, [in LXX chiefly for חֶדֶר;] 1. a treasury. 2. a store-chamber (Arist., Xen.;). 3. an inner chamber.
ἐν-τρέπω [in LXX for כָּנַע ni., כָּלַם ni.,] to turn about; metaphorically, put to shame: with accusative, pass., mid., to reverence: with accusative of person(s) (cl. with genitive).
[in LXX chiefly for צָבָא;] 1. = στρατός, an army, a host: of angels, of the stars of heaven. 2. As sometimes in cl. (poët.), = στρατεία: T (WH, RV, στρατεία).
(θαυμάζω), [in LXX for פָּלָא and cogn. forms, יָרֵא ni., אַדִּיר,] wonderful, marvellous: (LXX).

τό (ὁμοιόω), [in LXX for דְּמוּת, תַּבְנִית, תְּמוּנָה,] that which is made like something; (a) concrete, an image, like­ness: (b) abstract, like­ness, resemblance: ἐν ὁ. εἰκόνος. SYN.: εἰκών, ὁμοίωσις
[in LXX for נָקָם, רִיב,] 1. custom. 2. right. 3. a judicial hearing; hence its result, the execution of a sentence, punishment: δ. τίνειν, δ. υπεχειν, Ju 7. 4. Personified, justice, vengeance.
to go out for foraging, (Polybius Historicus)

τό (χράομαι) [in LXX: (נֶכֶס), (כֶּסֶף), frequently in Sir, 2 and 4 Mac;] a thing that one uses or needs (and generally, a matter, event, business); hence in pl., (a) wealth, riches: οἱ τά χ. ἔχοντες, (b) money: sing. (rare in cl.) of a special sum of money.
(φρονέω), [in LXX for בִּין, חָכָם;] practically wise, sensible, prudent: opposite to μωρός, to ἄφρων, φ. παρ᾽ ἑαυτῷ (EV, wise in one's own conceit), compar., -ώτερος. SYN.: see: σοψός
[in LXX chiefly for נְחֹשֶׁת;] copper: by meton., of copper coin.
1. mostly in plural Γίγαντες, the Giants, a savage race destroyed by the gods, (Odyssey by Homer); the sons of Gaia, (Hesiod) 2. as adjective mighty, Ζέφυρος γίγας (Aeschulus Tragicus)
[in LXX for הָפַךְ,] 1. to turn down, turn over; as, the soil. 2. to overturn, overthrow: pass. pf. ptcp., (LXX).
(fem. of δαμάλης, a bullock), [in LXX chiefly for פָּרָה, עֶגְלָה;] a heifer.
adv., [in LXX for אֶחָד, פַּעַם;] (a) once: Heb_9:26-27; ἔτι ἅ., ἅ. τ. ἐνιαυτοῦ, καί ἅ. κ. δίς, twice: (b) once for all: Ju 3 5.
ἔπ-αυλις, -εως, ἡ (αὐλή), [in LXX for חָצֵר, טִירָה, (l.with),] a dwelling, habitation: (LXX).
συλ-λέγω [in LXX chiefly for לָקַט;] to bring together, collect, gather up: with accusative of thing(s), pass., with accusative, before ἀπό, id. before ἐκ, before εἰς.
ἐκ-κόπτω, [in LXX for כָּרַת,] to cut out, cut off, cut down: of a hand, foot, a tree, figuratively, of a branch, before ἐκ, metaphorically, τ. ἀφορμήν.

(WH, Ἐβ-), -α, -ον (Aram, עִבְרַי), as subst., ὁ Ἑ., [in LXX for עֵבֶר, עִבְרִי;] a Hebrew. 1. In OT, of Israelites in contrast with those of another race. 2. In NT as the correlative of Ἑλληνιστής, a Jew who had adopted, in greater or less degree, Greek culture and Greek language. The distinction was not merely linguistic (DB, ii, 325)…
adv (ἀνά), (a) up, upwards: (b) above (opposite to κάτω): Act_2:19; with art. ἡ, τά, ἕως ἄ. (up to the brim).

1. a bar used as a lever, a crowbar, handspike, Lat, vectis, used for moving ships, (Odyssey by Homer); for forcing doors and gates, (Euripides) 2. the stake which Ulysses ran into the Cyclops' eye, (Odyssey by Homer) 3. a wooden bar, placed across gates on the inside and secured by the βάλανος, (Aeschulus Tragicus)
τό [in LXX chiefly for כּוֹכָב;] (a) mostly in pl. (as in cl.), the stars: (b) in sing., only of some noted star; the symbol or image of a star.
[in LXX chiefly for כָּבָה;] of fire or things on fire, to quench: with accusative, pass., [44, 46]. Metaphorical: τὸ πνεῦμα. ζβέννυμι, for σβ-, T.
[in LXX chiefly for יָסַד;] to lay the foundation of, to found: with accusative, τ. γῆν, (LXX); pass., metaphorically, (R, mg., settle); pass..
Tyre, a maritime city of Phænicia: Τ. κ, Σιδών.

[in LXX chiefly for מָצוֹק, צַר;] 1. necessity: ἔχειν ἀ-, with inf., to be compelled, (Rec., R, mg.), Ju 3, ἐξ ἀ., κατ᾽ ἀ., of necessity, Phm 14; ἀ. μοι ἐπίκειται, n. is laid on me, with inf. (= ἀναγκαῖον ἐστι), 2. force, violence, hence pain, distress: pl., ἐν ἀ..
(in Attic, βασιλεία, βασιλίς), [in LXX chiefly for מַלְכָּה;] a queen.

1. of or belonging to war, (Pindar), —; τὰ πολέμια whatever belongs to war, war and its business, (Herdotus Historicus), 2. of or like an enemy, hostile, (Pindar),—;as Substantive an enemy, (Herdotus Historicus), attic; οἱ π. the enemy, (Thucydides): —; τὸ π. hostility, (Thucydides) 3. generally, opposed, adverse…

[in LXX chiefly for יָבֵשׁ, its parts and deriva­tives, also for חָרָבָה,] dry: metaphorically (of a sinner), ξύλον ξ., of members of the body shrunken by disease, withered: of the hand, of the dry land, ἡ ξηρά: γῆ.
[in LXX chiefly for נָחָשׁ;] a serpent, snake: as typical of wisdom and cunning, of Satan.

[in LXX chiefly for הָפַךְ, also for סָבַב,] to turn: with accusative of thing(s) dative of person(s), = ἀποσ-, to bring back, reflexively, to turn oneself, with accusative before εἰς, = μετασ-, to change. Pass., reflexive, to turn oneself: before εἰς, ptcp., στραφείς, with indic., id. before πρός, (WH, R, om.), metaphorically…
eighty, Lat. octoginta, (Thucydides),—;ionic and doric ὀγδώκοντα, (Iliad by Homer)
(αἰχμάλωτος), [in LXX chiefly for שׁבה;] = αἰχμαλωτίζω, which see, to lead captive: (LXX).
conj. (ἐπί, εἰ), when, since; 1. of time, when, after: (Rec., WH, mg.). 2. Of cause, since, because: (Rec., WH, mg.), ἐ. οὖν. With ellipsis, otherwise, else: ἐ. ἄρα, introducing a question.
a particle of assurance, verily, truly; εἰ (εἶ) μ. (= cl., ἦ μ. in LXX and π.), now verily, full surely: (LXX).

[in LXX: (עָתִיד) (אַחֲרוֹן); elsewhere for fut., and frequently in Wi, II, 4Mac;] to be about to be or do; 1. with inf.; (a) of intending or being about to do of one's own free will: with inf. praes., (Field, Notes, 240), with inf. aor., (b) of compulsion, necessity or certainty: with inf. praes., with inf. aor.. 2. Ptcp.…

(φοβέω), [in LXX chiefly for יָרֵא, also for דְּחַל, אָיֹם;] fearful, whether act, or pass.; 1. act., = δεινός, causing fear, terrible (LXX): 2. Pass., = δειλός, feeling fear, timid (cl. in both senses).
(ὅμοιος), [in LXX chiefly for דָּמָה;] 1. to make like, with genitive and dative; pass., to be made or become like: before ὡς. 2. to liken, compare: with dative, accusative, πῶς όμοιώσωμεν, pass..
[in LXX chiefly for זָנָה;] a prostitute, harlot. Metaphorical, of Babylon (i.e. Rome).

[in LXX chiefly for גָּזַל, טָרַף;] to seize, catch up, snatch away, carry off by force: with accusative of thing(s), τ. βασιλείαν τ. θεοῦ, with accusative of person(s), Ju 23; pass., before ἕως, εἰς, πρός.

(i.e. ὁ τὴν εὐνὴν(bed) ἔχων), [in LXX for סָרִיס, Wis.3:14, Sir.20:4;] an emasculated man, a eunuch: one such holding, as was common, high office, as of chamberlain, at court, metaphorically, of one naturally incapacitated for or volun­tarily abstaining from wedlock.
ἀντ-ὲχω (ἀντί, ἔχω), [in LXX for חָזַק hi.,] 1. trans., to hold against. 2. Intrans., to withstand. Mid. 1. in cl., to hold out against. 3., to hold firmly to, cleave to: with genitive.
(κλαίω), [in LXX chiefly for בְּכִי;] crying, weeping, κ. καὶ ὀδυρμός, (LXX); ὁ κ. καὶ ὁ βρυγμός.
τό (πλέω), [in LXX chiefly for אֳנִיָּה;] a boat, also (= obsolete ναῦς) a ship: and frequently in Gosp. and Ac.
poët, and late prose, [in LXX for אכל;] to eat.
(-ᾶ, Rec.), indecl. (but τὸ Σιναῖον, FlJ, Ant., iii, 5, 1; τὸ Σιναῖον ὄρος, ib. ii, 12, 1), τό (Heb. סִינַי), Sinai
ἀπο-ρίπτω (Rec. -ρρίπτω, c1.), [in LXX for שָׁלַךְ hi.,] to throw away, cast forth: reflexively.

(epic ἶσος, so sometimes Rec.), -η, -ον, [in LXX for כְּ֜, Jb; אֶחָד, ff.; 2Ma.9:15, 4Ma.13:20-21,] equal, the same in size, number, quality, δωρεά, μαρτυρίαι, ἴ. ποιεῖν, with accusative and dative, ἑαυτὸν τ. θεῷ, τὰ ἴ. ἀπολαβεῖν, n. pl., ἴσα, adverbially, τ. θεῷ.
(θεός), [in LXX: (אֵל, אֱלֹהִים, אֱלוֹהַּ), Sir.6:35, 1-37 II Ma.1:1-29, 4Mac.25 *;] divine: δύναμις, φύσις, τὸ θ., the Deity (so in cl.; of God, in Philo and FlJ).
see: ὑπερεῖδον. ὑπερ-εῖδον, aor. [in LXX for עָלַם hi., מַעַל,] to overlook: with accusative of thing(s)

and in late Gk., also -εος, τό, [in LXX for קִנְאָה,] 1. zeal: κατά ζῆλος, with genitive obj., (LXX), before ὑπέρ, with genitive subj., θεοῦ, πυρός. 2. jealousy: (WH, txt, RV), πλησθῆναι ζήλου; pl., ζῆλοι, WH, mg.

interrog. pronom. adj. (corresponding to the demonstr. τοῖος and the relat. οἷος), [in LXX chiefly for זֶה אֵי־;] of what quality or sort: absol., n. pl., with subst.; (a) prop., in direct questions: (b) in indirect questions = ὁποῖος: ποῖας (sc. ὁδοῦ).
ἐπ-αν-ίστημι [in LXX chiefly for קוּם;] to raise up against; mid., to rise up against: before ἐπί, with accusative of person(s).

[in LXX chiefly for פָּרָה;] 1. trans., to make to grow. Pass., to grow, increase, become greater: τῇ ἐπιγνώσει τ. θεοῦ, εἰς σωτηρίαν. 2. In later Gk. (but nowhere in LXX), intrans., to grow, increase: of plants, of infants, of a multitude, of the increase of the Gospel: ὁ λόγος ηὔξανε, of Christ as a leader…
[in LXX chiefly for מוּל;] (Ion., Epic. and late writers), to cut around (Hdt.), hence, to circumcise (π. τὰ αἰδοῖα, Hdt.). Pass. and mid., to be circumcised, receive circumcision: Metaphorical.

illative particle, expressing a more subjective or informal inference than οὖν, then: prop. (as in cl.), the second word in the sentence, ἐπεὶ ἄρα, (with another word between); as the first word, so prop. in apodosis after protasis with εἰ, (κενὸν ἄρα), often in interrogations, direct and indirect, τίς (τί) ἄρα, εἰ ἄρα, εἴπερ ἄρα…
[in LXX chiefly for אֵפֶר;] ashes: ἐν σάκκῳ καὶ σ..
wheat, (Homer); also in plural, (Odyssey by Homer)
(ἄλλος), [in LXX chiefly for חָלַף, מוּר hi.,] 1. to change. 2. to transform. 3. to exchange: with accusative, before ἐν (= בְּ,) instead of simple genitive.
[in LXX chiefly for שׁוֹר;] a bull.
[in LXX chiefly for hi.;] to strike, smite, beat: with accusative, of mourners, τὰ στήθη, ἐπὶ τ. σιαγόνα, εἰς τ. κεφαλήν. Metaphorical, of God inflicting evil: of disquieting conscience.
adv., strengthened for ὡς (in Hom, at the beginning of a clause, in the form ὣς δ᾽ αὔτως, later in one word), in like manner, just so, likewise: with verb to be supplied from context.
κυνός, ὁ, ἡ, [in LXX forכֶּלֶב;] a dog: metaphorically, as a word of reproach.

and -ύω, [in LXX chiefly for חָגַר, also for אָזַר,] to gird (with dupl, accusative, as ὁ περιζωννύων με δύναμιν,): pass., αἱ ὀσφύες περιεζωσμέναι, π. ζώνην χρυσῆν. Mid., to gird oneself: with accusative of thing(s) (figuratively), τ. ὀσφύν.
[in LXX chiefly for שֵׁשׁ, בּוּץ;] byssus, a fine species of flax, also the linen made from it.

τό (= cl. παραπέτασμα) [in LXX chiefly for פֹּרֶכֶת (the veil of the Holy of Holies), also for מָסָךְ (the outer veil), Num_3:26, (elsewhere κάλυμμα);] in NT always the inner veil or curtain of the Temple (or Tabernacle): figuratively, ἡ σὰρξ αὐτοῦ.

[in LXX for הָלַל hith.,] to boast or glory: absol., (LXX) " (LXX), with accusative of thing(s), before ἐν (LXX), ἐν (τ.) θεῷ, ἐν κυρίῳ, (LXX) (LXX); ἐν Χ. Ἰησοῦ, before ἐπί with dative, περί, with genitive, εἰς, ὑπέρ, with genitive of person(s), ἐνώπιον τ. θεοῦ.

(οἰκτείρω), [in LXX, usually in pl., chiefly for רַחַם;] compassion, pity. σπλάγχνα οἰκτιρμοῦ, a heart of compassion, in pl. (as LXX for Heb. רַחַם), οἰ. τ. θεοῦ, ό πατὴρ τῶν οἰ, σπλάγχνα κ. οἰ.. SYN.: ἔλεος, q.v

τό (ζωός, alive), [in LXX for חַי (chiefly) and cognate forms; frequently in Wis;] a living creature, an animal: ff. ff.; ζῴων τ. αἷμα, ἄλογα ζ., Ju 10. SYN.: θηρίον, in which the brutal, bestial element is emphasized, and which is never used of sacrificial animals. On the other hand, ζ. is the more comprehensive…
[in LXX chiefly for נְקֵבָה;] female: as subst., ἡ θ., a female, a woman: τὸ θ...
ἐπ-ονομάζω [in LXX chiefly for קָרָא;] to name, call by a name, surname: pass..
τό [in LXX for עֵץ,] a tree: δ. ἀγαθόν, δ. καλόν, δ. σαπρόν, γίνεσθαι δ., γ. εἰς δ..
(μακρός), adv. (chiefly late), [in LXX for רָחוֹק, רָחַק,] from afar, afar: ἀπὸ μ..

τό, [in LXX for חַטָּאָה, עָוֺן;] an act of disobedience to divine law (Lft., Notes, 273), a sinful deed, a sin: WH, mg.; αἰώνιωv ἀ. (DCG, i, 788a). SYN.: ἀγνόημα, ἁμαρτία, ἀνομία, ἀσέβεια, ἥττημα, παράβασις, παρακοή, παρανομία, παράπτωμα (ν. Cremer, 100; Tr., Syn., § lxvi; DB, iv, 532; DCG, l.with; Westc, Eph., 165 f.)
ἀνα-βιβάζω (causal of ἀναβαίνω), [in LXX chiefly for עָלָה hi., also for רָכַב hi.,] to make go up, draw up, as a ship (Xen.): σαγήνην.
(= Hom. μόγος), in cl. chiefly poët., [in LXX for תְּלָאָה, עָמָל,] toil, labour, hardship, distress. SYN.: κόπος, πόνος

(φῶς) [in LXX for אוֹר hi, יָרָה hi.,] 1. intrans., to shine, give light (Arist., Plut., a1.): before ἐπί. 2. Trans. (a) to illumine, enlighten: with accusative, pass.. Metaphorical, of spiritual enlightenment: R, txt., (b) to bring to light, make known (Polyb.): R, mg..
(φέρω), [in LXX chiefly for מַס, also for מִדָּה,] tribute paid by a subject nation: φ. δοῦναι (1Ma.8:4 1Mac), ἀποδοῦναι, τελεῖν. SYN.: κῆνσος, τέλος
a satrap, viceroy, Lat. satrapa, (Xenophon Historicus) Persian word.

[in LXX for זֵד, גֵּאֶה, לוּץ,] showing oneself above others; (a) in good sense, pre-eminent, splendid; (b) more frequently in had sense, and so always in Scr., arrogant, haughty, disdainful: διανοίᾳ καρδίας, opposite to ταπεινός (as in), " (LXX). SYN.: ἀλαζών, ὑβριστής, see Tr., Syn., § xxix
(ὥρα), [in LXX for נָאָה, טוֹב, יָפָה,] seasonable, timely, esp. of ripe fruits; hence, blooming, beautiful (both of things and persons): (LXX, ὥρα).
(ἀπάτη), [in LXX for פָּתָה, נָשָׁא hi.,] to deceive: with accusative, with accusative of person(s), dative of thing(s), pass..
(dim, of θύρα), [in LXX chiefly for חַלּוֹן;] a window.
[in LXX chiefly for יוֹנָה;] a dove
(συγγενής), [in LXX chiefly for מִשְׁפָּחָה;] 1. kinship. 2. By meton., kinsfolk, kindred
[in LXX for סָפַר pi., פָּקַד pi.,] to number.

[in LXX chiefly for לָקַח, also for יָרַשׁ,] 1. with accusative of thing(s), like παραδέχομαι, correl. to παραδίδωμι, to receive from another: of the mind, with inf., before παρά, with gem, τ. Χριστόν (Lft., in l). 2. C. accusative of person(s), to take to or with oneself: γυναῖκα, μεθ᾽ ἑαυτοῦ, before εἰς, κατ᾽ ἰδίαν, mid.…

1. acquisition, (Thucydides); κατ᾽ ἔργου κτῆσιν according to success in the work, (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. (from perfect) possession, (Sophocles Tragicus), 3. as collective, = κτήματα, possessions, property, (Homer); in plural, (Herdotus Historicus)
[in LXX chiefly for נָטָה, also for תָּקַע,] to make fast, to fix; of tents, to pitch.
ἀπ-άγω [in LXX for נָהַג, הָלַךְ hi.,] to lead away: (R, mg.), esp. of leading to trial (so as law term in Attic), prison and death: of the direction of a way.
[in LXX chiefly for עָבַר;] 1. to go beside, accom­pany. 2. to go past, pass by: before διά, with genitive, (WH, mg.).

(δίκαιος), [in LXX chiefly for צָדַק pi., hi., (1) as, (2) as;] 1. in cl., (a) with accusative of thing(s), to deem right; (b) with accusative of person(s), to do one justice; pass., δικαιοῦσθαι, to be treated rightly, opposite to ἀδικεῖσθαι. 2. In NT, as in LXX, and as usual with verbs in -όω from adjectives of moral meaning…
(νέμω, to pasture), [in LXX chiefly for מִרְעֶה, also for נָוֶה,] 1. a pasture, pasturage: figuratively, 2. a grazing, feeding; metaphorically, of a spreading sore, (Polyb.).
(σκληρός), [in LXX chiefly for קָשָׁה hi., also for חָזַק;] to harden. Metaphorical, to harden, make stubborn: with accusative of person(s), T. καρδίας. Pass., to become hardened.
[in LXX for תָּמָר תִּמֹּר;] the date palm, palm: τὰ βαΐα τῶν φ., of palm branches, φοίνικες.

(ὁμός, θυμός), [in LXX for יַחַד (frequently in Jb), Wis.10:20,] with one mind, with one accord: (Hatch, Essays, 63 f., argues that the un-cl. sense together, which is found in, Wis.18:5, 12 (but not Wis.10:20), should be attached to the NT instances, but see Abbott, Essays, 96; MM, xviii).

[in LXX for מְנוֹרָה;] a lampstand: of that in the Tabernacle, metaphorically, of the two witnesses, of the seven churches of Asia, of the removal of a church from its position, κινεῖν τ. λυχνίαν κ.τ.λ..
(πίπτω), [in LXX chiefly for נֶגֶף, מַפֶּלֶת, and cogn. forms;] a falling, fall: metaphorically.
(ἀσεβής), [in LXX for פָּשַׁע, רָשַׁע;] to be ungodly, act profanely: with cogn. accusative, Ju 15.
ἐν-οικέω, -ῶ [in LXX chiefly (29/36) for יָשַׁב;] to dwell in; metaphorically, before ἐν, with dative of person(s): ὁ θεός, τ. πνεῦμα, ὁ λόγος, πίστις, ἁμαρτία.

(κόλλα, glue), [in LXX chiefly for דָּבַק;] 1. to glue or cement together. 2. Generally, to unite, to join firmly. Pass., to cleave to, join (oneself to): with dative of person(s), (LXX), τ. πόρνῃ, τ. Κυρίῳ, with dative of thing(s), ἅρματι, τ. ἀγαθῴ, of sins joining together, ἄχρι τ. οὐρανοῦ, of dust.

[in LXX for נָבָל, frequently in Sir.;] 1. prop., of the nerves, dull, sluggish. 2. Of the mind, dull, stupid, foolish: (T, WH, txt., R, om.); of things, παράδοσις, (T, WH, txt., R, om.): ζητήσεις, τὸ μ. τ. θεοῦ, τὰ μ. τ. κόσμου.

(τιμή), [in LXX chiefly for יָקָר;] valued, hence, (a) precious, costly, highly valued: primarily, of money value, λίθος, pl., compar., -ώτεφος, Rec.; superl., -ώτατος, in extended sense, καρπός, αἷμα, ἐπαγγέλματα, (b) held in honour, honoured, esteemed worthy: with dative, ὁ γάμος, ψυχή.
(Rec. Ἠσαΐας), -ου, ο (Heb. יְשַׁעְיָה), Isaiah, the prophet: ἀνεγίνωςκεν τ. προφήτην Ἠ., ἐν τ. Ἠ..
(εὖ, σέβομαι), [in LXX: (צַדִּיק), (חָסִיד), (נָדִיב), and frequently in Sirach and 4Maccabees;] pious, godly, devout. SYN.: θεοσεβής, θρῆσκος

όν [in LXX: (מִקְדָּשׁ); τό ἱ, (בַּיִת), (עֲזָרָה); very frequently in I -4 Mac;] 1. in Hom., marvellous, mighty, divine. 2. (Also in Hom, and later cl.) consecrated to the deity, sacred: pl., ἱ. γράμματα. 3. As subst., (a) (so in Hom.), τὰ ἱ., sacrifices, sacred rites, sacred things: (b) later, τὸ ἱ.., a consecrated or sacred place…
(φίλος), [in LXX chiefly for אַהֲבָה;] friendship: with genitive obj..

(an Oriental word, first used by Xen. of the parks of Persian kings and nobles) [in LXX chiefly for גַּן, ff., also for עֵדֶן, פַּרְדֵּס,] 1. a park, pleasure-ground, garden (LXX), an orchard. 2. Paradise, the abode of the blessed dead.

[in LXX chiefly for הָלַךְ pi., hith.;] to walk: absol., with pred., γυμνός, ἐπάνω; διά, with genitive, ἐν, ἐν τ. σκοτίᾳ, figuratively, Jn; ἐπί, with genitive, id. with dative, μετά, παρά, with accusative. Metaphorical, of living, passing one's life, conducting oneself (like ἀναστρέφομαι in Xen., Plut., LXX, π.; M, Deiss., BS…
ῶνος, ὁ [in LXX chiefly for כְּתֹנֶת:] the garment worn next the skin, a tunic: Ju 23; dieting. from ἱμάτιον

and ῥήσσω, [in LXX chiefly for בָּקַע, also for קָרַע,] 1. to rend, break asunder: pass.. 2. Of the voice, with accusative, φωνήν, to break forth into speech: absol., (LXX). 3. = ῥήσσω, to throw or dash down. SYN.: θραύω, κατάγνυμι
[in LXX for שְׂעֹרָה;] barley: pl. (as usually in cl.).
(poët. in cl.), [in LXX chiefly for מַר;] 1. sharp, pointed. 2. sharp to the senses; of taste, bitter: opposite to γλυκύ, metaphorically, harsh, bitter
white linen: (WH, mg.). λευκός, ή, -όν [in LXX chiefly for לָבָן;] 1. bright, brilliant: of clothing, ὡς χιών, ἐν λ.. (sc. ἱματίοις), θρόνος. 2. white: figuratively, of garments, of ripened grain.
δι-αρπάζω [in LXX for בָּזַז, גָּזַל, שָׁסַס,] to plunder.
[in LXX chiefly for בָּלַע;] 1. to drink down, swallow. 2. to devour. Metaphorical, to swallow up, consume: pass., (LXX).
[in LXX chiefly for זוּב;] to flow.
(γέρων), [in LXX for זָקֵן;] a council of elders, senate; in NT, of the Sanhedrin (Cl. Rev., i, 43f.; DB, ext., 99).

[in LXX chiefly for ידע;] to make plain, declare: with accusative, with dative of person(s), with dative of person(s), before περί (pass.), before εἰς. SYN.: ἐμφανίζω, to make manifest, render visible to the sight; δ. to render evident to the mind.
τος, ὁ [in LXX chiefly for תַּנִּין;] a dragon, a mythical monster: figuratively, of Satan.
[in LXX chiefly for חָתַת ni.;] to terrify. Pass., to be terrified: (WH, mg., θροηθέντες).
[in LXX chiefly for מִזְרָק;] a shallow bowl (= Lat. patera), used for pouring libations.
κατ-οικία, -ας, ἡ (κατοικέω), [in LXX chiefly for מוֹשָׁב,] 1. a dwelling. 2. a settlement (Polyb.).
σύν-τριμμα, -τος, τό (συντρίβω), [in LXX chiefly for שֶׁבֶר; also for שֹׁד,] a fracture. Metaphorical, calamity, destruction: " (LXX).

[in LXX for גַּן, גַּנָּה, גִּנָּה,] a garden.

1. a headland, foreland, cape, (Homer), 2. a mountain-top, summit: used by (Homer) only in the phrase κατ᾽ ἄκρης from top to bottom, i. e. utterly, πόλιν αἱρέειν κατ᾽ ἄκρης (Herdotus Historicus); so in attic, κατ᾽ ἄκρας utterly, [variant datesTragica Adespota, (Plato Philosophus) 3. the citadel of a city, Lat. arx, (Xenophon Historicus)

ἐξ-ανίσημι [in LXX chiefly for קוּם;] 1. trans., to raise up: σπέρμα. 2. In 2 aor. act., intrans., to rise.

ἐχθές (Rec. χθές), adv., [in LXX for תְּמוֹל,] yesterday. ἐχθές, adverb ={χθές}, yesterday, ( 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 175, “Th.” 616, ἀπ᾽ ἐ. “Anthologia Graeca” 11.35 (1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus); μέσφα τό γ᾽ ἐ. 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 2.144); οὐ γάρ τι νῦν γε κἀ. today or yesterday…

[in LXX chiefly for עַתּוּד, also for צָפִיר, תַּיִשׁ;] a he-goat.

(δίψα, thirst), [in LXX chiefly for צָמֵא;] to thirst: absol., " (LXX), figuratively, with accusative (= cl. with genitive), τ. δικαιοσύνην.
ό [in LXX chiefly for תְּכֵלֶת;] hyacinth; (a) in cl., a flower, prob. the dark blue iris; (b) in late writers, a precious stone of the same colour, perhaps the sapphire.
(οἶκτος, pity), [in LXX for רָחַם pi., חָנַן,] to pity, have compassion on. with accusative of person(s), (LXX). SYN.: ἐλεέω, q.v

1. a going up, mounting on horseback, (Xenophon Historicus):—; πᾶσα ἄμβασις = πάντες ἀναβάται, all the horsemen, (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. an expedition up from the coast into Central Asia, as that of the younger Cyrus, (Xenophon Historicus) 3. a way up, ascent of a tower or mountain, (Herdotus Historicus)
[in LXX chiefly for רָעַשׁ;] to shake, move to and fro: τ. γῆν, (LXX); pass., ἡ γῆ, (LXX); συκῆ. Metaphorical, to agitate, stir up, with fear or some other emotion.

1. to err from the mark, fail, (Xenophon Historicus): to miss one's aim, (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. to err, do wrong, sin, (Herdotus Historicus), attic; with accusative cognate, ἐξ. τι to commit a fault, (Herdotus Historicus), 3. in Pass. to be mismanaged, (Plato Philosophus)

(χράομαι), [in LXX chiefly for טוֹב, also for יָקָר, יָשָׁר ( א A);] serviceable, good; (a) of things, good, pleasant: of food (as often in cl.), οἶνος, ζυγός, (EV, easy); in ethical sense, ἤθη, (b) of persons, good, kind, gracious: of God, τ. χρηστὸν (= ἡ χρηστότης) τοῦ θεοῦ.

indecl. (Heb. אָדָם), Adam: Ju 14. Christ ὁ ἔσχατος Ἀ..

Mid., 1. to have set before one. 2. to deposit with another, give in charge or commit to: with accusative and dative. 3. to bring forward, quote as evidence: before ὅτι.
[in LXX for שַׁחַר, בֹּקֶר,] daybreak, dawn: ὄρθρου βαθέως (M, Pr., 73), at early dawn, ὄρθρου, ὑπὸ τὸν ὄ..
[in LXX chiefly for פָּגַע;] 1. to go to meet. 2. to meet; with dative.

(μέρος), [in LXX chiefly for חָלַק;] to divide; (a) to divide into parts: metaphorically, pass., (WH, R, ing.), (Rec., R, txt.); μεμέρισται ὁ Χριστός, as in late authors, of factional division, καθ᾽ ἑαυτοῦ, ἐφ᾽ εαυτόν, (b) to distribute: with accusative of thing(s) and dative of person(s), as in later usage, to bestow: mid.…

(> ἁγνός), [in LXX always ceremonially, chiefly for קָדַשׁ;] to purify, cleanse from defilement; (a) ceremonially: (b) morally. SYN.: καθαρίζω, which see.
[in LXX for לוּחַ;] anything flat and broad. 1. a plain (poët.). 2. In late writers, a flat stone, a tablet.
to act lawlessly, περί τι (Herdotus Historicus)

ἐμ-πίπρημι, ἐμπρήθω, [in LXX chiefly for שָׂרַף;] to set on fire: πόλιν, pass., of the body, to become inflamed.

δι-αίρεσις, -εως, ἡ (διαιρέω), [in LXX chiefly for מַחֲלֹקֶת;] 1. a distinction, diference. 2. a division, distribution.
[in LXX for שׁוֹט,] a whip, scourge: metaphorically, of disease or suffering as a divine chastisement

In Attic writers, the mind, its operations and results; (a) mind, understanding; (b) purpose, intention: (with) judgment, opinion: (d) counsel, advice: Phm 14; (e) royal purpose, decree (as in Da…

(ἀρέσκω), [in LXX for יָשָׁר,] pleasing, agreeable: with dative of person(s), before ἐνώπιον, with genitive, ἀρεστόν ἐστιν, with accusative and inf.

1. to run away or off, escape, or flee from, especially by stealth, (Odyssey by Homer), attic; of runaway slaves, (Xenophon Historicus); of soldiers, to desert, (Xenophon Historicus) 2. with accusative to flee, shun, (Herdotus Historicus)
(μήτμρ), [in LXX chiefly for רֶחֶם;] the womb: (LXX).

(μήν), see: εἰ, iii, 7. εἰ, conjunctive particle, used in conditions and in indirect questions. I. Conditional, if; 1. with indic, expressing a general assumption; (a) pres.: before indic, pres., before imperat., before fut. indic., before pf. or aor., with negation in apodosis, similarly, before impf., before quæst.…
fem. Σύρα a Syrian: WH, mg.

(καλός), [in LXX for parts and derivatives of יָטַב;] finely, rightly, well: λέγειν, λαλεῖν, as exclamation of approval, κ. ποιεῖν, with dative of person(s) (cl. accusative; WM, § 32, 1 β), with accusative of thing(s), with ptcp., (M, Pr., 131), προϊστάναι (-ασθαι), διακονεῖν, ἀνατρέφεσθαι, ironically, κ. ἔχειν, to be well. Compar.…

[in LXX chiefly for מָכַר ni.;] to sell: with accusative of thing(s), with genitive (of price), with accusative of person(s) (of slavery), hence metaphorically.

τό dimin. of ποτήρ (πίνω), [in LXX chiefly for כּוֹס:] a wine cup: a (WH, R, mg., cm.), πίνειν ἐκ τοῦ π., with genitive of thing(s), τ. εὐλογίας, by meton., of the contents of the cup, b (WH, R, mg., cm.), with genitive of person(s). Metaphorical, of experience of divine providence; of prosperity…
(τρέφω), [in LXX for לֶחֶם, מָזוֹן, אֹכֶל,] nourishment, food. Metaphorical.
[in LXX for יָנָה, עָשַׁק,] to exercise power over, oppress: with accusative of person(s); with genitive of person(s), (ὑμᾶς, T); pass..
[in LXX chiefly for אַרְבֶּה, also for חָגָב,] a locust.

νεομηνία (Att.. contr., νουμ-, Rec.), -ας, ἡ (νέος, μήν), [in LXX chiefly for חֹדֶשׁ;] new moon: of the Jewish festival.

(μελέτη, care), [in LXX chiefly for הָגָה m;] 1. with genitive, to care for (Hes.). 2. C. accusative to attend to, practise. 3. to study, ponder: (LXX).
[in LXX for H661, H5362 hi., H6822 pi.,] 1. to surround, encompass. 2. to comprehend, include, contain, esp. of books: with accusative, Rec.; accusative to a late usage, intrans., it stands written.
1. to send away from home, (Odyssey by Homer),—;Pass. to be settled in a far land, to emigrate, (Plato Philosophus) 2. to colonise a place, send a colony to it, with accusative, (Herdotus Historicus)

Later confined by philos. writers to intrinsic eminence-moral goodness, virtue; (a) of God: (b) of men: pl. (Isa, Es, ll. with), excellencies
δι-αν-οίγω [in LXX for פֶּטֶר (Ex, Nu), פָּקַח, פָּתַח,] to open up completely, to open: (LXX); pass.. Metaphorical, δ. τ. νοῦν, τ. καρδίαν, pass., οἱ ὀφθαλμοί, of explaining, τ. γραφάς.
(contr. fr. συκέα), -ῆς, ἡ (σῦκον), [in LXX for תְּאֵן;] a fig-tree.
