1. a staff or stick to lean upon, a walking-stick, (Homer): metaphorically of the daughters of Oedipus, σκῆπτρα φωτός his staffs or supports, (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. a staff, as the badge of command, a sceptre: in (Homer) borne by chiefs, and transmitted from father to son…
[in LXX chiefly for קִינָה;] a lamentation: Rec.

(νηστεύω), [in LXX for צוֹם;] fasting, a fast; (a) of voluntary abstinence from food: (WH, R, txt., om.), (WH, txt., R, txt., om.), of the Day of Atonement, (b) of involuntary abstinence. SYN.: ἀσιτία, q.v
(-ους), τό [in LXX chiefly for שֶׁקֶר, also for כַּחַשׁ, כָּזָב;] a falsehood, untruth, lie: opposite to ἡ ἀλήθεια, to τὸ ἀληθές, ποιεῖν ψ., ἐν πάσῃ δυνάμει κ. σημείοις κ. τέρασιν ψεύδους.

τό (στερεόω), [in LXX: ff., Dan LXX, TH, (רָקִיעַ), (שַׁחַק), (סֶלַע), I (82), Sir.43:1, 8, 1Ma.9:14 *;] a solid body; (a) a support, foundation; metaphorically, strength ( Mac, ll. with); steadfastness, firmness: τ. πίστεως, (b) the dome of heaven (believed to be a solid canopy), the firmament (LXX).
(Attic, ἐλάα), -ας, ἡ [in LXX for זַיִת;] 1. an olive tree: τ. ὄρος τῶν ἐ. (זַיִת הַר,), the Mount of Olives: τὸ καλούμενον ἐ.. 2. an olive (Aristoph.).
ἀνα-βλέπω [in LXX chiefly for נָשָׂא;] 1. to look up: before εἰς, (Xen., Plat.). 2. to recover sight: al
(πίνω), [in LXX chiefly for מִשְׁתֶּה;] a drinking bout, carousal. SYN.: see: κραιπάλη
(πορεύω), [in LXX chiefly for הֲלִיכָה and cogn. forms;] 1. a journey. 2. a going: metaphorically ("the rich man perishes while he is still on the move," Hort., in l).

adv. (ἔνθεν), [in LXX chiefly for זֶה;] 1. of place, hence: ἐ. καὶ ἐ. (for cl. ἔνθεν κ. ἔνθεν), on this side and on that, on each side, similarly, ἐ. καὶ ἐκεῖθεν. 2. Of time, thereupon. 3. Causal; hence, therefore. ἔνθεν, adv., [in LXX for זֶה, פֹּה,] hence.

1. of Place, here, there, Lat. hic, illic, (Herdotus Historicus), ἐνταῦθά που here- abouts, (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. like ἐνταυθοῖ, with sense of motion towards, hither, thither, Lat. huc, illuc, (Iliad by Homer), attic 3. with genitive, ἐντ. τῆς ἠπείρου (Thucydides); ἔντ. τῆς πολιτείας in that department of government…

[in LXX for עֵנָב;] a bunch of grapes. "σ. is properly the ripe grape-cluster as opposite to ὄμφαξ, cf., as contrasted with βότρυς, it describes the grapes rather than the cluster on which they grow" (Swete, Apoc., 187 f.).
[in LXX chiefly for הָפַךְ;] to turn about, change. Pass. and mid., to turn oneself about; metaphorically, to change one's mind.
ἀπο-τίνω (or -τίω) [in LXX chiefly for שׂוּם pi.;] to pay off, repay: Phm 19.
1. from above, above, (Euripides) 2. οἱ ἐπ. men of former time, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus)
verbal adj. of δέχομαι, [in LXX chiefly for רָצוֹן:] acceptable: (LXX) 24, " (LXX).
τό, see: ἐνέδρα. ἐν-έδρα, -ας, ἡ (ἕδρα, a seat), [in LXX: (אָרַב)*;] a lying in wait, an ambush: (Rec. ἔνεδρον, a form frequently in LXX).

[in LXX chiefly for חָתַם, also for סָתַם (Da TH);] to seal, (a) for security: τ. καρπὸν τοῦτον, figuratively, (b) for concealment, hence, metaphorically, to hide (Da TH,): (with) for distinction, metaphorically, mid., (d) for authentication.
(νεάν = νέος) [in LXX for נַעַר, בָּחוּר;] a young man.
a settlement far from home, a colony settlement, (Herdotus Historicus), εἰς ἀπ. στέλλειν to send away so as to form a settlement, (Herdotus Historicus); ἀπ. ἐκπέμπειν (Thucydides)
to raise up, exalt, [variant datesAnthology Palantina, in Mid.
[in LXX chiefly for חָרָשׁ;] an artificer in wood, stone or metal, but esp. a carpenter.
(ἀκή, a point), [in LXX chiefly for קוֹץ, also for סִיר, שַׁיִת,] a prickly plant, thorn, brier; in NT always pl..
[in LXX for pi., hi.,] to make to remain over, preserve. Mid. (a) to keep or save for oneself: τ. ψυχήν, (b) to get or gain for oneself, get possession of.
ἀπο-κλείω [in LXX chiefly for סָגַר;] to shut fast.

(κόλος), [in LXX for כָּלָא, מָנַע,] to hinder, re­strain, forbid, withhold: with accusative and inf., inf. om., accusative om., with accusative of person(s) and genitive of thing(s), with accusative of thing(s), id. before τοῦ μή, id. before ἀπό.

ἐπι-τάσσω [in LXX for אָמַר, צָוָה,] to command, charge: with accusative of thing(s), with dative of person(s), id. with accusative of thing(s), Phm 8; id. with inf., id. with imperat., with accusative and inf.. SYN.: κελεύω
[in LXX for פֶּרֶךְ,] strength, force, violence.
(μάστιξ) [in LXX chiefly for נָכָה hi.;] to scourge: with accusative, metaphorically.
[in LXX for אֱדֹם, ἐ. θάλασσα for סוּף -יָם,] red: ἡ ἐ. θάλασσα, the Red Sea.

1. Dep. 2. to lead from a point, and so, generally, to lead the way, go first, οἱ ἀφηγούμενοι the van, (Xenophon Historicus) 3. to tell or relate in full, explain, (Herdotus Historicus): perfect in passive sense, τὸ ἀπηγημένον what has been told, (Herdotus Historicus)

1. to advise, counsel, Lat. consulere alicui, with dative pers. et infinitive, to advise one to do a thing, (Herdotus Historicus), 2. without the infinitive, ς. τινί τι (Herdotus Historicus); ς. τι to recommend a measure, (Herdotus Historicus), attic:—;Pass., τὰ συμβουλευόμενα the advice given, (Xenophon Historicus) 3…

δια-μαρτύρομαι, depon., of Ionic origin, intensive of the simple μαρτύρομαι, which see, [in LXX chiefly for עוּד hi., usually with dative of person(s),] solemnly to protest: in adjuration, before ἐνώπιον τ. θεοῦ, (Cremer, 415).
(χίλιοι, ἄρχω) [in LXX chiefly for אַלּוּף שַׂר;] a chiliarch, the commander of a thousand, esp. a Roman military tribune, the commander of a cohort: more generally, of officers of similar rank.
[in LXX for נֶשֶׁר;] an eagle: (Rec. ἀγγέλου). Where carrion is referred to, ἀ. is probably a vulture.
Eliab - a name found only in LXX at with no equivalent in the Hebrew text
συν-αθροίζω [in LXX chiefly for קָבַץ;] to gather together, assemble: with accusative of person(s), pass.. ἀθροίζω, [in LXX chiefly for קָבַץ;] to Gather, assemble.
ἀπο-φέρω [in LXX for הָלַךְ,] to carry off, bear, or lead away: with accusative. Pass..

μεθ-ίστημι and (late form,) μεθιστάνω, [in LXX for סוּר hi.,] trans. in Pres., impf., fut. and aor. 1, to change, remove: with accusative of thing(s), ὄρη, with accusative of person(s): before εἰς, before ἐκ, pass., of causing death. Metaphorical, with accusative of person(s), to pervert.

(ἵστημι), [in LXX chiefly for עָמַד, its parts and derivatives, also for רִיב (Pr 1714),] 1. a standing, place, status: σ. ἔχειν. 2. insurrection, sedition. 3. In poets and late prose, strife, dissension.
τό (ποιέω), [in LXX chiefly for מַעֲשֶׂה (frequently in Ec);] that which is made or done, a work.
to prevail over, τινός: absolute to prevail, gain the mastery, (Herdotus Historicus); of a name, to prevail, become current, (Herdotus Historicus)

a gate-keeper, warder, porter; (Aeschulus Tragicus); also as feminine, ἡ π. δωμάτων γυνή (Euripides):—;metaphorically, τοῖον πυλωρὸν φύλακα τροφῆς such a watchful guardian of thy life, (Sophocles Tragicus)

τό (μυέω), [in LXX: Dan LXX TH ff. (רָז), Tob.12:7, 11, Jdth.2:2, Wis.2:22, Sir.3:18 Ma.13:21 *;] 1. that which is known to the μύστης (initiated), a mystery or secret doctrine, mostly in pl., τὰ μ.. 2. In later writers (Menand., Incert., 168), that which may not be revealed (not, however, as in the modern sense…
(ταλαίπωρος) [in LXX chiefly for שֹׁד;] 1. hard work (Hippocr.). 2. hardship, suffering, distress: (LXX) pl..
[in LXX chiefly for גֶּחֶל;] coal, charcoal. ἄ. πυρός, a burning coal.

ἔκ-στασις, -εως, ἡ (ἐξίστημι) [in LXX: (חֲרָדָה); (פַּחַד),] 1. a displacement (Arist.). 2. An abnormal condition of the mind, in which the subject passes out of his usual self-control (Hippocr.); in NT (Kennedy, Sources, 121 f.); (a) a trance: (b) amazement.
ἐπ-εῖδον 2 aor. without Pres. in use; [in LXX chiefly for רָאָה;] to regard with attention, look upon (in cl., of the gods) 1. with a view to bless: with inf.. 2. To punish: before ἐπί.
1. the twentieth day of the month (entry ἡμέρα); (Hesiod): the days from 21 to 30 were called αἱ εἰκάδες (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. the sixth day of the Eleusinian mysteries, (Euripides)
(τρέμω), [in LXX for רַעַד, רַעַד, פַּחַד,] trembling, quaking, esp. from fear: φόβος κ. τ..

άρ-οικος, -ον [in LXX chiefly for גֵּר, תּוֹשָׁב;] 1. in cl. Attic, dwelling near, neighbouring; as subst., a neighbour. 2. In late writers (LXX, Philo) and in Iuser. (Deiss., BS, 227 f.; Kennedy, Sources, 102), foreign, alien; as subst., an alien, a sojourner: (LXX), metapb., ξένοι καὶ π. (opposite to συμπολίτης), π. καὶ παρεπιδήμους.
καθ-ήκω [in LXX: impers., (32), (מִשְׁפָּט); τὰ κ., (דָבַר),] 1. to come down, come to. 2. to be fit, proper: impers., with accusative and inf., τὰ μὴ καθήκοντα.
(θηλή, a breast), [in LXX chiefly for יָנַק hi.;] 1. of the mother, to suckle. 2. Of the young, to suck: μαστούς.
[in LXX for צַיִד, טָרַף, רֶשֶׁת, and cogn. forms;] 1. a hunting, chase. 2. prey, game (c1.). 3. As in = רֶשֶׁת, a net.

(φίλος), [in LXX: (אָהַב), (נָשַׁק), La (רֵעַ) Wis.8:2,] 1. to love (with the love of emotion and friendship, Lat, amare; v, SYN.): with accusative of person(s), ἐν πίστει, with accusative of thing(s), with inf.. 2. to kiss: with accusative of person(s). SYN.: ἀγαπάω ω, the love of duty and respect
[in LXX chiefly for מָהַר pi.;] quick, swift, speedy: opposite to βραδύς, Ja 119.

[in LXX for רעה;] prop., of a herdsman, to feed: metaphorically, of Christian pastoral care. Pass., of cattle, to feed, graze. SYN.: ποιμαίνειν, to tend, shepherd, a wider term, including oversight as well as feeding.
(λέπω, to peel), 1. peeled. 2. fine, thin, small, light; hence, in late Gk., as subst. τὸ λ., a small coin (one-eighth of an as, AV, mite).

ἔκ-γονος, -ον (ἐκγίγνομαι, to be born of), [in LXX for פְּרִי (neut.), בֵּן,] 1. with genitive, born of. 2. As subst., ὁ, ἡ ἔ., a child, son or daughter; in pl., descendants: τέκνα ἢ ἔ., children or grand-children.
a cub, whelp, especially a lion's whelp, (Iliad by Homer), attic; of other animals, (Euripides); in poets also of men, Ἀχίλλειος σκ. (Euripides)
1. a young woman, girl, maiden, (Iliad by Homer) 2. as adjective youthful, (Euripides) 3. new, [variant datesAnthology Palantina

1. to strip or despoil a slain enemy of his arms, (Hesiod); with accusative of persons or things, Κύκνον σκυλεύσαντες ἀπp ὤμων τεύχεα having stript the arms of Cycnus from his shoulders, (Hesiod) 2. with accusative rei et genitive pers. to strip the arms off an enemy, (Xenophon Historicus); so, ἀπὸ τῶν νεκρῶν σκ…
one mounted, of Pentheus in the tree, (Euripides): a horseman, rider, (Xenophon Historicus)
[in LXX for עָשָׁן;] smoke: ἀτμὶς καπνοῦ, (LXX).

[in LXX chiefly for חׇפְשִׁי;] free; (a) in civil sense, not a slave: fem., (b) as regards restraint and obligation in general: before ἐκ, ἀπό, with inf., from the law, from sin, τῇ δικαιοσύνῃ, as regards righteousness, (Cremer, 249).
(ἀγρός), [in LXX for שָׂדֶה,] 1. living in fields, wild: μέλι.. 2. savage, fierce: Ju 13.

1. the point of the shoulder, where it joins the collar-bone, the acromion, (Xenophon Historicus):—; the shoulder, [variant datesAnthology Palantina 2. the front or the uppermost part of a ship, [variant datesAnthology Palantina 3. the shoulder-strap of a tunic, (Euripides)

(ἱλάσκομαι), [in LXX: 4Ma.17:22; neut., (17) ff. ff., ff. (כַּפֹּרֶת), (עֲזָרָה) *;] propitiatory (μνῆμα, FlJ, Ant., xvi, 7, 1; θάνατος, 2Mac, l.with): of Christ, as subst., το ἱ. (sc. ἐπίθεμα, where the word first occurs in LXX and where ἱ. ἐ. = כַּפֹּרֶת, elsewhere rendered simply τὸ ἱ; cf. Deiss., 124 ff.; Westc., He., in l).

[in LXX chiefly for קָנֶה, ff.,] a reed: " (LXX); hence, accusative, to its various uses, (a) a reed-pipe, flute; (b) a reed-staff, staff: (with) a measuring reed or rod (Ez, l.with): (d) a writing reed, a pen: III Jn 13.

to make a false note in music: metaphorically to go wrong, offend, err, τι in a thing, (Euripides), εἴς τινα (Aeschines Orator):—;Pass., πλημμελεῖσθαι ὑπό τινος to be ill-treated by one, (Plato Philosophus)

1. untrodden, impassable, inaccessible, of mountains, (Herdotus Historicus), of a river, not fordable, (Xenophon Historicus) 2. of holy places, not to be trodden, like ἄθικτος, (Sophocles Tragicus): metaphorically pure, chaste, ψυχή (Plato Philosophus) 3. of horses, not ridden, (Lucian) 4. active, ἄβ. πόνος a plague that hinders walking…
[in LXX chiefly for צָפָה;] 1. a watcher, watchman. 2. a mark on which to fix the eye. Metaphorical, of an aim or object.
(τιμή), [in LXX for חוֹר,] honoured, prized, precious: of persons, compar., of things, metaphorically, λίθος, " (LXX).
(ἐνέδρα), [in LXX chiefly for אָרַב;] to lie in wait for: with accusative of person(s).
Βοός and Βοές (RV, Βοάζ, Rec. Βοόζ), ὁ, indecl. (Heb. בֹּעַז), Boaz.

ὑπο-τάσσω [in LXX for דָבַר hi., דָּמַם, שׂוּם, שִׁית,] 1. as a military term, to place or rank under (Polyb.). 2. to subject, put in subjection: pass.. Mid., to subject oneself, obey: absol., with dative of person(s), (T, WH, txt., R, om.), imperat..
ἀνα-βαθμός, -οῦ, ὁ (ἀναβαίνω), [in LXX for מַעֲלָה: מַעֲלָה: ff, ᾠδὴ τῶν ἀ., tit.)*;] 1. a going up, an ascent (Pss, ll. with ?). 2. a step (LXX); p1., a flight of stairs.
(ἰάομαι), [in LXX chiefly for מַרְפֵּא;] a healing, cure: pl.. SYN.: see: θεραπεία, 2; ἴαμα, 2
[in LXX chiefly for שָׁחַת hi.,] 1 1 to destroy entirely. 2. In moral sense (as LXX), to deprave, corrupt: pass. pf. ptcp., before τ. νο ν.
δια-φυλάσσω [in LXX chiefly for שָׁמַר (as);] to guard carefully (M, Pr., 116), defend: with accusative, (LXX).
[in LXX for רפה hi.,] 1. to let, permit: with accusative, with inf., with accusative and inf. (M, Pr., 205).32. 2. to let alone, leave: ἀγκύρας.
late form of ξυρέω. ξύρω, rare form of ξυρέω, aor. mid., ξύρασθαιι for -ᾶσθαι (Rec., Edd.).

(πίμπλημι), [in LXX chiefly for שָׂבֵעַ and cognate forms;] a filling up, satiety: πρὸς π. σαρκός (RV, against the indulgence of the flesh; but ICC, in l, for the full satisfaction of the flesh, op. cit., 276 ff.).
ἀπο-λείπω [in LXX for H2308 יָתַר,] 1. to leave, leave behind: pass., to be reserved, remain. 2. to desert, abandon: Ju 6.
(later form of δν-), [in LXX for אָפֵל, עֲרָפֶל,] darkness, gloom (including "an element of tempest," Tr., Syn., §with). SYN.: ἀχλύς, ζόφος, σκότος (Tr., l.with; DB, i, 457a).
(πικρός), [in LXX chiefly for מַר and cognate forms;] bitterness; (a) of taste; (b) metaphorically, of temper, character, (LXX), ῥίζα πικρίας, χολὴ π., a malignant disposition.
τό [in LXX for צִיץ,] a flower. " (LXX).

(λείπω), [in LXX chiefly for יָתַר, also for שְׁאָר,] the remaining, the rest, 1. pl., οἱ λ.: with subst., absol., οἱ λ. οἱ (B1., § 47, 8), οἱ λ. τ. ἀνθρώπων, τὰ λ., 2. Neut. sing. (accusative ref.), adverbially, τὸ λ.; (a) for the future, henceforth: (Lft., Notes, 232 f.), anarth. (Deiss., LAE, 17616, 1885, 20), τοῦ λ., (b) besides…
τό (δέμω, to build), [in LXX for גָּג;] chiefly in poets and late (not Attic) prose; 1. a house, hall. 2. In LXX, house-top: ἐπὶ τ. δῶμα, ἐπὶ τ. δώματος, -άτων.
(ταράσσω), [in LXX for חָלָה, מְהוּמָה,] trouble, disturbance: τ. ὕδατος, [4]. In pl. (as in cl.), tumults: Rec.

νοιεω νοέω, -ῶ (νοῦς), [in LXX chiefly for בִּין, also for שָׂכַל hi., etc;] 1. to perceive with the mind, understand: absol., with accusative, with dative instr., τ. καρδίᾳ, pass., before ὅτι, with accusative and inf.. 2. to think, consider: absol., with accusative of thing(s).
(βάσανος), [in LXX: Sir.4:17, and frequently in Wi, II, 4Mac;] 1. prop., to rub on the touchstone, put to the test. 2. to examine by torture, hence, generally, to torture, torment, distress.
τό (dimin. of σχοῖνος, a rush), [in LXX chiefly for a rope.
(σύν, βουλή), [in LXX for יָעַץ and cogn. forms;] a counsellor, adviser: (LXX).
1. a thought, piece of reasoning, argument, (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. an invention, device, (Xenophon Historicus)

[in LXX: I, Tob.8:18, and frequently in 1-4Mac;] to urge on, bid by word of mouth, order, command (mostly of one in authority): with accusative and inf. aor., with ellipse of accusative, with accusative and inf. Pres., with ellipse of accusative, ptcp. aor.. SYN.: see: ἐντέλλω
Alexander 1. Son of Simon of Cyrene: 2. A kinsman of the High Priest. 3. A certain Jew. 4. A coppersmith. 5. Perh. = 4.
(ἐλέγχω) [in LXX: frequently in Pr, Jb (יָכַח) יָכַח) Wis.5:1-23, Sir.3:1-31,] a proof, test.
[in LXX chiefly for בְּהֵמָה;] four-footed: of beasts, neut. pl..

(variant form of βύβλος, the Egyptian papyrus, paper made from its fibrous coat), [in LXX for סֶפֶר, the form βύβ- being sometimes used;] a book, a roll, used much less frequently than βιβλίον, and with a "connotation of sacredness and veneration" (MM, Exp., x), β. τ. ζωῆς.
[in LXX (frequently pl. as in Hom.) chiefly for צֵלָע;] the side: ([[WH]] R, mg.).
[in LXX for נָבַט hi., רָאָה,] to take note of, perceive, consider carefully: with accusative of thing(s), with accusative of person(s).

1. to rule over, with dative, (Homer): absolute to have or hold power, (Odyssey by Homer) 2. to prevail in battle, be victorious, conquer, (Iliad by Homer) 3. with genitive to prevail over, get the mastery of an enemy, (Herdotus Historicus), attic:—;also to become master of, Lat. potiri, τῆς θαλάσσης, τῶν Ἑλλήνων (Herdotus Historicus)…

1. Dep. to be gone, to have gone, Lat. abesse (not abire), in perfect sense, and imperfect ὠιχόμην in pluperfect sense, directly opposite to ἥκω, to have come, while ἔρχομαι, to go or come, serves as the present to both, (Homer),—;often with participle, οἴχεται φεύγων is fled and gone, (Iliad by Homer)…
ἐπ-αινέω, -ῶ [in LXX for הָלַל pi., שָׁבַח pi.;] to praise: with accusative, before ὅτι, absol., before ὅτι.
τό (ὑποδέω), [in LXX for נָעַל;] a sole bound under the foot, a sandal: τ. ποδῶν, (LXX). SYN.: σανδάλιον, q.v
(μέσος, ἡμέρα), [in LXX chiefly for צֹהַר, al; also for נֶגֶב, Dan LXX,] 1. noon. 2. the South.

1. any one connected by marriage, Lat. affinis, (Aeschulus Tragicus): 2. a son-in-law, Lat. gener, (Homer) 3. a brother-in-law, a sister's husband, (Iliad by Homer); or, a wife's brother (Sophocles Tragicus) 4. = πενθερός, a father-in-law, (Euripides) 5. doric and aeolic a bridegroom, wooer, suitor, (Pindar)
(poët., διπλός, whence corp. -ότερον), -όη, -όον (-οῦ, -ῆ, -οῦν) [in LXX for כָּפַל, מִשְׁנֶה, and cognates;] twofold, double: διπλότιρον, in twofold measure.
a drawing, dragging, tugging: a drawing on or towards a thing, attraction, force of attraction, (Plato Philosophus)
(ὅρκος), [in LXX: (שָׁבַע hi.);] 1. to make one swear (Xen., Polyb., a1.). 2. to adjure: with dupl. accusative.
(τελέω), [in LXX chiefly for מוּת, מָוֶת;] 1. a finishing. 2. an end: τ. βίου: also without βίου, the end of life, death.
[in LXX chiefly for גְּדִי;] a kid: WH, txt.
[in LXX chiefly for בּחר;] = αἱρέομαι, to choose: (LXX, ἀντιλήμψομαι).
ῶ [in LXX chiefly for רָעַע hi.;] to do harm, to do evil: (Cremer, 329).

adv. (κατά), [in LXX for מַטָּה, תַּחַת and cogn. forms;] 1. down, downwards (with verbs of motion). 2. below, beneath: " (LXX); ἕως κ.. τὰ κ. (opposite to τ. ἄνω). Compar. κατωτέρω: ἀπὸ διετοῦς καὶ κ..
ἐκ-τρέφω [in LXX for גָּדַל,] 1. prop., of children, to nurture, bring up. 2. to nourish.

1. a wagon, wain, opposite to the war-chariot ( ἅρμα), Lat. plaustrum, (Homer) 2. with genitive a wagon-load of, πετρῶν, σίτου (Xenophon Historicus) 3. the carriage of the plough, Lat. currus, (Hesiod):—; Charles' wain in the heavens, the Great Bear ( ἄρκτος), (Homer) 4. = ἁμαξιτός, [variant datesAnthology Palantina

1. on foot, πεζοί fighters on foot, opposite to horsemen, (Homer):—;also on land, going by land, opposite to sea-faring, (Homer):—;so, ὁ πεζὸς στρατός, or ὁ πεζός alone, sometimes foot-soldiery, infantry, opposite to cavalry ἡ ἵππος); (Herdotus Historicus) 2. ὁ πεζός, also, a land-force or army, opposite to a naval force…
τό (κύω, to be pregnant, to swell) [in LXX chiefly for גַּל;] a wave: pl., κ. θαλάσσης, figuratively, Ju 13. SYN.: κλύδων, q.v
καθ-ίημι [in LXX: (נוּחַ hi.), and seel., *;] to send or let down: before εἰς, διά, with genitive, ib., ptcp., before ἐπί, with genitive, ἐκ.
(cl. = ἱεράομαι) [in LXX chiefly for כָּהַן pi.;] to be a priest, officiate as a priest.
τό [in LXX chiefly for נֵתַח;] a member, limb of the body: (WH, mg.), pl. (as always in cl.), τὰ μ.: ff. Metaphorical, πόρνης, of Christians, μ. ἀλλήλων, Χριστοῦ, σώματος Χριστοῦ.
1. to spend entirely, (Demosthenes Orator):—; to exhaust, (Plutarch) 2. to destroy utterly, (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;Pass., (Demosthenes Orator)

1. to pour different ways, to disperse, (Herdotus Historicus):—; to cut up a victim, (Homer) 2. to dissolve, break up, destroy, (Xenophon Historicus) 3. metaphorically to confound, τὰ βεβουλευμένα (Herdotus Historicus) 4. Pass. to be poured from one vessel into another, (Herdotus Historicus) 5. to run through, spread about…
of cedar, (Iliad by Homer) from κέδρος
(θέρος), [in LXX chiefly for קָצַר;] to reap: figuratively, with accusative, τ. σαρκικά, φθοράν, ζωὴν αἰώνιον, τ. γῆν.

τό (ἀνατίθημι), Hellenistic for Attic ἀνάθημα; 1. prop. = τὸ ἀνατιθέμένον, that which is laid by to be kept, a votive offering. 2. [As equiv. in LXX for חֵרֶם,] devoted, a thing devoted to God, hence; (a) of the sentence pronounced, a curse: (b) of the object on which the curse is laid, accursed.

1. in these tenses Causal, to place or set under, τί τινι (Herdotus Historicus); τρεῖς σταυροὺς ὑπίστησι plants three piles in the lake to support a house, (Herdotus Historicus):—;metaphorically, γνώμας ὑποστήσας σοφάς having laid them as a foundation, (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. to post secretly or in ambush, (Herdotus Historicus) 3…

δι-έ-οδος, -ου, ἡ [in LXX chiefly for תּוֹצָאָה, as ff, and frequently in Jos;] in π. of the conclusion of a trial (MM, Exp., xi); a way out through, an outlet; pl., δ. τῶν ὁδῶν, RV, the partings of the highways.
[in LXX for נָתַץ, הָרַס,] to dig down: (LXX).
(ταχύς) adv., [in LXX chiefly for מְהֵרָה and cognate forms;] quickly, hastily: with suggestion of rashness.
(θρῆνος), [in LXX chiefly for יָלַל hi., also for קַיִן pit.,] 1. intrans., to lament, wail. 2. Trans., to bewail: with accusative of person(s). SYN.: κλαίω, κόπτομαι, λυπέομαι, πενθέω.
[in LXX chiefly for יָשָׁר;] straight; (a) in height, straight, upright: (b) in line, straight, direct: figuratively, (LXX).
[in LXX for לוּץ, עָרִיץ, בְּלִיַּעַל,] pestilence: pl., metaphorically, of persons, a pest.

(πῦρ) [in LXX chiefly for צָרַף;] to set on fire, burn up. In NT always pass., 1. to be set on fire, to burn: ptcp., glowing. Metaphorical, of grief or indignation, of lust. 2. Of metals, to be refined or purified by fire.
ή (πνέω), [in LXX chiefly for נְשָׁמָה;] 1. a blowing, blast, wind. 2. a breathing, breath.
(στενάζω), [in LXX for אֲנָחָה, אֲנָקָה, נְאָקָה,] a groaning: (LXX κραυγή).
[in LXX chiefly for עָדַן;] softness, daintiness, luxuriousness.
-ή, -όν (ὄρος), mountainous, hilly; ἡ ὀ. (sc. χώρα), the hill-country (LXX for הַר)

ἀπο-λύω [in LXX for שׁוּב, frequently in 1-4 Mac;] 1. to set free, release: a debtor, metaphorically, of forgive­ness. 2. to let go, dismiss (Field, Notes, 9 f.): of divorce, τ. γυναῖκα: with ref. to Gk. and Rom. (net Jewish) custom, τ. ἄνδρα. Mid., to depart
ἔμ-πορος, -ου, ὁ (πόρος, a journey), [in LXX chiefly for סָחַר, רָכַל;] 1. a passenger on shipboard, one on a journey. 2. a merchant.
[in LXX for נָקֹד, רִקְמָה,] many-coloured, variegated. Metaphorical, various, manifold.
ἐπι-φαίνω [in LXX for עוּר hi.,] 1. to show forth. 2. (= pass. in cl.) to appear: with dative of person(s), metaphorically, with dative, (Cremer, 567).
(πύλη), [in LXX chiefly for פֶּתַח, שַׁעַר;] 1. the porch or vestibule of a house or palace: 2. The gate-way or gate-tower of a walled town.
[in LXX chiefly for שֶׁלֶג also (in Da) for תְּלַג;] snow.
[in LXX for עִוֵּר;] blind: as subst., ὁ τ., " (LXX), Metaphorical.
[in LXX chiefly for נָכָה hi., ho.;] to strike, smite: pass..
[in LXX for בָּרָק;] lightning: pl., of a lamp, shining brightness.
(ὑάκινθος), [in LXX for תַּחַשׁ, תְּכֵלֶת;] of hyacinth, hyacinthine, "doubtless meant to describe the blue smoke of a sulphurous flame" (Swete).
[in LXX: (חוֹתָם) (חָח), Sir.17:22,] 1. a seal, signet. 2. The impression of a seal or signet, a seal: on a book or roll, metaphorically.
(ἐρημόω), [in LXX for שָׁמֵם, שָׁמֵם, חׇרְבָּה,] a making desolate, laying waste: βδέλυγμα ἐρημώσεως (Da, ll. with, 1Ma.1:54), " (LXX).

ἐπι-τελέω, -ῶ [in LXX for כָּלָה, עָשָׂה,] to complete, accomplish, execute: with accusative of thing(s), of religious services, art. inf.. Mid., (a) to complete for oneself, make an end: (b) to pay in full, pay the tax, be subject to: with accusative.

ἐξ-ωθέω, -ῶ [in LXX chiefly for נָדָה hi.;] 1. to thrust out. 2. to drive out of the sea, drive on shore: (WH, txt., ἐκσῶσαι). *ἐκ-σώζω, to preserve from danger, bring safe. ἐξ-ωθέω, -ῶ [in LXX chiefly for נָדָה hi.;] 1. to thrust out. 2. to drive out of the sea, drive on shore: (WH, txt., ἐκσῶσαι). *ἐκ-σώζω, to preserve from danger…
(Heb. הַגָּלִיל, the circle, district), Galilee, the name of the northern region of Palestine in NT times: Γ. τῶν ἐθνῶν, (LXX); θάλασσα τῆς Γ..

(ἀρχή), [in LXX chiefly for קֶדֶם;] original, ancient. SYN.: παλαιός, old, without the reference to beginning and origin contained in ἀ. The distinction is observed in π.. ἀ. is the antithesis to καινός: παλ. to vέος

adv. of place, correlat. of ποῦ, where. I. Prop., of place, 1. where; (a) in relative sentences, with indic: after nouns of place, for relat. prepositional phrase, before ἐκεῖ., id. pleonast. (= Heb. שָׁם... אֲשֶׁר; Aram. תַּמָּן.. דּ; of.), ὅ.... ἐκεῖ, ὅ.... ἐπ᾽ αὐτῶν, ὅ. ἄν, wherever (M, Pr., 168), with imperfect indic., with Pres…
[in LXX for נָגַע hi., מְטָא,] 1. to come before another, anticipate (cl.): with accusative of person(s). 2. In late writers and MGr., to come, arrive: before εἰς, ἄχρι, ἐπί.

1. an organ, instrument, tool, for making or doing a thing, (Sophocles Tragicus),—;of a person, ἁπάντων ἀεὶ κακῶν ὄργ. (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. an organ of sense, (Plato Philosophus) 3. a musical instrument, (Plato Philosophus) 4. a surgical instrument, (Xenophon Historicus) 5. a work, product…
τό [in LXX chiefly for נֹגַהּ;] light, brightness, usually with genitive of something that shines or reflects: of the moon, of a lamp, (WH, RV, φῶς). SYN.: αὐγή, q.v

1. the twentieth, (Odyssey by Homer); epic also ἐεικοστός, (Iliad by Homer) 2. εἰκοστή, ἡ, a tax of a twentieth, Lat. vicesima, levied by the Athenians on imports and exports from the allies in lieu of tribute, (Thucydides)

τό (γάζα, φυλακή), [in LXX chiefly for לִשְׁכָּה, נִשְׁכָּה, once for גְּנָזִים; το͂ γ., τᾶ γ., of a temple treasury, Ma.3:6,] treasury: also, apparently, the trumpet-shaped chests into which the peoples' temple-offerings were thrown (DB, iv, 96; DCG, ii, 748).

[in LXX: (רָצוֹן), frequently in Sir; in Inscr. (I.G., 5960), LXX, and NT = εὐδόκησις (Died.);] good pleasure, good-will, satisfaction, approval: with genitive obj., ἐν ἀνθρώποις εὐδοκία, Rec., R, mg., WH, mg., -ας, Lk, l.with, R, txt., WH, txt..

1. to set upright, erect, (Euripides):—;metaphorically to keep straight, set right, (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. to accomplish successfully, bring to a successful issue, (Plato Philosophus): —;Pass. to succeed, prosper, (Herdotus Historicus); δρᾶν κατώρθωσαι thou hast rightly purposed to do, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 3. intransitive as in Pass…

ὑπο-μονή, -ῆς, ἡ (ὑπομένω) [in LXX for מִקְוֶה and cogn. forms; frequently in 4Mac;] 1. a remaining behind (Arist.). 2. patient enduring, endurance: δι᾽ ὑπομονῆς, with genitive of person(s), (ICC, in l), with genitive of thing(s), before ἐν. SYN.: see: μακροθυμία, and cf. Hort on

δια-λογισμός, -οῦ, ὁ (διαλογίζομαι) [in LXX chiefly for מַחֲשָׁבָה;] a thought, reasoning, inward questioning: " (LXX), κριταὶ δ. πονηρῶν, genitive of qual., χωρὶς ὀργῆς καὶ δ. (where perh. δ., like מְזִמָּה, in Ps 138(139):20, implies evil intention).
(δόλος), [in LXX—chiefly in Pss, Pr, Sir—for;] deceitful.
τό [in LXX for עָב, שַׁחַק, עָנַן;] a mass of clouds, a cloud; metaphorically as in Hom., Hdt.,), of a dense throng.

(-ττων, Heb_7:7, WH, 1Ti_5:9), -ον (formed, with superl. ἐλάχιστος, from the epic ἐλαχύς, little, and serving as compar. of μικρός), [in LXX for מָעַט,] less, in age, rank or quality: " (LXX), neut., -ον, adverbially.
(ἔσω), adv., [in LXX for בַּיִת, פָּנִים and cognate forms;] 1. from within. 2. within: τὸ ἔ., id. with genitive.
[in LXX chiefly for סָגַר;] to shut: θύραν, τ. ἄβυσσον, pass., θύρα, (pl.), δεσμωτήριον, πυλῶνες. Metaphorical, τ. οὐρανόν, τ. σπλάγχνα, τ. βασιλείαν, id. absol., τ. θύραν.
(κόπος), [in LXX: (שָׁכַךְ), (חָדַל), חָדַל), (שָׁתַק),] to grow weary; of the wind (Hdt., Jh., l.with), to abate, cease raging.

1. to recover what is lost, rescue, (Sophocles Tragicus): Mid., ἀνασώζεσθαί τινα φόβου to recover one from fear, (Sophocles Tragicus):—;Mid. in proper sense, ἀν. τὴν ἀρχήν to recover the government for oneself, (Herdotus Historicus):—;Pass. to return safe, of exiles, (Xenophon Historicus) 2. in Mid. also to preserve in mind, remember…
[in LXX chiefly for יָרֵא, with neg.;] to be of good courage: imperat., θάραει, -εῖτε.
[in LXX chiefly for כָּסָה pi.;] to cover up; mid., to cover or veil oneself: τ. κεφαλήν.

[in LXX for נָשָׂא,] 1. to take care of. 2. to carry off safe. 3. to carry off as booty. 4. to bear or carry. Mid., to bear for oneself, hence, (a) to receive: (b) to receive back, recover (in cl. so also act.): metaphorically, of requital, παρὰ Κυρίου.

and (elsewhere, as usually in Attic) -οῦτον, correlat. of ὅσος, of quantity, size, number, so great, so much, pl., so many: of time, so long, χρόνος, pl., (ἔτη), before ὥστε, absol.: pl., of price, τοσούτου, dative, τοσούτῳ κρείττων, τ. μᾶλλον ὅσῳ, καθ᾽ ὅσον... κατὰ τ..

[in LXX for יֶתֶר and cogn. forms;] 1. more than sufficient, over and above, abundant: with genitive (a popular substitute for πλειών, Bl., § 11, 3.4), id. with ellips. genitive, εκ περισσοῦ, Rec., T.. Compar. neut., -ότερον: with genitive, adverbially, more abund­antly, with genitive, π. πάντων, pleonast., μᾶλλον π.. 2…

στρέφω [in LXX chiefly for הָפַךְ;] to turn about, turn, change: pass., (LXX), in evil sense, to pervert, corrupt. μετα-τρέπω [in LXX: 4Ma.6:5 4Mac 4Mac 4Mac 4Mac *;] to turn about, turn: with accusative.

(πλέον), [in LXX for עֲדַף, רָבָה,] I. Intrans. 1. Of persons; (a) to abound in (Arist.); (b) to superabound: (LXX). 2. Of things, to abound, superabound. II. Trans., to make to abound. SYN.: περισσεύω, q.v
1. a refuge, place of refuge, (Herdotus Historicus): with genitive, κ. κακῶν refuge from evils, (Euripides) 2. a way of escape, excuse, (Demosthenes Orator)
(λίθος, βάλλω), [in LXX for סָקַל, רָגַם,] to pelt with stones, to kill by stoning, to stone: with accusative of person(s), pass., (LXX).
(αἰχμή, a spear, ἁλίσκομαι, to be taken), [in LXX chiefly for שָׁבָה, גּוֹלָה;] captive: (LXX).
(αἰσθάνομαι), [in LXX chiefly for דַּעַת;] perception. SYN.: ἐπίγνωσις, which see.

τό (γράφω), [in LXX for סֵפֶר,] 1. that which is traced or drawn, a picture. 2. that which is written; (1) a character, letter: (2) a writing, a written document; (a) a bill or account: (b) a letter: (with) τὰ ἱερὰ γ., the sacred writings, i.e. the OT: (so in Philo, Vit. Mos., iii, 39); (d) τὸ γ., the letter…
adv. (ἄδικος), [in LXX for שׁקר, עול,] unjustly, undeservedly.
(παλαιός), [in LXX chiefly for בָּלָה, pi., in pass. for בִּי qal.;] to make or declare old: pass., to become old: of things worn out by time and use, " (LXX); τὸ παλαιούμενον. SYN.: γηράσκω
(πατήρ), [in LXX chiefly for מוֹלֶדֶת;] prop. poët. fern. of πάτριος, of one's fathers; as subst., ἡ π. = πάτρα, fatherland, country, home, native place: WH, mg., of one's own town.
ἐπί-λοιπος, -ον (λοιπός), [in LXX for יָתַר, שָׁאַר;] still left, remaining: χρόνος.
[in LXX: (בָּרָא),] to prepare, make ready: τ. ὁδόν, οἶκον, σκηνήν, κιβωτόν, pass. pf. ptcp., λαον κ..
τό (καυχάομαι), [in LXX chiefly for תְּהִלָּה, תִּפְאָרָה;] 1. a boast (Pind.). 2. ground or matter of glorying.
conjunct. for δι᾽ ὅ, wherefore, on which account: δ. καί.

1. to hem in a city, blockade, beleaguer, besiege, (Herdotus Historicus), attic:—;Pass. to be besieged, in a state of siege, (Herdotus Historicus); of Scamander, to be dammed back, (Plato Philosophus) 2. metaphorically to be besieged, pestered, (Xenophon Historicus)

τό (neut. of ὑπερῷος, above, ὑπέρ) [in LXX for עֲלִיָּה and cogn. forms;] 1. in cl., the upper story or upper rooms where the women resided (Hom., a1.). 2. In LXX and NT, an upper chamber, roof-chamber, built on the flat roof of the house.
[in LXX chiefly for רֵעַ and cognate forms, also Sir.11:6 ff.,] a companion, comrade: (WH, ἑτέροις); voc., as term of address, my friend.

to furnish the oar with its thong: Mid., τροποῦτο κώπην ἀμφὶ σκαλμόν fastened his oar by its thong round the thole, (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;Pass., of the oar, to be furnished with its thong, (Aristophanes Comicus)
(Heb. אֲבִיָּה, אֲבִיָּהוּ), ὁ, indecl. (in FlJ, Ἀβίας, -α), Abia, Abijah. 1. Son of Rehoboam. 2. A priest of the line of Eleazar.

[in LXX for תְּהִלָּה, נְגִינָה, שִׁיר,] a hymn; (a) in cl. a festal song in praise of gods or heroes; (b) in LXX and NT a song of praise addressed to God. SYN.: ψαλμός, that which is sung to a musical accompaniment; ᾠδή, the generic term for song
[in LXX: (אֶחָד) (חֶבֶר), Wis.7:3,] 1. common (general; = Lat. communis): κ. πίστις, σωτηρία, Ju 3 2. common (ordinary; = vulgaris); hence in LXX and NT, unhallowed, unclean.
(ὄφελος), [in LXX chiefly for יָעַל hi.;] to help, benefit, do good, profit: absol., οὐδέν, with accusative of person(s), with dupl. accusative, pass., with accusative.
[in LXX for אָנַח ni., אָנַק,] to groan ("the word denotes feeling which is internal and unexpressed," Mayor, Ja., 162): (EV, murmur); ἐν ἑαυτοῖς, (cf. ἀνα-, συ(ν)-στενάζω). SYN.: see: κλαίω
(genitive -έως, vernac., Lk, l.with; Bl., §8, 5), -εῖα, -ύ, [in LXX chiefly for עמק;] deep; metaphorically, ὄρθρου βαθέως, early dawn, ὕπνος, τὰ β. τοῦ Σατανᾶ.
δια-χωρίζω [in LXX: ff (בָּדַל hi.), ff. (פָּרַד ni.),] to separate entirely. Mid., to separate oneself, depart: before ἀπό.
adv (ἄνω), (a) from above: ἀπὸ ἄ., ἐκ τῶν ἄ., meaning, from heaven. (b) from the first, from the beginning: whence (with) anew, again: πάλιν ἄ..
(κατακλύζω), [in LXX chiefly for מַבּוּל, also for שֶׁטֶף,] a flood, deluge.
(πλατύς), [in LXX chiefly for רָחַב hi.;] to make broad, enlarge, extend: with accusative of thing(s). Metaphorical, pass., ἡ καρδία, ὑμεῖς.
-ης, ἡ (Heb. עַזָּה), Gaza, in OT, one of the five chief cities of the Philistines.

1. a half-ass, i. e. a mule, (Homer),—; proverbial, ἐπεὰν ἡμίονοι τέκωσι, i. e. never, (Herdotus Historicus) 2. the ἡμ. ἀγροτέρα of (Iliad by Homer) 2. 851 is probably the wild ass. 3. as adjective, βρέφος ἡμίονον a mule- foal, (Iliad by Homer); ἡμ. βασιλεύς a mule- king, half-Mede half-Persian, (Oracle quoted in Herdotus Historicus)
δια-τηρέω, -ῶ [in LXX for שָׁמַר, נָצַר, before ἀπό (for מִן), as in (8);] to keep carefully: before ἐκ.

late form of νίζω, [in LXX chiefly for רָחַץ;] to wash, usually of a part of the body: with accusative of person(s), τ. πόδας, mid., reflexive, to wash oneself: τ. χεῖρας, τ. πόδας, τ. πρόσωπον. νίζω, see: νίπτω SYN.: λούω, πλύνω
(ἀγαπάω), [in LXX chiefly for יָתִיד, יָדִיד;] beloved; (a) by God: of Christ, of men, (b) by Christians, of one another: frequently as form of address, ib.; opposite to ἐχθρός.
(ἀγνοέω), [in LXX chiefly for אָשָׁם, שְׁגָגָה;] ignorance.
[in LXX chiefly for קָרָא;] to call to. Mid., to call to oneself: with accusative of person(s), Metaphorical, of the Divine call: with inf., before εἰς.

Ion, and trag. form of δύω, [in LXX chiefly for בּוֹא;] to enter, sink into; of the sun (sc. όντον), set. δύω, see: δύνω δύνω Ion, and trag. form of δύω, [in LXX chiefly for בּוֹא;] to enter, sink into; of the sun (sc. όντον), set. δύω, see: δύνω

(ὑγιής), [in LXX chiefly for שָׁלוֹם, and frequently in To;] to be sound, healthy, in good health. In Past. Epp. (as also in cl.) metaphorically, ὑ. ἐν τ. πίστει, τ. πίστει, τ. ἀγάπῃ, τ. ὑπομονῇ, ἡ ὑγιαίνουσα διδασκαλία, λόγοι ὑγιαίνοντες.
(genitive -ονος), comp. of ἀγαθός, [in LXX chiefly for טוֹב;] neut. as adv., better, very well: (also D). On elative use in these passages, see M, Pr., 78, 236.
(μακάριος), [in LXX for אָשַׁר pi., pu.;] to bless, pronounce blessed or happy: with accusative of person(s).
τό (ἄγγος), [in LXX chiefly for כְּלִי;] a vessel.
1. a reaping, harvesting, (Iliad by Homer) (metaphorically of slaughter). 2. harvest, harvest time, (Hesiod) 3. the crop or harvest reaped, Lat. seges, [variant datesAnthology Palantina

1. of or belonging to one's father, Lat. patrius, (Pindar), 2. = πατρικός, derived from one's fathers, hereditary, οἱπ. θεοί (Herdotus Historicus), —; τὰ πάτρια, Lat. instituta majorum, κατὰ τὰ πάτρια (Aristophanes Comicus), rarely in singular, τὸ πάτριον παρείς neglecting the rule of our fathers, (Thucydides) Cf. πατρῷος.

δια-κρίνω [in LXX for שׁפט, דִּין,] 1. to separate, hence, to distinguish, discriminate, discern: μηδὲν δ., οὐδὲν δ. μεταξύ, σε, τὸ σῶμα. 2. to settle, decide, judge, arbitrate: (ICC, in l.), ib. 31. Mid, and pass.; 1. to get a decision, contend, dispute: before πρός, with dative, Ju 9; absol., Ju 22 (R,mg.). 2…
(σῆμα, a sign), [in LXX for רוּעַ hi., תָּקַע,] to give a sign, signify, indicate: with accusative of thing(s), with accusative and inf., before quæst. indir..
(rarely ἡ), [in LXX for לְבוֹנָה, Sir.24:15,] 1. in cl., the frankincense-tree. 2. (Occas. in cl.) frankincense.

1. to be placed or laid by or upon, to lie by or upon, οὔατα προσέκειτο handles were upon it, (Iliad by Homer); τῇ θύρᾳ προσκεῖσθαι to keep close to the door, (Aristophanes Comicus); δοκοὶ τῷ τείχει προσκείμεναι lying near the wall, (Thucydides):—; ὁ προσκείμενος ἵππος the inside horse (turning a corner), (Sophocles Tragicus) 2…

[in LXX, of physical blemishes: ff., (מאוּם); of mental defect, Sir.20:24,] 1. in cl. poets and late prose, blame, disgrace. 2. In LXX, perb. because of resemblance to a physical blemish; metaphorically, of licentious persons.

(ὄνομα), [in LXX for זָכַר, נָקַב, קָרָא;] 1. to name, mention, or address by name: pass., of the use of the Divine name in praise and worship. 2. to name, call, give a name to: (T, R, txt. om.), pass., before ἐξ (cl.).
[in LXX for אָרֹךְ, רָחוֹק and cognate forms,] of space and time, long: μακρὰ προσεύχεσθαι. of distance, far, far distant: χώρα.
(ἐνδέω, to lack) [in LXX for חָסֵר, אֶבְיוֹן,] in want, needy
[in LXX: (עִקֵּשׁ), (σ. ὁδοῖς πορεύεσθαι, for: דֶּרֶךְ עָקַשׁ), (עָקֹב),] curved, bent, winding (opposite to ὀρθός, εὐθύς): (LXX). Metaphorical, crooked, perverse, unjust.

[in LXX: (יָעַד hoph,),] used as passive of τίθημι, to be laid, to lie; (a) of persons: an infant, a dead body, (b) of things, to lie, be laid or set, stand: trop., Θεμέλιος, before prep. with accusative, πρός, εἰς, ἐπί, trop., κάλυμμα. Metaphorical, ὁ κόσμος ἐν τ. πονηριῷ κ., to be laid down, appointed: of law, with dative of person(s)…
(εὐθύς), [in LXX chiefly for יֹשֶׁר, מִישׁוֹר and cognate forms;] uprightness: (LXX).
(περιέχω), [in LXX for מָצוּד, מָצוֹר,] 1. compass, circumference. 2. a portion circumscribed, a section.
(ὄλλυμι, to destroy), [in LXX for שֹׁד. שָׁדַד,] ruin, destruction, death: αἰώνιος, εἰς ὄ. τῆς σαρκός, for physical discipline, to destroy carnal lusts.

(νίκη), [in LXX: (זָכָה), frequently (חָמַד); in 4Mac;] to conquer, prevail: absol., of Christ, C. inf., of Christians, before ἐκ (RV, come victorious from), as law-term (cl.), (LXX); with accusative of person(s), ([WH], R, mg., om.); of Christ, (τ. κόσμον), of Christians, τ. πονηρόν, αὐτόν (ref. to ὁ κατήγωρ,)…
(-ους), τό, [in LXX for מְצוּלָה,תַּחְתִּי,] depth: τὸ β., the deep sea: metaphorically, β. πλούτου... Θεοῦ, τὰ β. τ. Θεοῦ (the Divine counsels), ἡ κατὰ βάθους πτωχεία, deep poverty.
(Rec. ἀλληλούϊα; Heb. הָלַל יָהּ, praise the Lord), [in LXX in the titles of certain Psa (104 (105),), and at the end of; also Tob.13:18, 3Ma.7:13;] hallelujah, alleluia.

1. of or for a man, (Aeschulus Tragicus), for αὐλοὶ ἀνδρεῖοι, see. αὐλός. 2. manly, masculine, (Herdotus Historicus), attic; in bad sense, stubborn, (Lucian):—;neuter τὸ ἀνδρεῖον, by crasis τἀνδρεῖον, = ἀνδρεία, (Euripides) 3. of things, strong, vigorous, (Aristophanes Comicus)
ἀ-δύνατος, -ον, [in LXX for אֶבְיוֹן, דַּל,] 1. of persons, unable, powerless: figuratively. 2. Of things, impossible.

(ἧλιξ, of the same age, mature), [in LXX: (קוֹמָה), Wis.4:9, Sir.26:17, frequently in 2-4 Mac;] always of age or maturity; "a stage of growth whether measured by age or stature"; 1. (a) age: (R, mg.), (b) full age, maturity. 2. stature.
(σφάζω), [in LXX for טָבַח, הֲרֵגָה,] slaughter: (LXX); πρόβατα σφαγῆς, (LXX); ἡμέρα σφαγῆς.
δια-φθορὰ, -ᾶς, ἡ (διαφθείρω), [in LXX chiefly for שָׁחַת, and cogn. forms;] 1. destruction. 2. corruption (physical or moral): of the grave, (LXX).

later form of γνωστός (γιγνώσκω), [in LXX for various parts of ידע;] known: with dative, (Rec.), γ. σημεῖον, a notable (EV) sign, one that is matter of knowledge, γνωστὸν, τὸ γνωστὸν θεοῦ, in pl., as subst., γνωστοί, acquaintances, so in sing., (WH).
(Heb. צִידוֹן), Sidon, a maritime city of Phœnicia.
[in LXX: chiefly (ἡ π.) for כִּכָּר;] round about, neighbouring. In LXX and NT, as subst., ἡ π. (sc. γῆ), the region round about: ἡ π. τοῦ Ἰορδάνου, by meton. for the people of the same region.
[in LXX for נָכָה hi., כָּתַת pi.,] to cut up, cut in pieces: ἑαυτὸν λίθοις.
Dep. to be evil, act wickedly, play the rogue, (Aristotle Philosopher); οἱ πεπονηρευμένοι (Demosthenes Orator)
ἐπ-αύριον, adv. [in LXX for מָחָר, elsewhere, for מׇחֳרָת;] on the morrow: in NT, ἡ ἐ. (sc. ἡμέρα), al

[in LXX chiefly for שָׁלַח;] to send; (a) of persons: with accusative, absol., ptcp. before verb., ptcp. before διά, of teachers sent by God, with accusative and dative, before πρός, with accusative, before λέγων, before εἰς, with accusative loc., before εἰς (of purpose), with inf., (b) of things: before εἰς, id., of purpose…
[in LXX: (שִׁיר), Dan LXX TH ff. (זְמָר), Sir.22:6,] skilled in the arts, esp. in music; as subst., ὁ μ., a minstrel, musician.
(χρόνος), [in LXX chiefly for אָחַר pi.;] to spend or take time, to tarry, linger, delay: before ἐν, with dative loc., with inf..
ὑπο-ζύγιος, -α, -ον [in LXX for חֲמוֹר;] under the yoke; as subst., τ., a beast of burden; colloq., an ass, and so always in LXX and NT: (LXX).
1. behind, after, in the rear, (Homer); with genitive, (Odyssey by Homer) 2. of Time, hereafter, afterwards, henceforth, (Odyssey by Homer)
ἐμ-παίζω [in LXX for עָלַל hithp., שָׂחַק,] = Attic προσ-, καταπαίζω, to mock at, mock (Hdt.): with dative, pass., absol..

(ἀγορά), [in LXX chiefly for שׁבר, קנה;] 1. to frequent the ἀγορά. 2. to buy in the market, purchase: absol., with accusative of thing(s), before παρά, with genitive of person(s), (LXX, Polyb.); ἐκ, with genitive pret., metaphorically.
1. heard, audible, (Homeric Hymns), 2. that should be heard, (Sophocles Tragicus)
(δίδωμι) [in LXX for חֹק, frequently in Sir.;] 1. properly, the act of giving. 2. Objectively, a gift. SYN.: see: δόμα
[in LXX for דָּם, פֶּה,] murder, slaughter: φ. μαχαίρης, pl..

1. outside, opposite to ἐντός: 2. as preposition with genitive outside, out of, far from, with genitive, (Homer): outside of, free from, (Herdotus Historicus), attic; ἐκτὸς ἐλπίδος beyond hope, Lat. praeter spem, (Sophocles Tragicus) 3. of Time, beyond, (Herdotus Historicus) 4. except, ἐκτὸς ὀλίγων (Xenophon Historicus) 5. absolute…
ἐκ-τινάσσω [in LXX for נָעַר ni., pi.,] to shake off: κονιορτόν, χοῦν. Mid.: κονιορτόν, ἱμάτια.
ἐπι-λέγω [in LXX chiefly for בָּחַר;] 1. to say in addition (Hdt.). 2. to call by name, to call. 3. to choose; mid., to choose for oneself.
-ου (ἑκατόν, ἄρχω,), [in LXX for מֵאָה שַׂר;] a centurion.
τό [in LXX chiefly for שׁוּשַׁן;] a lily.
(dimin. of κεφαλή), [in LXX for מְגִלָּה, וָו,] 1. a little head. 2. an extremity, capital (of a column). 3. (As in,) a roll: κ. βιβλίου, (LXX).

1. a peg on which to hang clothes, arms, (Homer), ἀπὸ πασσαλόφι ζυγὸν ᾕρεον (Iliad by Homer); ἀπὸ πασσάλου αἴνυτο τόξον (Odyssey by Homer); ἐκ πασσαλόφι κρέμασεν φόρμιγγα (Odyssey by Homer) 2. a gag, (Aristophanes Comicus)
longsuffering, patient, [variant datesAnthology Palantina: adverb -μως, (New Testament)
(-ους), τό, [in LXX for עָפָר, קַרְקע,] bottom, pavement, ground.

(ψωμός, a morsel), [in LXX chiefly for אָכַל hi.;] to feed with morsels (as children or the sick; Hippocr.), hence, generally, in late writers, to feed, nourish: with accusative of person(s), (LXX); with accusative of thing(s), to give out for food.
[in LXX chiefly for שָׁלַף,] in cl. poët. for ἕλκω; mostly used in mid., to draw: μάχαιραν

(τέλος), [in LXX for כָּלָה, pi.,] 1. to bring to an end, complete, finish: τ. δρόμον, τ. λόγους, τ. παραβολάς, τ. πόλεις, pass., with ptcp.. 2. to execute, perform, complete, fulfil: pass.. 3. to pay (frequently in cl.).
(ἐλάιττων), [in LXX (where also -σσῶ) chiefly for חָסֵר, and very frequently in Sir;] to make less: (LXX); pass..
1. a marking out by boundaries, limitation, (Aristotle Philosopher) 2. the definition of a word, (Aristotle Philosopher)
(πεδίον, a plain), [in LXX chiefly for שְׁפֵלָה (ἡ π.);] level, plain.
δανίζω (late form of cl. -είζω, Rec., Bl., § 3; Thackeray, Gr., 85f.) [in LXX chiefly for לוה;] to lend money on interest: mid., to borrow. SYN.: κίχρημι, to lend in a friendly way.
to be a man, be valiant
to be a man, be valiant
(ἀ- neg., ὕδωρ) [in LXX for צִיָּה, יְשִׁימוֹן (γῆ ἄ),] waterless: τόποι, πηγαί, νεφέλαι, Ju 12.

1. to judge, to give judgment on a thing, decide or determine a point, (Iliad by Homer), 2. with accusative cognate, δίκας δ., to adjudge a penalty, (Herdotus Historicus); δ. φυγήν τινι to decree it as his punishment, (Aeschulus Tragicus); δ. φόνον ματρός to ordain her slaughter, (Euripides); δ. τοῦ ἐγκλήματος [i.e…

-τος, τό (πίπτω), [in LXX: (מַפֶּלֶת), (14) (פֶּרֶץ), (שֹׁד), Jdth.8:19, Wis.4:18,] 1. a fall, metaphorically, a misfortune, calamity. 2. That which has fallen; (a) of buildings, a ruin (Polyb.); (b) of living creatures, in cl. usually with genitive, νεκρῶν, but also absol., as in late writers and NT, a fallen body, a carcase, corpse: π…

[in LXX for נָחַם ni.,] to change one's mind or purpose, hence, to repent; in NT (exc.), of repentance from sin, involving amendment: before ἀπό, ἔκ, (מִן שׁוּב); ἐπί, absol., with inf., ἐν σάκκῳ κ. σποδῷ. SYN.: μεταμέλομαι, q.v
τό [in LXX chiefly for רֶשֶׁת, שְׂבָכָה;] general term for a net: SYN.: ἀμφίβληστρον, σαγήνη.
indecl. (Heb. אָמוֹץ, עָמוֹס, אָמוֹן, 4 ff. B) 1. as in 2Ki, Lc. B (Α. Ἀμμών; Jos., Ἀμμών, "Αμωσσς), Amon. 2. Amos.
ἐφ-ημερία, -ας, ἡ (ἐφήμερος), [in LXX chiefly for מִשְׁמֶרֶת, מַחֲלֹקֶת;] 1. a course of daily services. 2. a class or course of priests detailed for service in the temple.

(φωνή), [in LXX for קָרָא,] I. Intrans. 1. Of persons, to call out, cry out, speak aloud: φωνῇ μεγάλῃ, ἐφώνησε (φωνῇ μεγάλῇ) λέγων, φωνήσαντες ἐπύθοντο. 2. Of the cries of animals (rarely in cl.; Je, l.with): of a cock, to crow. II. Trans. (in cl. chiefly poët.), with accusative of person(s), to call, summon, invite: to address…

[in LXX for שָׂטָן (as), exc. (צַר, צָרַר);] slanderous, accusing falsely. As subst., ὁ, ἡ, δ.; (a) generally (of. Es, ll. with), a slanderer, false accuser: (b) as chiefly in LXX, of Satan, the Accuser, the Devil: Ju 9, εἶναι ἐκ τοῦ δ., τέκνα τοῦ δ., υἱὸς, metaphorically, of Judas, (Cremer, 121; DCG, ii, 605).
[in LXX chiefly for דָּבָר, דִּבְרָה;] 1. loquacity = Very talkative. 2. talk, speech, conversation.
[in LXX chiefly for כּוֹכָב;] a star: metaphorically, ὁ ἀ. ὁ πρωϊνός; ἀ. πλαῆται, Ju 13; ἀ. ἑπτά, symbolizing the angels of the seven churches.
(ἡμεῖς), poss. prop. of first of person(s), our: Jn; τὸ ἡ., WH, txt., R, mg. (τὸ ὑμ., Rec., WH, mg., R, txt.); oἱ ἡ., our (people).
τό [in LXX chiefly for עָלֶה;] a leaf.
[in LXX: Jer, (רָפָה),] 1. to loose from the side, set free. 2. to weaken, enfeeble; pass., to be en­feebled, esp. by a paralytic stroke: " (LXX).
ἐννενήκοντα, see: ἐνεν-. ἐνενήκοντα (Rec. ἐννεν-), οἱ, αἱ, τά indecl., ninety.
1. named, to be named, and οὐκ ὀνομαστός not to be named or mentioned, i. e. abominable, Lat. infandus, (Odyssey by Homer) 2. of name or note, notable, famous, (Theognis Elegiacus)
(θυμός), [in LXX for דָּמָה pi.,] to reflect on, ponder: with accusative of thing(s).

ἐπ-έχω [in LXX for חָדַל, also Sir.8:1 Ma.5:25 2Mac,] 1. to hold upon. 2. Like παρέχω, to hold out, offer: λόγον ζωῆς. 3. to hold or direct towards, Sc.νοῦν; (a) absol., to intend, purpose; (b) to observe, give attention to: before πῶς, with dative of person(s). 4. to stay, wait: (in legal phrase, MM, Exp., l.with).
τό (καίω), [in LXX for חֹם, חֹרֶב,] heat.
and -ων, τά (Heb. עֲמֹרָה), Gomorrah, one of the cities of the plain: " (LXX), Ju 7.
1. to run off or away, (Herdotus Historicus), attic 2. to run hard, of one training for a race, (Aristophanes Comicus)
συν-πορεύομαι (Rec. σνμπ-), [in LXX chiefly for הָלַךְ;] 1. to journey together: with dative of person(s). 2. to come together.
adv. (ἀληθής). [in LXX chiefly for אָמֵן and cogn. forms;] truly, surely.
(παῖς), [in LXX: (צָחַק pi.); and more frequently for (שָׂחַק pi.;] prop., to play as a child, hence, generally, to play (as with singing and dancing): (LXX).
τό [in LXX chiefly for תֶּבֶן;] chaff.

1. to boil, seethe, (Herdotus Historicus), attic: proverbial of useless labour, λίθον ἕψεις (Aristophanes Comicus); with genitive partitive, ἥψομεν τοῦ κορκόρου we boiled some pimpernel, (Aristophanes Comicus):—;Pass. to be boiled, (Herdotus Historicus) 2. of metals, to smelt, refine, (Pindar) 3. metaphorically…
[in LXX chiefly for רִיב, also for נָצָה ni.,] 1. to fight. 2. to quarrel, dispute: πρὸς ἀλλήλους.
to make childless:—; Pass. to be deprived of children, [variant datesAnthology Palantina
ἐπι-χέω [in LXX chiefly for יָצַק.,] to pour upon.

-ές (ἀ- neg., σθένος, strength), [in LXX for עָנִי,] without strength, weak, feeble. Rhetorically, τό ἀ. τ. θεοῦ, God's action of apparent weakness: of bodily debility, sick, sickly: (Rec.), (Rec.), In moral and spiritual sense.

1. a kettledrum, such as was used especially in the worship of Cybele, (Herdotus Historicus) 2. a drum-stick: generally, a staff, cudgel, (Aristophanes Comicus) 3. in Virgil tympana are wheels of solid wood.

(λήθω = λανθάνω, hence primarily, unconcealed, manifest; hence, actual, real), [in LXX for אֶמֶת,] (a) of things, true, conforming to reality: (b) of persons, truthful. SYN.: ἀληθινός, real, genuine, ideal, as opposite to spurious or imperfect ἀληθής, true to fact, as opposite to false, lying, denotes the actuality of a thing: ἀληθινός…

1. a dog-collar, especially a large wooden collar, put on mischievous dogs, (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. a sort of pillory, (Euripides) 3. χρύσεος κλ. a collar of gold, [, variant datesAnthology Palantina
a selling, sale, ὠνῇ τε καὶ πρήσι (ionic dative) χρέονται (Herdotus Historicus); ἐπὶ πρήσι for sale, (Herdotus Historicus); πρᾶσιν ποιεῖσθαι (Aeschines Orator)
συ-στέφω [in LXX chiefly for קָשַׁר;] 1. to twist together: with accusative of thing(s). 2. Pass., of persons, to gather themselves together: (WH, R, mg.).
the liver, (Homer),—; ὑφ᾽ ἥπατος φέρειν, of pregnant women, (Euripides):—;in [variant datesTragica Adespota as the seat of the passions, anger, fear, answering therefore to our "heart."

(compar., from ἔξω; opposite to ἐσώτερος) [in LXX chiefly for חִיצוֹן;] outer: σκότος.

mostly in plural pieces of wood, rubbed one against another to produce fire, (Homeric Hymns)
1. the lobe of the ear, (Iliad by Homer) 2. the lobe of the liver, (Aeschulus Tragicus): generally, the liver, (Aeschulus Tragicus)
τό [in LXX chiefly for parts and derivatives of מָהַר;] swiftness, speed. Adverbially, ἐν τ. (ταχέως), quickly, speedily, soon.

(πάλαι), [in LXX: (14) (יָשֵׁן), יָשֵׁן), (בָּלֶה),] old, ancient; opposite to νέος, καινός: οἶνος, διαθήκη, ἐντολή, ζύμη, ὁ π. ἄςθρωπος, neut. pl., καινὰ καὶ π., of things not merely old, but worn by use (as Jo, l.with, LXX). SYN.: see: ἀρχαῖος

παρ-αγγέλλω (παρά, ἀγγὲλλω), [in LXX for שָׁמַע pi., hi.,] 1. to transmit a message (Æsch., Eur.). 2. to order, command: with inf., with accusative of thing(s), before ἵνα (M, Pr., 207; Bl., § 69, 4), with dative of person(s), R, txt., before λέγων, with inf. aor., id. with neg., μή, with inf. pres., id. with neg., ιή, with accusative…
any hole or pit dug in the ground, Lat. puteus, (Homer): a natural trough for washing clothes in, (Odyssey by Homer):—; a hole, such as a fire makes in the snow, (Xenophon Historicus)

a fighter, warrior, (Homer): doric adjective, μαχα_τάς, warlike, (Pindar)
[in LXX for לְחִי;] the jawbone, jaw, cheek.

τό (dimin. of κόρη), [in LXX chiefly for נַעֲרָה, in Joel, for יַלְדָּה;] a colloquial word which survives in MGr. (Kennedy, Sourcs, e154), girl, maiden.

(L, Ἰεζ-; Tr. -βέλ; Rec. -βήλ) ἡ, indecl. (Heb. אִיזֶבֶל; LXX as txt.; FlJ, Ἰεζαβέλη), Jezebel: symbolically.
