[in LXX chiefly for קַשׁ,] a stalk of corn, stubble.
(κόνις or κονία, dust, ὄρνυμι, to stir up), [in LXX for אָבָק,] in cl., dust stirred up; in NT, simply dust.
a hoof, the solid hoof of the horse and ass, (Iliad by Homer), attic:—;after (Homer), like χηλή, the cloven hoof of horned cattle, (Homeric Hymns)

(καλέω), [in LXX for קָרָא, מִקְרָא,] called, invited (as to a banquet, Æsch., 1Sa Ma.5:14); in NT, always of the Divine call; (a) to some office: κ. ἀπόστολος, (b) to salvation: Ju 1; κ. καὶ ἐκλεκτοὶ κ. πιστοί, in gosp. disting. fr.ἐκλεκτός, (WH, txt., R, omit), κ. Ἰησοῦ Χρ., κ. ἅγιοι, saints by calling.
1. a herd of cattle, (Herdotus Historicus) 2. a means of beguiling, [variant datesAnthology Palantina
(σιγή), [in LXX for חָרַשׁ, חָשָׁה,] 1. intrans., to be silent, keep silence. 2. Trans., to keep secret; pass., to be kept secret. SYN.: ἡσυχάζω, σιωπάω

to throw all together into confusion, to confound, disturb, trouble, Lat. conturbare, (Iliad by Homer), attic:—;Pass., αἰθὴρ πόντῳ ξυντετάρακται air is confounded with sea, (Aeschulus Tragicus): to be thrown into confusion, of soldiers, (Thucydides); of social order, (Sophocles Tragicus); metaphorically of persons, to be confounded…

1. to turn or direct towards a thing, (Homer), mostly followed by a preposition, τρ. τινὰ εἰς εὐνήν to shew him to bed, (Odyssey by Homer); τρ. πόλεις ἐς ὕβριν (Thucydides); τρ. κεφαλὴν πρὸς ἠέλιον (Odyssey by Homer) 2. Pass. to turn one's steps, turn in a certain direction, τραφθῆναι ἀν᾽ Ἑλλάδα to roam up and down Greece…
όν (δέος), [in LXX for רַךְ,] cowardly, fearful.

[in LXX chiefly for מְעַט;] short; (a) of time; short, little: βραχύ, μετὰ β., β. τι, a short time, RV, mg.; (b) of distance: (with) of quantity or value, little, few: RV, txt.; pl., διὰ βραχέων, in few words.

(δίδωμι), [in LXX chiefly (-άν) for חִנָּם, as;] a gift: δ. τ. θεοῦ, τ. Χριστοῦ, τ. πνεύματος, τ. δικαιοσύνης, τ. χάριτος, ἀνεκδιηγήτὶῳ δ.. Acc, δωρεάν, adverbially (as frequently in LXX), (a) freely, as a gift: (b) in vain, uselessly: ( LXX). SYN.: see: δόμα
(τίκτω), [in LXX for נֶשֶׁךְ,] (a) a bringing forth, birth; (b) offspring. Metaphorical, of the produce of money lent out, interest, usury.
(Rec. τρυβλίον), -ου, τό [in LXX chiefly for קְעָרָה;] a bowl, dish.

1. a rib: mostly in plural the ribs, the side, (Iliad by Homer),—;also in singular, (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. of places, πλευρὸν νεῶν the side of the bay where the ships lay, (Sophocles Tragicus); τὸ δεξιὸν πλ. the right flank (of an army), (Xenophon Historicus)
πρό-θεσις, -εως, ἡ [in LXX: (עֵרֶךְ), (מַעֲרֶכֶת), (פָּנִים), 1Ma.1:22, 2Ma.3:8,] 1. a setting forth: οἱ ἄρτοι τῆς π., ἡ π. τῶν ἄρτων. 2. a purpose.

συν-εῖδον irreg. aorist of συνοράω, [in LXX: 1Ma.4:21 א, 2Ma.2:24 2Mac 2Mac R 2Ma.5:17 2Mac 2Mac 2Mac Ma.2:8 A *;] 1. to see together or at the same time (Arist., Xen.). 2. to see in one view, hence, of mental vision, to comprehend, understand.

(οἶκος), [in LXX for דּוֹד, שְׁאֵר, in, οἰ. τοῦ σπέρματος for בָּשָׂר;] in or of the house (opposite to ξένος, ἀλλότριος); (a) of things; τὰ οἰ., household affairs or goods; (b) of persons, of the same family or kin; as subst., οἱ οἰ., kinsmen: with genitive of person(s), of the family of: metaphorically, τ. θεον, τ. πίστεως (Lft.…
(ἀσφαλής), [in LXX for בָּטַח,] 1. firmness. 2. certainty. 3. security.

an Attic strengthened form of νῦν (in cl. always of time, and most often strictly of the pres.), [in LXX: Ma.4:1-26, Ep. Je*;] now; 1. of time: with praes., Phm 9 11; with pf., with pret., (WH, mg.), ἡ ν. ἀπολογία. 2. Of logical sequence (not so in cl.): (νῦν, WH) (νῦν, WH, txt.), (νῦν, WH, txt.).
[in LXX for צַר,] narrow: fig (v MM, xxiii).
ἀν-οικο-δομέω, -ῶ [in LXX for בָּנָה, גָּדַר;] to build. again, rebuild.
compound adv., [in LXX for עַל, מֵעָל,] above: as prep. with genitive.
(onomat. from the battle-cry ἀλαλά), [in LXX chiefly for רוּעַ hi., יָלַל;] prop, to raise a war-cry, shout with triumph or joy; rarely of grief, to wail: of a cymbal, ἀλαλάζον (RV. clanging).
(αἰχμάλωτος), [in LXX chiefly for שׁבה;] in late writers = cl. αἰχμάλωτον ποιῶ (ἄγω), to take or lead captive: before εἰς, metaphorically.
ἐξ-εραυνάω (Rec. ἐξερευνάω), -ῶ, [in LXX for חָקַר, נָצַר,] to search out, search carefully: before περί.
ἐκ-φεύγω [in LXX for נוּס,] to flee away, escape: absol., before ἐκ, with accusative of person(s), with accusative of thing(s), τ. χεῖρας αὐτοῦ.

ἐμ-βλέπω [in LXX for רָאָה,), פָּנָה; metaphorically, (נָבַט hi.), Sir.2:10,] to look at: with accusative of thing(s), with dative of person(s), (ἐνέβλεψεν), absol., to look, metaphorically, to consider.

1. light, nimble, [variant datesTragica Adespota; used by (Homer) only in neuter plural as. adverb κοῦφα προβιβάς stepping lightly on, (Iliad by Homer):—;metaphorically, κουφότεραι φρένες too buoyant, (Pindar) 2. metaphorically also light, easy, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 3. empty, unsubstantial, vain, (Sophocles Tragicus) 4…

[in LXX for אַהֲבָה, which is also rendered by ἀγάπησις and φιλία;] love, goodwill, esteem. Outside of bibl. and eccl. books, there is no clear instance. In NT, like ἀγαπάω, -ῶ, 1. Of men's love: (a) to one another, (b) to God. 2. Of divine love; (a) God's love: to men, to Christ, (b) Christ's love to men. 3. In pl.…

[in LXX for פּוּץ hi.,] in vernac. and in Ion, and late writers for σκεδάννυμι, to scatter: ὁ λύκος, ὁ μὴ συνάγων μετ᾽ ἐμοῦ σκορπίζει, pass., before εἰς, with accusative loc., of one who dispenses blessings, (LXX) (of. δια-σκορπίζομαι).
to make small or fine: to thresh out, winnow, [variant datesAnthology Palantina:—;Pass. to be reduced, grow lean, (Aristotle Philosopher); τοὺς ὤμους λεπτύνεσθαι (Xenophon Historicus)
(εἰρήνη), [in LXX chiefly for שׁלם, שׁקט;] 1. to bring to peace, reconcile (so 1Ma.6:60). 2. to keep peace, be at peace.
ἀνα-δείκνυμι [in LXX: (יָדַע), Dan LXX (מָנָה), (מָצָא), 1Esdra.6.2, 3Mac.9 *;] 1. to lift up and show, show forth, declare. 2. to consecrate, set apart, (Strab., Plut., Anth.).
[in LXX: (חַד), (קַל), (שָׁנַן),] 1. sharp. 2. Of motion, swift: (LXX ταχινός).
adv., denoting sequence; 1. of time; then, next: before genitive abs., in enumerations. 2. In argument; (a) therefore, then, (b) furthermore.
[in LXX chiefly for חוּל, also for חָבַל pi.,] to have birthpangs, to travail: (LXX), metaphorically.
ἀ-παίδευτος, -ον (παιδεύω), [in LXX for כְּסִיל, chiefly in Wis. lit.;] uninstructed, ignorant.

1. Act. = Lat. perdo, 2. to destroy, make an end of, (Homer) 3. to lose, θυμόν, ψυχήν, μένος, ἦτορ ὀλέσαι to lose life, (Homer); πόνον ὀλέσαντες having lost their labour, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 4. Mid., = Lat. pereo, 5. to perish, come to an end, (Homer); also with accusative cognate, κακὸν οἶτον…
[in LXX chiefly for עוּף;] to fly. πετάομαι, [in LXX: *;] false form of ποτάομαι, poët., frequentat. of πέτομαι, Rec. for πέτομαι
(Τ, Κάϊν), ὁ, indecl. (in FlJ, Κάϊς, -ιος), (Heb. קַיִן;), Cain: Ju 11.

1. originally a tree (which indeed comes from the same Root), commonly the oak, Lat. quercus, (Homer), sacred to Zeus, who gave his oracles from the oaks of Dodona, (Odyssey by Homer);—;hence, αἱ προσήγοροι δρύες (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;proverbial, οὐ γὰρ ἀπὸ δρυός ἐσσι οὐδ᾽ ἀπὸ πέτρης thou art no foundling from tree or rock, i. e…
προ-βαίνω [in LXX chiefly for בּוֹא;] to go forwards, go on, advance. Metaphorical, of age, ἐν τ. ἡμέραις.
(= μηδαμῆ, -δαμά, adv. fr. μηδαμός = μηδείς) [in LXX chiefly for הָלִלָה, הָלילָה;] by no means, not at all. μ., Κύριε (sc. τοῦτο γένοιτο).
1. that which has grown, a plant, tree, (Iliad by Homer), 2. generally a creature, of men, (Euripides) 3. like ἔρνος, of men, a descendant, child, (Euripides)
(θήρα), [in LXX for צוּד,] to hunt, ensnare, catch: metaphorically.

(ἄπορος, ἀ- neg., πόρος, a way, resource), [in LXX for צָרַר, מוּךְ,] to be at a loss, be perplexed: absol., (ἐποίει, R, mg.); mid., be in doubt: absol., with accusative, before περί, ἐν, περὶ τίνος λέγει. SYN.: διαπορέω, διακρίνομαι, διστάζω, μετεωρίζομαι
ἐπ-έκεινα adv. (= ἐπ᾽ ἐκεῖνα), [in LXX: (הָלְאָה),] beyond; with genitive, (LXX)
[in LXX chiefly for שָׂחַק,] to deride, laugh scornfully at: with genitive of person(s).
adv., twice: δ. τ. σαββάτου, καὶ ἅπαξ κ. δ., δ. ἀποθανόντα, Ju 12; δ. μυριάδες.
(βύσσος), [in LXX chiefly for שֵׁשׁ, בּוּץ,] made of βύσσος, fine linen.
[in LXX chiefly for קָדַד;] to bow the head, stoop down: before κάτω. κατα-κύπτω, [in LXX: 4 (שָׁקַף hi.)*;] to bend down, stoop: (κάτω κύψας, Rec., WH, mg.).
[in LXX chiefly for טבל;] (a) to dip: (ἐμβ-, L); (b) to dip in dye, to dye.

(μνήμων, mindful) [in LXX for זָכַר;] 1. to call to mind, remember: absol., with genitive of person(s), τ. πτωχῶν, with genitive of thing(s), with accusative obj. (as more frequently in cl.), of persons, of things, before ὅτι, πόθεν, πῶς. 2. to make mention of: with genitive, before περί.
τό (μέγας) [in LXX chiefly for קוֹמָה;] greatness.
[in LXX chiefly for תּוֹלָע and cogn. forms;] a worm: of the kind which preys upon dead bodies, metaphorically, of fut. punishment.
1. ionic and epic ῥοιή, a pomegranate-tree, (Odyssey by Homer) 2. the fruit, a pomegranate, (Homeric Hymns) 3. a knob shaped like a pomegranate, (Herdotus Historicus)

τό (καθαρίζω). [in LXX for טָהֵר, טׇהֳרָה,] cleansing, purification: with genitive subjc., τ. Ἰουδαίων, with genitive obj., of women after childbirth, of lepers, with genitive of thing(s), τ. ἁμαρτιῶν, (Cremer, 319).
by crasis for καὶ ἄν, with subjunc., 1. and if: with ellips.. 2. Concessive, even if. 3. As intensive of simple καί (M, Pr., 167; WM, 730; Jannaris, Gr., 598), even, at least.
that which is broken, a fragment, wreck, piece, (Aeschulus Tragicus) from * θραύω
to make quite desolate, leave destitute, abandon, (Sophocles Tragicus); ἐξ. γένυν δράκοντος making it destitute of teeth, (Euripides):—;Pass. to be left destitute, (Aristophanes Comicus)

(τάσσω), [in LXX: (מָקוֹם), (דִּבְרָה), 2Ma.9:18,] 1. an arranging, hence, in military sense, disposition of an army, battle array. 2. arrangement, order. 3. due order: (ICC, in l); κατὰ τάξιν. 4. office, order: (LXX), " (LXX).

1. to fall away, slip away, escape, (Xenophon Historicus) 2. of reports and rumours, to spread abroad, (Xenophon Historicus) 3. to fall asunder, crumble in pieces, (Plato Philosophus) 4. to fail utterly, go quite wrong, (Aristophanes Comicus)
παρ-ίημι [in LXX: (פָּרַשׂ pi.),] 1. to pass by or over, let alone, disregard. 2. to relax, loosen; pass., to be relaxed, weakened, exhausted: παρειμένας χεῖρας, (LXX ἀνειμ-).
(δειλία), [in LXX for חתת ni., פּחד,] = the more frequently ἀποδ-, to be cowardly, timid, fearful.
thirst, (Iliad by Homer), ποτοῦ for drink, (Plato Philosophus)
[in LXX for זָנָה;] 1. to prostitute the body for hire. 2. to commit fornication: (WH, mg). Metaphorical, of idolatry.
[in LXX for רֹאשׁ, לַעֲנָה, מְרֵרָה;] gall: metaphorically.

τό (neut. of δαιμόνιος, -α, -ον, divine), [in LXX for שֵׁד, אֱלִיל, (frequently in To);] 1. as in cl.; (a) the Divine power, Deity; (b) an inferior divinity, deity or demon (as in magical π, Deiss., BS, 281; MM, Exp., x): ξένα δ.. 2. (a) in OT, heathen deities, false gods (e.g., (96):5); (b) in NT, evil spirits…
to make fast and sure, fortify, (Polybius Historicus): —;the Mid. just like Act., (Xenophon Historicus)
to draw out, (Iliad by Homer); so in Mid., ἐκσπασσαμένω ἔγχεα having drawn out their spears, (Iliad by Homer)

δια-τάσσω [in LXX for שׂוּם, שָׁמַר,] to charge, give orders to, appoint, arrange, ordain: with dative, before inf.. Mid., with accusative, with dative, before inf.. Pass., τὸ διατεταγμένον, τὰ διαταχθέντα, διαταγείς.

(σοφός), [in LXX chiefly for חָכָם;] to make wise, instruct: with accusative of person(s), (cf.. As depon., -ομαι; (a) intrans., to become wise (I2, and frequently in Sir.7:5,); (b) trans., to invent, devise cleverly: pass..
(χορός, ἡγέομαι) [in LXX for כּוּל pilp.;] 1. to lead a χορός. 2. to defray the cost of a χορός. 3. In late writers, metaphorically, with accusative, to supply, furnish abundantly.

anything received, income, (Aeschulus Tragicus); λ. καὶ ἀνάλωμα receipt and expense, (Plato Philosophus): generally, gain, profit, Lat. lucrum, (Sophocles Tragicus), παντὸς ἥττων λήμματος unable to resist any temptation of gain, (Demosthenes Orator); often in plural, (Demosthenes Orator)

1. absolute to be lord or master, gain the mastery, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 2. with genitive to be lord or master of, (Homeric Hymns), δεσπόζειν φόβης to own the lock of hair, (Aeschulus Tragicus); metaphorically to master, δ. λόγου (Aeschulus Tragicus) 3. with accusative to lord it over, (Euripides)
ἀνα-λύω [in LXX: I, Tob.2:9, Jdth.13:1, Sir.3:15, Wis.3:1-19 Mac.10 *;] 1. to unloose. 2. to unloose for departure, depart: from life, 3. to return.
(ἀνάγκη), [in LXX: (שֹׁטֵר), I Ma.2:25,] to necessitate, compel by force or persuasion, constrain: with accusative, id. with inf., pass., C. inf..

τό (διαδέω, to bind round), [in LXX for כֶּתֶר (as),] the band round the τιάρα of a Persian king; a diadem, the badge of royalty. SYN.: στέφανος, the badge of "victory, of valour, of nuptial joy, of festal gladness ".
(ἀγαλλιάω), [in LXX (most frequently in Pss. and often coupled with εὐφροσύνη, as Ps 44(45):15) chiefly for גִּיל;] exultation, exuberant joy: Ju 24; χαρὰ καὶ ἀ., (Cremer, 592).
τό (δοκέω), [in LXX chiefly for דָּת, טְעֵם;] 1. an opinion. 2. A public decree, ordinance: of Roman rulers, of the Jewish law, of the Apostles, (Cremer, 205).
(ταλαίπωρος), [in LXX Chiefly for שָׁדַד pu.;] 1. to do hard labour, suffer hardship or distress. 2. In cl. occasionally trans., to weary, distress (so,).

a lover, properly of persons, (Aristophanes Comicus),—;metaphorically of things, τυραννίδος (Herdotus Historicus); πολέμων (Euripides); ἐρ. πραγμάτων = πολυπράγμων, (Aristophanes Comicus); ἐρ. τοῦ πονεῖν fond of work, (Aristophanes Comicus); ἐρ. ἐπαίνου (Xenophon Historicus)
[in LXX: (כָּבַשׁ), Sir.17:4,] to gain or exercise dominion (over); (a) absol. (Arist.); (b) with genitive. SYN.: (κατεξουσιάζω)
[in LXX chiefly for דָּבַק;] to glue to; pass., reflexive, to stick to, cleave to (Plat.): metaphorically, before πρός, (R, txt.), (LXX).
τό [in LXX for פָּצַע, חָלַל,] a wowed.
(τρύζω, to murmur, coo), [in LXX for תּוֹר;] a turtle-dove.
ἄ-μεμπτος, -ον (μέμφομσι), [in LXX chiefly for תָּם;] blameless, free from fault: (WH, mg., -ως). SYN.: ἄμωμος, ἀνέγκλητος, ἀνεπίλημπτος, which see (Tr., Syn., § ciii)
ή [in LXX for עׇרְלָה;] the prepuce, foreskin (LXX), hence abstr., uncircumcision: By meton., the uncircumcised.
(καταστρέφω), [in LXX: (אֵיד),] 1. overthrow: (WH, om.). 2. Metaphorical, subversion, upsetting.
(πόλις), [in LXX chiefly for רֵעַ;] 1. a citizen: with genitive loc.. 2. a fellow-citizen: with genitive of person(s), " (LXX).
to hold cheap, to depreciate, disparage, (Xenophon Historicus)

see: δωρεά. δωρεά, -ᾶς, ἡ (δίδωμι), [in LXX chiefly (-άν) for חִנָּם, as;] a gift: δ. τ. θεοῦ, τ. Χριστοῦ, τ. πνεύματος, τ. δικαιοσύνης, τ. χάριτος, ἀνεκδιηγήτὶῳ δ.. Acc, δωρεάν, adverbially (as frequently in LXX), (a) freely, as a gift: (b) in vain, uselessly: ( LXX). SYN.: see: δόμα
[in LXX chiefly for נָשַׁק;] to kiss fervently, kiss affectionately.
[in LXX: (עָצַב hith.), Psa, (דָּמַם), Dan LXX TH Sus (רָדַם ni.), Sir.12:12,] 1. to strike or prick violently. 2. to stun. 3. Of strong emotion, pass., to be smitten: τὴν καρδίαν.
ἀν-αλίσκω, [in LXX chiefly for אָכַל also for כָּלָה,] 1. to expend. 2. to consume, destroy: Rec. WH, mg.

1. neuter πῖον, genitive πίονος, fat, plump, Lat. pinguis, (Homer); π. δημός rich fat, (Iliad by Homer); of oil, (Herdotus Historicus) 2. of soil, fat, rich. (Iliad by Homer); also, πίονα ἔργα pingues segetes, (Iliad by Homer); ὀπώρας πίων ποτός, of wine, (Sophocles Tragicus) 3. of persons and places, rich, wealthy, (Homer)…
to press, urge, or hasten on, (Aeschines Orator)
(-ους), τό [in LXX: (שְׁחִין);] 1. a wound (Hom.). 2. a sore, an ulcer.

1. of persons, 2. with accusative rei, to drop, let fall or shed drop by drop, (Iliad by Homer), 3. with dative rei, αἵματι στ. to drip with blood, (Aeschulus Tragicus); στάζων ἱδρῶτι (Sophocles Tragicus);—;rarely with genitive, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 4. intransitive of things, to drop, fall in drops, drip, trickle, (Herdotus Historicus)…
[in LXX for קָרַב, נָגַשׁ,] to come near, approach: with dative of person(s).
1. to cover with gold-leaf, gild, (Herdotus Historicus) 2. to make golden (i. e. splendid), (Plutarch)
(WH, -ία), -ας, ἡ (ἱερατεύω), [in LXX for כָּהַן pi., כְּהֻנָּה, exc. (אֵפוֹד)*;] priesthood, office of priest.
(τελειόω), [in LXX chiefly for מִלֻּא,] fulfilment, completion, perfection.

1. a putting together, composition, combination, (Plato Philosophus); γραμμάτων συνθέσεις, i. e. syllables and words, (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;also, of an author's composition, (Isocrates Orator) 2. metaphorically, like συνθεσία, an agreement, treaty, (Pindar) 3. Lat. synthesis was a suit of clothes, (Martialis Epigrammaticus Latinus)…

συν-έρχομαι [in LXX for הָלַךְ, בּוֹא, אָסַף ni.,] 1. (cl.) to come together, assemble: T, WH, txt., before εἰς, with accusative loc., ἐπὶ τ. αὐτό, with dative of person(s), WH, mg., R, ἐν ἐκκλησίᾳ, ἐνθάδε, WH, mg.; ὅπου, with inf., εἰς τ. φαγεῖν, εἰς τ. ἧσσον, of sexual intercourse. 2. In later sense…
(οἰκτείρω), in cl. poët, for ἐλεήμων, [in LXX chiefly for רַחוּם;] merciful.
[in LXX: (מִקְשָׁה); σ. πέτρα, (צַר),] hard, firm, solid: τροψή, θεμέλιος, figuratively. Metaphorical, (a) in bad sense, hard, cruel; (b) in good sense, steadfast, firm: τ. πίστει.
[in LXX for עָלַם ni.,] to escape notice, be hidden (from): with accusative of person(s), as in common cl. idiom, before ptcp., ἔλαθον ξενίσαντες, entertained unawares.
adv. (= παρὰ τὸ χρῆμα), [in LXX: (פִּתְאוֹם),] on the spot, forthwith, instantly.
indecl. (Heb. מִיכָאֵל, who like God?), Michael, the Archangel: Ju 9.
κατ-αν-αλίσκω [in LXX chiefly forאָכַל;] 1. to use up, spend. 2. to consume: of fire, ptcp., (LXX).
[in LXX for דָּרַךְ,] 1. intrans., to tread, walk: before ἐπάνω ὄφεων κ.τ.λ. (figuratively). 2. Trans., to tread on, trample: τ. ληνόν, of the desecration of Jerusalem by its enemies.

[in LXX: (נָשָׁה), (חוֹב), Wis.12:15, 20,] to owe, be a debtor: with accusative of thing(s), Phm 18; id. with dative of person(s). Pass., to be owed, to be due: τ. ὀφειλόμενον. Metaphorical: absol., with accusative of thing(s) and dative of person(s), with inf., to be bound or obliged to do (of. Westc., Epp. Jo., 50), Jn Jn…
τό, dimin. of οὖς, [in LXX for אֹזֶן;] an ear.

1. raised from the ground, hanging, Lat. suspensus, (Herdotus Historicus);—;of high ground, (Thucydides) 2. like μετάρσιος, in mid-air, high in air, Lat. sublimis, (Herdotus Historicus); Ἀήρ, ὃς ἔχεις τὴν γῆν μ. poised on high, (Aristophanes Comicus); τὰ μ. χωρία the regions of air, (Aristophanes Comicus); τὰ μ. things in heaven above…
γεύομαι, [in LXX chiefly for טעם;] to make to taste. Mid., to taste eat: absol., with genitive, with accusative. Metaphorical, ῥῆμα θεοῦ, θανάτου, before ὅτι, (Cremer, 148).
καθ-έδρα, -ας, ἡ (κατά, + ἔδρα, a seat) [in LXX for מוֹשָׁב and cogn. forms;] a chair, seat: of teachers.

1. to run by or past, (Iliad by Homer) 2. to outrun, overtake, (Iliad by Homer): π. τὰ τότε κακά to go beyond, exceed them, (Euripides) 3. to run through or over, run across (a space of ground expressed or implied), (Xenophon Historicus) 4. to run over, i. e. treat in a cursory way, (Isocrates Orator):—; to slight, neglect…
[in LXX chiefly for זָהָב;] gold: of golden ornaments, (Rec., WH, mg.), (Rec., WH, mg.) (Rec., WH, mg.); of images, of gold coin.
eighteenth: ὀκτωκαιδεκάτῃ (i.e. ἡμέρᾳ); on the eighteenth day, (Odyssey by Homer)
adv., [in LXX for רָחוֹק and cogn. forms;] from afar.
(κεράννυμι), [in LXX for יָצַר,] a potter: ὁ ἀγρὸς τοῦ κ., (LXX).
adv. (in older Attic, πρόσω), [in LXX for רָחוֹק,] far off: " (LXX), comparat., πορρώτερον (-ρω, T).

κατ-αρτίζω [in LXX chiefly in Ps and Ezra (כְּלַל);] to render ἄρτιος, i.e. fit, complete; (a) to mend, repair: (b) to furnish completely, complete, equip, prepare: pass., mid., (LXX), (LXX); (with) in ethical sense, to prepare, complete, perfect: (EV, restore), pass., (Field, Notes, 167).

1. an alliance offensive and defensive (opposite to an ἐπιμαχία, defensive), (Herdotus Historicus), συμμαχίαν ποιεῖσθαι πρός τινα (Herdotus Historicus); τινί (Thucydides) 2. generally, the duty of an ally, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 3. = τὸ συμμαχικόν, the body of allies, (Herdotus Historicus): also, the country of one's allies…

(κτίζω), [in LXX: (קִנְיָן), A (הוֹן), Tob.8:5, Wis.2:6, Sir.16:17, 3Ma.2:2,] 1. a founding, settling, foundation (cl.). 2. In LXX and NT, (a) the act of creating, creation: (Swete, in l), (b) that which has been created, creation: καινὴ κ., πάσῃ ἀνθρωπίνῃ κ. (Hort., in l), collectively, of the sum of created things (Wis.19:6…

1. all together, all at once, all in a body, (Homer), attic; in attic, the Art. is often added in the case of Numerals, πέντ᾽ ἦσαν οἱ ξύμπαντες (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. with collective nouns, the whole, ὁ ς. στρατός (Herdotus Historicus); στρατὸς ς. (Sophocles Tragicus); ξύμπασα πόλις the state as a whole, (Thucydides); ξ…
1. a sense of pain, pain, suffering, (Herdotus Historicus), 2. of mind, pain, grief, (Sophocles Tragicus)

τό mostly (in NT always) in pl., σπλάγχνα, -ων, τά, [in LXX: (רַחַם, elsewhere rendered by οἰκτιρμοί, and by ἔλεος,), (בֶּטֶן), Wis.10:5, Sir.30:7, 2Ma.9:5 (6),] the inward parts. Metaphorical, of the seat of the feelings and of the feelings themselves, the heart, affections: Phm 7 12 20, σ. οἰκτιρμοῦ, σ. καὶ οἰκτιρμοὶ, σ…
[in LXX chiefly for חֵךְ, al; (גָּרוֹן);] the larynx, throat: metaphorically, of speech, " (LXX).

1. an earthen vessel, Lat. testa, (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. a tile or potsherd, especially the tablet used in voting; (Plato Philosophus) 3. a sort of earthenware castanet, (Aristophanes Comicus) 4. the hard shell of testaceous animals, as snails, muscles, tortoises, (Homeric Hymns)

1. to blossom, bloom, of the youthful beard, (Odyssey by Homer); of flowers and plants, (Hesiod), 2. metaphorically, 3. to be bright with colour, ἀνθεῖν φοινικίσι (Xenophon Historicus) 4. to be in bloom, (Pindar); ἐν ὥραι, ἐφ᾽ ὥραι ἀνθεῖν to be in the bloom of youth, (Plato Philosophus) 5. to flourish in wealth and prosperity, (Hesiod)…
ἐπι-φέρω [in LXX chiefly for שָׁלַח;] 1. to bring upon or against: κρίσιν, Ju 9. 2. to impose, inflict.
(βόσκω), [in LXX for עֵשֶׂב, דֶשֶׁא, חָצִיר;] 1. grass, fodder. 2. green herb. SYN.: λάχανον, a garden herb, a vegetable.

[in LXX chiefly for מטר;] 1. to wet. 2. In late Gk. writers and vernac. = ὕειν, to send rain, to rain (Kennedy, Sources, 39, 155): trop., β. πῦρ κ. θεῖον, impers., βρέχει, it rains: with ὐετός as subj..

[in LXX: (לָקַח), (סוּג hi.), Sir.44:16, 2Ma.7:24, al;] 1. to transfer to another place: with accusative, pass., (LXX); before εἰς, 2. to change: with accusative, pass., before εἰς, figuratively, i.e. to make one thing a pretext for another, χάριν εἰς ἀσέλγειαν, Ju 4. Mid., to change oneself, pass over: before ἀπό and εἰς.
συν-καλύπτω (Rec. συγκ-), [in LXX chiefly for כָּסָה pi.;] to veil or cover completely: with accusative, pass..
ἁλός, ὁ variant for ἅλας: Rec. WH, mg., R, mg.

1. under the hand, in hand, (Odyssey by Homer) 2. of persons, under any one's hand, under command, subject, τινι (Herdotus Historicus), λαβεῖν τινα ὑποχείριον to get into one's power, (Euripides); ἔχειν τινὰ ὑπ. (Thucydides)
[in LXX chiefly for צחק, שׂחק;] to laugh: fut., γελάσω) (M, Pr., 154), ib. 21.

1. to make quickly, (Sophocles Tragicus); τοῖα σπερχόμενος ταχύνει such are the words which in his eager haste he speaks, (Euripides) 2. intransitive to be quick, to make haste, speed, hurry, (Aeschulus Tragicus)
τό [in LXX for קֶבֶר, קְבוּרָה;] 1. a memorial, record. 2. (a) (cl.) a monument: (b) a sepulchre, tomb: and frequently in Gospels, SYN.: μνῆμα

to empty out, leave desolate, (Aeschulus Tragicus); ἐκκενοῦν θυμὸν ἐς σχεδίαν γέροντος to pour out one's spirit into Charon's boat, i. e. give up the ghost, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus); ἐκκ. ἰούς to shoot all one's arrows, [variant datesAnthology Palantina:—;Pass. to be left desolate, (Aeschulus Tragicus)
(μισθός) [in LXX (mid.) chiefly for שָׂכָר;] to let out for hire. Mid., to hire: with accusative.
τό (διίστημι), [in LXX for רֶוַח,] an interval, space: of time (Sir, prol. 24).
1. to cover over, hide away, conceal, (Homer), 2. absolute to use concealment, to conceal oneself, of the gods, (Odyssey by Homer)
[in LXX chiefly for מָכַר;] 1. to exchange or barter. 2. to sell: οἱ πωλοῦντες, with accusative of thing(s), (sc. αὐτά, αὐτόν). Pass., with genitive pretii.
-ας, ἡ (μαλακός), [in LXX chiefly for חֳלִי,] 1. prop., softness, effeminacy. 2. In NT, as in LXX, = ἀσθένεια, weakness, sickness: νόσος καὶ μ.. SYN.: see: ἀσθένεια

1. that which is slain or offered, a victim, sacrifice, offering, [variant datesTragica Adespota, (Thucydides), πάγκαρπα θ. offerings of all fruits, (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. sacrifice, as an act, (Sophocles Tragicus): metaphorically, θ. λεύσιμον a sacrifice to be avenged by stoning [the murderers,]
παρ-άλιος, -ον (in cl., chiefly -α, -ον), [in LXX for יָם, חוֹף, with prep.;] by the sea; ἡ π., the sea coast.
(θάπτω), [in LXX chiefly for קָבַר and cognate forms;] burial.
(γῆ), [in LXX chiefly for שָׁכֵן;] a neighbour.
(ἑορτή), [in LXX for חָגַג;] to keep festival.

(Hellenized form), and Μαριάμ, indecl., ἡ (Aram. מַרְיָם; Heb. מִרְיָם) Mary. In NT; 1. the mother of Jesus: ff., ff.. M. Magdalene. 3. The wife of Clopas and mother of James the little, and Joses. 4. The sister of Martha and Lazarus: ff.. 5. The mother of John Mark. 6. A Christian greeted by St. Paul.
(-ους), τό (late form of δίψα), [in LXX chiefly for and cognates;] thirst.

(κακός), adv., [in LXX: Wis.18:19, 4Ma.6:17.; κ. εἰπεῖν, ἐρεῖν (אָרַר, קָלַל pi.), (27), κ. ἔχειν (חָלָה,] badly, ill; (a) in physical sense: κ. ἔχειν, to be ill, πάσχειν, (WH, mg.); δαιμονίζεσθαι, κακοὺς κ. ἀπολέσει, evil that they are, he will evilly, (b) in moral sense, wrongly: κ. λαλεῖν, είπεῖν, with accusative of person(s)…
genitive, χρωτός, ὁ [in LXX chiefly for בָּשָׂר;] in cl. rare in prose, the surface of the body, skin.
(dimin. of πτέρυξ), [in LXX chiefly for כָּנָף;] 1. a little wing. 2. Anything like a wing, as a turret, battlement: τ. ἱεροῦ.
(T, ἅλα), -ατος, τό, late form of cl. ἅλς, -ος, ὁ, [in LXX chiefly for מְלַח;] salt, lit, and figuratively: like cl. ἅλες, wit, of wisdom and grace in speech.
ἐπ-ακολουθέω, -ῶ [in LXX (chiefly metaphorically) for אָחַר, הָלַךְ,] to follow after; in NT metaphorically; absol.: with dative of person(s), of sins, τ. ἴχνεσιν, ἔργῳ ἀγαθῷ.
(χείρ, ποιέω), [in LXX (of idols) for אֱלִיל;] made by hand (i.e. of human handiwork): of temples, of circumcision.
τό (τάσσω), [in LXX chiefly for דֶּגֶל, also for חַי, רַגְלִי;] that which has been arranged or placed in order; esp. as military term, a company, troop, division, rank: metaphorically.
(ἥδομαι, to be glad) [in LXX: (טַעַם), Wis.7:2, and frequently in 4Mac;] pleasure: pl.
and πρᾷος (Or πρᾶος, ν. Bl., § 3, 3), -α, -ον, [in LXX for עָנָו, עָנִי;] gentle, meek: " (LXX).
a song, a lyric ode, or lay, (Plato Philosophus)
[in LXX chiefly for קוּם;] 1. to abide in. 2. to abide by, be true to: before ἐν; τ. πίστει, τ. διαθήκῃ, (LXX); with dative, τ. γεγραμμένοις: (LXX).
1. fortieth, Lat. quadragesimus, (Thucydides) 2. τεσσαρακοστή [ μοῖρα], a fortieth, a coin of Chios, (Thucydides)

1. of or for war, (Thucydides); ἀσπὶς πολεμικωτάτη most fit for service, (Xenophon Historicus) 2. ἡ -κή (i.e. τέχνη); the art of war, war, (Plato Philosophus): —; τὰ πολεμικά warlike exercises, (Thucydides) 3. τὸ πολεμικόν the signal for battle, (Xenophon Historicus) 4. the military class, opposite to the civilian…
δια-φεύγω [in LXX: (פָּלִיט), (שָׂרִיד),] to flee through, escape.
ἐκ-διώκω [in LXX for בָּרַח hi., צָמַת, הָדַף,] to chase away, drive out.
[in LXX chiefly for נָגַף ni.;] 1. trans., to cause to stumble. 2. Intrans., to stumble. Metaphorical, in moral sense.

(κρύπτω) [in LXX for אָטַם, מִסְתָּר,] hidden, secret: ὁ κ. τῆς καρδίας ἄνθρωπος, neut., ἐν τῷ κ., ἐν κ., ὁ ἐν κ. Ἰουδαῖος, pl., τὰ κ. τ. σκότους, τ. ἀνθρώπων, τ. καρδίας, τ. αἰσχύνης. κρυφαῖος, -αία, -αῖον (κρύφα = κρυφῆ) [in LXX for מִסְתָּר,] hidden, secret: ἐν τῷ κ..
(χαράσσω), [in LXX for סֹלְלָה, מָצוֹר,] 1. a pointed stake 2. a palisade or rampart.
adv. (εὐθύς), [in LXX: (פִּתְאוֹם), Wis.5:12, 1Ma.11:12,] straightway, at once, directly: and frequently in Mt, Lk, Jo, Ac (in Mk, εὐθύς), which see)
(Σιδών), of Sidon, Sidonian; (a) the region: sc. χώρα, (b) the people.
ἅρκος (Rec. (cl.) ἅρκιος), [in LXX for דֹּב;] -ου, ὁ, ἡ, a bear.

ἐπι-ζητέω, -ῶ [in LXX chiefly for דָּרַשׁ, 4, also for בָּקַשׁ,), פָּקַד, 4;] "directive" of ζητέω (MM, Exp., xiv), to inquire for, seek after, wish for: with accusative of thing(s), with accusative of person(s), with inf..

1. as preposition, 2. with genitive loci, outside, before, παρὲκ λιμένος (Odyssey by Homer); παρὲξ ὁδοῦ out of the road, (Iliad by Homer) 3. like χωρίς, besides, except, exclusive of, παρὲξ τοῦ ἀργύρου (Herdotus Historicus) 4. with accusative out by the side of, along side of, παρὲξ ἅλα (Iliad by Homer)…
παρ-εν-οχλέω, -ῶ, [in LXX for לָאָה hi.,] to annoy concerning a matter (παρά): with dative of person(s).
[in LXX for עָבַר,] 1. trans., to step over, trans­gress (R, overreach:). 2. Intrans., to transgress: metaphorically.
[in LXX chiefly for שִׁרְיוֹן and cogn. forms;] a breastplate: θ. τ. δικαιοσύνης, θ. πίστεως.

1. fearful, terrible, dread, dire, (Homer), δεινὸν ἀϋτεῖν, βροντᾶν to shout, thunder terribly, (Iliad by Homer); δεινὸν δέρκεσθαι, παπταίνειν, ἰδεῖν to look terrible, (Homer); but, δεινὸς ἰδέσθαι fearful to behold, (Odyssey by Homer); δεινὸς μὲν ὁρᾶν, δεινὸς δὲ κλύειν (Sophocles Tragicus):—; τὸ δεινόν danger, suffering, awe, terror…
ἀν-ορθόω, -ῶ (ἀνά, ὀρθόω, to set straight, set up), [in LXX chiefly for כּוּן hi.;] to set upright or straight again, restore: of persons, of things, σκηνήν.
μή-τε negative particle, differing from οὔτε as μή from οὐ, neither, nor: μήτε... μήτε, neither... nor, μὴ (μηδὲ)... μήτε... μήτε, T.

(οἶκος + νέμω, to manage) [in LXX chiefly for עַל;] 1. prop., the manager of a household or estate, a house- or land-steward (usually a slave or freedman): ὀ οἰ. τ. πόλεως. 2. Metaphorical, an administrator, a steward: of Christian ministers, of Christians generally.

(προσφέρω), [in LXX: (פָּנִים) (מִנְחָה), I, Sir.14:11,] 1. a bringing to, offering. 2. (Less frequently in cl.), a present, an offering; in NT, of sacrificial offerings: περί ἀμαρτίας, with genitive obj..
1. the thirtieth, (Herdotus Historicus), 2. τριακοστή, a duty of one-thirtieth, (Demosthenes Orator)
(μυκτήρ, the nose), [in LXX: 4, (לָעַג), (נָאַץ) (בָּזָה), 1Ma.7:34,] to turn up the nose or sneer at, mock: pass..
ἀπο-κρύπτω [in LXX chiefly for סָתַר;] to hide, conceal, keep secret: with accusative, pass..

τό (πληρόω), [in LXX for מְלֹא;] the result of the action involved in πληρόω (Lft., Col., 255 if.; AR, Eph., 255 ff.), hence, 1. in passive sense, that which has been completed, complement, plenitude, fullness: " (LXX) (AR, 42 ff.) (AR. 87 ff.), of time, κοφίνων (σφυρίδων) πληρώματα, basketfuls. 2. In active sense…
(πολύς, τέλος) [in LXX for יָקָר,] very costly, very precious, of great value: metaphorically.

1. Persian, (Aeschulus Tragicus), 2. as Substantive, (.] (entry γῆ); Persis, Persia, now Farsistan, (Herdotus Historicus) 3. (entry γυνή); a Persian woman, (Xenophon Historicus) 4. (entry χλαῖνα); a Persian cloak, (Aristophanes Comicus)

1. to be weary with toil, to be sore distressed, (Iliad by Homer):—; to work hard, labour, (Euripides), with accusative cognate, μ. μόχθους, πόνους to undergo hardships, or to execute painful tasks, (Euripides); μ. μαθήματα to toil at learning, (Euripides) 2. with accusative objecti, τέκνα ἁμόχθησα the children whom I toiled for…
παρ-οικία, -ας, ἡ, [in LXX: (גּוֹלָה), La (מָגוֹר; and cogn. forms), I, Jdth.5:9, Wis.19:10, Sir prol. Sir.1:26 Ma.6:36 3Mac *;] a sojourning.
1. a commander, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 2. the Roman praefectus, (Plutarch)

(ἀντιλαμβάνομαι) [in LXX for עֹז, זְרוֹעַ, frequently in Mac.; frequently also in π. in petitions to the Ptolemies in sense of βοήθεια;] 1. cl. a laying hold of, an exchange. 2. Hellenistic (LXX, π.) help: pl. of ministrations of deacons; (DB, ii, 347 f.; Cremer, 386).
(σείω), [in LXX chiefly for רַעַשׁ;] a shaking, commotion, as a tempest at sea: esp. an earthquake.
(γίγνομαι), [in LXX for אָב, אֵם;] a begetter, a father; mostly in pl., οἱ γ., parents: accusative pl., γονεῖς.

[in LXX: (חָלָה ni.), Wis.12:27, Sir.38:16,] to suffer, be acted on, as opposite to acting, often limited by a word expressive of good or evil; (a) of misfortunes (most frequently without any limiting word): absol., before ὑπό, with genitive, ὑπέρ, with dative ref., περί, with genitive (before ὑπέρ), διά, with accusative…

(παρακαλέω), [in LXX: Nam.3:7, (נָחַם, its parts and derivatives), (תַּחֲנוּן), Ma.10:24 1Mac Ma.7:24 2Mac *;] 1. a calling to one's aid, summons (Thus.), hence, appeal, entreaty. 2. exhortation, encouragement: λόγος (τῆς) π., υἱὸς π.. 3. consolation, comfort (Phalar., LXX): Phm 7; τ. γραφῶν, θεὸς τῆς π., π. τοῦ Ἰσραήλ, Lk
(μνάομαι), [in LXX for זֵכֶר, זִכְרוֹן;] memory, remembrance, mention: μ. ποιεῖσθαι, with genitive, to remember. SYN.: μνεία, q.v

(κολάζω), [in LXX: (מִכְשׁוֹל), λαμβάνειν τὴν κ. (כָּלַם ni.); Wis.11:13, Mac.5 *;] correction, penalty, punishment. SYN.: τιμωρία, requital. Arist. distinguishes between κ. as that which, being disciplinary, has reference to the sufferer, and τ. as that which, being penal, has reference to the satisfaction of him who inflicts…
adv. (ὁμός), together; (a) prop., of place: (b) without idea of place.
(χλόη), [in LXX for יֶרֶק,] (a) pale green: χόρτος, πᾶν χ., (b) pale: ἵππος.
(ἐχθρός), [in LXX for אֵיבָה, שִׂנְאָה,] enmity. ἀηδία, -ας, ἡ (ἀ- neg., ἦδος, pleasure), [in LXX: (שִׂיחַ)*;] 1. of things or persons, unpleasantness, odiousness 2. dislike (Plat.). disagreement: D.
(δέρμα), [in LXX for עוֹר;] of skin, leathern.
συν-χέω (Rec. συγ-), [in LXX for בָּלַל, רָגַז,] to pour together, commingle, confuse; metaphorically, confound, throw into confusion, stir up trouble.
indecl. (in FlJ., Ant., i, 16, 1, Κάρρα, -ας, ib. 6, 5, Χαρρά, -ᾶς; so LXX: E, B, elsewhere -άν­Heb. חָרָן), Haran, a town in N.W. Mesopotamia.
thirteenth, (Homer), ἡ τρισκαιδεκάτη (i.e. ἡμέρα); the 13 th day, (Odyssey by Homer)
(WH. -τινός), -ή, -όν (σκότος), [in LXX chiefly for חֹשֶׁךְ and cogn. forms;] dark: opposite to φωτεινός.
(Rec. Ἄ-), ἡ, indecl. (in FlJ, Ἀγάρα, -ης, Heb. הָגָר), Hagar.
[in LXX chiefly for סָבַב;] to encircle, encompass: of a besieged city.
ἀφ-ικνέομαι, -οῦμαι [in LXX for בּוֹא,] perfective of ἱκνέομαι, to come (M, Pr., 247), to arrive at, come to, reach: metaphorically.
(ὁρμή), [in LXX for שׁוּב,] 1. causal, to set in motion, urge on. 2. Intrans., to hasten on, rush: before εἰς, ἐπί, with accusative.
ἕν-δεκα, οἱ, αἱ, τά indecl., eleven: of the eleven apostles, οἱ, ἕ..
[in LXX chiefly for נָגַשׁ, קָרַב;] 1. trans., to bring near (Luc.). 2. Intrans., to approach: with dative, (WH, προσενέγκαι).
indecl. (Heb. זֶרַח,), Zerah, an ancestor of Jesus.
[in LXX for יָרַד hi.,] to bring down: αἰτιώματα, ψῆφον, to cast a ballot, pass., to be borne down: ὕπνῳ, ἀπὸ τ. ὕ..

συν-κρίνω (Rec. συγκ-) [in LXX chiefly for פָּתַר;] 1. to compound, combine: R, mg.1 (Lft., Notes, 180 f.). 2. In Arist. and later writers (Wis.7:29, a1.) = παραβάλλω, to compare: 1Co, l.with, R, txt. (Field, Notes, 168), 3. In LXX, of dreams, to interpret (Co, l.with, R, mg. 2.

[in LXX: 4 (רָגַל pi.), 1Ma.5:38 (A)*;] to view closely, inspect, spy out: with accusative.

ἐν-δείκνυμι [in LXX for לָכַד, גָּמַל, רָאָה hi.;] to mark, point out. Mid„ 1. to show forth, prove: with accusative of thing(s), before ἐν, with dative of person(s), (LXX), before εἰς, (with cogn. accusative). 2. to manifest (by act): with accusative of thing(s) and dative of person(s).

1. a putting together, arranging, arrangement, organisation, order, (Thucydides): rule, (Demosthenes Orator) 2. a systematic treatise, (Aristotle Philosopher): a narrative, (Polybius Historicus) 3. grammatical construction, syntax, (Lucian) 4. a body of troops, ἡ εἰς μυρίους ς. their contingent towards 10, 000, (Xenophon Historicus) 5…
συν-καλέω (Rec. συγκ-), -ῶ, [in LXX for קָרָא;] to call together: with accusative. Mid., to call together to oneself.
[in LXX: (עָלָה),] 1. trans., to bring forth, produce (of men, to beget); pass., to spring up, grow. 2. Intrans., in 2 aor., pf., plpf., and rarely in present, to spring up.

1. sprung from the land itself, Lat. terrigena: αὐτόχθονες, οἱ, like Lat. Indigenae, aborigines, natives, (Herdotus Historicus); of the Athenians, (Euripides), 2. as adjective indigenous, (Herdotus Historicus)
ἀπο-θήκη, -ης, ἡ (ἀποτίθημι), [in LXX for אוֹצָר, טֶנֶא,] a storehouse, granary.
[in LXX chiefly for לוּן;] to mutter, murmur: before κατά, πρός, περί, μετ᾽ ἀλλήλων, with accusative, before περί.

(πειράζω), [in LXX for מַסָּה, עִנְיָן;] 1. = πεῖρα, an experiment Diosc.). 2. a trial, of ethical purpose and effect, whether good or evil (a) in good or neutral sense: esp. of afflictions sent by God: pl., (b) of trial regarded as leading to sin, temptation: of the temptation of Jesus by the devil, εἰσφέρειν (ἔρχεσθαι, εἰσέρχ-) εἰς π.…
(βάλλω), [in LXX for חֵץ, יָרָה,] a dart, javelin: Rec. (LXX).

[in LXX for גַּנָּב;] a thief. Fig., ὡς κ. ἐν νυκτί. Metaphorical, of false teachers. SYN.: λῃστής, a robber, a brigand who plunders, openly, with violence; κ. is a thief who steals in secret, by fraud and cunning (Tr., Syn., § xliv)
[in LXX for אָיַב, צוּר, שָׂטַן,] 1. to lie opposite to. 2. to oppose, withstand, resist: with dative, as participial subst. (ὁ) ἀντικείμενος, (Cremer, 746).

1. a pattern or model of the thing to be executed, Lat. exemplar, an architect's plan, (Herdotus Historicus); a sculptor's or painter's model, (Plato Philosophus) 2. a precedent, example, (Thucydides); ἐπὶ παραδείγματος by way of example, (Aeschines Orator) 3. an example, i. e. a lesson or warning, π…

1. to draw a boundary through, divide by limits, separate, (Herdotus Historicus) 2. to distinguish, determine, define, (Herdotus Historicus), 3. to determine, declare, (Sophocles Tragicus); with infinitive to determine one to be so and so, (Demosthenes Orator); with infinitive omitted…

1. the hearth, fire-place, (Homer); the sanctuary of suppliants, καθέζετο ἐπ᾽ ἐσχάρῃ ἐν κονίῃσιν (Odyssey by Homer):—; a pan of coals, a brasier, (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. πυρὸς ἐσχάραι the watch-fires of the camp, (Iliad by Homer) 3. an altar for burnt-offerings, (Odyssey by Homer)

ἐκ-φοβέω, -ῶ [in LXX chiefly for חָרֵד hi.;] to frighten away, terrify: with accusative of person(s).

ἐπί-σκοπος, -ου, ὁ (σκοπός, a watcher), [in LXX for פָּקַד, its parts and derivatives, אֵל, נָגַשׂ: Wis.1:6, 1Ma.1:51 *;] a superintendent, guardian, overseer: (ICC, in l); as technical term for a religious office (Deiss., BS, 230 f.), in later Paul. epp. of the head of a church (Vg. episcopus), a bishop.

1. an old man, Lat. senex, (the prose form is πρεσβύτης); (Sophocles Tragicus):—; ὁ πρέσβυς is used much like ὁ πρεσβύτερος, the elder, (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;plural πρέσβεις, elders, always implying dignity, chiefs, princes, (Aeschulus Tragicus); epic πρέσβηες (Hesiod) 2. (Homer) uses only the comparative and Sup.…
(μιμνήσκω), [in LXX for זָכַר, its parts and deriva­tives;] remembrance, mention (= μνήμη): μ. ποιεῖσθαι, with genitive of person(s), Phm 4; μ. ἔχειν, with genitive of person(s).
(μέγας) [in LXX: (גָּדוֹל), frequently in Sir;] magnificent, splendid.
(ἄροτρον), [in LXX: (חָרַשׁ), (עֲדַר);] later form of ἀρόω, to plough.

1. shameless, (Homer) 2. with genitive, ἀναιδέα δηϊοτῆτος insatiate of strife, (Iliad by Homer) 3. of things, λᾶας ἀναιδής the reckless stone, of Sisyphus, (Odyssey by Homer); ἔργ᾽ ἀναιδῆ (Sophocles Tragicus): —; τὸ ἀναιδές, contracted τἀνειδές, = ἀναίδεια, (Euripides); ἐπὶ τὸ ἀναιδέστερον τραπέσθαι (Herdotus Historicus) 4. adverb -δῶς…
a measured out line; a piece of measured out land

ἐπ-εγείρω [in LXX for עוּר hi., קוּם hi.,] to rouse up, excite: C. accusative of thing(s), διωγμόν, ψυχάς.

dative, -ῃ (but in., ει), accusative, -ην, ὁ (Heb. יוֹחָנָן, LXX: Ἰωανάν, -ννάν, Je 47 (40):8, Aq.), Hellenized form of Ἰωανάν, John ( I (41)*), viz., 1. John the Baptist: 2. [in LXX for עָנָה, נָבַע hi.,] of men or animals, to utter a sound or voice: absol., before ἐν φωνῇ, with accusative, ὑπέρογκα.

adv., [in LXX for צֶדֶק,] 1. righteously. 2. justly.

ἀπ-αιτέω, -ῶ [in LXX: (נָגַשׂ), Sir.20:15, Wis.15:8,] to ask back, demand back.

ἐκ-πίπτω [in LXX: (הֶבֶל), (סוּר), (שָׁלַךְ hi.),] to fall out of, fall from, fall off: before ἐκ τ. χειρῶν, absol., of the withering of flowers (as LXX, ll with), " (LXX); of navigators falling off from a straight course, Metaphorical, with genitive of thing(s): absol., fall from its place, fail, perish.

see: ἐνκ-. ἐν-καινίζω, [in LXX: (to renew), Ps 50(51):10 (Br-m pi.); (to dedicate) (-^jn); (aliter in Heb.), Si 33(36):6, 1Ma.4:36,54,57 Ma.2:29 *;] 1. to innovate (Eust.). 2. to renew (LXX ut supr.). 3. to initiate, inaugurate, dedicate (LXX ut supr.): διαθήκην, ὁδόν, ib. (Cremer, 323).

προ-ηγέσμαι [in LXX: (בְּרוֹשׁ), (פָּנִים), 2Ma.4:40,] 1. to go before as leader (in cl., with genitive, dative). 2. In a sense not elsewhere found, ἀλλήλους προηγούμενοι = ἀ. ἡγούμενοι ὑπερέχοντας: Ro, l.with.
τό (μισθόω), [in LXX: (19), (אֶתְנַן), (נֵדֶה, נָדָן), *;] 1. price, hire (cl, and LXX). 2. In sense not found elsewhere, a hired dwelling.
[in LXX for צוֹק,] narrowness of space, want of room. Metaphorical, difficulty, distress: θλίψις καὶ (ἢ) σ., (EV, anguish); pl.. SYN.: θλίψις, q.v
[in LXX: (שָׂבַר pi.),] to await, expect: with accusative of person(s), with accusative of thing(s), with accusative and inf., with inf..
ἀ-σύνετος, -ον [in LXX: (נָבָל). (נָפַל), (כְּסִיל), Wis.2:1-24, Sir.6:1-37 *;] without understanding or discernment: (Swete, in l).
[in LXX chiefly for סָבַב;] to go about (as an itinerant): (περιελόντες, WH, R, mg.), τ. οἰκίας, from house to house.
a sword, (Homer); distinguished from μάχαιρα, q. see.

τό, [in LXX: (כּבד), Jdth.7:4, Sir.13:2, 2Ma.9:10, 3Ma.5:47 *;] weight; (a) a weight, burden, lit. and metaphorically: ἀλλήλων τὰ β., one another's faults, ἐν β., burdensome: R, txt., but see infr.; (b) in late Gk., dignity, authority: ἐν βάρει. SYN.: ὄγκος, an encumbrance; φορτίον, a burden, that which is borne.
1. numberless, countless, infinite. 2. As a definite numeral, in pl., μύριοι, -αι, -α, ten thousand.
(ἄτιμος), [in LXX chiefly for בָּזָה;] = ἀτιμάζω, to dishonour, treat with indignity: Rec.
(φροντίς, thought), [in LXX: (דָּאַג), (חָשַׁב),] to give heed, take thought (in cl. usually absol., with accusative, with genitive), with inf..
1. an inclosed space: 2. for cattle, a fold, byre, stable, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus), 3. the setting of a ring, [variant datesAnthology Palantina

παρ-άγω [in LXX chiefly for עָבַר;] 1. trans., to lead by, lead aside, lead into, lead forward, 2. Intrans., (a) to pass by: R, txt., before παρό, with accusative, (b) to go away, depart; metaphorically, to pass away: mid., Jn.
to be weak and sickly, (Xenophon Historicus)
(θερμός), [in LXX chiefly for חָמַם;] to warm, heat; mid., to warm oneself.

1. to play the σῦριγξ, to pipe, (Euripides); with accusative cognate, συρίζων ὑμεναίους (Euripides) 2. to whistle, hiss, (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;with accusative cognate, συρίζων φόνον hissing forth murder, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 3. to hiss an actor, Lat. explodere, (Demosthenes Orator)
[in LXX for צָפַן,] to lay up, store up: of riches, id. with dative of person(s), with accusative of thing(s), θησαυροὺς ἑαυτῷ, pass., metaphorically, ὀργὴν ἑαντῷ.

(Heb. אָמֵן, verbal adj. fr. אמן, to prop. ni., be firm), [in LXX: I, Tob.8:8 Ma.7:23, 4Ma.18:24 (elsewhere ''א is rendered ἀληθινός, ἀληθῶς, Je 35 (28):6; γένοιτο, ff., (41):13 71 (72):19 105 (106):48,)*.] 1. As adj., ὁ ἀ.. 2. As adv., (a) in solemn assent to the statements or prayers of another: ὁ ἀ., (b) similarly…

(οἶκος, + δέμω, to build), [in LXX: A (בִּירָה), (בָּנָה, מִבְנֶה), Sir.22:16,] = cl. οἰκοδομία, -δόμησις (Thuc., Plat.), 1. the act of building; in NT always metaphorically, building up, edifying: with genitive obj., λαλεῖν, λαβεῖν, οἰ.. 2. = οἰκοδόμημα, a building: metaphorically.
(ἰάομαι), [in LXX for רָפָא;] a physician: (om. WH, R, mg.).

[in LXX: (חָבַר), Wis.6:23, Sir.13:1,] to have a share of, go shares in (something) with (some one), take part in: with genitive of thing(s) (as usually in cl., so Pr, l.with), with dative of thing(s), with dative of person(s), before εἰς, ἐν.
(ὑπάρχω), [in LXX for רְכוּשׁ, הוֹן,] 1. subsistence, existence. 2. In late writers, = τὰ ὑπάρχοντα, substance, property: pl..
adv., [in LXX: (מֵעוֹלָם) (תָּמִיד), Ps 94(95):10,] ever; 1. of continuous time, unceasingly, perpetually. 2. Of successive occurrences, on every occasion.
ἐκ-τίθημι [in LXX for נָתַן ni.,] to set out, expose: Metaphorical, to set forth, expound: with accusative of thing(s).
1. the elephant, (Herdotus Historicus) 2. the elephant's tusk, ivory, (Iliad by Homer)

ἐν-τυγχάνω [in LXX: Da TH (קֶרֶב) Wis.8:20 Ma.2:25 2Mac 2Mac 2Mac Ma.6:37; before κατά, 1Ma.8:32 1Mac 1Mac *;] 1. to fall in with. 2. to meet with in order to converse. 3. to petition, make petition: with dative of person(s), before ὑπέρ with genitive of person(s), (θεῷ, not expressed); before κατά, against.

1. a composition, of words and sentences, (Lucian) 2. a conventional agreement, convention, compact, (Plato Philosophus); ἐκ συνθήκης, ex composito, by agreement, (Plato Philosophus); κατὰ συνθήκην conventionally, (Aristotle Philosopher) 3. the article of a compact or treaty, (Thucydides):—;mostly in plural the articles of agreement…
(ἄ-νοος, without understanding), [in LXX: (אִוֶּלֶת), Wis.15:18,] folly, foolishness: expressed in violent rage.

(ἄγω), [in LXX: (לאה), Wis.4:2, II Mac.6, 4Mac.5 *;] 1. a gathering, esp. for games. 2. a place of assembly. 3. a contest, struggle, trial; metaphorically, (a) of the Christian life as a contest and struggle: (b) solicitude, anxiety.
concessive particle, [in LXX: Wis.11:9, Mac.11 *;] although: with ptcp..
later, second; (neu.) finally, last of all posterior, in place or time; subsequent, later, last, finally, last of all Tim.
1. to bind with fetters, to bind fast, make fast, (Odyssey by Homer) 2. to shackle, trammel, constrain, (Homer); with infinitive to constrain one to do a thing, (Homer)

1. to thrive, flourish, prosper, Lat. florere, vigere, (Herdotus Historicus):—;with dative to abound in a thing, (Homeric Hymns) 2. Pass. in same sense, οἱ Λακεδαιμόνιοι εὐθηνήθησαν (Herdotus Historicus); τὴν πόλιν εὐθενεῖσθαι (Demosthenes Orator) derivation uncertain
[in LXX for שָׁטַף,] to inundate, deluge: pass..
ἐκ-δι-ηγέομαι, -οῦμαι depon., [in LXX chiefly for סָפַר, pi.;] to tell in detail, relate, declare: (LXX).
(νοῦς), [in LXX: Wis.2:14, Da TH Sus *;] 1. thinking, consideration. 2. a thought, purpose, design. SYN.: ἐνθῦμησις, which see (Cremer, 439)

1. a quarrel, wrangle, strife, (Homer), 2. strife of words, railing, abuse, a taunt, reproach, (Iliad by Homer) 3. a strife at law, dispute before a judge, (Odyssey by Homer) 4. battle, fight, (Homer); ν. φυλόπιδος (Odyssey by Homer); of dissensions between whole nations, νεῖκος πρὸς Καρχηδονίους (Herdotus Historicus) 5. cause of strife…
δια-νόημα, -τος, τό (διανοέομαι, to think), [in LXX for מַחֲשָׁבָה, frequently in Sir;] a thought.
to tremble, esp. with fear: with ptcp. (in cl more frequently with inf.).
(T, Καϊ-; Rec. Καϊνάν), ό, indecl. (Heb. קֵינָן), Cainam, Cainan; 1. son of Enos. 2. Son of Arphaxad ( (LXX).
(πλοῦτος), [in LXX chiefly for עָשַׁר hi.;] to make rich, enrich: with accusative of person(s), pass.. Metaphorical, of spiritual riches, with accusative: of person(s), before ἐν, pass..
συν-οικέω, -ῶ [in LXX for בַּעַל;] to dwell together: of man and wife, with dative of person(s)
to pile a load upon a beast's back, (Herdotus Historicus); ἵππον ἐπ. to saddle it, (Xenophon Historicus)

1. to put to sleep, (Euripides); ἄημα ἐκοίμισε πόντον, i. e. the winds suffer the sea to rest—; by ceasing, (Sophocles Tragicus): metaphorically, μεγαληγορίαν κ. to lay pride asleep, (Euripides); so, κ. τὰς λύπας (Xenophon Historicus):—;Pass., παῖς κοιμίζεται (Euripides) 2. of the sleep of death, (Sophocles Tragicus); also in Mid.…
[in LXX for דָּרַשׁ;] 1. to inquire: with accusative of thing(s), before quæst. indir., quæst. dir., before παρά, with genitive of person(s). 2. to learn by inquiry: before ὅτι.
[in LXX chiefly for עָשַׁר hi.;] to be rich, aor., to become rich: before ἀπό (Sir.11:18), ἐκ, ἐν. Metaphorical, π. εἰς θεόν, of God, εἰς πάντας, aor., I became rich, pf., I have become rich.

(μάρτυς), [in LXX chiefly for עֵד (עֵד, also for עוּד hi. (, La), עָנָה;] (a) prop., to be a witness, bear witness, testify: absol., parenthetical, with dative of person(s) (comm. and incomm.; El., § 37, 2), id. before ὅτι, accusative and inf., with accusative of thing(s) (cl.), with accusative cogn., before περί…
προ-αιρέω, -ῶ [in LXX: for חָשַׁק,] to bring forth or forward. Most frequently in mid., to take by choice, prefer, propose.

1. to break up, cut up, (Herdotus Historicus) 2. to thrash soundly, pound well, (Xenophon Historicus);—;Pass., perfect infinitive συγκεκόφθαι (Aristophanes Comicus); participle συγκεκομμένος (Euripides)

ἀν-έχω [in LXX chiefly for אָפַק hithp.;] to hold up; in NT always mid., to bear with, endure: in cl. most frequently with accusative, but in NT with genitive of person(s), before μικρόν τι, with genitive of person(s) and with genitive of thing(s), with dative of thing(s), (v M, Th., in l); before εἴ τις, absol.…
[in LXX for נשׁךְ, exc. (שׂרף);] to bite: metaphorically.

1. that which is shot, an arrow, (Herdotus Historicus), ὅσον τ. ἐξικνέεται the distance of a bowshot, (Herdotus Historicus); πρὶν τ. ἐξικνεῖσθαι before an arrow reached them, (Xenophon Historicus); ἐντὸς τοξεύματος within bow-shot, (Xenophon Historicus); ἔξω τοξεύματος (Thucydides):—;metaphorically…
συν-ανα-βαίνω [in LXX for עָלָה;] to go up with: with dative of person(s), before εἰς, with accusative loc..
to excite to war, make hostile, (Xenophon Historicus)

(ζωός, alive, γένεσθαι), [in LXX, (חָיָה pi., hi.), (חַי)*;] 1. in cl., to engender, produce alive, endue with life. 2. In LXX. and NT, to preserve alive (DCG, ii, 606; Cremer, 274): (EV, quickeneth; R, mg., preserveth).

(δικάζω), [in LXX for שָׁפַט;] a judge: " (LXX). SYN.: κριτής, WH. "gives prominence to the mental process" (Thayer). δ. is the forensic term. In Attic law, the δικασταί were jurors, with a κριτής as presiding officer
a guard in front; in plural outposts, videttes, piquets, (Xenophon Historicus); in singular, ἡ πρ. αὐτοῦ his advanced guard, (Xenophon Historicus); διὰ προφυλακῆς with an advanced guard, (Thucydides)
(βία), [in LXX for אָנַשׁ, עַז, צַר,] violent.
[in LXX for טָבַע pu., A, בָּלַע pi., שָׁטַף,] to throw into the sea, sink or drown therein: pass..
to sweeten:—; Pass. to be sweetened, to turn sweet, (Moschus Bucolicus)
(πικρός), [in LXX for מָרַד, קָצַף,] to make bitter: pass., metaphorically, to embitter (LXX): pass., before πρός.

ἀπο-τίθημι [in LXX chiefly for נוּחַ hi.;] to put off or aside; in NT always mid., (a) to put of from oneself as a garment: τ. ἱμάτια, metaphorically, in ethical sense, to put of, lay aside: (b) to stow away, put: ἐν τ. φυλακῇ.
(μοιχός), [in LXX: (נָאַף);] to commit adultery: absol., with accusative fem.. Pass., of the woman, WH, mg.). Metaphorical, of idolatry, before μετ᾽ αὐτῆς.
[in LXX for סַפִּיר;] sapphire (perh. = lapis lazuli).
(πούς), [in LXX: (7) (חֹשֶׁן), (מְעִיל), (31) (אֵפוֹד), אֵפוֹד), (בַּד), (4) (מַחֲלָצָה), Wis.18:24, Sir.27:8 *;] reaching to the feet. of a garment. SYN.: στολή, see Tr., Syn., § 1

1. a ring on a horse's breast-band, to fasten it to the peg ἕστωρ); at the end of the carriage-pole, (Iliad by Homer) 2. an eyelet-hole in sails, through which the reefing-ropes were drawn, (Herdotus Historicus)

(ἵλαος = ἵλεως) [in LXX for סָלַח, 4, La, Da TH; כָּפַר pi., נָחַם ni., *;] 1. in cl., with accusative of person(s), to conciliate, appease, propitiate. 2. In LXX (Thackeray, Gr., 270, 1.), Inscr. (Deiss., BS, 224 f.), and NT, to be propitious, merciful (with dative of thing(s),): with dative of person(s) (4). 3. As in Philo, to expiate…
(τρέπω), [in LXX: Wis.7:18,] a turning: esp. of the revolution of heavenly bodies, figuratively.
(καταπαύω), [in LXX chiefly for מְנוּחָה, ἡμέρα τῆς κ., 2Ma.15:1] 1. in cl., a putting to rest, causing to cease. 2. In LXX and NT, rest, repose: (LXX)
to tell out, make known, declare, (Odyssey by Homer): to betray a secret or mystery, (Herdotus Historicus)
(-ους), τό (ζεύγνυμι, to yoke), [in LXX chiefly for צֶמֶד,] 1. a yoke of beasts. 2. a pair of any­thing, (LXX).
τό indecl. (Aram. שִׁכְרָא), [in LXX for שֵׁכָר (also rendered μέθυσμα,),] fermented liquor, strong drink.
[in LXX for פִּסֵּחַ;] lame, halt, maimed.
(Rec. -λίτης), ου, ὁ [in LXX: (יִשְׂרָאֵל), (יִזְרְעֵאלִי; Luc. Ἰεζραηλίτης),] an Israelite, the name expressive of theocratic privilege: ἀληθῶς Ἰ., ἄνδρες Ἰ..
[in LXX for קָצַר, בָּצַר,] to gather in: with accusative, (a) of the fruit, (b) of that from which it is gathered.
(λυτρόω), [in LXX: גְּאֻלָּה), (פָּדָה, פִּדְיוֹם, פְּדוּת), *;] a ransoming, redemption (αἰχμαλώτων, Plut., Arat., 11): of the mediatorial work of Christ, in general sense, deliverance.
(and Ραχάβ, Ραχάβη, -ης, in FlJ), ἡ, indecl. (Heb. רָחָב) Rahab.
ἀνα-θεματίζω (ἀνίθεμα), [in LXX chiefly for חָרַם hi., 1Ma.5:5;] to devote to destruction, declare or invoke ana­thema: absol., ἐαντόν, to bind oneself under a curse.
1. thickness, (Odyssey by Homer):—; absolute, πάχος in thickness, (Herdotus Historicus) 2. π. σαρκός stoutness, (Euripides)
genitive, -ονoς (ἐπίσταμαι) [in LXX: (בִּין ni.), I, Sir.10:25,] knowing, skilled.
τό (later form of Attic δρεπάνη, δρέπω, to pluck), [in LXX for מַזְמֵדָה, חֶרְמֵשׁ,] a sickle, pruning-hook.

ἐξ-ετάζω (ἐτάζω (rare), to examine), [in LXX: A (דָּרַשׁ), דָּרַשׁ), (בָּחַן), Wis.6:3, Sir.3:21,] to examine closely, inquire carefully (of): before περί (with ἀκριβῶς), before τίς, with accusative of person(s). SYN.: ἀνακρίνω, ἐραυνάω
(τέχνη), [in LXX for חָרָשׁ,] a craftsman, artificer: of God (Wis.13:1). SYN.: δημιουργός, which see, and cf. Tr., Syn., § cv
1. a bringing in, supplying, (Thucydides) 2. a bringing in to one's aid, introduction, (Thucydides) 3. a drawing on, alluring, (Demosthenes Orator)
to be an ally, to be in alliance, (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;generally, to help, aid, succour, τινί (Sophocles Tragicus),—;Pass. to be assisted, (Lucian)
[in LXX for אִישׁוֹן, שָׁלֵו,] 1. quietness. 2. stillness, silence
(fem. of πενθερός), [in LXX for חֲמוֹת;] a mother-in-law.
(νοῦς, τίθημι, hence, put in mind), [in LXX: (כָּהָה pi.), (יָסַר pi., בִּין), Wis.11:10 *;] to admonish, exhort: with accusative of person(s).
δια-λείπω [in LXX for יחל (as),] to intermit, leave off for a time.
[in LXX: (עָרַךְ),] to prepare, make ready: absol., mid., to prepare, make preparations: pass..
plotting against, τινι (Plato Philosophus): treacherous, (Xenophon Historicus)
[in LXX chiefly for חֶדֶר, Jol.2:16; I,] a bed-chamber; ὁ ἐπὶ τοῦ κ., a chamberlain.

1. a looking out, watch, guard, as a duty, (Herdotus Historicus); φρουρὰν ἄζηλον ὀχήσω shall keep unenviable watch, (Aeschulus Tragicus); φρουρὰ ὄμματος my watchful eye, (Sophocles Tragicus); φρουρᾶς ᾄδειν to sing while on guard, (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. a prison, (Plato Philosophus) 3. of persons, a watch, guard, garrison…
(φεύγω), [in LXX chiefly for מָנוֹס and cogn. forms;] flight.
(= βόθρος, more frequently in cl.), [in LXX chiefly for פַּחַת;] a pit.
(WH, -λία), -ας, ἡ [in LXX for יָעַל hi., בֶּצַע,] 1. assistance, help. 2. profit, advantage, benefit: Ju 16.

1. to put in trim, στολίσας νηὸς πτερά having trimmed the sails, (Hesiod) 2. to equip, dress:—;Pass., ἐστολισμένος δορί armed with spear, (Euripides) 3. metaphorically to deck, adorn, [variant datesAnthology Palantina
μετ-αλλάσσω [in LXX: (מוּת), Es.1:3 Mac.9 *;] 1. to exchange: τ. ἀλήθειαν... ἐν τ. ψεύδει, the truth for a lie, Rom_1:25. 2. to change: with accusative before εἰς, Rom_1:26 (ἀλλάσσω).

δια-φέρω [in LXX for שְׁנָא (שְׁנָא;] 1. trans., (a) to carry through: before διά, (b) to carry about, spread abroad: pass.. 2. Intrans., (a) to differ: τὰ διαφέροντα, impers., διαφέρει, it makes a difference, it matters: (b) to excel: with genitive, τὰ διαφέροντα.

1. sweet to the taste or smell, (Homer); to the hearing, (Homer); then of any pleasant feeling or state, as sleep, (Homer):—;with infinitive, ἡδὺς δρακεῖν (Aeschulus Tragicus); ἡδὺς ἀκοῦσαι λόγος (Plato Philosophus):—; ἡδύ ἐστι or γίγνεται it is pleasant, (Homer),—;so, οὔ μοι ἥδιόν ἐστι λέγειν I had rather not say…

ἐπι-δείκνυμι [in LXX: (פּוּחַ hi.), (בּוֹא hi.), Esp. Ma.15:32, al;] 1. to show, exhibit, display: with accusative and dative. Mid., to display for oneself or as one's own. 2. to show, point out, prove: with accusative, with accusative and inf..
[in LXX chiefly for שָׁכַר and cognate forms;] drunkenness: pl., SYN.: see: κῶμος
τό [in LXX chiefly for צִפּוֹר;] dimin. of στρουθός a sparrow.
[in LXX: Wis.18:9; 4Ma.12:1-19 *;] to have or get a share of, partake of: with genitive of thing(s), τροφῆς, with accusative of thing(s) (of the whole), to get: καιρόν.

genitive, φρενός, ἡ, [in LXX most frequently in Pr and chiefly for לֵב; also 3Ma.4:16 3Mac;] chiefly in Hom. and Trag., but also in Plat., both sing. and pl.; 1. in physical sense, the parts about the heart, midriff. 2. heart, mind, thought: pl..
ἐξ-αγγέλλω [in LXX chiefly for סָפַר pi.;] to tell out, proclaim: [, "shorter conclusion"] (Cremer, 29).
[in LXX for פְּתִי, תָּם,] (a) as in cl., of persons, simple, guileless: (b) of things, undamaged.
τό (κτάομαι), [in LXX for כֶּרֶם,] a possession, property.
which of two. Neut., adverbially, πότερον, whether.
any kind of dressed food; but mostly in plural, pastry, cakes, sweetmeats, (Herdotus Historicus)

1. to creep, crawl, Lat. serpo, repo, and generally to move slowly, walk, (Homer); of reports, to creep on, spread, like Lat. serpit rumor, (Sophocles Tragicus); ὁ πόλεμος ἑρπέτω let it take its course, (Aristophanes Comicus); of calamities, (Sophocles Tragicus)

1. as adjective down-rushing, τὸν καταρράκτην ὀδόν (attic for οὐδόν); to the downward entrance [of Hades,] 2. as Substantive broken water, a waterfall, Lat. cataracta, (Strabo Geographus) 3. a kind of portcullis, (Plutarch) 4. a sea-bird, so called from rushing down upon its prey, a gull, (Aristophanes Comicus)
to catch scent of, smell, scent, track, with genitive, (Herdotus Historicus), absolute, (Plato Philosophus)
indec. (Heb. רָם), Aram: (R, txt., WH, Ἀρνεί).
a brick, (Herdotus Historicus), πλίνθους ἑλκύσαι, εἰρύσαι, Lat. ducere lateres, to make bricks, (Herdotus Historicus); ὀπτᾶν to bake them, (Herdotus Historicus)

προ-τίθημι [in LXX: (עָרַךְ) (שׂוּם),] 1. to set before, set forth publicly; so also in mid.: with accusative of person(s). 2. Mid., to set before oneself, propose, purpose: with inf., with accusative of thing(s).

to hew in stone, (Septuagint Greek Bible)

ἀπο-στολή, -ῆς, ἡ (ἀποστέλλω), [in LXX: (for שָׁלַח and its cognates), 1Es.9:5, Bar.2:25, 1Ma.2:18, 2Ma.3:2 *.] 1. In cl., a sending away, as, an expedition (Hdt.). 2. In LXX (a) discharge, dis­missal; (b) a gift (Ma.2:13). 3. In NT, the office of an Apostle of Christ, apostleship: (Cremer, 530).

συμ-φέρω [in LXX: (טוֹב), (נָאוֶה), Sir.30:19,] 1. trans. to bring together: with accusative of thing(s). 2. Intrans., and mostly impers., συμφέρει, it is expedient, profitable or an advantage: with inf. (M, Pr., 210), with dative, before ἵνα. Ptcp., ςυμφέρων, profitable: pl., as subst., τὸ σ., profit.
1. incurable, (Plato Philosophus), 2. of persons, incorrigible, (Plato Philosophus); ἀνιάτως ἔχειν to be incurable, (Plato Philosophus)

ἐκ-ριζόω, -ῶ [in LXX: (שֶׁרֶשׁ), (נָתַשׁ), (גָּרַשׁ A, עָקַר BS), (עָקַר), Dan LXX, Wis.4:4, Sir.3:9 Ma.5:51, 2Ma.12:7 *;] to root out, pluck up by the roots: with accusative of thing(s), Ju 12.

depon., [in LXX for שָׁאַג;] of animals, to roar, howl: λέων.

Mid., also frequently in both these senses; (with) to promise: with dab. of person(s), with accusative of thing(s), with dative of person(s) and accusative of thing(s), ἐπαγγελίαν, with inf., before λέγων, ptcp.…

[in LXX for עָנַן, תִּמֹּר,] vapour: ἀ. καπνοῦ, (LXX).

1. a sinew, tendon; in plural, the tendons of the feet, (Iliad by Homer) 2. metaphorically in plural, τὰ νεῦρα τῆς τραγῳδίας, of lyric odes, their sinews, vigour, (Aristophanes Comicus); τὰ νεῦρα τῶν πραγμάτων (Aeschines Orator) 3. gut, cord made of sinew, for fastening the head of the arrow to the shaft…

ἐπι-τιμάω, -ῶ [in LXX for גָּעַר, Sir.11:7,] 1. to honour. 2. to raise in price 3. to mete out due measure; (a) to award; (b) to censure, rebuke, admonish: absol., with dative, Ju 9; before ἵνα, before λέγων, λέγει. SYN.: ἐλέγχω, q.v
όν (αἶσχος, shame, disgrace), [in LXX: ff. (רַע, רֹעַ), Jdth.12:12,] base, shameful.
[in LXX for רָגַל pi.;] a spy.
[in LXX for חָבַשׁ,] to bind up: τ. τραύματα.

ἀπ-έχω [in LXX chiefly for רָחַק;] 1. trans., (a) to hold back, keep off; (b) to have in full, to have received: with accusative, Phm 15; impers., ἀπέχει (Field, Notes, 39), it is enough. 2. Intrans., to be away, distant: absol., before ἀπό. Mid., to abstain: with genitive, before ἀπό.
[in LXX chiefly for עָבַד;] to enslave.
ό (ἐφίστημι), [in LXX: 4, (פָּקִיד), (נָגִיד), 2Ma.5:22,] a chief, commander, master.

συν-βιβάζω (Rec. συμ-), [in LXX: (יָרָה hi.); (יָדַע hi.), (בִּין hi.), Da TH (שָׂכַל hi.) *;] 1. to join or knit together, unite. 2. to compare, consider, conclude (Plat.). 3. to deduce, prove, demonstrate (Arist.). 4. As in LXX ("translation Greek," = ἐμβιβάζω, metaphorically), to teach, instruct: R, mg..
in plural φλιαί, = σταθμοί, the doorposts, jambs, (Odyssey by Homer); in singular, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus)
a staff, cane, (Aristophanes Comicus): borne as a badge of office by the δικασταί, (Demosthenes Orator)
[in LXX for חָמֵץ, שְׂאֹר, *;] leaven: τ. ἄρτου. Metaphorical, of a moral influence or tendency, always, exc. in the Parable of the Leaven, for evil: ζ. τ. Φαρισαίων, (Cremer, 723).
ἐν-άρχομαι [in LXX chiefly for חָלַל hi.;] to begin, make a beginning.
[in LXX for חֲלִי,] disease, sickness: (Aq.). SYN.: see: ἀσθένεια
[in LXX: (אָוֶן), (תְּלוּנָה), Wis.1:10, 11 Sir.46:7 *;] a murmuring, muttering: ἄνευ γ., pl., χωρὶς γ..
1. to throw the head back, in token of denial (which we express by shaking the head), (Homer), 2. with accusative rei, to deny, refuse, (Iliad by Homer)
τό (περιβάλλω), [in LXX chiefly for כְּסוּת, לְבוּשׁ and cognate forms;] that which is thrown around, a covering, in NT, (a) a mantle: " (LXX) (b) a veil.

1. transitive to burn, burn up, (Iliad by Homer):—;Pass. to take fire, blaze up, (Iliad by Homer) 2. metaphorically to kindle, inflame with passion, (Sophocles Tragicus):—;Pass., like Lat. uri, to burn with passion, be inflamed, (Sophocles Tragicus) 3. to light up, Ζεὺς βέλος φλέγων making it blaze or flash, (Aeschulus Tragicus)…
(ὑφαίνω), [in LXX chiefly for חָשַׁב;] woven. ὑφαίνω, [in LXX for אָרַג,] to weave: T, WH, mg.
(ποιέω) [in LXX chiefly for מַעֲשֶׂה and cognate forms;] 1. a making. 2. a doing (Sir.19:18).
[in LXX for חׇכְמָה, מַעֲשֶׂה, עֲבֹדָה;] art, craft, trade: (WH, R, mg., om.).

1. to twine or plait together, (Plato Philosophus); τινί with a thing, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus); συμπλέκοντες τὼ χεῖρε εἰς τοὐπίσω joining their hands behind them, (Thucydides) 2. Pass. to be twined together, entwined, entangled, (Euripides); ἴχνη συμπεπλεγμένα tracks entangled, crossing in different directions…
a garment under a coat of mail, (Plutarch)
το (χρίω), later form of χρῖμα, [in LXX for מִשְׁחָה and cogn. forms;] an anointing, unction: Jn.
[in LXX for מֹר;] myrrh, a resinous gum used as an unguent and for em­balming.

1. to scratch away, lacerate, (Herdotus Historicus) 2. to engrave, inscribe, νόμους (Plutarch) 3. to paint over, (Lucian) 4. to fill tablets with writing (Euripides) 5. to write down, register, record, (Plato Philosophus)

[in LXX for יָדַע hi.,] 1. to manifest, exhibit: ἐαυτόν, with dative of person(s), (DCG, ii, 112b). Pass. and mid., to show oneself, appear. 2. to declare, make known: before ὅτι, with dative of person(s), with accusative of thing(s), before πρός, κατά, with genitive of person(s), περί. SYN.: δηλόω, q.v
(σπείρω), [in LXX chiefly for זֶרַע;] = σπορά, 1. sowing or seedtime. 2. seed sown (so usually in late Gk.): a (LTr.); metaphorically, of almsgiving, b.
1. to stand out or project from, τινός (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. absolute to stand out, appear, (Aristophanes Comicus)
τό [in LXX for רֶגֶל,] the leg from the hip downwards: ?
1. the warp in the ancient upright loom, (Hesiod) 2. a thread, (Batrachomyomachia)

1. the thread which is passed between the threads of the warp στήμων, tela), the woof or weft, Lat. subtemen, (Hesiod), 2. κροκύς, the flock or nap of woollen cloth, cloth with curly nap, (Aristophanes Comicus): in plural, μαλακαῖς κρόκαις with cloths of soft wool, (Pindar); κρόκαισι with flocks of wool, (Sophocles Tragicus)
to purify:—; Mid. to purify oneself by offerings, τοῖς θεοῖς to the gods, (Euripides)
ἐκ-δίδωμι [in LXX for נָתַן,] 1. to surrender, give up, give out. 2. to let out for hire (Hdt.); mid.; to let out to one's advantage.
τό, (in FlJ, also ἡ), indecl. [in LXX: τὸ μάν, ff., elsewhere τ. μάννα, ff., (מָן, Aram. מַנָּא);] manna: symb..
enclosed by walls, beleaguered, besieged, (Herdotus Historicus)

1. to pray to a god, with dative, (Iliad by Homer):—;with accusative to invoke, (Odyssey by Homer) 2. with accusative et infinitive to pray that, (Iliad by Homer):—;with infinitive only, to pray to be so and so, (Odyssey by Homer) 3. to pray something for one, τί τιν; sometimes in good sense, ἀρ. τινι ἀγαθά (Herdotus Historicus)…

1. false accusation, slander, calumny, ἐπὶ διαβολῇ εἰπεῖν (Herdotus Historicus); διαβολὰς ἐνδέχεσθαι to give ear to false accusations, (Herdotus Historicus); ἐμὴ δ. the slanders against me, (Plato Philosophus) 2. a quarrel, enmity, (Thucydides)
a way through, thoroughfare, passage, (Herdotus Historicus), ἄστρων δίοδοι their pathways, (Aeschulus Tragicus); δ. αἰτεῖσθαι, to demand a passport or safe-conduct, (Aristophanes Comicus)
[in LXX for יָרַד:] to cause to go down, cast down: pass., ἕως ᾅδου, (WH, R, mg.), (WH, mg.).

δια-σπορά, -ᾶς, ἡ (διασπείρω), [in LXX of Israelites dispersed and exiled in foreign lands, as (זַעֲוָה) (נָדַח ni.), (נער); by meton., of the exiles themselves (as Ma.1:27);] a dispersion: δ. τῶν Ἑλλήνων, metaphorically, of Christians (DB, iii, 782 f.).

1. delicate, dainty, (Euripides),—; τὸ τρυφερόν effeminacy, ἐς τὸ τρυφερώτερον to more effeminate habits, (Thucydides):—;neuter as adverb, τρυφερόν voluptuously, (Aristophanes Comicus); τρ. λαλεῖν to speak softly, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus)
[in LXX: (קָנָא pi., hi.), (חָרָה hith.), Sir.30:3 *;] to provoke to jealousy: (LXX).
ἀ-νόητος, -ον (ἀ- neg., νοητός; νοέω), [in LXX: (אֱוִיל), Sir.42:8,] 1. not thought on, not understood (Hom., Plat.). 2. not understanding, foolish. SYN.: ἀσύνετος

1. Lat. fall-o (the sigma being lost):—; to make to fall, throw down, overthrow, properly by tripping up, to trip up in wrestling, (Homer), σφ. ναῦς to throw her on her beam-ends, (Plutarch); ἵππος σφ. τὸν ἀναβάτην throws him, (Xenophon Historicus):—;Pass. to be tripped up, (Aristophanes Comicus); of a drunken man, σφαλλόμενος reeling…

to strike down: metaphorically to strike with amazement, astound, terrify, (Thucydides),—;Pass. to be panic-stricken, amazed, astounded, κατεπλήγη (aorist2) (Iliad by Homer); attic aorist2 infinitive, καταπλαγῆναι (Thucydides); 2nd plural perfect καταπέπληχθε (Thucydides); with accusative, καταπλαγέντες τὸν Φίλιππον (Demosthenes Orator)
[in LXX: (כָּבַד), Jol.2:8, Sir.8:15 *;] = καταβαρέω: pass., Pres. ptcp..
[in LXX for רֹמַח,] 1. a spear-head. 2. a lance, spear: ([WH], R, mg.).
ἀνα-κράζω [in LXX for קָרָא,] to cry out, shout.
[in LXX for צָלַח, דָּלַג pi.,] to leap: of water, to spring up.

1. the chariot-board, on which two could stand, the drive ἡνίοχος); and the combatant παραιβάτης); (Homer) 2. the war-chariot itself, (Iliad by Homer):—;in (Odyssey by Homer) a travelling-chariot. 3. a seat, chair, stool, (Homer), attic

1. to hinder or prevent from a thing, τινά τινος (Xenophon Historicus); with infinitive, ἀπ. τινὰ ποιεῖν to prevent from doing, forbid to do, μὴ ποιεῖν τι (Euripides) 2. with accusative only, to keep off, hinder, (Oracle quoted in Herdotus Historicus): —;absolute to stop the way, (Thucydides):—;impersonal…
τό (κηρός, wax), [in LXX for נֹפֶת, צוּף,] honeycomb: κ. μελίσσιον, (Rec.; WH, txt., R, txt., omit).
[in LXX for כּוֹבַע, קוֹבַע;] a helmet: figuratively, with genitive explic., π. τ. σωτηρίου.
(τραῦμα), [in LXX chiefly for חָלַל;] to wound.
[in LXX for נוּם, etc;] to nod in sleep, fall asleep. Metaphorical, of negligence or delay, ἡ ἀπώλεια αὐτῶν οὐ νυστάζει.

(ἄγρυπνος, seeking sleep; ἀγρεύω, ὕπνος), [in LXX chiefly for שׁקד;] to be sleepless, wakeful; metaphorically (LXX) = cl. ἐγρήγορα, to be watchful, vigilant. SYN.: γρηγορέω, which see; νήφω, associated with γ. in, expressing a wariness which results from self-control, a condition of moral, not merely mental alertness.

ἀέρος, ὁ, [in LXX: (= (18):11 שׁחק), Wi.8;] in Hom., Hes., the lower air which surrounds the earth, as opposite to the purer αἰθήρ of the higher regions; generally, air: of the air as the realm of demons, ἀ. δέρειν, of striving to no purpose, εἰς ἀ. λαλεῖν, of speaking without effect, not being understood.
a mina (Let.), mna, in Attic a weight and sum of money = 100 δραχμαί.
(ἐλέφας, ivory), [in LXX for שֵׁן;] of ivory.
to tread together, trample under foot, (Babrius Fabularum Scriptor):—;Pass. to be trampled under foot, (Aeschines Orator)
(κολνμβάω), [in LXX for בְּרֵכָה, 4,] a swimming pool, pool.
ἔπ-αινος, -ου, ὁ [in LXX for תְּהִלָּה,] praise.
(εὐρύς, broad + χώρα), [in LXX for רָחַב ni., and cognate forms, exc. (גֹּרֶן;) spacious, broad.
(χεῖρ), [in LXX for חָשַׁב, גָּמַל,] 1. to pat one's hand to. 2. to take in hand, attempt: with inf..
ου, ὁ, [in LXX for הלל pi, עֹז;] poët, and Ion., 1. = μῦθος, a tale. 2. = Att. ἔπαινος, praise: (LXX). 3. In π., a decree.
τό (ἰάομαι), [in LXX for מַרְפֵּא (,] 1. most frequently in cl., a means of healing, remedy. 2. = ἴασις, a healing (Plat.; Jer, l.with): pl..

1. a saying, speaking, speech, (Odyssey by Homer), ἡ ἀπὸ Σκυθῶν ῥῆσις the Scythian phrase, (Herdotus Historicus) 2. a resolution, declaration, (Herdotus Historicus) 3. a tale, legend, (Pindar) 4. a phrase or passage, a speech in a play, (Aristophanes Comicus)
adv. (ἡδύς, sweet), [in LXX: (עָרַב),] gladly, with pleasure: superlat., ἥδιστα, very gladly (B1., § 11, 3).
πρό-γονος, -ον (προγίνομαι), [in LXX: Sir.8:4,] 1. born before. 2. As subst., in pl., οἱ π., ancestors, forefathers: of living parents (so Plat.).
[in LXX: Jdt.3.2-3, Sir.30:18, Dan LXX Bel Mac.5*;] to lie beside, be near, be present.
[in LXX: Tob.1:7, 1Ma.14:32,] 1. to spend, expend: with accusative, before ἐπί, with dative of person(s), ὑπέρ. 2. to consume, squander: ἐν τ. ἡδσναῖς.
(ὅμιλος), [in LXX: (רָוָה pi.),] to be in company with, consort with; hence, to converse with: with dative, before πρός.
(σπουδή), [in LXX chiefly for בָּהַל;] to make haste; hence, to be zealous or eager, to give diligence: with inf., with accusative and inf..
of or belonging to swine, ὑεία κοιλία pig's tripe, (Aristophanes Comicus):—; θηρίον ὕ., as a type of brutish ignorance, (Plato Philosophus)
[in LXX: (יְהַב), Sir.30:24, al;] (in cl. chiefly poët.) care, anxiety: pl., with genitive obj..

[in LXX: (נָאָה pi.),] 1. to be clearly seen. 2. to resemble. 3. to be fitting or becoming, to suit: with dative, impers., with dative, id. before inf., πρέπον ἐστίν, with dative of person(s) and inf., with accusative and inf..

1. going round, compassing, encircling, (Euripides) 2. as Substantive, περίβολος = περιβολή, ἐχίδνης περίβολοι the spires or coils of a serpent, (Euripides); in plural walls round a town, (Herdotus Historicus); so in singular, (Thucydides) 3. an enclosure, circuit, compass, π. νεωρίων (Euripides); of a temple, the precincts, (Plutarch)
[in LXX: (יָרֵא), Wis.3:19, Sir.3:21,] hard; (a) hard to do or deal with, difficult; (b) hard to bear, painful, grievous: καιροί, (with) of persons, hard to deal with, harsh, fierce, savage.
[in LXX: (הָרַג), (בָּתַק pi.), 2Ma.8:1-36;] to kill off, slay: with accusative.

μετ-εωρίζω (μετέωρος, (a) in mid air; (b) buoyed up; (with) in suspense; Thuc.; in π. opposite to ἀμέριμνος, see Zorell, see word) [in LXX: Ob 4 (גָּבַהּ hi.), (נָשָׂא ni.), (רוּם), 2Ma.5:17 2Mac Ma.6:5 *;] to raise on high. Metaphorical, (a) to buoy up; pass., to be elated, puffed up (b) to be anxious, in suspense.
ά-χρηατος, -ον [in LXX: (חֵפֶץ אַיִן), Wis.2:11, Sir.16:1,] useless; unserviceable: opposite to εὔχρηστος, Phm 11.
τοι-γαρ-οῦν an inferential particle, [in LXX: Sir.41:16,] wherefore then, so therefore.

[in LXX: 2Ma.9:20 2Mac 2Mac 2Mac 2Mac; 3Ma.6:1-41 *;] to strengthen; most frequently in pf., ἔρρωμαι, to put forth strength, be strong, hence, often in imperat., ἔρρωσο, ἔρρωσθε, farewell (Lat. vale): Rec., R, mg.
the fourth day of the month, (Hesiod)

τό (σύν + ἕδρα, a seat) [in LXX: (סוֹד), (מַת), (דִּין) (קָהָל); Ma.14:5, 4Ma.17:17 *;] 1. a council: of a local Jewish tribunal. 2. The supreme ecclesiastical court of the Jews, the Sanhedrin (i.e. Talmudic סַנְהֵדְרִין = συνέδριον): (WH, R, mg., om.) of a meeting of the Sanhedrin, of the place of meeting.

1. to satisfy, delight, gladden, cheer, (Homer), attic:—;absolute to give delight, (Odyssey by Homer); τὰ τέρποντα delights, (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. Pass. and Mid., 3. with genitive rei, to have full enjoyment of a thing, have enough of it, (Homer); metaphorically, τεταρπώμεσθα γόοιο let us take our fill of lamentation, (Homer) 4…
the character of a μεγαλοπρεπής, magnificence, (Herdotus Historicus)
[in LXX: (חֶלְאָה), (חֵמָה),] 1. an arrow. 2. rust (Ez, l.with). 3. poison: figuratively, (Ps. l.with).

[in LXX: (רָשַׁע hi.), La (עָוַת pi.), Wis.2:20,] to pass sentence upon, condemn; in cl., with genitive of person(s) (accusative of thing(s)); in late writers (so LXX), with accusative of person(s) (θανάτῳ, Wis, l.with): absol. (as Plat., Legg., 958c), pass.. δικάζω, to judge.

1. a mist, fog, (not so thick as νέφος or νεφέλη); (Iliad by Homer); κονίης ὀμίχλη a cloud of dust, (Iliad by Homer) 2. metaphorically a mist over the eyes, (Aeschulus Tragicus): darkness, gloom, [variant datesAnthology Palantina
1. thoughtful, intelligent, (Odyssey by Homer) 2. in one's right mind, (Herdotus Historicus)
ἀν-ελεήμων, -ον (-ἀ, ἐλεήμων), [in LXX for אַכְזָר;] without mercy.
[in LXX for בּין, חפז, ידע;] to perceive: withaccusative of thing(s), (Cremer, 619 f.).

1. Radic. sense, to pour: 2. properly of liquids, to pour out, pour, (Homer), Zeus χέει ὕδωρ, i. e. he makes it rain, (Iliad by Homer); χέει χιόνα βορέας (Euripides); absolute, χέει it snows, (Iliad by Homer):—;Mid. to pour for oneself, especially of drink-offerings, χοὰς χεόμην νεκύεσσι (Odyssey by Homer),—;Pass.…
[in LXX: (נָבִיא)*;] a false prophet (= cl. ψευδόμαντις)

[in LXX for אַשָּׁף, Dan LXX TH,] 1. one of the Μάγοι, a Median tribe (Hat). 2. a Magian, one of a sacred caste, originally Median, who seem to have conformed to the Persian religion, while retaining some of their old beliefs: 3. a wizard, sorcerer.
a girdle round the loins, apron, (Plutarch)
τό [in LXX: (29-30) (לֵב),] the breast: as a sign of penitence, τύπτειν (εἰς) τὸ σ.
[in LXX for חַבּוּרָה,] a bruise, wound from a stripe: (LXX).
[in LXX for שׁוּר,] to look around (at). Mid., to look about one (at): absol., with inf., with accusative of person(s), πάντα.
[in LXX chiefly for רָמָה pi.;] 1. to miscalculate. 2. to reason falsely, hence, to mislead.

ἐπι-γαμβρεύω (γαμβρός, a connection by marriage) [in LXX: ff., (חָתַן hithp.), R (יָבַם pi.), 1Ma.10:54-56 *;] 1. to enter into affinity with: with dative (LXX, H. with, exc.). 2. to marry: with accusative.

ἐμ-πορεύομαι depon. (ἔμπορος), [in LXX chiefly for סָחַר;] 1. to travel, esp. for business. 2. to traffc, trade. 3. C. accusative of thing(s) (a) to traffic in; (b) to import: (, for יָבַל hoph.). 4. C. accusative of person(s), to make a gain of.
1. good mother, dame, (Odyssey by Homer) 2. a fostermother, nurse, (Euripides):—;also a true mother, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 3. a midwife, (Plato Philosophus)
(δεσμός), [in LXX for אָסַר, אָלַם pi.,] 1. to put in chains. 2. to bind, tie together: φορτία.
ὑπο-τίθημι [in LXX for שׂוּם,] to place under, lay down. Metaphorical, τ. τράχηλον ὑποθεῖναι, to risk one's life: mid., to suggest.
[in LXX for זְאֵב;] a wolf: figuratively.

1. to send before, send on or forward, (Homer): also, to send something to another, ἀγγελίας, φήμην (Odyssey by Homer):—; (Homer) often with an infinitive added; αἰετὼ προέηκα πέτεσθαι, οὖρον προέηκεν ἀῆναι (Odyssey by Homer) 2. to send away, dismiss, let go, (Iliad by Homer); τήνδε θεῷ πρόες let her go to the god, i. e…

(μέριμνα), [in LXX: (דָּאַג),] 1. to be anxious: absol., μηδὲν μ., with dative of thing(s), before περί, πῶς, εἰς τὴν αὔριον. 2. to care for: with accusative, τὰ τ. κυριου, τὰ τ. κόσμου, τὰ περί ὑμῶν, before ὑπέρ, with genitive (a construction otherwise unknown), ἑαυτῆς.
δι-αγγέλω [in LXX for ספר pi.,] to publish abroad, proclaim: with accusative, " (LXX).
[in LXX for אֵזוֹב;] hyssop, of which a bunch was used in ritual sprinklings: of a branch or rod (?) of hyssop.

κατ-εργάζομαι (emphatic form of ἐργάζομαι), [in LXX for פָּעַל, (9 exx., each for a different Heb. word);] to effect by labour, achieve, work out, bring about: with accusative, pass., with accusative of thing(s) and dative of person(s), id. before διά, with genitive of person(s), τ. σωτηρίαν, with accusative of person(s) before εἰς, (RV…
(φθείρω) [in LXX for שַׁחַת, חֶבֶל,] destruction, corruption, decay: opposite to ζωὴ αἰώνιος, by meton., of that which is subject to corruption, of moral decay.
[in LXX: (עָלָה);] 1. to go up besides. 2. to go up higher.

(ἐλαία), [in LXX for זַיִת;] olive-grove, olive-garden (so in FlJ and in π.; Deiss., BS, 209 ff.; MM, Exp., iii; M, Pr., 49, 69, 235): (where EL, ll with, proposes the conjectural emendation ἐλαιῶν for -ῶνος).

1. one who flees from his country, a runaway, fugitive, a banished man, exile, refugee, Lat. exul, profugus, (Herdotus Historicus), attic; φυγάδα ποιεῖν τινα (Xenophon Historicus); κατάγειν φυγάδας to recall them; 2. of an army, put to flight, (Sophocles Tragicus)

τό (προσκόπτω), [in LXX: (מוֹקֵשׁ), (נֶגֶף), Jdth.8:22, Sir.17:25,] (a) a stumble, stumbling: λίθος προσκόμματος (= נֶגֶף אֶבֶן, Isa, l.with), figuratively, " (LXX); (b) = προσκοπή, an occasion of stumbling, a stumbling-block: metaphorically, (Plut.). SYN.: σκάνδαλον
(χρυσός) [in LXX chiefly for צָפָה pi.;] to gild, cover with gold: pass., with dative, χρυσίῳ.
