(ἀδελφός), [in LXX: 1Ma.12:10,17, 4Mac.5 *;] 1. abstract, brotherhood, brotherly affection (LXX). 2. Concrete, the brotherhood, the Christian community.

(ἁγιάζω), [in LXX: (מִקְדָּשׁ), Sir.7:31,] as an active verbal noun in -μός, it signifies properly the process τὸ ἁγιάζειν, rather than the resultant state, ἁγιωσύνη, hence, 1. consecration; 2. sanctification: so strictly in. Elsewhere it perhaps inclines to the resultant state: (Cremer, 55, 602).

[in LXX: (סֻכָּה), B.l א (יָוֵן), (שָׁמִיר), Wis.11:17, Sir.28:10, 2Ma.2:24, 4Ma.1:29 *;] 1. wood, forest, woodland. 2. wood, timber, fuel. 3. = Lat. materia, esp. in Philosophy, matter (Arist. and later writers; Wis, ll. with).

1. a going or coming to, an approach, ἡ πρ. μάλιστα ταύτῃ ἐγένετο the approach was most feasible on this part, (Herdotus Historicus); ἀπείπατο τὴν πρ. rejected his advances, (Herdotus Historicus); πρ. μελάθρων approach to the halls, (Euripides) 2. an onset, πρόσοδοι τῆς μάχης onsets or attacks, (Euripides) 3. like πομπή II…
[in LXX: (הָלַךְ hi.); (סָבַב hi., ho.); (עָבַר hi), 2Ma.4:38 2Mac *;] 1. to lead about or around: with accusative of person(s). 2. Intrans., to go about: before ἐν, with accusative loc..
καθ-οπλίζω [in LXX: (תָּפַשׂ), Mac.9*;] to arm fully: pass..

[in LXX: (פָּרַד),] 1. trans., to leave, leave behind; pass., to be left behind, to lack before prep. (as more usual in cl.), ἐν, with genitive of thing(s). 2. Intrans., to be gone, to be wanting: with dative of person(s), τὰ λείποντα.
(πλεονέκτης), [in LXX for בֶּצַע;] the character and conduct of a πλεονέκτης. 1. advantage. 2. desire for advantage, grasping, aggression, cupidity, covetousness: pl.. SYN.: φιλαργυρία, avarice

[in LXX (mid.): (חָתַת ni.), (26), Wis.7:14 Ma.5:1, 3Ma.1:19 3Mac *;] 1. prop., to set, place, arrange, fit out; hence, mid., to set oneself for, prepare (Wis, xi Mac, ll. with). 2. to bring together, gather up (in Hom. of furling sails), hence to restrain, check; mid., to restrain or withdraw oneself, hold aloof, avoid: before ἀπό, (cf…

more frequently as depon., -ομαι, and so in LXX and NT (πολίτης), [in LXX: Ma.6:1 2Mac Ma.3:4 3Mac; 4Ma.4:1-26 *;] to be a citizen, live as a citizen: metaphorically, of conduct as based on heavenly citizenship.
ἀν-όσιος, -ον (ἀ- neg., ὅσιος), [in LXX: (זִמָּה, Wis.12:4, 2Ma.7:34 2Mac Ma.2:2 3Mac Ma.12:11 *;] unholy, profane (Cremer, 464).
adv. (πικρός), [in LXX for מַר, מָרַר pi.;] bitterly: metaphorically, ἔκλαυσε π..
τό (στρατός + πέδον, a plain), [in LXX: (חַיִל), 2Ma.8:12,] (a) a military camp; (b) an army.
(οὐδαμός, not even one), adv., [in LXX: 2-4Mac.8*;] in no wise, by no means: (OT).
(ἀσθενής), [in LXX for כָּשַׁל,] weakness, frailty, sickness: ἐν ἀ., pl.. SYN.: μαλακία, νόσος
to burn down, burn up, consume, πυρί (Iliad by Homer),—;Pass. to be burnt down, (Thucydides)
[in LXX: (רִיב hi.), (סוּג ni.), Sir.4:25, 3Ma.2:28, 4Ma.4:7 4Mac *;] cοntradict, oppose, resist; absol.: with dative, with accusative and inf., T; pass..

[in LXX: (עֶוֶל) (אֱוִיל),] slight, worthless, of no account, both of persons and things in various shades of meaning, in NT, as frequently in cl., always with distinct moral reference, worthless, bad: opposite to ἀγαθός. SYN.: see: ἄθεσμος

1. to twine or enfold round:—;Pass. to fold oneself round, with dative, ἱστῷ περιπλεχθείς (Odyssey by Homer); absolute, δίκτυον εὖ μάλα περιπλεκόμενον close folding, (Xenophon Historicus) 2. to complicate, entangle, (Lucian) 3. to wrap up in words, (Aeschines Orator)
manliness, manhood, manly spirit, Lat. virtus, [variant datesTragica Adespota
(ὀρέγομαι), [in LXX Wis.14:2, Sir.18:30 Ma.1:33 4Mac *;] the most general ward for all kinds of desire, longing, appetite: of lust, SYN.: see: πάθος
[in LXX: ὄ. ἐκλεκταί, I2 (בַּרְבֻּר)*;] a bird; specif., a cock, a hen: (WH).
τό [in LXX chiefly for פַּת־בַּג (Da);] the chief meal of the day, dinner, supper: δ. ποιεῖν, κυριακὸν δ., metaphorically (Dalman, Words, 118), δ. τ. γάμου τ. ἀρνίου, δ. τ. μέγα τ. Θεοῦ.

1. to make fat, fatten, (Euripides); π. χθόνα to fatten the soil, of a dead man, (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;Pass. to be or become fat, (Plato Philosophus), 2. metaphorically, 3. to increase, enlarge, πλοῦτον (Pindar) 4. to make wanton, excite, (Aeschulus Tragicus): —;Pass. to wax fat and wanton, (Aeschulus Tragicus)…
to look angry or sullen, be of a sad countenance, (Aristophanes Comicus), from σκυθρωπός
ἐν-τροπή, -ῆς, ἡ [in LXX: (כְּלִמָּה)*;] 1. with genitive of person(s), respect, reverence. 2. Absol., shame.
1. ripeness of fruits, (Aristotle Philosopher) 2. the bloom of youth, (Xenophon Historicus)
[in LXX for מוֹט,] in poets and late prose, a tossing, as of an earthquake; esp. the tossing, the rolling swell of the sea.

1. anything set upright: 2. a ship's mast, ἱστὸν στῆσαι or στήσασθαι to step the mast, (Homer):—; a rod, pole, (Herdotus Historicus) 3. the beam of the loom, which stood upright, instead of lying horizontal as in our looms, (Homer); ἱστὸν στήσασθαι to set up the beam and so begin a web, (Hesiod); ἱστὸν ἐποίχεσθαι to traverse the loom…

(μετανοέω), [in LXX: Wis.11:23, Sir.44:16 *;] after-thought, change of mind, repentance: of repentance from sin, βάπτισμα μετανοίας, ἡ εἰς θεὸν; μ. ἀπὸ νεκρῶν ἔργων, εἰς μ. καλεῖν, id. ἄγειν, ἀνακαινίζειν, εἰς μ. χωρῆσαι, μ. δοῦναι.
1. an adulteress, (New Testament):as adjective adulterous, (New Testament) 2. as Substantive = μοιχεία, (New Testament)

1. to fear, absolute, (Homer), followed by a preposition, δ. περί τινι to be alarmed, anxious about.., (Iliad by Homer), attic; ἀμφί τινι, περί τινος, ὑπέρ τινος (Iliad by Homer):—;followed by a relative clause with μή.., Lat. vereor ne.., I fear it is.., followed by subjunctive; rarely by indicative…
[in LXX: א (סוּפָה), (סַעַר), Wis.5:14, 23, Sir.48:9, 12 *;] a hurricane, whirlwind. SYN.: θύελλα, which see, and cf. ἄνεμος
1. feathered, (Herdotus Historicus), 2. winged, (Herdotus Historicus) 3. πτερωτοί (i.e. ὄρνιθες); feathered fowl, birds, (Euripides)
ἐμ-φυσάω, -ῶ (φυσάω, to blow), [in LXX for נָפַח,] to breathe into, breathe upon.
(T, Rec. Φαλέκ, L, mg., Φάλεγ), ὁ indecl. (Heb. D, Ge 1116), Peleg.

1. to be gone away, to be far from, with genitive, (Iliad by Homer), attic 2. absolute to be gone, to have departed, to be absent, (Odyssey by Homer): hence, to be gone, to have perished, ἀποίχεται χάρις (Euripides): of persons, to be dead and gone, (Pindar)
with the face towards, facing, τινι (Xenophon Historicus): face to face, (Xenophon Historicus)
περι-καθ-ίζω [in LXX for חָנָה, לָחַם ni.,] 1. to invest, besiege. 2. to sit around: L, txt.

particle of affirmation, yea, verily, even so; in answer to a question: before λέγω ὑμῖν, repeated for emphasis, ναὶ ναί (opposite to oὒ oὔ): ἤτω ὑμῶν τὸ ναὶ ναί, ν. καὶ οὔ, ἵνα ᾖ... τὸ ναὶ ναί, τὸ ν., in assent to an assertion: in confirmation of a previous assertion: Phm 20; in solemn asseveration.
[in LXX for רוּץ;] to run to.
[in LXX: (רָאָה ni.), Tob.12:19 *;] late present as from ὤφθην (= ὁράω); mid., ὀπτάνομαι, to allow oneself to be seen, to appear. with dative.
(θεοσεβής), [in LXX (אֱלֹהִים יִרְאָה), (אֲדֹנָי id.), Sir.1:24, Bar.5:4, 4Ma.7:6 4Mac, א 4Ma.15:28 א 4Ma.17:15 *;] fear of God, godliness.
1. the silver fir, pinus picea, (Iliad by Homer) 2. an oar, (Homer): also a ship or boat, like Lat. abies, (Euripides)

(δοκιμή), [in LXX: ἀργύριον δ. (עֲלִיל), and as seel. for δόκιμος (B), ἀργυρίου δ. (זָקַק pual.), (Bab); εἰ δ.ίστιν (יְקָר), א with a vid, Q *)*;] = δόκιμος, tested, approved: τὸ δ. ὑμῶν τ. πίστεως, that which is approved in your faith, (where Hort suggests the seel. δόκιμος, found in some cursives), (but see Mayor…
(ἄντλος, bilge-water in a hold), [in LXX for שָׁאַב,] 1. prop., to bale out. 2. Generally, to draw water: absol., ὕδωρ.
(δράσσομαι), [in LXX: in Hex. for in בֶּקַע, שֶׁקֶל Ezra for אֲדַרְכֹּן, דַּרְכְּמוֹן;] a drachma, nearly equal to the Roman denarius: (DCG, ii, 200).

1. afternoon, ἔσσεται ἢ ἠὼς ἢ δείλη ἢ μέσον ἦμαρ (Iliad by Homer); divided into early and late ( πρωί̈α and ὀψία), περὶ δείλην πρωί̈ην, or δείλης ὀψίης (Herdotus Historicus); τῆς δείλης in the course of the afternoon, (Xenophon Historicus) 2. the late afternoon, evening, (Xenophon Historicus)
(ἔρις), [in LXX for מָרָה,] to wrangle, strive: (LXX, κεκράζεται).
ἀπο-δεκατοω, [in LXX for עָשַׂר in both senses foll., e.g. (1) (2);] 1. with accusative of thing(s), to tithe, pay a tenth of. 2. C. accusative of person(s), to exact tithes from. 3. to decimate.

1. the good which man obtains τυγχάνει); by the favour of the gods, good fortune, luck, success, (Theognis Elegiacus), σὺν τύχῃ (Sophocles Tragicus); θείᾳ τύχῃ, Lat. divinitus, (Herdotus Historicus),—; hence Τύχη was deified, like Lat. Fortuna, Τύχη Σώτειρα (Pindar); T. Σωτήρ (Aeschulus Tragicus) 2. generally, fortune, chance…

1. Dep. 2. to take omens from the flight and cries of birds, Lat. augurium, capere, (Xenophon Historicus) 3. generally, to divine from omens, augur, with accusative et infinitive, (Xenophon Historicus)
(on the spelling μείγ-, ν. B)., § 3, 5) [in LXX for עָרַב hith.,] to mix, mingle: with accusative and dative, with accusative before ἐν, before μετά. SYN.: κεράννυμι, q.v

(σῆμα, a mark), [in LXX: (קָשַׁר), Ma.11:37 1Mac Ma.15:36, 3Ma.6:1 *;] 1. bearing a mark; of money, stamped, coined. 2. Metaphorical, (a) in good sense, notable, illustrious: (b) in bad sense, notorious.
adv. (βαρύς), [in LXX: β. φέρειν, (חרה בעיני); β. ἀκούειν, (כּבד hi.)*;] heavily, with difficulty: " (LXX).
adv., [in LXX: (בֶּטַח), Tob.6:4, Wis.18:6, Bar.5:7, 1Ma.6:40, 3Ma.7:6 *;] (a) safely: (b) assuredly.

1. to set straight: 2. in height, to set upright, set up one fallen or lying down, raise up, (Iliad by Homer); ὀρθοῦν κάρα, πρόσωπον (Euripides):—;of buildings, to raise up, rebuild, or, generally, to erect, build up, (Euripides):—;Pass. to be set upright, (Iliad by Homer), simply to rise from one's seat, stand up…
πάρ-οδος, -ου, ἡ [in LXX: (דֶּרֶךְ),] a passing or passage: ἐν π., in passing.

1. the hollow bottom or stand of a cup, Lat. fundus, (Iliad by Homer), 2. of the sea, the bottom, depth, (Hesiod), 3. the bottom or foundation of a thing, in plural, χθόνα ἐκ πυθμένων κραδαίνειν (Aeschulus Tragicus); ἐκ π. ἔκλινε κλῇθρα (Sophocles Tragicus); δίκας π. the anvil-stand on which is forged the sword of retribution…

1. to produce again, to let grow, πώγωνα (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) 2. Pass., with aorist2 active ἀν-έφυν, pf. ἀμ-πέφυ_κα, to grow up, (Herdotus Historicus), 3. to grow again, of the hair, (Herdotus Historicus)
τό (ἀγνοέω), [in LXX: (מִשְׁגֶּה), Tob.3:3, Jdth.5:20, Sir.23:2 Ma.13:39 *;] a sin of ignorance.
1. to boil out or over, break out, of curses, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 2. with genitive, εὐλέων ἐξέζεσε boiled over with worms, i. e. bred worms, (Herdotus Historicus)
(ἄστυ, a city), [in LXX: (טוֹב), (οὐκ ἀ. יָרַט), (בָּרִיא), Jdth.11:23, Dan LXX, Sus Ma.6:23 *;] 1. of the town. 2. (Like Lat. urbanus), (a) courteous, (b) elegant, comely, fair (as in Ex, l.with).
the tail of a beast, (Aristophanes Comicus)
ἄ-λογος, -ον [in LXX: (שָׂפָה עָרֵל), (נָפַל), Wis.11:15-16, 4Ma.3:1-21 *;] 1. without reason, irrational: ζῷα, Ju 10. 2. contrary to reason.
(φλόξ), [in LXX: (לָקַח hith.), (לָהַט pi.), Da TH (94) (חָרַךְ ithp.), Sir.3:30, 1Ma.3:5 *;] to set on fire, burn, burn up: figuratively.
(ὀψέ), [in LXX: (3), Jol.2:23, (מַלְקוֹשׁ), (אָפִיל)*;] poët. and late for ὄψιος, late: ὑετὸς ὄ., the latter rain, with ellipsis of ὑετός, Ja 57.
feminine of θεράπων, a waiting maid, handmaid, (Herdotus Historicus)
[in LXX for רֵחֶה,] 1. = μύλη, a mill (Strab., Plut., LXX). 2. a mill-stone (Anth.): (T); μ. ὀνικός.

1. to mix together, commingle, (Homeric Hymns); to mix one thing with another, τί τινι (Herdotus Historicus), attic; with accusative only, συμμίξαντες τὰ στρατόπεδα having combined them, (Herdotus Historicus):—;Pass., of a river, to be mingled with another river, with dative, (Iliad by Homer): to join forces, of two armies…
συν-δέω [in LXX for שָׁבַץ,] (a) to bind together; (b) to bind together with: pass..
a bird which migrates with the quails, perhaps the land-rail, ludicrously applied to Latona, the Ortygian mother (compare Ὀρτυγία)), (Aristophanes Comicus)

(μέτρον), [in LXX: (מָדַד), Da Th (מָדַד), Wis.4:8 *;] 1. to measure, of space, number, value, with accusative of thing(s), with dative instr.. Metaphorical, ἑαυτὸν ἐν ἑαυτῷ. 2. to measure out, give by measure: prov., ἐν ὧ μέτρῳ κ.τ.λ..
[in LXX: (יָרָה),] to strike down with an arrow, shoot dead: (LXX) (Rec.; WH, R, om.).

(ζηλόω), [in LXX for קַנָּא (θεὸς ζ.), קַנּוֹא, Nam.1:2 (θεός); pl., I; ζ. τῶν νόμων, 2Ma.4:2;τὸν ζ. Φινεές, 4Ma.18:12 *;] 1. in cl. an emulator, zealous admirer. 2. eagerly desirous, zealous; (a) absol., as in OT, ll. with; (b) with genitive obj.: (zealous to acquire or to defend), τ. νόμου (2Mac, l.with), παραδόσεων…
τό (κριτής), [in LXX: (מִשְׁפָּט), Dan LXX TH, (דִּין), Su, *;] 1. a means of judging, test, criterion. 2. a tribunal.
ζημόω, -ῶ (ζημία), [in LXX chiefly for עָנַשׁ;] to damage. Pass., to suffer loss, forfeit, lose: absol., before ἐν, with accusative of thing(s), τ. ψυχήν, ἑαυτόν, τ. πάντα.

[in LXX for אמר, with dative, (קָרָא אֶל), Wis.12:12, Sir.46:19;] 1. to call in, demand. 2. to bring a charge against, accuse: with dative of person(s) (as in cl.), before κατά, with genitive of person(s). Pass., to be accused: with genitive of thing(s); στάσεως, ὦν (perh. by attraction = ἅ), before περί, with genitive of thing(s)…

ὑπο-στέλλω [in LXX: (גּוּר), (נָשָׂא פָּנִים), (עָפַל pu.), (כָּלָא), Wis.6:7, 3Ma.5:28 *;] 1. to draw in, let down. 2. to draw back, withdraw: ἑαυτόν. Mid., to shrink or draw back: (LXX); before τοῦ, with inf., οὐδέν.
[in LXX: (יָסַף hi.), Sir.11:5,] frequent. of φέρω, denoting repeated or habitual action, most commonly used of clothing, weapons, to bear constantly, wear.
the wind that comes from the rising sun, the east wind, Lat. subsolanus, (Herdotus Historicus)

a bell, (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;in fortified towns an officer went round at night with a bell to challenge the sentries, and see that they were awake, (Thucydides); ὡς κώδωνα ἐξαψάμενος like one with an alarm-bell in his hand, (Demosthenes Orator)
1. a leaf, mostly in plural, (Homer):—; poetry, νεικέων πέταλα contentious votes (compare πεταλισμός); (Pindar) 2. a leaf of metal, (Lucian)

1. to fasten from, i. e. to, a thing, with genitive, (Homer); τι ἔκ τινος (Herdotus Historicus) 2. metaphorically, ἐξ. στόματος λιτάς to let prayers fall from one's mouth, (Euripides) 3. ἐξ. τί τινι to place upon, (Euripides) 4. Mid. to hang on, (Iliad by Homer) 5. to hang a thing to oneself, carry it about one, wear, (Euripides)
[in LXX for עֲבֹדָה, שָׁרַת; ἔργα, Num_7:5; στολαί; σκευή, *;] of or for service, ministering: πνεύματα.
[in LXX for חוֹר, חֲגָו,] an opening, a hole.
τό (κλάω), [in LXX for פַּת, פֶּלַח;] a broken piece, fragment

1. to bear fruit or bear as fruit, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 2. Mid. to get fruit for oneself, i. e., 3. to reap crops from land, (Herdotus Historicus): metaphorically to exhaust or drain, τὴν Ἑλλάδα (Aristophanes Comicus) 4. to enjoy the interest of money, (Demosthenes Orator); so in perfect passive…
adv. (= Hom., κατένωπα), [in LXX:] over against, before: with genitive, τ. δόξης, Ju 24; metaphorically, τ. θεοῦ.
ὑός, ὁ, ἡ [in LXX for חֲזִיר;] swine: fem. (sow)
[in LXX chiefly for שָׁאַג, also for נָבַע,] 1. to spit or spue out. 2. Prop., of oxen (Hom.), to bellow, roar; whence, as in LXX, to speak aloud, utter: (LXX).
a vulture, (Iliad by Homer); compare αἰγυπιός.
α, -ον [in LXX: (עֶלְיוֹן), (מַעַל), Tob.8:3 *;] only in neut., as adv., (a) of motion, higher: (b) of rest, above, before.
1. far-shining, far-beaming, (Homeric Hymns) 2. of distant objects, far-seen, conspicuous, (Theognis Elegiacus) 3. adverb -γῶς, clearly, distinctly, (New Testament)
to besprinkle all round, especially in sacred rites:—;Mid. to purify oneself, (Theophrastus Philosophus)
-ον, and -η, -ον, [in LXX, (סָפִיחַ), Wis.17:6 *;] 1. of persons, acting of one's own will. 2. Of inanimate things and natural agencies, of itself, of its own accord: γῆ; πύλη.
1. to cut in pieces, (Lucian) 2. to distribute, (Xenophon Historicus)
(also -ος, -ον), [in LXX: A, (שָׂכִיר), Tob.5:11, Sir.7:10 *;] hired; as subst., ὁ μ., a hired servant: (Anth., Plut.).
ἐν-περι-πατέω, -ῶ [in LXX: (הָלַךְ hithp.), Wis.19:21;] to walk about in or among: before ἐν., dative of person(s), (LXX)
[in LXX: (רָדַף),] to run down: before ἐπί, with accusative of person(s).
[in LXX: (לַח), (חָדָשׁ), (זוּר), Sir.9:10 *;] 1. originally, freshly slain. 2. Generally (from Æsch. on), new, fresh, recent: ὁδός.
(> ἁγνίζω), [in LXX: (נֵזֶר) (חַטָּאָה),] purification: in ceremonial sense, (LXX).

a rasor, (Homer),—;proverb, ἐπὶ ξυροῦ ἵσταται ἀκμῆς ὄλεθρος ἠὲ βιῶναι death or life is balanced on a rasor's edge, (Iliad by Homer); ἐπὶ ξυροῦ τῆς ἀκμῆς ἔχεται ἡμῖν τὰ πράγματα (Herdotus Historicus); βεβὼς ἐπὶ ξυρῷ τύχης (Sophocles Tragicus)

[in LXX: B (עֲבֹדָה צָבָא), (פָּעַל), (גָּמַל), I, Wis.15:11 *;]; 1. intrans., to be at work or in action, to operate (opposite to ἀργέω): before ἐν, with dative of person(s), with dative of person(s), before εἰς (Lft., in l). 2. Trans., to work, effect, do: with accusative of thing(s), id, before ἐν, with dative of person(s), ἐ…
1. an earthen pot, a pot for boiling, pipkin, Lat. olla, (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. χύτραι, pots of pulse offered to inferior deities, (Aristophanes Comicus)

1. a furrow made in ploughing, Lat. sulcus, (Homer), αὔλακ᾽ ἐλαύνειν to draw a furrow, (Hesiod) 2. metaphorically of a wife as the bearer of children, (Sophocles Tragicus) 3. metaphorically also, a furrow in the skin, a gash, wound, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 4. = ὄγμος, a swathe, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (Prob. from same Root as ὁλκός…

(πανοῦργος), [in LXX: (עׇרְמָה), Sir.19:25 (Sir.34:10) (in all cases in good or indifferent sense)*;] cleverness, in cl. nearly always in bad sense, craftiness, cunning, knavery: (LXX, φρόνησις, for עׇרְמָה).
(ζωός, alive, + ἀγρεύω) [in LXX chiefly for חָיָה hi.;] to catch alive, take captive: metaphorically, pass..
anything twisted up together: a body of men, a crowd, concourse, (Polybius Historicus) from συστρέφω

1. to frighten, scare, alarm, Lat. terrere, (Iliad by Homer) 2. intransitive to crouch or cower down for fear (compare πτώσσω), properly of animals, (Sophocles Tragicus); of men, (Pindar), attic; πτ. βωμὸν ὕπο (Euripides); also with accusative loci, πτ. βωμόν to flee cowering to the altar, (Euripides) 3…
1. a bee, Lat. apis, (Homer), 2. one of the priestesses of Delphi, (Pindar) 3. = μέλι, honey, (Sophocles Tragicus)

τό (βαίνω), [in LXX: (מִדְרָךְ), (מִגְדָּל), I, Sir.19:30 Ma.13:26 *;] 1. a step, stride, pace. 2. a raised place, a platform reached by steps, originally that in the Pnyx at Athens from which orations were made; frequently of the tribune or tribunal of a Roman magistrate or ruler: β. τοῦ θεοῦ, τ. Χριστοῦ.
[in LXX for גַּרְזֶן, קַרְדֹּם;] an axe.
[in LXX: (רֶכֶס),] rough: ὁδοί (Is, l.with), (LXX); τοποί (i.e. rocky).

1. to make to live with, (Isocrates Orator); ς. τινὶ τὴν θυγατέρα to give him one's daughter in marriage, (Herdotus Historicus) 2. to combine in one city, unite under a capital or metropolis, ξ. πάντας (i.e. ἐς τὰς Ἀθήνας)) (Thucydides):—;Pass., ξυνοικισθείσης πόλεως the city having been regularly formed…
τό, [in LXX for כְּלִי, כְּלוּב;] a vessel.
[in LXX for אמר hi., בּחר,] to take; Mid., -ομαι, to choose. (Cf. ἀν-, ἀφ-, δι-, ἐξ-, καθ-, περι-, προ-αιρέω.)

1. dust, a cloud of dust, stirred up by men's feet, (Iliad by Homer); also in plural, like Lat. arenae, (Homer), 2. sand or soil; (Iliad by Homer) 3. ashes, in plural like Lat. cineres, (Odyssey by Homer) 4. a fine powder, sprinkled over wrestlers' bodies after being oiled…
the part between the knee and ankle, the leg, Lat. tibia, (Homer)
1. abandonment, τῶν νεῶν (Herdotus Historicus) 2. (from intransitive) of sun or moon, an eclipse, (Thucydides)
Substantive and adjective, (Sophocles Tragicus), a grass that mules fed on.
(παχύς, thick) [in LXX: (שָׁמֵן),] to thicken, fatten; pass., to grow fat. Metaphorical, to make dull or stupid (τ. ψυχάς, Rut.); pass., to wax gross: ἡ καρδία„, " (LXX).

1. a half-boot, (Xenophon Historicus):—; κρηπῖδες soldiers' boots, i. e. soldiers themselves, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) 2. generally, a groundwork, foundation, basement of a temple or altar, (Herdotus Historicus),—;metaphorically, κρηπὶς σοφῶν ἐπέων (Pindar); οὐδέπω κρηπὶς κακῶν ὕπεστι we have not yet got to the bottom of misery…
fit for battle, warlike, (Herdotus Historicus), attic; οἱ μ. the fighting men, soldiery, and in Egypt the warrior-caste, (Herdotus Historicus); τὸ μ. the effective force, (Thucydides)

1. the neck, throat, of men and beasts, (Homer), 2. metaphorically any narrow passage, a neck of land, isthmus, (Herdotus Historicus) 3. a narrow sea, strait, (Herdotus Historicus); of the point at which the Danube spreads into several branches, (Herdotus Historicus) 4. a narrow mountain-pass, defile, (Herdotus Historicus)
ἐγ-κρύπτω, [in LXX for טמן,] to conceal in: with accusative, before εἰς.
[in LXX for שׁוּעָל;] a fox: metaphorically, of Herod.
(σκότος), [in LXX for חָשַׁךְ, קָדַר, שָׁחַר;] to darken. Metaphorical, of the mind! pass..

1. to push back, stop short, check, ἵππον χαλινῶι (Xenophon Historicus) 2. Mid., ἀνακρούεσθαι πρύμνην to put one's ship astern, by backing water, (Aristophanes Comicus); so ἀνακρούεσθαι alone, (Thucydides); also, ἐπὶ πρύμνην ἀν., (Herdotus Historicus):—;metaphorically to put back, (Plato Philosophus) 3. in Music, to strike up…

1. to put the feet in bonds, to fetter, (Herdotus Historicus): —;Pass., ἐμπεποδισμένος τοὺς πόδας (Herdotus Historicus) 2. generally, to hinder, thwart, impede, Lat. impedire, τινά (Aristophanes Comicus); πρός τι in a thing, (Isocrates Orator):—;Pass., (Sophocles Tragicus) 3…
the small grapes left for gleaners, [variant datesAnthology Palantina: hence, (Aristophanes Comicus) calls poetasters ἐπιφυλλίδες, mere gleanings.
συν-στέλλω (Rec. συσ-), [in LXX: (כָּנַע ni.), Sir.4:31,] 1. to draw together, contract, shorten: of time. 2. to wrap up: of enshrouding a body for burial (Eur.), with accusative.
see: Ἰωβήδ. Ἰωβήδ (WH, -βήλ, Lk, l.with; Rec., RV, Ὠβήδ), ὁ, indecl., Jo bed (Obed).
προ-βάλλω [in LXX for חוּד, מָרַק,] 1. to throw before. 2. to put forward: with accusative, of trees, to put forth, produce (sc. φύλλα).
[in LXX for צמח,] 1. to sprout. 2. In late Gk., causal, to make to grow, produce: with accusative.

τό (ὑστερέω), [in LXX: (מַחְסוֹר), (חֶסְרוֹן), (ὑ. εἶναι, חֲשַׁח) *;] (a) that which is lacking, deficiency, shortcoming: with genitive puss., with genitive of thing(s), (b) need, want, poverty: opposite to περίσσευμα, (eccl.).

γνωστός, -ή, -όν, later form of γνωστός (γιγνώσκω), [in LXX for various parts of ידע;] known: with dative, (Rec.), γ. σημεῖον, a notable (EV) sign, one that is matter of knowledge, γνωστὸν, τὸ γνωστὸν θεοῦ, in pl., as subst., γνωστοί, acquaintances, so in sing., (WH).

(περισσός), [in LXX: (מַרְבִּית), (יָתַר ni., יוׄתֵר), Tob.4:16, Sir.10:27, Sir (Sir.33:29), 1Ma.3:30 *;] I. Prop., intrans., 1. of things, to be over and above the number (Hes.), hence, (a) to be or remain over: (b) to abound, be in abundance. 2. Of persons, (a) to abound in, have in abundance: with genitive, T…
to portion out:—;Mid. to receive as one's portion, (Plutarch)
τό (μετά + ὤψ, an eye), [in LXX for מֵצַח;] the forehead.
(μάταιος), [in LXX: 4, הָבַל,] to make vain, foolish.
ἀνα-βάλλω [in LXX: (עָבַר), (עָטָה);] to defer, put off: mid..

1. well-looking, goodly, comely, of outward appearance, (Herdotus Historicus), attic; εὐπρ. ἰδεῖν fair to look on, (Xenophon Historicus); εἶδος εὐπρεπής (Euripides) 2. decent, seemly, fitting, becoming, (Herdotus Historicus); τελευτὴ εὐπρεπεστάτη a most glorious end, (Thucydides) 3. specious, plausible, (Herdotus Historicus)…

1. to shoot with the bow, τινός at a mark, (Iliad by Homer); εἴς τινα (Herdotus Historicus):—;metaphorically to aim at, with genitive, (Euripides):—;absolute to use the bow, (Herdotus Historicus), καθ᾽ ὑπερβολὰν τοξεύσας having shot too high, (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. with accusative to shoot or hit with an arrow, τινά (Euripides):—;Pass…
(ὕβρις), [in LXX for גֵּאֶה,] 1. intrans., to wax wanton, run riot. 2. Trans., to outrage, insult, treat insolently: with accusative of person(s).
born or descended from, Lat. oriundus, (Herdotus Historicus): in plural descendants, (Herdotus Historicus); ἀπόγονοι τεαί thy offspring, (Sophocles Tragicus)
τό [in LXX: (לֶחֶם), Tob.2:1, 4,] 1 1, prop., breakfast. 2. In late Gk. = cl. δεῖτνον, dinner.
(Rec. -εία, as in cl.), -ας, ἡ (πραγματεύομαι) [in LXX for חֲשַׁל,] 1. careful application, hard work. 2. business, occupation: pl..
[in LXX for שִׁקְמָה (pl.);] the mulberry tree, the sycamine. (In LXX, σ. appears to represent the συκόμορος, but St. Luke distinguishes between the two; see ICC, in l; DB, iv, 634.)
ἀπ-εῖπον, 2 aor. without present in use [in LXX for מָאַס, אָמַר,] 1. to tell out. 2. to forbid. 3. to renounce: 1 aor. mid..

1. initiation in the mysteries, (Herdotus Historicus), ἐς χεῖρας ἄγεσθαι τὴν τελετήν to take in hand the matter of initiation, (Herdotus Historicus):—;in plural mystic rites at initiation, (Euripides), 2. a festival accompanied by such rites, in plural, (Pindar); in singular, (Euripides)

(χρῆμα), [in LXX: A (דָבַר pi.),) (שָׁאַג), *;] 1. to transact business, hence, to consult, deliberate; hence in later writers, 2. to make answer; of an answer by an oracle; in FlJ, LXX and NT, of divine communications, to instruct, admonish, warn: pass., with inf., 3. to assume a name (as in business), be called.
acting in folly; for no cause

(κοινός), [in LXX: (חָבֵר), (חֲבֶרֶת),] 1. as adj., = κοινός. 2. As subst., ὁ, ἡ κ., (a) a partner, associate, companion: Phm 17; with dative of person(s), with genitive of person(s), id. before ἐν, (b) a partaker, sharer: with genitive of thing(s).
[in LXX chiefly for מֶתֶג;] a bridle.
ἀπο-φθέγγομαι [in LXX for נָבָא,] to speak forth, give utterance.
τό (dimin. of χώρα, χῶρος), [in LXX: (כֶּרֶם), 2Ma.11:5 2Mac 2Mac Ma.15:20 *;] 1. a place, region. 2. an estate, property, piece of land.

1. one who stands before, a front-rank-man, (Xenophon Historicus) 2. a chief, leader of a party, (Herdotus Historicus); ὁ πρ. τοῦ δήμου (Thucydides) 3. generally, a president, ruler, (Aeschulus Tragicus), προστάται τῆς εἰρήνης its chief authors, (Xenophon Historicus) 4. one who stands before, a protector, guard, champion…
[in LXX: (נָדִיב), (חוּשׁ),] willing, ready: neut., τὸ π. = ἡ προθυμία, οὕτως τὸ κατ᾽ ἐμὲ (= cl. τὸ ἐμὸν) π..
(παρά, θάλασσα) [in LXX: (יָם חוֹף),] by the sea.
1. destruction, death, (Euripides) 2. metaphorically confusion, φρενῶν (Aeschulus Tragicus)
(θέλω) [in LXX: (רָצוֹן), (חֵפֶץ), LXX (צְבִי), Tob.12:18, Wis.16:25, 2Ma.12:16, 3Ma.2:26 *;] in colloq. and MGr. = τὸ θέλειν, will.

[in LXX; (רָאָה), Tob.2:2, Jdth.15:8, 2Ma.2:4 2Mac Ma.5:47 *;] to behold, look upon, contemplate, view (in early writers with a sense of wondering), in NT apparently always in literal, physical sense of "careful and deliberate vision which interprets... its object": with accusative of thing(s), with accusative of person(s), with ptcp.…
[in LXX: (יָשָׁר לֵבָב), Tob.7:8,] eagerly, readily, with a ready mind.
δια-δέχομαι [in LXX for מִשְׁנֶה (Deiss., BS, 115), פַּרְבָּר;] to receive through another, receive in turn.
to cover, (Xenophon Historicus): metaphorically, ὕπνος στ. τινά covers, embraces one, (Sophocles Tragicus):—;Pass., πλοῖον ἐστεγασμένον a decked vessel, (Antipho Orator)

ἐπ-αγγελία, -ας, ἡ (ἐπαγγέλλω), [in LXX: (סֵפֶר),] 1. a summons. 2. a promise: esp. in NT of the divine promises, with inf., γίνεται, with dative of person(s), before πρός, έπαγγέλεσθαι τὴν ἐ., ἔχειν ἐπαγγελίας, εἷναι νἐ έπαγγελίᾳ, ἡ γῆ τῆς ἐ., τὰ τέκνα τῆς ἐ., τ. πνεῦμα τῆς ἐ. τ. ἅγιον, αἱ διαθῆκαι τῆς ἐ., ἡ ἐ. τ. θεοῦ, pl., αἱ ἐ. τ…

1. to send off in different directions, send to and fro, send about or round, (Herdotus Historicus) 2. to send over or across, (Aristophanes Comicus): to transmit, ἐπιστολήν (Thucydides); so in Mid., (Thucydides)
1. a besieging, siege, (Herdotus Historicus), 2. metaphorically a besieging, pestering, (Plutarch)
(a Persian word), [in LXX for גִּנְזִין, II, גִּזְבָּר, II; *;] treasure.
to place or post in:—;Pass., σφενδονᾶν ἐντεταγμένος posted to use the sling, (Xenophon Historicus)
[in LXX: (נָפַל),] to fall down: before εἰς, ἐπί with accusative.

(derivation unknown), [in LXX for נַעַר, שָׁרַת pi.: א B, Ma.9:17 *;] 1. in general, a servant, attendant, minister: δ. θεοῦ, δ. Χριστοῦ, cf. ὁ δ. ὁ ἐμός, δ. περιτομῆς, δ. καινῆς διαθήκης, δ. δικαιοσύνης, δ. [εὐαγγελίου], δ. [ἐκκλησίας]. 2. As technical term for Church officer, a deacon: fem.. SYN.: δοῦλος, bondman; θεράπων…

[in LXX: (לָקַח), (לֵב מָלֵא) Jdth.14:13, 2Ma.4:2, 3Ma.3:21 R, 4Ma.8:18 *;] to have courage, to venture, dare, be bold: absol, before ἐπί, with inf., Ju 9; to submit to (in cl. usually absol. in this sense), τολμήσας εἰσῆλθεν, took courage and went in.
(ἄγω), [in LXX: Ma.4:16 Ma.4:10 *;] 1. a carrying away. 2. a leading, guiding; metaphorically, training; hence, from the expression ἀ. τοῦ βίου, absol., conduct, way of life.

παρ-ακούω [in LXX: (עָבַר, עָשָׂה, with neg.) (חָרַשׁ hi.), (שָׁמַע, with neg.), I, Tob.3:4 *;] 1. to overhear. 2. to hear amiss or imperfectly. 3. Later, to hear without heeding, take no heed: with genitive.

a proposition carried by vote: especially a measure passed in the ἐκκλησία, a decree, (Aristophanes Comicus); τὸ Μεγαρέων ψ. the decree concerning them, (Thucydides); so, περὶ Μεγαρέων ψ. (Thucydides); ψ. γράφειν to bring in a decree, (Aristophanes Comicus); ψ. ἐπιψηφίζειν, of the πρόεδροι, to put it to the vote, (Aeschines Orator); ψ…
1. to besprinkle or bespatter, (Aristophanes Comicus):—;Pass., καταπαττόμενος (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. with accusative rei, to sprinkle or strew over, (Aristophanes Comicus)

or στρώννυμι, [in LXX for יַצַע hoph.,] to spread: ἱμάτια ἐν τ. ὁδῷ (εἰς τ. ὁδόν), of making a bed, στρῶσον (sc. τ. κλίνην) σεαυτῷ, of furnishing a room, ἐστρωμένον, spread with carpets or carpeted couches.
(ἁρπάζω), [in LXX (as also ἅρπαγμα) for גָּזֵל,] pillage, plundering, robbery.
1. to light up, (Odyssey by Homer),—;Mid. to light oneself a fire, (Herdotus Historicus) 2. Pass., metaphorically to fire up, with anger, (Herdotus Historicus)
διό-περ conjunct., [in LXX: Jdth.8:17; Jdt.8.1-36; 2Ma.5:1-27 *;] for which very reason.

1. to be ashamed to do a thing, with infinitive, (Homer), rarely with participle, αἴδεσαι μὲν πατέρα προλείπων feel ashamed of deserting him, (Sophocles Tragicus):—;absolute, αἰδεσθείς from a sense of shame, (Iliad by Homer) 2. with accusative pers. to stand in awe of, fear, respect, αἰδεῖο θεούς (Iliad by Homer), and of things…

ἐπί-γνωσις, -εως, ἡ, [in LXX: (B. γν-), (דַּעַת), Jdth.9:14, 2Ma.9:11 *;] acquaintance, discernment, recognition: with genitive of thing(s), Phm 6; τ. ἀληθείας, τ. ἁμαρτίας, with genitive of person(s), of God: of Christ: of God and Christ: κατ ̓ ἐ., ἔχειν ἐν ἐ..
1. a means of defence: in plural battlements, (Iliad by Homer),—;in singular the battlements, parapet, (Iliad by Homer) 2. generally, a defence, protection, (Aeschulus Tragicus)

1. courage, boldness, (Iliad by Homer); θρ. ἰσχύος confidence in strength, (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. in bad sense, over-boldness, daring, rashness, audacity, impudence, attic, (Herdotus Historicus)
[in LXX: (מִרְמָה), Wis.1:12, al;] a wandering. Metaphorical, a going astray, an error (in NT always with respect to morals or religion): Ju 11.
ὑπ-αντάω, -ῶ [in LXX: Dan LXX (קָרָה), Sir.9:3,] to go to meet, meet: with dative of person(s), (ἀπ-, WH, txt.), of meeting in battle.
[in LXX: (שָׁבַר hi.), Wis.7:13,] to give a share of, impart: with dative of person(s) and accusative of thing(s), and (with ellipse of accusative); with dative of person(s), absol., ὁ μεταδιδούς.

(βλάσφημος), [in LXX: (נֶאָצָה), Da TH (96) (שׁלה), Tob.1:18, 1Ma.2:6, 2Ma.8:4 *;] (a) railing slander: Ju 9, (b) spec., impious speech against God, blasphemy: ὄνομα βλασφημίας, with genitive obj.; πρὸς τ. θεόν, (Cremer, 570; DB, i, 305; DCG ii, 423).
to drive from a country, banish, (Xenophon Historicus)
to peep out of a place, with genitive, (Babrius Fabularum Scriptor)
more commonly as depon., πειράομαι, [in LXX for נָסָה;] to try, attempt.
adv., [in LXX: 1Ma.12:11, II Mac.4, 3Ma.6:33 *;] unremittingly, incessantly.

ἀπο-γραφή, -ῆς, ἡ (ἀπογράφω) [in LXX: (כָּתָב), I, AB, 2Ma.2:1, 3Ma.2:32 3Mac 3Mac 3Mac *;] 1. a written copy. 2. As law term, a deposition (Demos.). 3. In late writers, a register, enrolment, census.

(prob. onomatop., descriptive of unintelligible sounds), [in LXX: Ps 113 (114):1 (לעז), (36) (בּער), 2Ma.2:21 Ma.3:24 *;] barbarous, barbarian, strange to Greek language and culture (and also, after the Persian war, with the added sense of brutal, rude).
adv. (ὁμίς), yet: ὅ. μέντοι, but yet, nevertheless, by hyperbaton, out of its proper position.
1. pain of body, (Iliad by Homer) 2. pain of mind, grief, distress, (Homer) 3. anything that causes pain, [, variant datesAnthology Palantina

[in LXX: A, Sir.5:7,] 1. trans., to throw over or beyond. 2. Intrans., to run beyond. In both senses, metaphorically, to exceed, surpass, transcend: with genitive obj..
[in LXX; B1, 2Ma.5:12 2Mac, III Mac; 3Ma.3:4 Mac3 *;] a soldier: metaphorically, σ. Χριστοῦ Ἰησ..
(εὐεργέτης), [in LXX: (עֲלִילָה), Wis.16:11, 24, 2Ma.6:13 2Mac Ma.8:17 *;] a good deed, kindness, benefit: with genitive of person(s) (εὐ. πόλεως, Plat., leg., 805b)
ἐμ-παιγμός, -οῦ, ὁ, [in LXX: (קַלָּסָה), Ps B א1 קָלָה ni.), Wis.12:2, Sir.27:28, 2Ma.7:7, 3Ma.5:22 *;] a mocking.

1. that may be taken or conquered, (Herdotus Historicus); that may be understood, (Plato Philosophus) 2. ( αἱρέομαι) to be chosen, eligible, (Plato Philosophus), ζοῆς πονηρᾶς θάνατος αἱρετώτερος (Menander Comicus) 3. chosen, elected, (Plato Philosophus)

ἀνά-στασις, -εως, ή (ἀνίστημι), [in LXX: (קוּם), La (קִימָה), קִימָה), title., Dan LXX Ma.7:14 2Mac *;] 1. a raising up, awakening, rising. 2. a rising from the dead; (a) of Christ: ἐξ ἀ. νεκρῶν, (ICC, in l); ἐκ νεκρῶν, (b) of persons in OT hist. (e.g. ff.): (with) of the general resurrection: ἀ. ἐκ νεκρῶν, τῶν νεκρῶν, ἀ. ζωῆς…

1. to be around a place, with dative, (Thucydides); τὰ περιόντα circumstances, (Demosthenes Orator) 2. to be better than, superior to another, surpass, excel, with genitive, (Iliad by Homer); περίεσσι γυναικῶν εἶδός τε μέγεθός τε (Odyssey by Homer); οἳ περὶ μὲν βουλὴν Δαναῶν περὶ δd ἐστὲ μάχεσθαι λπαρr εθυαλσs μάχην)) (Iliad by Homer)…

see: μάλα. μάλα adv., [in LXX for אֲבָל, Dan LXX, compar. for מ, (31), μᾶλλον ἠ (מ), superlat., 2Ma.8:7, 4Ma.4:22;] I. Pos., very, very much, exceedingly. II. Compar., μᾶλλον. 1. Of increase, more; with qualifying words: πολλῷ, πόσῳ, τοσούτῳ... ὅσῳ. 2. Of comparison, the more: ἔτι μ. καὶ μ., with compar., πολλῴ μ. κρεῖσον, μ. διαφέρειν…
adv. (περισσός) [in LXX: (יֶתֶר -עַל), Da TH (יַתִּיר, יֶתֶר) 2Ma.8:27 2Mac A *;] beyond measure, exceedingly, abundantly. Compar. (a) περισσότερον; (b) περισσοτέρως: π. μᾶλλον, opposite to ἧττον.
[in LXX: (מְבָרֵךְ אָוֶן), Wis.1:6, Sir.3:16, 2Ma.9:28 *;] (a) evil-speaking, slanderous, blasphemous: (b) as subst. a blasphemer: (Cremer, 570).
συν-τέμνω [in LXX chiefly for חָרַץ;] 1. to cut in pieces. 2. to cut down, cut short: metapb., λόγον, (LXX).

1. to strike or dash against, τί τινι (Iliad by Homer); ἀψῖδα πέτρῳ πρ. letting it dash against, (Euripides); τὸν πρὶν ὄλβον ἕρματι πρ. to wreck his happiness on a rock, (Aeschulus Tragicus); πρ. θηρία τινί to set them on him, (Demosthenes Orator); πρ. δόρυ τινί (Euripides):—;without any notion of violence, to put to, apply…

1. strong, staunch, stout, sturdy; with infinitive, καρτερὸς ἐναίρειν strong to kill, (Iliad by Homer); τὰ καρτερώτατα the strongest, (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. with genitive possessed of a thing, lord or master of it, (Theognis Elegiacus) 3. like καρτερικός, steadfast, patient, πρὸς πάντα (Xenophon Historicus): obstinate…
1. that which is fed or fatted: in plural fatted beasts, cattle, (Sophocles Tragicus), of sheep, (Euripides); of horses, (Euripides); of pigs, (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. food, (Aeschulus Tragicus)

to march against, make war upon, τινί (Euripides),—; to make an expedition, εἰς Θετταλίαν (Aeschulus Tragicus); with accusative, (Sophocles Tragicus):—;absolute, (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;so in Mid., with perfect passive, ἐπιστρατεύεσθαι ἐπ᾽ Αἴγυπτον (Herdotus Historicus); with dative, (Euripides)
ἄ-τοπος, -ον (τόπος), [in LXX: for אָוֶן,] 1. out of place, not befitting. 2. marvellous, strange (of symptoms, Hipp.): hence, in late Greek, with ethical sense, 3. improper, unrighteous.
εὔ-καιρος, -ον [in LXX: (עֵת), 2Ma.14:29 2Mac Ma.4:11 3Mac *;] timely, seasonable, suitable (Cremer, 740): ἡμέρα, βοήθεια.

1. to cut out, (Iliad by Homer); ὀϊστὸν ἐκτάμνειν μηροῦ to cut an arrow from the thigh, (Iliad by Homer) 2. to cut trees out of a wood, cut down, (Iliad by Homer); of planks, to hew out, hew into shape, ὃς νήϊον ἐκτάμνῃσιν (epic for -τέμνῃ); (Iliad by Homer) 3. to cut away, sever, (Pindar) 4. to castrate, (Herdotus Historicus)
(σκότος), [in LXX for חָשַׁךְ;] to darken; in NT always pass., -ομαι, to be darkened: of the heavenly bodies, (Rec., WH, mg.). Metaphorical, of the mind, " (LXX).
1. a violent snorting, neighing, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 2. metaphorically wanton behaviour, insolence, [variant datesAnthology Palantina
(-ους), τό [in LXX: Sir.20:26, 4Ma.1:29 4Mac 4Mac 4Mac 4Mac *;] 1 1, a haunt, abode. 2. = ἔθος, custom, manner: pl..
[in LXX: (קוּט ni.), Wis.4:16 Ma.3:8 4Mac *;] 1. to work; hence, from the effect of continued work, 2. to be weary: 3. to be sick.
(βίος), [in LXX: (חיה), Wis.4:4 א 1, Sir.40:28, 4Ma.5:22 *;] to spend life, to live: τ. χρόνον βιῶσαι (cl., more frequently 2 aor., -ναι). SYN.: ζάω.

1. to blow out, ποταμὸς ἐκφυσᾷ μένος pours forth its strength, (Aeschulus Tragicus): metaphorically, ἐκφ. πόλεμον to blow up a war from a spark, (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. to breathe out, ὕπνον ἔκφ. i. e. to snore, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus)
1. to burn by applying fire below, (Herdotus Historicus): to offer secret sacrifices, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 2. to light under, (Lucian)
(τιμή + οὖρος, a guardian) [in LXX: (שָׁכֹל pi), Wis.12:20,] 1. to help. 2. to avenge; mid., to avenge oneself on, punish: act, in this sense.
(ἔρημος), [in LXX: (חָרַב, חׇרְבָּה), (שְׁמָמָה), Wis.17:17, Sir.47:17, Bar.4:33, 4Ma.18:8 *;] a solitude, wilderness.
1. to trip up one's heels, upset, Lat. supplantare, (Demosthenes Orator) 2. metaphorically, ὑπ. καὶ ἀνατρέπων (Plato Philosophus)
to sharpen, whet, μαχαίρας (Aristophanes Comicus); λόγχην (Xenophon Historicus):—;Mid., ἀκονᾶσθαι μαχαίρας to sharpen their swords, (Aristophanes Comicus)
by night, nightly, Lat. nocturnus, (Aristophanes Comicus); ν. γενέσθαι to happen by night, (Aristophanes Comicus)
(ἔδαφος) [in LXX chiefly for רטשׁ pu.;] 1. to beat level like a threshing floor (Theophr.). 2. to dash to the ground (Field, Notes, 74): (cf. (137):9,).
πρό-φασις, -εως, ἡ (φήμι), [in LXX: (עֲלִילָה), ??עֲלִילָה), ??(5-6) (עִלָּה), *;] a pretence, pretext: (WM, R, txt., om.).
(φαντάζω), [in LXX: (חֲזִיז), חֲזִיז), Wis.18:17 *;] 1. as philos. term, (a) imagination; (b) = φάντασμα (Plat., Arist.). 2. In later writers, show, display.
(πάροιμος, by the way), [in LXX. Pr title, (מָשַׁל) subscr., Sir.6:35 *;] 1. a wayside saying, a byword, maxim, proverb. 2. In NT, of figurative discourse, a parable, allegory. SYN.: παραβολή, q.v

an unripe grape, πάροιθε δέ τ᾽ ὄμφακές εἰσιν (Odyssey by Homer); ὅτ᾽ ὄμφακες αἰόλλονται (Hesiod); ὅταν δὲ τεύχῃ Ζεὺς ἀπp ὄμφακος οἶνον, i. e. autumn, when the unripe grapes become fit to make wine, (Aeschulus Tragicus)
(ὑβρίζω), [in LXX chiefly for גֵּאֶה;] a violent, insolent man: (EV, injurious). SYN.: ἀλαζών, ὑπερήφανος, see Tr., Syn., § xxix

[in LXX: א2, (אָרַךְ, אַף אָרַךְ), Sir.2:4,] 1. actively = καρτερέω, to persevere (Plut., 2, 593 F). 2. Passively, to be patient, long-suffering: absol., before ἕως, with genitive, ἐπί, with dative, ib. (Sir.2:4); πρός, with accusative, ἐπί, with dative, εἰς. SYN.: ὑπομένω, q.v
[in LXX chiefly for חֵרֶם;] a drag-net, seine. SYN.: ἀμφίβληστρον, δίκτυον
τό (φρύγω, to parch), [in LXX chiefly for קַשׁ, also for חָרוּל,] a dry stick: pl., brushwood.
1. to pass by, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) 2. with accusative to go past, (Lucian)
(ἀκριβής), [in LXX: Dan LXX TH (יַצִּיב), Wis.12:21, Sir.16:25 *;] exactness, precision.
pitch, Lat. pix, (Iliad by Homer), proverbial, ἄρτι μῦς πίττης γεύεται, i. e. he has got the first taste of misery, (Demosthenes Orator)
1. one who melts gold, of one who gilds the horns of a victim, (Odyssey by Homer) 2. a goldsmith, (Demosthenes Orator)
the settlement of a colony, (Aristotle Philosopher)
the round of a ladder, (Euripides) from κλῖμαξ
(ὅμοιος), [in LXX: (מִין), Wis.14:19, 4Ma.15:4 *;] likeness: καθ᾽ ὁμοιότητα, in like manner, id. with genitive (MM, xviii), after the likeness (of).
ἐξ-ανα-τέλλω [in LXX: (צָמַח hi.); (זָרַח) *;] 1. trans., to cause to spring up (LXX). 2. Intrans. (as ἀνατέλλω,), to spring up.

1. to discover and make known, (Herdotus Historicus), with infinitive to give notice that.., (Aeschines Orator):—;Pass., with participle, κατεδέδεκτο ἐοῦσα χρηστή had been proved to be good, (Herdotus Historicus) 2. to invent and teach, introduce, exhibit, (Aristophanes Comicus); with infinitive to shew how to do, (Herdotus Historicus)
τό (θέρω, to heat), [in LXX chiefly for קַיִץ;] summer.

Lat. ver, spring, ἔαρος νέον ἱσταμένοιο in time of early spring, (Odyssey by Homer); ἅμα τῷ ἔαρι at the beginning of spring, (Herdotus Historicus); ἐξ ἦρος εἰς Ἀρκτοῦρον (Sophocles Tragicus):—;metaphorically of the prime or flower of anything, (Herdotus Historicus), ἔαρ ὁρᾶν to look fresh and bright, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus)…
τό (λαχαίνω, to dig), [in LXX: (יֶרֶק, יָרָק) *;] a garden herb, vegetable: usually in pl.. SYN.: βοτάνη, q.v

-οῦμαι, depon., [in LXX: (כָּחַשׁ pi.), Wis.12:27 Ma.8:7 4Mac *;] 1. to deny, say no, opposite to είπεῖν: absol., before ἅτι, with inf., 2. In late Gk., with accusative of person(s), to deny, refuse to acknowledge, disown: Ἰησοῦν, Ju 4; ἑαυτόν, (prove false to) 3. C. accusative of thing(s) (in cl. to refuse), to deny, abjure
1. long-existing, of olden time, ancient, (Homeric Hymns) 2. lasting for long, (Aristotle Philosopher):—;comparative -ώτερος, (Plato Philosophus); Sup. -ώτατος, (Xenophon Historicus)
[in LXX (mid.): (לָקַח), (נָחָה: hi.), 2Ma.15:31, 3Ma.5:18 R, 4Ma.12:3 4Mac *;] to send after or for: pass., a. Chiefly in mid., to send for, summon b.

1. a ladder or staircase (because of its leaning aslant), (Odyssey by Homer),—; a scaling-ladder, (Thucydides); κλίμακος προσαμβάσεις (Aeschulus Tragicus):—; a ship's ladder, (Euripides) 2. a frame with cross-bars, on which persons to be tortured were tied, (Aristophanes Comicus) 3. in (Sophocles Tragicus)…
to grow stiff or numb, Lat. torpere, (Iliad by Homer) from νάρκη

1. of things, painful, distressing, Lat. molestus, (Herdotus Historicus), attic 2. of persons, 3. in good sense, causing sorrow by one's departure, (Euripides) 4. in bad sense, causing pain, troublesome, vexatious, offensive, (Sophocles Tragicus), 5. adverb λυπηρῶς, painfully, so as to cause pain, (Sophocles Tragicus)…

that which is brought by the wife (compare ἕδνον); a dowry, portion, Lat. dos, (Herdotus Historicus); also in plural of a dower, as consisting of divers presents, (Euripides); but, φερναὶ πολέμου, of a wife won in battle, (Euripides):—;in plural, also, bridal gifts, (Euripides)

1. an acorn, Lat. glans, the fruit of the φηγός, given to swine, (Odyssey by Homer):—; any similar fruit, the date, (Herdotus Historicus) 2. from similarity of shape, an iron peg, a bolt-pin, Lat. pessulus, passed through the wooden bar ( μοχλός) into the door-post…
a wayfarer, traveller, (Aeschulus Tragicus);—;in (Iliad by Homer), a fellow-traveller, or guide.
(τρεῖς, μήν) [in LXX (neut.): B 4 (חֹדֶשׁ שָׁלוֹשׁ) *;] of three months; as subst., τὸ τ. (= cl. ἡ τ.), a space of three months.

1. to bloom, abound, to be luxuriant, of fruit-trees, (Odyssey by Homer), often in participle perfect τεθηλώς, epic feminine τεθαλυῖα, as adjective, luxuriant, exuberant, (Odyssey by Homer); with accusative cognate, οὐ δένδρε᾽ ἔθαλλεν χῶρος the place grew no trees, θαλλούσης βίον ἐλαίας (Aeschulus Tragicus) 2. of other natural objects…
(κήρ-, T), -υκος, ὁ [in LXX: Dan LXX TH (כָּרוֹז), Sir.20:15, 4Ma.6:4 *;] a herald.

1. to have a thing sold to one, to buy, purchase, (Homer), attic; with dative pretii, πρ. κτεάτεσσιν ἑοῖσιν to buy with one's money, (Odyssey by Homer); with genitive, πρ. θανάτοιο to purchase by his death, (Pindar); πρ. τι ταλάντου (Xenophon Historicus); π. πολλοῦ (Xenophon Historicus); metaphorically…
1. to be softened or made effeminate, shew weakness or cowardice, (Thucydides) 2. to be softened or appeased, (Thucydides)
to shew light through, to dawn, (Herdotus Historicus)
1. a chariot-road, (Iliad by Homer) 2. a race-course for chariots, Lat. curriculum, (Plato Philosophus)
to bury in the earth, (Herdotus Historicus); ἐπὶ κεφαλὴν κατώρυξε buried head downwards, (Herdotus Historicus); ἐν τῇ κεφαλῇ (Aristophanes Comicus)
(chiefly in poets and late prose for ἐρυγγάνω), [in LXX for תָּמַךְ,] to prop, fix firmly: act., as mid., ἐρείσασα, of a ship driving ashore (RV, struck).

ἐν-έχω [in LXX: (סָתַם), Ma.6:10 *;] 1. to hold in; pass., to be held, entangled: with dative of thing(s); jig., ζυγῷ δουλείας, θλίψρεσιν. 2. to set oneself against, be urgent against.
with all the house, household and all, (Herdotus Historicus)
(ἐμφαίνω, to show in, exhibit), [in LXX: (כּוּן ni.), Wis.6:22; ἐ. γίνεσθαι, (יָדַע ni.), (דָּרַשׁ ni.)*;] manifest: metaphorically, (LXX).

to cry down, cry out against, with genitive, (Herdotus Historicus); κ. τινῶν ὅτι τὰς σπονδὰς λελυκότες εἶεν (Thucydides); with accusative to bawl down, outcry, (Aristophanes Comicus)

1. to sprinkle, φάρμακα πάσσων laying salves upon a wound, (Iliad by Homer): —;with genitive partitive, πάσσε ἁλός sprinkle some salt, (Iliad by Homer) 2. to besprinkle, χρυσῶι, ῥόδοις π. τινά (Aristophanes Comicus) 3. metaphorically to embroider, broider, (Iliad by Homer); π. ἀέθλους to work battles in embroidery, (Iliad by Homer)
adv. (ἔχω), in order, successively, next: τῇ ἑ. ἡμέρᾳ, ἐν τῷ ἑ. (sc. χρόνῳ), soon after, τῇ ἑ. (sc. ἡμέρα).

1. an axle, Lat. axis, (Iliad by Homer), 2. οἱ ἄξονες, the wooden tablets of Solon's laws, made to turn upon an axis, (Plutarch)

1. intransitive, in active present καταδύνω and middle καταδύομαι:—; to go down, sink, set, of the sun, ἠέλιος κατέδυ (Iliad by Homer); ἐς ἠέλιον καταδύντα till sun set, (Odyssey by Homer); of ships, to be sunk or rather to be disabled, (Herdotus Historicus):—;of persons, καταδεδυκώς having popped down, (Aristophanes Comicus) 2…
fem, of προφήτης, [in LXX: (נְבִיאָה) *;] a prophetess.
a taste, smack of a thing, (Euripides)

[in LXX chiefly for קַל, קָלָל;] light in weight easy to bear: θλίψρις (EV, our light affliction).
(περίειμι, to be over and above), [in LXX: (סְגֻלָּה, עַם)*;] one's own, of one's own possession: λαὸς π..

συν-εισ-έρχομαι [in LXX: (עִם בּוֹא),] to enter together: with dative of person(s), before εἰς, with accusative loc..

1. measured motion, time, rhythm, Lat. numerus, (Aristophanes Comicus), —; ἐν ῥυθμῷ in time, Virgil 's in numerum, (Xenophon Historicus); μετὰ ῥυθμοῦ (Thucydides); θάττονα ῥυθμὸν ἐπάγειν to play in quicker time, (Xenophon Historicus) 2. proportion or symmetry of parts, (Plato Philosophus) 3. generally, arrangement, order, (Euripides) 4…
εἴσ-ειμι [in LXX for בּוֹא;] to go in, enter: before εἰς, πρὸς Ἰάκωβον.
a pointing out, manifestation, explaining, shewing, (Thucydides); δ. ποιεῖσθαι = δηλοῦν, (Thucydides)
dry and hard all round, exceeding hard, of iron, (Sophocles Tragicus):—;metaphorically obstinate, stubborn, (Sophocles Tragicus)

1. Dep., used in present and imperfect: 2. intransitive to work for one's daily bread; generally, to toil, work, labour, (Homer) 3. to be poor or needy, Solon, (Euripides), 4. with genitive to be poor in, have need of, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 5. transitive to work at, prepare, get ready, δαῖτα πένοντο (Odyssey by Homer)…
1. an object of malignant joy, (Euripides) 2. malignant joy, (Euripides)
ἄπ-ειμι (εἰμί, sum) [in LXX for כָּחַד ni., נָדַח ni.;] to be absent.
1. a small torch, (Plato Philosophus) 2. a bandage for wounds, (Aristophanes Comicus)

1. any prominent part, ἀκρ. τοῦ οὔρεος a mountain- peak, (Herdotus Historicus) 2. a cape, promontory, (Herdotus Historicus) 3. the extremity of anything, ἀκρ. νηός a ship's beak, (Herdotus Historicus) 4. in plural the extremities of the body, hands and feet, fingers and toes, (Thucydides), τὰ ἀκρ. τῆς Νίκης her wings, (Demosthenes Orator)
(λέπω, to peel) [in LXX chiefly for קַשְׂקֶשֶׂת;] a scale
drinking, a drinking-bout, carousal, (Xenophon Historicus); παρὰ πότον, Lat. inter pocula, (Xenophon Historicus); ἐν τοῖς πότοις (Aeschines Orator)

1. to fall differently, undergo a change, μ. τὸ εἶδος (Herdotus Historicus), or εἰς ἄλλο εἶδος (Plato Philosophus): also, to change one's opinion suddenly, (Euripides); εἰ τρεῖς μόναι μετέπεσον τῶν ψήφων (Plato Philosophus) 2. to change, especially for the worse, μεταπίπτοντος δαίμονος if fortune changes, (Euripides)…
genitive, -ανος, -αίνης, -ανος, [in LXX: (שָׁחֹר),] black: opposite to λευκός, neut., τὸ μ., ink: II Jn 12.

δια-τρίβω [in LXX (יָשַׁב), (גּוּר), Tob.11:8, 12, Jdth.10:2, 2Ma.14:23 *;] to rub hard, rub away, consume; δ. χρόνον, ἡμέρας, to spend time. Intransitively with ellipse of object, to spend time, stay.
to have come back, to return, (Demosthenes Orator)

ἐξ-ηγέομαι, -οῦμαι [in LXX chiefly for סָפַר pi.;] to lead, show the way; metaphorically, to unfold, narrate, declare: with accusative of thing(s), with dative of person(s), θεόν (understood), before ὅσα, καθώς.
1. to decide finally, settle, of a judge, (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. to avenge, (Euripides)
τό (σφαγή), [in LXX: (זֶבַח), (טֶבַח), (נְדָבָה) *;] a victim for slaughter: (LXX).

συλ-λογίζομαι [in LXX chiefly for חָשַׁב pi.;] 1. to compute. 2. to reason.

(Heb. גַּמְלִיאֵל), Gamaliel the elder, a Pharisee and Doctor of the Law.
(-ους), τό (ὄξύς), [in LXX: (חֹמֶץ)*;] sour wine (posca, vin-Deu pays), the ordinary drink of labourers and common soldiers.

(ῥαντίζω), [in LXX for נִדָּה;] sprinkling: of the ceremonial sprinkling of blood for purification.

tin, Lat. stannum, (Iliad by Homer) It was melted, and then cast upon χαλκός, hence χεῦμα κασσιτέροιο a plating of tin, (Iliad by Homer) A foreign word.
to draw out in battle-order, of the officers:—;Mid. to draw themselves out, of the soldiers, (Xenophon Historicus)
ἀπο-λαμβάνω [in LXX: (לָקַח ( A, Ma.4:46 2Mac 2Mac Ma.18:23 *;] 1. to receive from another; absol., to receive as one's due: (seel. λάβῃ). 2. to receive back. 3. to take apart or aside.

1. to thrust, push, shove, force onwards or away, λᾶαν ἄνω ὤθεσκε he kept pushing it upwards, (Odyssey by Homer); ἀπ᾽ ὀφθαλμῶν νέφος ὦσεν Ἀθήνη (Iliad by Homer); ἐκ μηροῦ δόρυ ὦσε he forced the spear from the thigh, (Iliad by Homer); ὦσαί τινα ἀφ᾽ ἵππων (Iliad by Homer); ὦσαι ἑαυτὸν ἐς τὸ πῦρ to rush into the fire, (Herdotus Historicus)…

1. at the furthest point, and so either topmost = Lat. summus, or outermost = Lat. extremus: 2. highest, topmost, ἐν ἄκρηι πόλει = ἐν ἀκροπόλει, (Iliad by Homer); μέλαν ὕδωρ ἄκρον at its surface, (Iliad by Homer), 3. outermost, ἄκρη χείρ, ἄκροι πόδες, ἄκρος ὦμος the end of the hand, ends of the feet, tip of the shoulder…
ἐκ-πειράζω [in LXX: (נָסָה pi.) *;] = cl. ἐκπειράομαι, to put to the proof or test, make trial of, tempt: with accusative, of God, (LXX), (ib.), of Christ, (Cremer, 497).
ἀν-αίτιος, -ον (αἰτία), [in LXX: (נָקִי), Dan LXX TH Sus1:62, always of αἷμα *;] guiltless, innocent.
(ὑπακσύω), [in LXX: (לָמַם) (שָׁמַע),] giving ear, obedient, subject: with dative of person(s), εἰς πάντα.
ἀνα-πτύσσω [in LXX for פָּרַשׂ,] to unroll: τ. βιβλίον, (WH, R, ἀνοίξας).
ἀπο-κόπτω [in LXX for קָצַץ, כָּרַת,] to cut off. Mid., to mutilate oneself, have oneself mutilated.
(ἀσχήμαων), [in LXX: (עֶרְיָה); (קָלָה ni.)*;] to act unbecomingly, behave dishonourably: before ἐπί, ib..

1. to loosen beneath or below, ὑπέλυσε γυῖα made his limbs give way under him, (Iliad by Homer):—;Pass., γυῖα ὑπέλυντο (Iliad by Homer) 2. to loose from under the yoke, (Homer):—; to loose from bonds, (Odyssey by Homer); in Mid., τὸν ὑπελύσαο δεσμῶν thou didst free him from bonds by stealth, (Iliad by Homer) 3…
1. the chief of a φυ_λή, a phylarch, (Herdotus Historicus):—;used to translated the Rom. tribunus, (Plutarch) 2. at Athens, the commander of the cavalry furnished by each tribe, see. ἵππαρχος.
properly, the part behind the midriff μετὰ τὰς φρένας); the back, (Iliad by Homer)
Diminutive of κλῆμα:—;in plural brush-wood, fagot-wood, (Thucydides)
1. to dry up a river, (Herdotus Historicus):—;Pass. to be dried up, run dry, of rivers, (Herdotus Historicus) 2. generally to dry completely, τὰς ναῦς (Thucydides)
a satrapy, the office or province of a satrap, (Herdotus Historicus)

1. one who divines, a seer, prophet, (Homer),—;as feminine a prophetess, [variant datesTragica Adespota, (Thucydides) 2. metaphorically a diviner, foreboder, (Sophocles Tragicus) 3. a kind of grasshopper, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus)

(στενός + χῶρος, space) [in LXX: (אוּץ), (אָלַץ pi.), (20) (קָצַר) (צָרַר), 4Ma.11:11 *;] 1. to be straitened; metaphorically, to be anxious. 2. In late writers, trans., to straiten, compress: pass., trop..

1. to shake at or against, with the view of scaring, τί τινι (Iliad by Homer); Πέρσας ἐπ. to hold them out as a threat, (Plutarch); but, ἐπ. τὴν χεῖρα, in token of assent, (Lucian) 2. to set upon one, with dative, (Euripides)

(θόρυβος), [in LXX: Nam.2:3 (רָעַל ho.), Dan LXX (בָּעַת ni.), Wis.18:19, Sir.40:6 *;] 1. to make a noise or uproar: mid., of loud and ostentatious lamentation. 2. Trans., to trouble, throw into confusion: τ. πόλιν.
properly a path with no turnings, generally a path-way, road, (Homer)
(τρύω, to wear away), [in LXX: (נָקִיק),] = τρύμη, a hole: τ. ῥαφίδος, eye of a needle. SYN.: τρῆμα, τρύπημα
(ταράσσω), [in LXX for מְהוּמָה,] later form of ταραχή.
to force out:—;Pass., τόξον χειρῶν ἐκβεβιασμένον the bow forced from mine hands, (Sophocles Tragicus)

1. a pillar, Lat. columna, (Odyssey by Homer): a flogging-post, (Sophocles Tragicus); proverbial, ἔσθιε τοὺς Μεγακλέους κίονας eat the pillars of his hall, for being a spendthrift, he had nothing else left to give, (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. in plural the pillars guarded by Atlas, which keep heaven and earth asunder, (Odyssey by Homer)…

[in LXX: (נטה), and (נשׂא), Sir.6:25, Da TH Bel 36 *;] 1. to take up with the hands, to lift: λίθους. 2. to bear, to carry, as a burden, and metaphorically, to endure; 17. 3. In late writers (MM, Exp., ii, iii, x), (a) to take away; (, Heb.); (b) to carry off, steal.
to turn away from a thing:—;Pass. with future middle, aorist2 middle -ετραπόμην and passive -ετράπην [ ᾶ], to be turned from one's purpose, to be perplexed, (Demosthenes Orator)

(κλῆρος, νέμομαι, to possess) [in LXX: (יָרַשׁ), Sir.23:22 *;] 1. (as in cl.) an heir: of those who as sons of God inherit the privileges of the Messianic Kingdom; of Christ himself, of Abraham, of Christians. 2. (As in LXX: Jg, Mi, Je, ll. with) a possessor: (Cremer, 359 f.).
σύσ-σημον (T, συν-), -ου, τό (σῆμα), [in LXX: (מַשְׂאֵת), (נֵס) *;] a fixed sign or signal.

1. to dance a round or choral dance, (Sophocles Tragicus), especially of the Bacchic chorus, (Euripides):—; to take part in the chorus, regarded as a matter of religion, (Sophocles Tragicus): to be one of a chorus, (Aristophanes Comicus): —;with dative pers. to dance to him, in his honour, (Euripides) 2. generally, to dance…
1. nearness of kin, (Plato Philosophus) 2. rights of kin, right of inheritance, (Aristophanes Comicus)
garrulity, idle talk, (Aristophanes Comicus), (Theophrastus Philosophus) wrote περὶ ἀδολεσχίας.

1. a ring, circle, round, (Homer); ἀσπίδος κύκλος the round shield, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 2. Adverbial usages, κύκλῳ in a circle or ring, round about, (Odyssey by Homer), attic; with genitive, κ. τοῦ στρατοπέδου (Xenophon Historicus), 3. any circular body: 4. a wheel, (Iliad by Homer) 5. a place of assembly, the ἀγορά, (Iliad by Homer)…
(θάμβος) [in LXX for בָּעַת ni., pi.,] 1. to be amazed. 2. In late Gk., to astonish, terrify: pass., before ἐπί with dative of thing(s).
ἀνα-ψύχω [in LXX for נָפַשׁ ni., חָיָה, (frequently in sense of revive, refresh oneself);] to refresh: with accusative of person(s).

παρ-αιτέομαι, -οῦμαι [in LXX for בָּקַשׁ pi.,] 1. to beg of or from another. 2. to deprecate; (a) prop., with neg., to entreat that not: (b) to refuse, decline, avoid: o. accusative. 3. to beg off, ask to be excused, excuse: (, Field, l.with).

(αἰτία), [in LXX: (סבב) Dan LXX Bel 41, TH ib. 42, Su 53, 2Ma.4:47 Ma.1:11 *;] 1. causative of, responsible for; as subst., ὁ αἰ., the cause, author: τὸ αἰ., the cause. 2. blameworthy, culpable; as subst., ὁ αἰ., the culprit, the accused (Lat. reus); τὸ αἰ. (= αἰτία, 3), the crime.
looking dry, squalid, κόμη (Euripides): τὸ αὐχμῶδες drought, (Herdotus Historicus)

κατ-αντάω, -ῶ [in LXX: (חוּל), 2Ma.4:21 2Mac 2Mac 2Mac *;] to come to, arrive at: before εἰς, with accusative loc., before ἀντικρύ, with genitive. Metaphorical, before εἰς, with accusative of person(s), id. with accusative of thing(s), to attain to.
[in LXX chiefly for עָנָה;] to draw around, draw off or away. Metaphorical, to distract: pass..
[in LXX for קוּר, שָׁטַח;] to breathe, blow; hence, to make cool. Pass., to grow cool: metaphorically.
τό (dimin. of φόρτος), [in LXX chiefly for מַשָּׂא;] a burden, load: of the cargo of a ship, metaphorically. SYN.: βάρος, ὄγκος

to spread out sails or clothes, (Odyssey by Homer); χεῖρε πετάσσας, of one swimming, (Odyssey by Homer): metaphorically, θυμὸν πετάσαι to open one's heart, (Odyssey by Homer):—;Pass., mostly in perfect, to be spread on all sides, (Homer): participle spread wide, opened wide, of folding doors, πύλαι πεπταμέναι (Iliad by Homer)…
(στρέφω), [in LXX: (פָּתַל hithp.), 3Ma.4:14, 4Ma.9:17 4Mac 4Mac 4Mac *;] to twist, torture. Metaphorical, to twist or pervert language.
to go all round, with accusative, (Plutarch)

(μωρός), [in LXX: (בָּעַר ni.), R (שָׂכַל ni., pi.)*;] 1. cl., to be foolish, play the fool. 2. LXX and NT, causal, to make foolish: pass., to become foolish: of salt that has lost its flavour, become tasteless.
1. a raft, float (such as was made off-hand, compare σχέδιος II), (Odyssey by Homer); generally, a boat, ship, (Euripides) 2. a bridge of boats, of the bridge of Xerxes, (Herdotus Historicus)
enjoyment, delight, τινός from or in a thing, (Hesiod):—;absolute gladness, joy, delight, pleasure, (Theognis Elegiacus)
τό (ῥήγνυμι), [in LXX: (קֶרַע), (11) A (בְּקִיעַ) *;] 1. cl. (and so in LXX), a fracture; then by meton., that which is torn. 2. In NT, ruin.

1. thick, stout, (Homer):—; later, stout, fat, (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. of things, thick, massive, (Homer):—;adverb -έως, roughly, of stating or arguing, (Aristotle Philosopher); παχύτερον or -έρως, (Plato Philosophus) 3. of liquids, thick, curdled, clotted, (Iliad by Homer) 4. οἱ παχέες the men of substance, the wealthy class…
1. a hearing or listening, (Thucydides), 2. obedience to another, with genitive, (Thucydides)
(μετρέω), [in LXX: (סְאָה), (בַּת),] 1. a measurer (Plat.). 2. = ἀμφορεύς, an Attic measure, = 11⁄2 Roman amphoræ or about 9 Eng. gallons.
(μῆλον, a sheep or goat) [in LXX for אַדֶּרֶת, *;] a sheepskin.
1. to lick up, (Herdotus Historicus) 2. irregular participle perfect, γλώσσηισι λελειχμότες playing with their tongues, (Hesiod)
1. in arms, armed, (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. with armed men within, of the Trojan horse, (Euripides)

1. to shake in or at, (Sophocles Tragicus); κέλαδον ἐνς. πώλοις to drive a sound into their ears, (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. with accusative pers. to drive into, ἐνς. τινὰ ἀγρίαις ὁδοῖς (Sophocles Tragicus)
1. a land, country, (Homer) 2. earth, soil, (Iliad by Homer) 3. Γαῖα, as proper noun, Gaia, Tellus, Earth, spouse of Uranus, mother of the Titans, (Hesiod)
τό (ἄγκος, a bend), [in LXX חַכָּה,] a fish-hook.
ἀνα-φωνέω, -ῶ [in LXX for שָׁמַע hi., זָכַר hi.;] to cry out, exclaim.
τό (ἀρόω, to plough), [in LXX chiefly for אֵת;] a plough.
[in LXX for אַחֲרוֹן and cogn. forms;] latter, later: ἐν ὑ. καιροῖς. Neut., τὸ ὕ., used adverbially instead of ὑστέρως, afterwards, later: with genitive.

1. the bend of the arm, the elbow, (Homer) 2. generally the arm, like ἀγκάλη, (Pindar) 3. any bend, as the jutting angle of a wall, (Iliad by Homer): the bend or reach of a river, (Herdotus Historicus); ἕσπεροι ἄγκωνες, in (Sophocles Tragicus), seem to be the angle of the bay of Rhoeteium.
(ἀνίημι), [in LXX: 2Es.4.22 (שָׁלוּ), I, Wis.13:13, Sir.15:20 *;] a loosening, relaxation: by St. Paul, opposite to θλίψις, expressed or understood, relief. SYN.: ἀνάπαυσις.
ἐπί-θεσις, -εως, ἡ (ἐπιτίθημι), [in LXX: (קֶשֶׁר), Ez (עֲגָבָה) 2Ma.4:41 2Mac 2Mac *;] 1. a laying on: χειρῶν. 2. an attack, assault (2Mac, ll.with).
[in LXX: (נָשָׂא ni.),] to lift or raise over. Mid., to uplift oneself: before ἐπί, with accusative, of person(s).
ἐπι-ταγή, -ῆς, ἡ (ἐπιτάσσω), [in LXX: Dan LXX (פִּתְגָּם), I, Wis.14:16 Ma.7:20 *;] = cl., ἐπίταγμα, a command, μετὰ πάσης ἐ, with all authority.
προ-πέμπω [in LXX: I, Jdth.10:15, Wis.19:2, 1Ma.12:4, 2Ma.6:23 *;] 1. to send before, send forth. 2. to set forward on a journey, escort: with accusative of person(s), before εἰς, οὗ, ἕως, pass..
ἀπο-τάσσω [in LXX: (יָאַשׁ pi.), I, Ma.4:1-61 *;] to set apart. Mid., in late Gk. to take leave of: (b) to forsake.
κατ-ακολουθέω, -ῶ [in LXX: (רָאָה), 1Ma.6:23,] to follow after: with dative of person(s).
a growth of hair, hair, (Herdotus Historicus); ἐν γενείου συλλογῇ τριχώματος, i. e. just at the age of manhood, (Aeschulus Tragicus)
adv. [in LXX: ff, Dan LXX TH *;] readily: ἑ. ἔχω, to be ready (Deiss., BS, 252; MM, Exp., xiv): with inf..
(ὁδός, ἡγέομαι) [in LXX: Wis.7:15 Ma.4:2, 2Ma.5:15 *;] a leader on the way, a guide. Fig., ὁ. τυφλῶν, pl..
to laugh out, laugh loud, (Odyssey by Homer): metaphorically of a liquid, to rush gurgling out, (Euripides)

1. to stand aloof from, depart from, be far from, with genitive, (Aeschulus Tragicus); ἀπ. φίλων to fall off from one's friends, (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. absolute to stand aloof or afar off, (Aeschulus Tragicus)

1. a bending, winding, of a river, (Herdotus Historicus) 2. the turning in a race-course, turning-post, (Aristophanes Comicus): metaphorically, μῦθον ἐς καμπὴν ἄγειν to bring a speech to its middle or turning point, (Euripides); καμπὰς ποιεῖσθαι (Plato Philosophus)

1. a point, edge: proverbial, ἐπὶ ξυροῦ ἀκμῆς on the rasor's edge; ἀμφιδέξιοι ἀκμαί the fingers of both hands, (Sophocles Tragicus); ποδοῖν ἀκμαί the toes, (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. the highest point of anything, the bloom, flower, prime, of man's age, Lat. flos aetatis, ἀκμὴ ἥβης (Sophocles Tragicus); ἀκμὴ βίου (Xenophon Historicus)…
1. release or deliverance from a thing, with genitive, (Aeschulus Tragicus), 2. feebleness, faintness, (Demosthenes Orator)
ἐπι-τρέπω [in LXX (usually with seel. ἐπιστρ-): (עָזַב),] 1. to turn to, commit, entrust. 2. to yield, permit: with dative of person(s), id. with inf., with inf.. Pass., with dative and inf..

[in LXX: Jdth.8:25 Wis.18:2, 2Ma.1:11 2Mac A 2Ma.12:31 R, 3Ma.7:16 *;] to be thankful, give thanks: of giving thanks before meat, with dative pens., τ. θεῷ, Phm 4; before διὰ Ἰ. Χριστοῦ, R, WH, mg., ἐν ὀνόματι Χρ., before περί, ὅτι, ἐπι, with dative of thing(s), ὐπέρ, ὅτι, pass. (Deiss., BS, 122 f.). SYN.: see: αἰνέω; and cf. Cremer…
τό (πλάσσω), [in LXX chiefly for יֵצֶר;] that which is moulded or formed: (LXX).
[in LXX: א (no Heb. equiv.), Jdth.9:3, 10 Ma.18:8 *;] deceit, deceitfulness: τοῦ πλούτου, τῆς ἀδικίας, τῆς ἁμαρτίας, αἱ ἐπιθυμίαι τῆς ἀ.. pl., ἀπά ται: (WH, mg., R., txt., ἐν ἀγάπαις).
ἀπ-ελπίζω [in LXX: (אֶבְיוֹן), Jdth.9:11, Sir.22:21 Ma.9:18 *;] 1. to give up in despair, despair of (Polyb., Diod., LXX). 2. to hope to receive from or in return: with accusative.

[in LXX: Jdth.14:11, 2Ma.8:23 2Mac 2Mac *;] 1. (= Lat. spira) anything wound or rolled up, a coil. 2. As a military term used (by Polyb. and later writers) of a body of soldiers, a maniple (third part of a cohort) or cohort.

1. courage, to undertake or venture a thing, boldness, daring, hardihood, courage, (Pindar), attic; τῶνδε τόλμαν σχεθεῖν to have courage for this business, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 2. in bad sense, over-boldness, recklessness, Lat. audacia, [variant datesTragica Adespota, 3. a bold or daring act, [variant datesTragica Adespota

1. a writing or noting down, (Herdotus Historicus) 2. that which is written, a writing, book: a history, narrative, (Thucydides), 3. a written contract, a covenant, bond, Lat. syngrapha, (Thucydides); συγγ. ναυτικαί a bond to secure money lent on bottomry, (Demosthenes Orator)…
[in LXX: (מָצָא ni.), Tob.9:5,] to bring forth: with accusative of thing(s), before ἐκ.
[in LXX: Tob.12:2, Wis.10:8 Ma.12:22, 4Ma.9:7 *;] to hurt, injure: with accusative,[18].
τό, [in LXX: Sir.19:11, 1Ma.1:61, 2Ma.6:10, 3Ma.5:49, 4Ma.4:25 *;] 1. an unborn child. 2. a newborn child, a babe: ἀπὸ βρέφους, from infancy.
ἀνα-καινίζω (καινός), [in LXX: La (חָדַשׁ pi., hith)., (עָכַר ni.), 1Ma.6:9 *;] to renew: (Isocr., Plut.).
(μακρό-θυμος), [in LXX: (אַף אֹרֶךְ), (אַף אָרֵךְ), Sir.5:11, 1Ma.8:4 *;], patience, longsuffering: of men, esp. in experiencing troubles and difficulties, of God's forbearance. SYN.: ὑπομονή

to make new: hence, καί τι καινίζει στέγη and the house has something strange about it, (Sophocles Tragicus); καίνισον ζυγόν try on thy new yoke, handsel it, (Aeschulus Tragicus); κ. εὐχάς to offer new, strange prayers, (Euripides)
(εὔκαιρος), [in LXX: (עֵת), Sir.38:24, 1Ma.11:42 *;] fitting time, opportunity: before ἵνα, τοῦ, with inf..
ἐξ-άλλομαι [in LXX for קָלַל,] to leap up.
(Ἰουδαΐζω), [in LXX: 2Ma.2:21 2Mac 2Mac Ma.4:26 *;] Judaism, the observance of Jewish rites.
to paint from life, to paint, (Plato Philosophus)
[in LXX: 2Ma.3:7 2Mac 2Mac Ma.3:28, 4Ma.4:3 *;] to disclose, declare, make known: in forensic sense, to inform, report: pass., with dative of person(s).
(ὑπερέχω) [in LXX: (קוֹמָה), 2Ma.3:11,] a projection, eminence, as the peak of a mountain. Metaphorical (Arist.), excellence, pre-eminence: λόγου ἢ σοφίας, οἱ ἐν ὑ.
δια-βάλλω [in LXX: Dan LXX, Da TH; (25) (אֲכַל קְרַץ), 2Ma.3:11, 4Ma.4:1 *;] 1. to throw across. 2. To slander, defame, accuse falsely or maliciously: (Cremer, 120).
(ἅγιος), [in LXX: (30):4 96(97):12 (קֹדֶשׁ), 95(96):6 (עֹז), 144(145):5 (הוֹד), 2Ma.3:12 *;] holiness, the state in man resulting from ἁγιασμός, which see.
τό (δείδω), [in LXX: 2Ma.3:17, 30 *;] fear, awe, reverence: μετὰ εὐλαβείας καὶ δ.. SYN.: δειλία, φόβος.

(οὐρανός), [in LXX: (שַׁדַּי), DA TH A (שָׁמַיִם) 2Ma.3:39, 3Ma.6:28 3Mac Ma.4:11 AR, 4Ma.11:3 א*;] in or of heaven, heavenly (in Hom., of the Gods): οἱ ἐ., opposite to ἐπίγειοι and καταχθόνιοι, to χοϊκός, σώματα, βασιλεία, παπρίς, Ἱερουσαλήμ, κλῆσις, τὰ ἐ., opposite to ἐπίγειος, id., of the heavenly regions, ἡ δωρεὰ ἡ ἐ., (Cremer, 468).

1. a wild beast, beast of prey, (Iliad by Homer), joined with λέων, (Euripides); with λέαινα, [variant datesAnthology Palantina; also of Cerberus, (Sophocles Tragicus):—;in plural beasts, as opposite to birds and fishes, (Odyssey by Homer), 2. of any animal, as of birds, (Aristophanes Comicus), 3. any fabulous monster, as the sphinx…

[in LXX: Wis.7:27 Ma.6:1 2Mac 2Mac *;] to pass over from one place to another: with reference to the point of departure only, to withdraw, depart: of removal from this life, ἐκ τ. κότμου πρὸς τ. Πατέρα, metaphorically, ἐκ τ. θανάτου εἰς τ. ζωήν.
1. appearance, aspect, mien, (Pindar); periphrastic, σὴ πρ. thy presence, i. e. thyself, (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. a seeing, beholding, sight, view, (Euripides)

ὑπό-δειγμα, -τος, τό (ὑποδείκνυμι), [in LXX: Sir.44:16, 2Ma.6:28 2Mac Ma.17:23 *;] used by later writers (Xen. onwards) for παράδειγμα, (a) a figure, copy: (b) an example: for imitation, for warning. SYN.: ὁμοίωμα, τύπος, ὑποτύπωσις

ἐκ-πλήσσω (Attic -ττω,), [in LXX: (pass.), (שָׁמֵם hithp.), Wis.13:4, 2Ma.7:12, 4Ma.8:4 4Mac *;] 1. prop., to strike out, drive away. 2. to strike with panic or shock, to amaze, astonish: pass., before ἐπί, with dative of thing(s). SYN.: " πτωεῖν G?, to terrify, agitate with fear; τρεμεῖν, to tremble, predominantly physical; φοβεῖν…
(ἄπιστος), [in LXX: Wis.1:2, Sir.1:27, 2Ma.8:13 *;] 1. to disbelieve, be faithless: so prob. also. 2. = ἀπειθέω.

1. a dissolving, dissolution of governments, (Thucydides), 2. the dismissal or disbanding of a body of men, στρατιᾶς (Xenophon Historicus); εἰς κατάλυσιν till dismissal, of soldiers at a review, (Xenophon Historicus) 3. κ. τοῦ πολέμου an ending of the war, pacification, (Thucydides) 4. generally, an end, termination…
ἐπ-αν-άγω [in LXX: (רוּק hi.), Sir.17:26 Ma.9:21 2Mac *;] to bring up or back (sc. ναῦς); to put out to sea (DB, iii, 63b): intrans., to return.

1. to carry round along with or together, (Plato Philosophus) 2. [in LXX for סָכַן,] to heat, warm; metaphorically, (a) to inflame (Trag.); (b) to foster, cherish.
