1. to make things alternate, to transpose, (Plato Philosophus) 2. to change or alter a little, (Herdotus Historicus) 3. of Place, to pass by, go past, elude, (Xenophon Historicus):—; to get rid of, (Plutarch) 4. to go beyond, exceed in point of time, (Plutarch) 5. intransitive to pass by one another, to overlap, (Herdotus Historicus) 6…

κατ-αργέω, -ῶ (κατά, causative, ἀργός = ἀ-εργός), [in LXX: 2Es.4.21; 2Es.4.23; 2Es.5.5; 2Es.6.8 (בְּטֵל)*;] to make idle or inactive (χέρας, Eur., Phœn., 753): of soil occupied by an unfruitful tree. Metaphorical (Inscr.), to render inoperative or invalid, to abrogate, abolish: pass., before ἀπό (of persons), to be separated…

1. to put in or into a ship, (Odyssey by Homer), attic; so in Mid., (Odyssey by Homer):—;then, generally, to put in or into, (Hesiod), 2. metaphorically to put into a person, inspire, (Theognis Elegiacus);—; Mid., χόλον ἔνθεο θυμῷ thou didst store up wrath in thy heart, (Iliad by Homer); πατέρας ἔνθεο τιμῇ hold our fathers in honour…
see: ἐνκ- ἐνκαίνια (Rec. ἐγκ-), -ων, τά (ἐν, καινός), [in LXX for HSjrj, II, Da TH *;] dedication (anniversary of the cleansing of the Temple from the defilements of Antiochus Epiphanes).
a demanding back, (Herdotus Historicus); ἀπ. ποιεῖσθαι to make a formal demand, (Demosthenes Orator)

(εὐχάριστος), [in LXX: Wis.16:28, Sir.37:11, 2Ma.2:27 *;] 1. thankfulness, gratitude (Polyb.; Es, Sir, 2Mac, ll. with). 2. giving of thanks, thanksgiving (so in π. and Inscr.; M, Th., 41 f.): with dative of person(s), pl., (Cremer, 904).
δι-εγείρω [in LXX: Jdth.1:4, Ma.7:21 2Mac Ma.5:15 *;] to arouse completely, arouse as from rest or sleep: pass., of the sea. Metaphorical, of the mind: ἐν ὑπομνήσει.
adv., [in LXX: (חׇזְקָה), Jol.1:14, Jdth.4:12, 3Ma.5:9 *;] fervently, earnestly: compar., (WH br., R, mg., omits).
τό [in LXX: Jdth.10:8 *;] (a) height: (b) that which is lifted up, a barrier.

παρ-ουσία, -ας, ἡ [in LXX: A, Jdth.10:18, 2Ma.8:12 2Mac Ma.3:17 *;] 1. usually in cl., a being present, presence: opposite to ἀπουσία. 2. a coming, arrival, advent: in late writers as technical term for the visit of a king; hence, in NT, specif. of the Advent or Parousia of Christ.
an Egyptian couch with mosquito-curtains; conopium in (Horace)
(τέλειος), adv., [in LXX: Jdth.11:6, 2Ma.12:42, 3Ma.3:26 3Mac, R*;] completely, perfectly.

to pour round or over, τί τινι, properly of liquids, (Homer); of metal-workers, χρυσὸν κέρασιν περιχεύας having spread gold leaf round its horns, (Iliad by Homer); so in Mid., ὡς δ᾽ ὅτε τις χρυσὸν περιχεύεται ἀργύρῳ (Odyssey by Homer):—;Pass. to be poured around, περὶ δ᾽ ἀμβρόσιος κέχυθ᾽ ὕπνος (Iliad by Homer)…
ὑπο-δέχομαι [in LXX: Tob.7:8-9 Jdth.13:13 A, 1Ma.16:15, 4Ma.13:17 *;] to receive under one's roof, receive as a guest, entertain hospitably: with accusative of person(s), εἰς τ. οἶκον.
[in LXX: (שָׁכַב), Jdth.13:15, Wis.17:7 *;] 1. to lie down. 2. to lie sick: before ἐπί with genitive, id. with accusative, ἐν. 3. to recline at meals: before ἐν.
(πτωχός), [in LXX: (דָּלַל); A, (יָרַשׁ); (רוּשׁ), Tob.4:21 *;] 1. to be a beggar, to beg (so chiefly in cl.). 2. to be poor as a beggar, to be destitute, poor: opposite to πλούσιος ὤν.

1. to dress, clothe, wrap up, (Pindar); ἔπηξα δ᾽ αὐτὸν εὖ περιστείλας I planted the sword having wrapt it well with earth, i. e. planted it firmly, (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. to dress or lay out a corpse, Lat. componere, (Odyssey by Homer), attic: simply, to bury, (Plato Philosophus) 3. metaphorically to wrap up, cloak, cover, τἄδικ᾽ εὖ π…
[in LXX: (יָוָן), 1Ma.1:1 1Mac *;] with varying usage as to geographical limits; in NT = 'Αχαία, Greece.
θέμεν to throw a cloud over, (Pindar)
ἔν-ειμι 1. to be in, within: ptcp. pl., τὰ ἐνόντα. 2. to be possible: (R, mg.).
(τηρέω), [in LXX: Wis.6:18, (Sir.32:23), 1Ma.5:18, 2Ma.3:40, 3Ma.5:44 *;] 1. a watching, hence, imprisonment, ward. 2. a keeping: τ. ἐντολῶν.
ἐπι-νεύω [in LXX: (נָכַר ni.), 1Ma.6:57, 2Ma.4:10 2Mac 2Mac *;] to nod in command or approval, to nod approval, consent.
[in LXX: Wis.2:24 Ma.8:16, 3Ma.6:7 *;] envy: διὰ φθόνον, πρὸς φθόνον ἐπιποθεῖ τ. πνεῦμα.
(-ους), τό (ἔθω), [in LXX: Wis.14:16, Da TH Bel 15, 1Ma.10:89, 2Ma.11:25 Ma.18:5 א R*;] habit, custom; in, almost in the narrower sense of law (Deiss., BS, 251 f.).
[in LXX: (אֲגַם), (בְּרֵכָה) 1Ma.11:35, 2Ma.12:16 *;] a lake: of the Sea of Galilee, λ. Γεννησαρέτ, λ. τ. πυρός, καιομένη πυρί.
ἔν-τρομος, -ον [in LXX: Da TH (רָעַד hi.); ἔ. γίγνεσθαι, (רַעַשׁ), Wis.17:10, 1Ma.13:2 *;] trembling with fear (Pint.): (ἔκτρ-, WH, mg.).
ἐμ-βαίνω [in LXX for עָלָה,] to step into: (WH, RV omit); εἰς πλοῖον, to embark.

κατ-αλλάσσω [in LXX: (חָתַת), 2Ma.1:5 2Mac 2Mac *;] prop., to change, exchange; hence, of persons, to change from emnity to friendship, to reconcile: of the reconciliation of man to God (Lft., Notes, 288; ICC on Ro, l.with; DCG, ii, 474, 797), pass; of a woman returning to her husband.
not to be withstood, irresistible, (Xenophon Historicus)
[in LXX: (חָתַם), Wis.2:5 *;] to seal up, secure with a seal.

ἐξ-ουθενέω, -ῶ, [in LXX: and as seel. for -δενέω, -όω, -θενόω*;] to set at nought, despise utterly, treat with contempt: with accusative of person(s), with accusative of thing(s), pass., of persons: (T, -όω), of things λίθος, (LXX ἀπεδοκίμασαν); λόγος, τὰ ἐξουθενημένα. SYN.: ἀθετέω, καταφρονέω
unspeakable, unspeakably many or great, (Demosthenes Orator)
συν-αρπάζω [in LXX: (לָקַח), 2Ma.3:27 2Mac Ma.5:4 *;] "perfective " of ἁοπάζω, (a) to seize and carry away (so most commonly): (b) to seize and hold.
(μέλει), [in LXX: (מָרָה) (בַּעַל), Wis.3:10, 2Ma.4:14 *;] (a) absol., to be careless, not to care: (b) with genitive, to be careless of, to neglect.
(ἀνάγκη), [in LXX: Wis.16:3, Sir prol.22, 2Ma.4:23 2Mac Ma.1:2 *;] 1. necessary: comp. -αιότερον. 2. Of persons connected by bonds of nature or friendship, near, intimate: ἀ. φίλοι.

(κατά, ἀγορεύω), [in LXX: Dan LXX, (9), 1Ma.7:6 1Mac Ma.4:47 2Mac 2Mac Ma.9:14 *;] to make accusation, accuse, (a) in general: absol., with genitive of person(s) (cl., WM, 254), irreg. with accusative of person(s), (b) before a judge: absol., with genitive of person(s), (WH, txt., R, om.), id. with accusative of thing(s)…
προ-δότης, -ου, ὁ (προδίδωμι) [in LXX: 2Ma.5:15 2Mac 2Mac Ma.3:24 *;] a betrayer, traitor.
[in LXX: Dan LXX Ma.5:26 2Mac Ma.5:24 *;] 1. a viewing. 2. = θεώρημα, a spectacle, sight: (both senses in cl.).
ἀ-θέμιτος, -ον (θέμις, custom, right), [in LXX: 2Ma.6:5 Ma.5:20 *;] (a) of persons, lawless (III Mac, l.with); (b) of things, lawless, unlawful. SYN.: see: ἄθεσμος.
(φιλάνθρωπος, humane), [in LXX: Ma.6:22 2Mac Ma.3:15 3Mac *;] humanity, kindness.

1. to shew fort, display, produce, (Herdotus Historicus) 2. to make known, declare, (Herdotus Historicus): to give evidence of a thing, (Herdotus Historicus) 3. to shew by reasoning, shew, represent as doing or being, with participle, (Herdotus Historicus); and with participle omitted, ἀπ. ἑωϋτὸν αἴτιον (i.e. ὄντα) (Herdotus Historicus)…
deemed or to be deemed happy, enviable, (Herdotus Historicus), attic
παρ-αινέω, -ω [in LXX: 2Ma.7:25-26, 3Ma.5:17 3Mac *;] to exhort, advise: with accusative of person(s) and inf., absol., before λέγων.
ἄ-δηλος, -ον (δῆλος), [in LXX: Ps 50 (51):6 (בַּטֻחוֹת);] 1. unseen, unobserved, not manifest (Ps, l.with). 2. uncertain, indistinct.

1. to send forth, send to war, (Aeschulus Tragicus); ἐξ. τὴν ναῦν to start the ship, set it agoing, (Thucydides):—;Pass. to set out, start, (Herdotus Historicus), of arrows, to spring from the bow, (Euripides) 2. to excite to action, urge on, (Euripides) 3. intransitive, like Pass., to set out, start, of a ship…
κατ-αξιόω, -ῶ [in LXX: 2Ma.13:12, 3Ma.3:21 3Mac Ma.18:3 *;] to deem worthy: with accusative of person(s) and genitive of thing(s), pass. before inf..

1. to cut off, sever, (Iliad by Homer), attic:—;Pass., τὴν γλῶτταν ἀποτμηθείς having his tongue cut out, (Aeschines Orator) 2. to sever, divide, in a geographical sense, (Herdotus Historicus):—;Pass., of troops, to be cut off from the main body, (Xenophon Historicus) 3. Mid. to cut off for oneself, (Iliad by Homer)…

1. to pursue or practise a thing, make a practice of, make it one's business, Lat. studere rei, with accusative, (Herdotus Historicus), attic:—;also, ἐπ. τι πρός τι to invent for a purpose, (Herdotus Historicus); Pass. to be done with pains and practice, to be made so and so by art, (Herdotus Historicus); of dogs, to be trained…

1. to make close, cover or wrap up, enwrap, (Iliad by Homer); π. νῆα λίθοισι to surround a ship with stones, so as to protect it when laid up, (Hesiod):—; to cover thickly, of a youth's chin, (Odyssey by Homer); πυκ. στεφάνοις to cover thick with crowns, (Euripides); so in Mid.…
[in LXX: (יָד) (חֵלֶק) (מוֹקֵשׁ), 3Ma.4:8 *;] a noose, a slip-knot, a halter: metaphorically, a restraint (not, as AV, R, txt., a snare).

1. pitiable, in piteous plight, (Iliad by Homer), 2. of things, pitiable, piteous, lamentable, (Herdotus Historicus), 3. in active sense, piteous, (Odyssey by Homer); οἰκτρᾶς γόον ὄρνιθος, of the nightingale, (Sophocles Tragicus);—;neuter plural as regularly adverb οἰκτρῶς, (Aeschulus Tragicus) —;Besides comparative and Sup. οἰκτρότερος…
(in Att.. also πρανής), [in LXX: Wis.4:19, 3Ma.5:43 3Mac 3Mac *;] headlong, prone.
to be reproached, shameful, ignominious, (Euripides); ἐπονείδιστόν ἐστι is matter of reproach, (Demosthenes Orator)
1. a joy, (Euripides); plural joys, delights, (Euripides) 2. = χάρμα II, joy, delight, (Sophocles Tragicus)
ἀνα-φαίνομαι [in LXX for צָדַק hi., גָּלַשׁ;] to bring to light, make to appear: ἀναφάναντες τ. Κύπρον, i.e. having sighted C.: WH; pass., to appear, be made manifest
(= καί τοι, and so also written in cl.) concessive particle, [in LXX: 4Ma.2:6 *;] and yet, although: with ptcp..
(ἦθος), [in LXX: 4Ma.2:12 4Mac 4Mac 4Mac *;] 1 1 intimacy. 2. habit, custom: with genitive obj., habitual use, force of habit with respect to.

1. to swear in excuse, (Demosthenes Orator): to swear in the negative, ἐξ. τὸ μὴ εἰδέναι (Sophocles Tragicus):—;mostly in Mid., to deny or disown upon oath, swear formally that one does not know a thing, (Demosthenes Orator), 2. to decline an office by oath that one cannot perform it, (Aeschines Orator)
(-κία, T), -ας, ἡ (θρῆσκος), [in LXX: Wis.14:18, 27, Sir.22:5 A, 4Ma.5:6 4Mac *;] religion in its external aspect (MM, Exp., xv), worship: θ. τῶν ἀγγέλων. SYN.: see: θρῆσκος

1. to have enjoyment of a thing, to have the benefit of it, to enjoy, with genitive, (Herdotus Historicus), attic:—;with accusative added, ἀπολαύειν τί τινος to enjoy an advantage from some source, (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. ironically, to have the benefit of, τῶν Οἰδίπου κακῶν (Euripides): —;absolute to have a benefit, come finely off…
(παιδεύω), [in LXX: (מוּסָר), Sir.37:19, 4Ma.5:34 4Mac *;] 1. prop., a teacher, instructor. 2. a corrector, one who disciplines.
1. Dep. 2. to leap in or upon, with dative, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 3. to rush against (Sophocles Tragicus) 4. absolute to dance, (Aristophanes Comicus)
[in LXX: 4Ma.6:9 4Mac *;] 1. to examine on all sides, consider carefully (Aristoph.). 2. = ὑπερφρονέω, to have thouphts beyond, to despise.

suffering, wretched, Lat. miser, (Odyssey by Homer); ὦ τάλαιν᾽ ἐγώ (Aeschulus Tragicus); ὦ τάλαν (Sophocles Tragicus);—;with genitive causae, τάλαιν᾽ ἐγὼ τῆς ὕβρεως wretched that I am for this insolence, (Aristophanes Comicus):—;in bad sense, τάλαν wretch! (Odyssey by Homer)—;comparative τᾶλάντερος, η, ον: Sup. τᾶλάντατος, η, ον…
(χαρίζομαι), [in LXX: Wis.16:29, Sir.29:17, 25, 4Ma.9:10 *;] (a) ungracious, unpleasing; (b) ungrateful, thankless.
[in LXX: (שְׂרוֹךְ), Sir.33:26, 4Ma.9:11, al;] a thong, strap: for binding prisoners (Ma, Sir, ll. with), for fastening sandals, Mk.
(μῖμος, a mimic, an actor), [in LXX: Wis.4:2 Ma.9:23 4Mac: *;] to imitate.

εὐ-σεβέω, -ῶ, [in LXX: Dan LXX Sus Ma.9:6 אR, 4Ma.11:5 4Mac 4Mac 4Mac *;] to reverence, show piety towards; with accusative (else­where more frequently before εἰς., περί, πρός): οἶκον, θεόν, (Cremer, 525).
(σύμφωνος), [in LXX: Dan LXX TH, TH (סוּמְפּוֹנְיָה) 4Ma.14:3 A *;] 1. symphony, music: 2. a musical instrument.
marks of virginity; tokens of virginity
[in LXX for רוּם, רָתַח, metaphorically, 4Ma.18:20;] to boil, be hot; metaphorically, of anger, love, zeal: ptcp., fervent: τ. πνεύματι.

1. like αὐτόχθων, earthborn, of the primeval men, (Herdotus Historicus) 2. born of Gaia or Tellus, of the Titans and Giants, (Aeschulus Tragicus); so of things, portentous, furious, (Aristophanes Comicus)
συν-κατα-βαίνω (Rec. συγκ-), [in LXX: (יָרַד), Wis.10:13, Dan LXX TH *;] to go down with. In late writers also metaphorically (Wis, l.with), to condescend, on WH. see Rutherford, NPhr., 485 f.
(δύναμις), [in LXX for עָזַז, גָּבַר pi., hi., Da TH *;] to make strong, strengthen: (WH, mg.; ἐνδυν-, WH, txt., RV).
1. Lat. mola, a mill, a handmill turned by women, (Odyssey by Homer) 2. the nether millstone, (Aristophanes Comicus); the upper being ὄνος, (Aristophanes Comicus)
τό (ὑπό, πούς), [in LXX: La (הֲדֹם) *;] a footstool (= cl. θρᾶνος): metaphorically, (ὑποκάτω, WH, R, mg.), (all, except Mt, l.with, from LXX,).
a stepping upon, approaching: a means of approach, access, (Plato Philosophus); εἴς τινα ποιεῖσθαι ἐπ. to find a means of attacking one, (Herdotus Historicus)
the inwards, entrails, bowels, Lat. intestina, (Homer)

1. a rush, Lat. juncus, scirpus, (Herdotus Historicus), 2. a reed, used as an arrow or javelin, (Batrachomyomachia) 3. a place where rushes grow, a rushbed, (Odyssey by Homer) 4. a rush-rope, and generally, a rope, cord, (Oracle quoted in Herdotus Historicus) 5. a fence round a garden, [variant datesAnthology Palantina 6. a land-measure…

1. the swallow, (Odyssey by Homer),—; the twittering of the swallow was proverbially used of barbarous tongues by the Greeks, (Aeschulus Tragicus); χελιδόνων μουσεῖα; proverbs also, μία χελιδὼν ἔαρ οὐ ποιεῖ (Aristotle Philosopher) 2. the frog in a horse's foot, so called from its being forked like the swallow's tail, (Xenophon Historicus)

(διδάσκω), [in LXX: (אַלּוּף), (לָמַד), Sir.24:33 *;] teaching, instruction, in both active and objective senses, most frequently the latter: ὑγιαινοῦσα δ., pl., δ. τ. ἀνθρώπων, δ. δαιμονίων, δ. διδάσκειν, " (LXX) (Cremer, 182). SYN.: διδαχή

1. without fear: 2. fearless, intrepid, dauntless, (Pindar):—;adverb -βως, (Xenophon Historicus) 3. causing no fear, free from fear, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 4. ἄφοβοι θῆρες beasts which no one fears, i. e. cattle, (Sophocles Tragicus)
1. to let fall drop by drop, distil, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) 2. intransitive to fall in drops, distil, (Sophocles Tragicus)
[in LXX: (אִישׁ תַּחַת), Sir.9:9 *;] under or subject to a man, married: γυνή.

1. unavenged, i. e., 2. unpunished, ἀτ. γίγνεσθαι to escape punishment, (Herdotus Historicus):—; adverb -τως, with impunity, (Plato Philosophus) 3. for which no revenge has been taken, ἀτιμώρητον ἐᾶν θάνατον (Aeschines Orator) 4. undefended, unprotected, (Thucydides)
1. an arbiter, umpire, judge, with genitive rei, (Plato Philosophus); ἐπ. τῆς τιμῆς an appraiser, (Demosthenes Orator) 2. = συγγνώμων, pardoning, τινί (Moschus Bucolicus)

1. without hearing, of the dead, (Moschus Bucolicus) 2. with genitive not hearing a thing, never having heard it, ignorant of it, (Xenophon Historicus),—;absolute, σκαιὸς καὶ ἀν. ignorant, (Demosthenes Orator)

1. a stand or grate for pine and other wood used for lighting rooms, (Odyssey by Homer); ὧ χαῖρε, λ. νυκτός thou that lightest up the night, of the beacon-fire, (Aeschulus Tragicus); ἕσπεροι λαμπτῆρες the evening watch-fires, (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. generally, = λαμπάς 1 (Euripides)
a pledge put into the hand: surety, security, Lat. vadimonium, (Odyssey by Homer), attic
1. slanderous, envious, malignant, (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. as Substantive a slanderer, (Demosthenes Orator) 3. a sorcerer, (Demosthenes Orator)
1. to look aside, take a side look, (Aristophanes Comicus); π. θατέρῳ (i.e. ὀφθαλμῷ); to look suspiciously with one eye, (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. to see wrong, (Lucian)

1. to drink out or off, quaff liquor, (Odyssey by Homer): so, in perfect passive, ἐκπέποται (Odyssey by Homer); αἵματ᾽ ἐκποθένθ᾽ ὑπὸ χθονός (Aeschulus Tragicus) 2. to drain a cup dry, πλῆρες ἐκπ. κέρας (Sophocles Tragicus): metaphorically, ἐκπ. ὄλβον (Euripides)
1. Lat. fremitus, any loud noise, as the crackling of fire, (Iliad by Homer); roaring of a storm, (Aeschulus Tragicus); neighing of horses, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 2. rage, fury, (Euripides)
ἄπ-ειμι (εἰμί, sum) [in LXX for כָּחַד ni., נָדַח ni.;] to be absent.
1. to draw up in order, arrange, τὴν στρατιάν (Xenophon Historicus) 2. to appoint, ἐπί τι to do a thing, (Demosthenes Orator) 3. κατατάξασθαί τινι to make arrangements with one, (Demosthenes Orator)
to twist, twirl or whirl about, (Aristophanes Comicus):—;metaphorically to make dizzy, distract, (Aeschulus Tragicus): —;Pass. to whirl about, (Aeschulus Tragicus)
to discharge at, with dative, (Xenophon Historicus)
1. to flame up, take fire, (Xenophon Historicus) 2. metaphorically to break out anew, as war, (Plutarch) 3. to come to oneself again, revive, (Plutarch)

[in LXX: (יָבֵשׁ pi.), Wis.2:8 *;] in cl., 1. prop., to quench fire; pass., of fire, to die away, go out. 2. In various relations, to quench, waste, wear out; pass., to waste away; in later writers, of the withering of flowers and herbage (act., pass., Wis.2:8).
τό (ἐντέλλω), [in LXX: (אָשֻׁר), (מִצְוָה), (aliter in Heb.)*;] a precept: pl., (LXX).
δι-ορύσσω [in LXX: (חָתַר) *;] to dig through: with accusative, of house-breaking (as in π.; MM, Exp., xi), absol..
1. a lump of earth, a clod, Lat. gleba, (Odyssey by Homer) 2. like Lat. gleba, land, ground, soil, (Moschus Bucolicus)
1. throwing stones, (Xenophon Historicus) 2. as Substantive, πετροβόλος, an engine for throwing stones, Lat. ballista, (Polybius Historicus)

1. to hearken to, listen to, with genitive pers., accusative rei, (Thucydides), with genitive rei, (Thucydides) 2. absolute to listen, ὁ ἀκροώμενος a hearer, disciple, (Plato Philosophus) 3. to attend to, obey, τινός (Thucydides)
(ἀσφαλής), [in LXX: (חָזַק hi.), (תָּמַךְ), Wis.4:17 *;] to make firm, secure: mid., pass..

1. to make like to, represent by a likeness, portray, (Xenophon Historicus); εἰκὼν γραφῆι εἰκασμένη a figure painted to the life, (Herdotus Historicus); αἰετὸς εἰκασμένος a figure like an eagle, (Herdotus Historicus) 2. to liken, compare, τί τινι (Aeschulus Tragicus); εἰκ. τι καί τι (Herdotus Historicus): to describe by a comparison…
(ὄρθρος), [in LXX: (שָׁכַם hi.), Wis.11:22 *;] late form of ὄρθριος, early.
(ῥίζα), [in LXX: (שָׁרַשׁ), Sir.3:28 *;] to cause to take root. Metaphorical, to plant, fix firmly, establish: pass. (EV, rooted), ἐν ἀγάπῃ, (17); ἐν Χριστῷ.

1. to draw aside, pervert, (Pindar): —;Mid. to draw aside to oneself, draw away from, τί τινος (Odyssey by Homer) 2. to lead alongside, as one does a led horse, (Herdotus Historicus); παρέλκειν ἐκ γῆς to tow [boats] from the bank, (Herdotus Historicus) 3. κενὰς παρέλκειν (i.e. τὰς κώπας)…
1. want of education, (Thucydides) 2. ignorance, boorishness, coarseness, (Plato Philosophus), 3. with genitive, ἀπαιδευσίαι ὀργῆς from want of control over passion, (Thucydides)
to dry up things, of the wind, (Iliad by Homer); to dry up a stream, (Herdotus Historicus)

ἀ-σύν-θετος, -ον, [in LXX: (בָּגַד)*;] false to engagements, not keeping covenant, faithless.

1. the hollow of a shield or breastplate, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 2. any vessel, a vase, jar, urn, (Aeschulus Tragicus), πλεκτὸν κ. a basket, (Euripides) 3. anything that contains the body, (Sophocles Tragicus)
(Heb. גַּבְרִיאֵל, hero of God), the archangel Gabriel.

fit for ordering or arranging, especially in war, τ. ἀνήρ a tactician, (Xenophon Historicus); τακτικὸν ἡγεῖσθαί τι to think it a good piece of tactics, (Xenophon Historicus); οἱ τ. ἀριθμοί the regular battalions, (Xenophon Historicus): τὰ τακτικά the art of drawing up soldiers in array, tactics, (Xenophon Historicus)

of three stories or floors, (Herdotus Historicus)

1. to lie in, be wrapped in clothes, (Iliad by Homer) 2. ἔγκεισθαί τινι to be involved in a thing, (Euripides) 3. to press upon, of troops pressing upon the enemy, (Thucydides):—;with an adjective or adverb, πολλὸς ἐνέκειτο was very urgent, (Herdotus Historicus); πολὺς ἔγκειται he insists much upon a thing, with dative…

intransitive to make haste in a thing, (Lucian)

(βάλλω), [in LXX: (טחה), 2Ma.5:3, 3Ma.5:26 *;] a throw; λίθου β. (Thuc., v, 65, 2), a stone's throw.

(κῦρος, 1. authority. 2. validity), [in LXX for קוּם;] to confirm, ratify, make valid: pass..

1. to run upon or at, for the purpose of attack, (Iliad by Homer); of dogs, (Odyssey by Homer); so in attic to make an assault upon, τινί (Thucydides) 2. to run after, ἐπιδραμών in haste, eagerly, (Herdotus Historicus) 3. to run over a space, (Iliad by Homer): to run over or graze the surface, (Iliad by Homer) 4. to be spread over…
[in LXX: (אָמַר), Dan LXX Bel Ma.14:27 2Mac Ma.3:7 *;] to affirm, assert: with accusative and inf., with inf. and nom..
[in LXX: R (חָלַק, חַלֻּק); ὁδὸς λ., Α (בִּקְעָה); *;] smooth: opposite to τραχύς, (LXX).

anything used for anointing, unguent, fat, oil, (Plato Philosophus)

abiding by, steadfast, (Xenophon Historicus); ἔμμ. τινι abiding by a thing, (Xenophon Historicus)

a cleft: in (Odyssey by Homer), ῥῶγες μεγάροιο are narrow passages leading to the hall.

1. to cut in pieces, cut up, (Herdotus Historicus), so in Mid., (Euripides):—; Pass., τελαμῶσι κατατετμημένοις with regularly cut bandages, (Herdotus Historicus); σπλάγχνα κατατετμημένα (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. κ. χώρην ἐς διώρυχας to cut it up into ditches or canals, (Herdotus Historicus)…

adv. (ἀκριβής), [in LXX: (יָטַב), Da TH (יְצֵב), Wis.19:18, Sir.18:29;] with exactness, carefully: (M, Th., in l). Compar., ἀκριβέστερον.

1. carrying water, (Plutarch) 2. as Substantive, ὑδρ., a water-carrier, (Herdotus Historicus)

a terse pointed saying, an apophthegm, (Xenophon Historicus)

[in LXX: (בָּצַע), B*;] 1. intrans., to have more, to have an advantage (cl., with genitive of person(s)). 2. Trans., in late writers, to over­reach, defraud: with accusative of person(s), ἐν τ. πράγματιι, pass..
to roll down:—;Pass. to be rolled down or thrown off, (Herdotus Historicus)
that in which a thing is dipped, dye, (Plato Philosophus), see. βάπτω I. 3.

hung, hung up, hanging, κρ. αὐχένος hung by the neck, (Sophocles Tragicus); with genitive, also, hung from or on a thing, (Euripides): —; κρεμαστὴ ἀρτάνη, i. e. a halter, (Sophocles Tragicus); so, βρόχοι κρ. (Euripides)
a crescent, Lat. lunula: a covering to protect the head of statues (like the nimbus or glory of Christian Saints), (Aristophanes Comicus)

1. the navel, Lat. umbilicus, (Iliad by Homer), 2. anything central (like a navel): 3. the knob or boss in the middle of the shield, Lat. umbo, (Iliad by Homer) 4. a button or knob on the horse's yoke to fasten the reins to, (Iliad by Homer) 5. in plural the knobs at each end of the stick round which books were rolled, Lat. umbilici…
[in LXX: (פַּרְנַךְ),] to break, break in pieces: of bread, before εἰς, with accusative of person(s).
τό, [in LXX: (סָדִין), (פִּשְׁתֶּה)*;] a piece of fine linen, a linen cloth; (WH, R, mg., om.).
ἀν-αίρεσις, -εως, ἡ (ἀναιρέω), [in LXX: (הָרַג), (רָמָה), Jdth.15:4, 2Ma.5:13 *;] 1. a taking up or away (Thuc.). 2. a destroying, slaying, murder.
[in LXX: (לַח), (רָשׂב), Sir.39:13 wet, moist, opposite to ξηρός: of wood, sappy, green.
(ῥαπίς, a rod), [in LXX: I *;] 1. prop., to strike with a rod. 2. In late writers, to strike (the face) with the palm of the hand: with accusative of person(s), before εἰς τ. σιαγόνα.

1. to speak to one, to address, accost, (Homer), πρ. ὀνόματί τινα (Demosthenes Orator):—;with double accusative, τί προσείπω ς᾽ ἔπο; (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. to address as so and so, πρ. τινὰ ὡς ἀλλότριον (Plato Philosophus); πρ. τινὰ χαίρειν to bid him greeting, (Euripides) 3. to call so and so, to name…
[in LXX: before ἐπί, (דָּפַק);] with, accusative, τ. αὐλαίαν, Jdth.14:14 *;] to strike, knock: at a door (Κόπτειν, in Att..), with accusative, τ. θύραν.
(Ἑσρών, Lk, l.with; Rec. Ἑσρ-), ὁ, [in LXX both forms, ut supr.;] Esrom (AV), Hezron (RV), an ancestor of Jesus.
ἀπ-ελαύνω [in LXX for נָצַל, שָׁלַח;] to drive away.
sucking, young, tender, (Odyssey by Homer); γαλαθηνά (i.e. πρόβατα), (Herdotus Historicus)
1. a cook, (Herdotus Historicus), attic 2. a butcher, (Euripides) (From ! μαγ, Root of μάσσω, because baking bread was the business of the ancient cook.)
[in LXX for צָלַח, *;] to leap upon: before ἐπί with accusative of person(s).
[in LXX: (לָכַד ni.), A (קָרָא ni.), *;] 1. to cast lots. 2. to choose by lot. 3. to assign by lot, assign a portion: pass., ἐν ᾧ καὶ ἐκληρώθημεν.
divination by the flight or cries of birds, Lat. augurium, (Euripides)
ἀνα-κρίνω [in LXX: (חָקַר), Dan LXX Su, LXX, TH Su *;] to examine, investigate, question (Lft., Notes, 181 f.): in forensic sense. SYN.: see: ἐξετάζω

1. to hurl a javelin, τινός at one, (Iliad by Homer); ἐπί τινι (Iliad by Homer):—;the weapon is put in dative, ἀκόντισε δουρί darted with his spear, (Iliad by Homer); also in accusative, ἀκόντισαν ὀξέα δοῦρα darted their spears, (Odyssey by Homer) 2. with accusative pers. to hit with a javelin, (Herdotus Historicus), Pass…

1. to pick up, gather up, ὀστέα (Iliad by Homer):—;Mid. to pick up for oneself, (Herdotus Historicus); ἀν. πνεῦμα to collect one's breath, [variant datesAnthology Palantina 2. to reckon up, τὸν χρόνον (Plutarch): —;Pass., ἀναλεγόμενον being recounted, (Xenophon Historicus)
1. caught or detected in anything, (Sophocles Tragicus); with participle, ἐπίλαμπτος ἀφάσσουσα caught in the act of feeling, (Herdotus Historicus) 2. suffering, (Demosthenes Orator)

1. to stick fast in the ground, plant firmly, (Iliad by Homer), 2. Pass., with perfect and pluperfect active, to stand fast or firm in, (Iliad by Homer); absolute, στήλη καταπεπηγυῖα (Herdotus Historicus)
to be or go lame, (Plato Philosophus)
(καθαρός), [in LXX: (דּוּשׁ ho.), א*;] to cleanse: of pruning.
to whisper, say into the ear, (Plato Philosophus):—;metaphorically, ὅταν πλάτανος πτελέᾳ ψιθυρίζῃ when the plane whispers to the elm, (Aristophanes Comicus)

1. intransitive to be bereaved of a person or thing, with genitive, (Odyssey by Homer) 2. absolute to be bereaved of a husband, to be widowed, live in widowhood, (Demosthenes Orator),—;of a man, to be a widower, (Plutarch); so, χηρεύσει λέχος (Euripides) 3. to live in solitude, of an exile, (Sophocles Tragicus) 4. transitive to bereave…
a deposit made by water, πρ. Νείλου, of the Delta of the Nile, (Aeschulus Tragicus) from προσχώννυ_μι

to make holy, purify, set free from guilt by offerings, Lat. expiate, (Euripides):—;Mid., στόμα ὁσιοῦσθαι to keep one's tongue pure, not to speak profanely, (Euripides):—;Pass. to be purified, (Plutarch)

twisted, crooked, (Aristotle Philosopher); of the brows, knit, wrinkled, [variant datesAnthology Palantina: metaphorically, στρεβλοῖσι παλαίσμασι by cunning dodges in wrestling, (Aristophanes Comicus)

1. to smooth or polish, (Homer); ἵπποισι κέλευθον λειανέω I will smooth the way, (Iliad by Homer) 2. to rub smooth, pound in a mortar, Lat. levigare, (Herdotus Historicus); to grind with the teeth, (Xenophon Historicus):—; generally, to crush, extirpate, (Herdotus Historicus) 3. to smooth away wrinkles…

1. the ceiling of a room, or (rather) the main beam which bears the ceiling, (Odyssey by Homer); in (Odyssey by Homer) 19. 544, the end of this beam outside the house. 2. generally, a roof, (Homer) 3. a house, hall, (Pindar); mostly in plural, like Lat. tecta, [variant datesTragica Adespota derivation uncertain
1. talk, prattle, (Moschus Bucolicus) 2. a prater, (Sophocles Tragicus)
closely shaded, thickly shaded, (Xenophon Historicus); σύσκιόν τι a closely-shaded place, (Lucian)
Ayin, the 16th letter of the Hebrew alphabet; used in LXX for acrostic Psalms such as
(Ob 20), τά (Heb. צָרְפַת), Sarepta, a city of Sidon.
[in LXX: (עָנָה),] to bear witness againt: with accusative of thing(s) and genitive of person(s).

1. to break up the ground, (Iliad by Homer) 2. to break through a wall, (Iliad by Homer):—;Pass., ἡ ναῦς ἀναρρήγνυται τὴν παρεξειρεσίαν the ship has its bow broken through, (Thucydides) 3. to tear open a carcase, of lions, (Iliad by Homer); of Ajax, δίχα ἀνερρήγνυ was cleaving them asunder, (Sophocles Tragicus) 4. to make to break forth…
δανιστής, -οῦ, ὁ, [in LXX: 4, (109):11 (נשׁה), (רָשׁ), Sir.29:28 *;] a money-lender.

to deceive utterly, (Demosthenes Orator):—; Pass. to be deceived, mistaken, (Demosthenes Orator); δ. τινος to be cheated of, deceived in a person or thing, (Xenophon Historicus); περί τι or τινι (Aristotle Philosopher)
συν-κάμπτω (Rec. συγκ-), [in LXX: (מעד hi.),] to bend completely, bend together: τ. νῶτον, figuratively, (LXX).

1. Dep.: 2. to set up as a pretext or excuse, allege by way of excuse, plead in excuse, with accusative, (Theognis Elegiacus), with infinitive to allege as an excuse that.., (Demosthenes Orator):—;absolute to make excuses, (Thucydides):—;aor1 προφασισθῆναι in passive sense, to be used as a pretext, (Thucydides) 3…

(βάπτω), [in LXX: 4 (טבל), Jdth.12:7, Sir.31 (34)30 *;] to dip, immerse, sink; 1. generally (in Polyb., iii, 72, of soldiers wading breast-deep; in i, 51, of the sinking of ships); metaphorically, to overwhelm; with cogn. accusative, βάπτισμα β.. Mid., 2. to perform ablutions, wash oneself, bathe (Ki, Jth, Si, ll. with): aor. pass…
προ-δίδωμι [in LXX: A (נָתַן), 4Ma.4:1,] 1. to give before, give first: ( (11) LXX,). 2. to betray (4Mac, l.with).

1. to be a horseman or rider, to ride, (Herdotus Historicus), attic:—;so in Mid., (Herdotus Historicus) 2. metaphorically of the wind, (Euripides) 3. to be a trooper, serve in the cavalry, (Xenophon Historicus) 4. of a horse, as we say "the horse rides (i. e. carries his rider) well," (Xenophon Historicus)

to bore through, pierce, perforate, (Homer):—;Pass., λίθος τετρημένος (Herdotus Historicus); ὁ οὐρανὸς τέτρηται the sky has holes in it, (Herdotus Historicus); χάσμα τῆς γῆς τετρημένον a chasm formed by perforating the earth, (Plato Philosophus)

1. to make sharp or pointed, sharpen, whet, (Hesiod) 2. to furnish with notches or teeth, like a saw, (Aristotle Philosopher):—;Pass., σκύταλον κεχ. ὄζοις a staff jagged or rugged with branches, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus): metaphorically, [ ὄμμα] ἠλεμάτοις ἀκτῖσι χαράσσεται sparkles with false lights…
Ion. and κοινή form of Att. κναφεύς (κνάπτω, to card wool), [in LXX for כָּבַס, 4, *;] a fuller, cloth-dresser.
1. made of reed, (Herdotus Historicus) 2. made of cane, (Herdotus Historicus)
(φυτεύω), [in LXX: 4 (נָטַע), (מַטָּע) *;] 1. a planting. 2. = φύτευμα, that which is planted, a plant (Inscr.).
1. to soften, (Xenophon Historicus) 2. to make tender, τοὺς πόδας (Xenophon Historicus)
indecl., Moloch, the god of the Ammonites: (LXX).
a station for περίπολοι, a guard-house, (Thucydides)

- ῆς, ἡ (ά αβάλλω), [in LXX for בּנף,] delay.
to set in a place, place in position, (Xenophon Historicus):—;Pass. to take up a position, (Xenophon Historicus)
(γεωργός), [in LXX: (עָשָׂה מְלֶאכֶת הַשָּׂדֶה), I Ma.14:8 *;] to till the ground: pass..
ἐκ-τελέω, -ῶ [in LXX: (כָּלָה), (Da TH), 2Ma.15:9 *;] to bring to an end, finish, complete.
(στρώννυμι), [in LXX: (רִצְפָּה, רָצַף)*;] paved with stones, esp. of tessallated work (Ca, i.e.); as subst., τὸ λ., a tessallated pavement.
(περιποιέω), [in LXX: (12) (מִחְיָה) (סְגֻלָּה), (9) *;] 1. preservation: (2 Ch, l.with). 2. acquisition, obtaining. 3. a possession: (LXX).
1. a carrying out of a corpse to burial, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 2. (from Pass.) of horses, a running away, (Xenophon Historicus)
τό (θυμιάω), [in LXX: (קְטֹרֶת), 4Ma.7:11 *;] 1. as in cl. (Hdt., iv, 162; Thuc., vi, 46) and LXX, a censer. 2. As in Philo., rer. div., § 46, FlJ, Ant., iv, 2, 4, the altar of incense: He, l.with.
(σάρξ), [in LXX: (בָּשָׂר), *;] = Lat. carneus, of the flesh, of flesh, fleshy. (Rec. has -ικός in all these passages except, but the evidence is decisive against it.) SYN.: σαρκικός, q.v

1. to urge on, further or promote an object, (Herdotus Historicus): of persons, to urge on, (Xenophon Historicus) 2. intransitive to hasten onward, (Euripides); ἐπισπ. εἴς τι to be zealous for, aim at an object, (Xenophon Historicus)

(ἵστωρ, one learned or skilled in) [in LXX: 1Es.1:3 *;] 1. with accusative of thing(s), to inquire into, learn by inquiry. 2. C. accusative of person(s), to inquire of or about. 3. to narrate, record. 4. In late writers, to visit, become acquainted with.
[in LXX: (קָרָא), I *;] to call from one place to another. Mid., to send for: with accusative.
τό [in LXX: (כֶּסֶת), I *;] a pillow, cushion.
to listen to a thing, with genitive, (Sophocles Tragicus)

1. to look laughing at one, τινά (Herdotus Historicus), with accusative cognate, προσγελᾶτε τὸν πανύστατον γέλων smile your last smile upon me, (Euripides) 2. metaphorically, like Lat. arrideo, to delight, ὀσμὴ βροτείων αἱμάτων με προσγελᾷ (Aeschulus Tragicus)
to flatter, (Aristophanes Comicus),—; Pass. to be flattered, be open to flattery, (Demosthenes Orator)
τό, [in LXX: I Ma.3:28 1Mac *;] 1. provisions, provision-money, soldiers' pay. 2. Generally, wages, hire: ὄ. τῆς ἁμαρτίας.
refrain, receive/be far, keep away from

(ἀργός), [in LXX: (בָּטֵל), I, Sir.33:27), 2Ma.5:25 *;] to be idle; τὸ κρίμα... ἀ., lingers.
[in LXX: Dan LXX (מָרַט) *;] to pluck, pluck off: στάχυας.
an advanced guard: οἱ προφύλακες = αἱ προφυλακαί, (Thucydides)
[in LXX: (יָחַשׂ) *;] 1. a journey in company. 2. By meton., κ company of travellers, a caravan.
1. = μύρτος, (Pindar) 2. a branch or wreath of myrtle, (Herdotus Historicus)
to throw out foam, of the sea:—;Pass., of ships, to be cast ashore, (Herdotus Historicus)
Dep. to be seated beside or near another, with dative, (Aristophanes Comicus)

[in LXX: (גָּזַר ni.), Wis.4:16, Dan LXX TH Sus, TH Sus *;] to give judgment against, condemn: with accusative of person(s), disting. fr. κρίνειν, before θανάτῳ (cl. -ου or -ον), pass.. Metaphorical, of condemning through a good example
μετ-έπειτα, adv. [in LXX: Jdth.9:5, Ma.3:24 *;] after­wards.
(πρῶτος) [in LXX: Ma.6:18 2Mac *;] to be first, pre-eminent, have the first place.

[in LXX: (עֲבֹדָה, with seel., ἀποσκ-, κατασκ-), Jdth.2:17 Ma.9:35 א, 2Ma.15:21 *;] 1. preparation. 2. equipment (Jth, ll with). 3. In Jewish usage, the day of preparation for a Sabbath or a feast: with genitive, τοῦ πάσχα, τ. Ἰoυδαίων, (it is the name for Friday in MGr.).

1. easily handled, easy to deal with, easy, εὐχερές ἐστι, with infinitive, (Batrachomyomachia); πάντα ταῦτ᾽ ἐν εὐχερεῖ ἔθου didst make light of them, (Sophocles Tragicus):—;adverb -ρῶς, (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. of persons, manageable, accommodating, kind, yielding, (Sophocles Tragicus):—;adverb, εὐχερῶς φέρειν (Plato Philosophus)…
πρό-δηλος, -ον [in LXX: Jdth.8:29, 2Ma.3:17 2Mac *;] 1. evident beforehand. 2. clearly evident.

to bear oneself proudly, prance, of horses, (Plutarch); and in Mid., (Xenophon Historicus):—;metaphorically to pride oneself on a thing, with dative, (Demosthenes Orator); ἐπί σφισι (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus)
[in LXX: Jdth.10:5 *;] a leathern pouch for victuals, a wallet.
[in LXX: Jdth.13:6, 4Ma.7:21 (and in Aq.,)*;] 1. a rod or bar (Jth, l.with). 2. a measuring rule; hence, metaph, 3. a rule or standard. 4. a limit (RV, province).
ὑπο νοέω, -ῶ [in LXX: Da TH (סְבַר), Tob.8:16, Jdth.14:14, Sir.23:21 *;] to suspect, conjecture: with accusative and inf..
(Att.. -ττω, and so 4Ma.14:9 4Mac) [in LXX: ( pi.),] 1. to be rough, bristle. 2. to shiver, shudder, tremble, from fear.

κατ-έρχομαι [in LXX: Tob.1:22, א Tob.2:1, Wis.11:22, 2Ma.11:29 *;] to come down, go down: before εἰς, Τ; ἀπό, ἀπό and εἰς, of coming to port by ship, before πρός, with accusative of person(s), metaphorically, of gifts from God.
τό (οἰκέω), [in LXX: (גַב), Tob.2:4, Wis.13:15 *;] a dwelling. As a euphemism for other definite terms, a prison (Thus., iv, 47 f.).
(ὄχλος), [in LXX: Tob.6:7, 3Ma.5:41 *;] to move, disturb; hence, generally, to trouble, vex: pass..
[in LXX: (קרע). Tob.2:10 *;] to rub in, anoint: mid., with dupl. accusative.
[in LXX: (לחם), Tob.7:8, Dan LXX *;] to take the chief meal of the day, to dine, to sup: (WH, br., R, mg. omits), metaphorically.
συν-πάρειμι (Rec. σνμπ-), [in LXX: Tob.12:12 ΑΒ, (?), Wis.9:10 *;] to be present together or with: with dative of person(s).

[in LXX: (רְחֹב), א, Tob.13:18, Sir.9:7 א1*;] 1. in cl., the force, rush, swing, of a moving body; esp. of a charge of soldiers. 2. In late Greek, a narrow road, lane, street: in Polyb., of a road in camp; in LXX and NT (π. also) of streets in a town.
ἀνα-πείθω [in LXX: (נָשָׁא hi.), 1Ma.1:11 *;] to per­suade, incite.

συν-ευ-δοκέω, -ῶ [in LXX: 1Ma.1:57, 1Ma.4:28 א1, 2Ma.11:24 2Mac *;] to join in approving, consent, agree to or with: absol., with dative of person(s), with dative of thing(s), with inf., (chiefly in late writers).
to enlist strangers, levy mercenaries, (Demosthenes Orator), from ξενολόγος
1. in FlJ, the region of Samaria. 2. a Samaritan woman.
a buckle-pin, (Euripides);—;in plural a buckle or brooch, (Iliad by Homer)
to rest under the same roof.
1. to help in loosing, (Euripides):—; to help to solve a difficulty or end a quarrel, (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. to rest under the same roof, (Aeschulus Tragicus); compare καταλύω.
(ἔθνος, ἄρχω), [in LXX: 1Ma.14:47 *;] an ethnarch, a provincial governor.

1. a glory, delight, honour, (Iliad by Homer), attic; ἀγάλματ᾽ ἀγορᾶς mere ornaments of the agora, (Euripides) 2. a pleasing gift, especially for the gods, (Odyssey by Homer) 3. a statue in honour of a god, (Herdotus Historicus), attic; an image, as an object of worship, (Aeschulus Tragicus); then generally,= ἀνδριάς, any statue…
[in LXX: Sir.11:7 Ma.2:7 *;] to blame, find fault: absol., with accusative, αὐτούς.
(WH, -θία), -ας, ἡ (κακοπαθής, suffering), [in LXX: (תְּלָאָה), תְּלָאָה), 2Ma.2:26-27, 4Ma.9:8 *;] distress, affliction.
(οἰκονόμος), [in LXX: (כּוּל pilp.), 2Ma.3:14 *;] to manage as house-steward, be a steward: absol., hence, generally, to manage, regulate, arrange (cl., 2Mac, Lc., 3Ma.3:2 R).
(ἀγών), [in LXX: 2Ma.3:14,16 *;] 1. a contest, wrestling (Eur., Xen.). 2. Of the mind, great fear, agony, anguish (Dem., Arist.).

(φωνή) [in LXX: (עָלַם ni.), Wis.4:19, 2Ma.3:29 *;] dumb, speechless: (LXX); of idols, of beasts, τοσαῦτα γένη φωνῶν καὶ οὐδὲν ἄ.—so many kinds of voices and none voiceless, i.e. without signification, unintelligible.

1. the character and conduct of a κακοῦργος, ill-doing, wickedness, villany, malice, (Odyssey by Homer), of a horse, viciousness, (Xenophon Historicus) 2. in plural malpractices, (Xenophon Historicus)
[in LXX (of God): Ma.3:39 2Mac Ma.2:21 *;] 1. an overseer (LXX, ll. with). 2. a spectator.

adv. (ἥδομαι, to be glad), [in LXX: 2Ma.4:12 2Mac Ma.3:15 3Mac *;] gladly.

1. safe from violence, inviolate, of persons seeking protection, (Euripides):—;with genitive, γάμων ἄσυλος safe from marriage, (Euripides) 2. of places, γῆν ἄσυλον παρασχεῖν to make the land a refuge, (Euripides)
to annoy or offend besides, τινα (Herdotus Historicus)
ὑπ-έχω [in LXX: (נָשָׂא), La (סָבַל), Wis.12:21, 2Ma.4:48 *;] to hold or put under. Metaphorical, to undergo, suffer: δίκην, Ju 7.
adv. (ἔχω), [in LXX: 2Ma.5:2, 3Ma.5:14 3Mac *;] 1. of place, near. 2. Of degree, almost, nearly.
genitive, Διός, dative, Διΐ, accusative, Δία, Zeus (Lat. Jupiter).

adv. (ἁπλοῦς), [in LXX: (תֹּם), Wis.16:27, 2Ma.6:6 *;] simply, sincerely, graciously. ("Later writers comprehend under the one word the whole magnanimous and honour­able type of character in which... singleness of mind is the central feature "-Hort, Ja., l.with)

a feeding on the inwards of a sacrifice

ἀνα-στενάζω [in LXX: La (אָנַח ni.), Sir.25:17), Da TH Sus Ma.6:30 *;] to sigh deeply.

(χλεύη, a jest), [in LXX: Wis.11:14, 2Ma.7:7, 4Ma.5:22 *;] to jest, mock, jeer.
[in LXX: (7) (הָלַל po.),] to carry about. Pass., metaphorically.
ἐκ-πληρόω [in LXX: 2Ma.8:10, 3Ma.1:2 3Mac *;] 1. to fill full, make up a number. 2. to fulfil (MM, Exp., xii; Cremer, 839).
(ξένος), [in LXX: Sir.29:25, 2Ma.9:6, 3Ma.7:3 *;] 1. to receive as a guest, entertain: with accusative of person(s), pass.. 2. In late writers, to surprise, astonish by strangeness: pass..
[in LXX: (18) (נָשַׁב hi.), (נָשַׁף), Sir.43:16, 20, Ep. Je 61, 2Ma.9:7 *;] to breathe, blow: of the wind, ηῇ πνεούσῃ (sc. αὔρᾳ). αὔρα, a breeze: τ. πνεούσῇ (sc. αὔρᾳ).

1. a thunderbolt, Lat. fulmen, (Homer), generally, thunder:—;but thunder properly was βροντή, Lat. tonitru; lightning was στεροπή, Lat. fulgur. 2. metaphorically, κεραυνὸν ἐν γλώσσῃ φέρειν, of Pericles, (Plutarch)
(ἐπιτρέπω), [in LXX: 2Ma.11:1 2Mac 2Mac *;] 1. an administrator, a steward. 2. a guardian (with genitive of person(s), 2Mac, ll. with).
to be steady, favourable, (Euripides):—; to be calm, tranquil, of the sea, (Lucian) from εὐστᾶθής
(altern. of τηλικόσδε, -ήδε, -όνδε, strength­ened form of τηλίκος), [in LXX: 2Ma.12:3, 3Ma.3:9, 4Ma.16:4 *;] 1. of persons, (a) of such an age, so old; (b) so young. 2. Of things, so great.
ἀνα-ζητέω, -ῶ [in LXX: (דָּרַשׁ), (בָּקַשׁ pi.), 2Ma.13:21 *;] to look for or seek carefully.

(ἀπό, λόγος), [in LXX: (רִיב) Ma.13:26 *;] 1. to defend: with accusative. 2. to defend one's self: absol., before ὅτι, τί, to adduce something in one's defence, (ταῦτα) (τὰ περὶ ἐμαυτοῦ); περί, with genitive of thing(s), and ἐπί, with genitive of person(s), with dative of person(s).

1. to aim or shoot at, with genitive, τοῦ σκοποῦ (Plato Philosophus), 2. metaphorically to aim at, endeavour after, (Plato Philosophus); στ. φίλων κριτῶν to aim at having friends as judges, (Xenophon Historicus) 3. to endeavour to make out, to guess at a thing, with genitive, (Isocrates Orator):—; absolute to make guesses, conjecture…
commander of a squadron of sixteen elephants
the commander of a squadron of elephants, (Plutarch)
(αἴφνης = ἄφνως, suddenly), [in LXX: Wis.17:15, 2Ma.14:17, 3Ma.3:24 *;] sudden, unexpected.

[in LXX: Ma.14:25, 4Ma.16:9 *;] to marry; 1. of the man, to marry, take to wife (ducere): absol., with accusative. 2. Of the woman, (a) mid. (and in late writers, pass.), to give oneself in marriage, marry (nubere): (b) in Hellenistic (M, Pr., 159), act. (as of the man), to marry: absol.. with accusative. 3. Of both sexes: absol., 36.
nobility of birth, high descent, (Aeschulus Tragicus); εὐγένεια παίδων = εὐγενεῖς παῖδες, (Euripides)
συν-έπομαι [in LXX: 2Ma.15:2, 3Ma.5:48 R 3Ma.6:21 *;] to follow with, accompany: with dative of person(s).

(παραβαίνω), [in LXX: (שֵׂט), 4 A, Wis.14:31, 2Ma.15:10 *;] 1. a going aside, a deviation (Arist.). 2. In later writers, an overstepping; metaphorically, transgression: τ. νόμου, ἐν π., τ. παραβάσεων χάριν, SYN.: see: ἁμαρτία
φιλ-άδελφος, -ον [in LXX: 2Ma.15:14, 4Ma.13:21 4Mac *;] loving one's brother, loving like a brother: of Christians' love for one another (EV, loving as brethren).

wages of manual labour: generally wages, pay, guerdon, reward, (Aristophanes Comicus):—;also in bad sense, τῆς ὑψηγόρου γλώσσης ἐπ. rewards for proud speech, (Aeschulus Tragicus); ξιφέων ἐπ. the wages of the sword, i. e. slaughter by it, (Sophocles Tragicus)
to treat despitefully, to insult or affront wantontly, τινά (Sophocles Tragicus), also τινός (Sophocles Tragicus):—;Pass., absolute, to wax wanton, (Sophocles Tragicus)
of good hope, hopeful, cheerful, sanguine, (Thucydides),—;with infinitive future, εὔελπις ἰσχύσειν (Aeschulus Tragicus); εὔελπις σωθήσεσθαι in good hope to be saved, (Thucydides)
ἀφ-ορμή, -ῆς, ἡ [in LXX: (הָמוֹן), Ma.3:2 *;] prop., a starting point; in war, a base of operations; metaphorically, an occasion, incentive, opportunity: ἀφ. λαμβάνειν, WH, mg., ἀφ. διδόναι.*
σύμ-φυτος, -ον (συμφύω, to make to grow together) [in LXX: (בָּצַר), א2, Ma.3:22 *;] 1. congenital, innate. 2. grown along with, united with: τ. ὁμοιώματι τ. θανάτου αὐτσῦ.
τό (τέκμαρ, a mark, sign), [in LXX: Wis.5:4 Ma.3:24 *;] a sure sign, a positive proof. SYN.: ἔνδειγμα, q.v
weeping, wailing, groaning, howling, mourning, lamentation, [, variant datesTragica Adespota
[in LXX: Ep. Je.28, 3Ma.4:5 3Mac *;] to make full use of, use to the uttermost, use up: with dative..

1. like χόλη, gall, bile, (Iliad by Homer) 2. generally metaphorically bile, gall, bitter anger, wrath, (Homer), attic; χόλος ἔδυ τινά (Iliad by Homer); χόλος ἔμπεσε θυμῷ (Iliad by Homer); χόλον πέσσειν, καταπέσσειν; χ. σβέσσαι παῦσαι (Iliad by Homer); χόλου παύεσθαι (Hesiod):—;with genitive objecti, anger towards or because of another…
(ὄρθρος), [in LXX: Ma.5:10 3Mac *;] early, in the early morning: Rec..
(Att.. -ττω), [in LXX: Sir.22:19, 3Ma.5:14 *;] to pierce: τ. πλευρὰν λόγχῃ, WH.
συν-τόμως, adv. (συντέμνω) [in LXX: Ma.5:25 *;] concisely, briefly.

(also -α, -ον; βαίνω), [in LXX: Wis.7:23, 3Ma.5:31 Ma.17:4 *;] firm, secure: ἄγκυρα, metaphorically, sure: ἐπαγγελία, ἐλπίς, λόγος, παρρησία, ἀρχή (τ. ὑποστάσεως), διαθήκη, κλῆσις κ. ἐκλογή, comp. (-ότερος), προφητικὸς λόγος.

1. to send besides or again, of messages, (Herdotus Historicus) 2. of the gods, to send upon or to, (Herdotus Historicus); especiallyby way of punishment, to send upon or against, let loose upon, (Euripides)
ἀφ-οράω, -ῶ [in LXX: 4Ma.17:10 (είς θεόν)*;] (a) to look away from all else at, fix one's gaze upon: metaphorically, (b) simply, to see: ἀφίδω.
to threaten violently, (Herdotus Historicus):—;so in Mid., (Aeschines Orator)
1. to drive back, (Odyssey by Homer) 2. to beat back an assailant, (Thucydides) 3. to stop:—; Pass. to be stopped, stop short, τινός from a thing, (Lucian)
(κενόδοξος), [in LXX: Wis.14:14, 2Ma.2:15 2Mac *;] 1. foolish fancy, vain opinion, error (LXX, ll. with). 2. vain­glory, groundless conceit.
(δοῦλος), [in LXX for עָבַד;] to enslave, bring into bondage: (LXX), metaphorically, pass., before ἐν, τ. θεῷ, τ. δικαιοσύνῃ, οἴνῳ, ὑπὸ τὰ στοιχεῖα τ. κόσμου, (Cremer, 217).
(ἄγαν, much, ἄχομαι, to grieve), [in LXX: Wis.5:22, Da TH Bel 28, 4Ma.4:21 *;] to be indignant: before περί, before ὅτι.
(WH, Ἰερ-; Rec. -μίτης), -ου, ὁ, [in LXX: Sir.50:27 (28) 2Ma.4:22 2Mac (V* -μήτης) 2Ma *;] an inhabitant of Jerusalem.
1. high-minded, noble, generous, (Xenophon Historicus) 2. in bad sense, arrogant: adverb -όνως, (Plato Philosophus)
adv. (ὁμ oλογέω), [in LXX: 4Ma.6:31 4Mac 4Mac *;] 1. as agreed, conformably with. 2. confessedly, by common consent.
to break one thing round or on another, τί τινι (Plutarch); π. τὸν Τίβεριν to divert it, (Plutarch)
ἀνα-τρέφω [in LXX: Wis.7:4 B, 4Ma.10:2 4Mac א*;] to nurse up, nourish, educate, bring up: WΗ, mg..

to compress, press tight, especially the throat, to strangle, throttle, choke, ἄγχε μιν ἱμὰς ὑπὸ δειρήν (Iliad by Homer); τὸν Κέρβερον ἀπῇξας ἄγχων (Aristophanes Comicus): metaphorically of creditors, (Aristophanes Comicus); of a guilty conscience, τοῦτο ἄγχει (Demosthenes Orator)
to bend down, so as to be concave, (Plato Philosophus):—;metaphorically, μ. ἐλπίδας to bend down, overthrow hopes, (Euripides):—;Pass. to be bent (by intreaty), (Aeschines Orator)

τό [in LXX: Wis.7:17 Ma.12:13 *;] prop., one of a row (στοῖχος) or series, hence, 1. the shadow-line of a dial (Aristoph.). 2. an elementary sound or letter of the alphabet (Anth., Plut., π.). 3. the elements or rudiments of knowledge; πτωχὰ σ., σ. τοῦ κόσμου. 4. The material elements of the universe (Plat.; LXX, ll. with). 5…
[in LXX: 4Ma.13:1 4Mac 4Mac *;] 1. to be overproud, high-minded (Æsch.): μὴ ὑ. παρ᾽ ὃ δεῖ φρονεῖν. 2. to overlook, think slightly of (Thuc., Plat.).
(φιλάδελφος), [in LXX: 4Ma.13:23 4Mac 4Mac *;] the love of brothers, brotherly love: of Christians' mutual love as brethren.

1. much-tangled, thick-wreathed, of a serpent's coils, (Euripides); of the polypus, with tangled, twisting arms, (Theognis Elegiacus) 2. metaphorically much-twisting, complex, intricate, [, variant datesAnthology Palantina
[in LXX: 4Ma.15:2 4Mac 4Mac *;] 1. in season. 2. for a season, temporary, transient: of plants, short-lived.
(φίλος, τέκνον), [in LXX: 4Ma.15:4-6 *;] loving one's children: of women, joined with φίλανδρος, which see.
(δίκη), [in LXX: Wis.12:12, Sir.30:6, 4Ma.15:29 *;] 1. without law, unjust. 2. exacting penalty from; as subst., an avenger: before περί, (in π., a legal representative; Milligan, Th., l.with).

1. (Homer) of wind, rain, furious, boisterous, (Herdotus Historicus); λ. πῦρ, κύματα, πόντος, (Euripides) 2. after (Homer), of men, boisterous, turbulent, violent, (Theognis Elegiacus), 3. greedy, (Pindar) 4. adverb λάβρως, violently, furiously, (Theognis Elegiacus) 5. greedily, (Aeschulus Tragicus)
ἄ-καρπος, -ον, [in LXX: (צַלְמָוֶת), Wis.15:4, 4Ma.16:7;] unfruitful, barren: figuratively, Ju 12.
1. to pillage, (Euripides),—;Pass., of a person, to be undone, (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. to carry off as plunder, (Thucydides)
1. a muzzle, put on a led horse, (Xenophon Historicus)
[in LXX: (זָמַם), (שָׁמַר), Da TH (12), Su *;] 1. to watch closely, observe narrowly: so mid., τ. πύλας, with evil intent, so mid.. 2. to observe scrupulously: mid..
ἐν-καυκάομαι, -ῶμαι [in LXX: 51(52):1 96(97):7 (הָלַל hithp.); Ps 73(74):4 (שָׁאַג); Ps 105(106):47 (שָׁבַח)*;] to take pride in, glory in: before ἐν.
a cooling, refreshing: relief, recovery, respite, (Plato Philosophus): from a thing, with genitive, (Euripides)

one who comes to seek protection, a suppliant or fugitive, who lays his ἱκετηρία on the altar or hearth, after which his person was inviolable; especially one who seeks purification after homicide, (Homer)
to make equal, (Sophocles Tragicus),—;Mid., ὄνυχας χεῖράς τε ἰσώσαντο, i. e. used them in like manner, (Hesiod):—;Pass. to be made like or equal to, with dative, (Odyssey by Homer)
a hunter, huntsman, (Iliad by Homer); κυσὶ θηρευτῇσι (Iliad by Homer); also of a fisher, (Herdotus Historicus)
1. the site of a house, (Xenophon Historicus), 2. the house itself, a building, (Thucydides)
τό, [in LXX: (pl., צֹאן בֵּן), (כֶּבֶשׂ), (צָעִיר)*;] a little lamb, a lamb.
(ψεύδω), [in LXX: (כָּזַב), A N2 (כָּזָב), Sir.15:8 *;] a liar: Jn Jn Jn Jn.
a wrong time: accusative as adverb, ἀωρίαν ἥκειν to have come too late, (Aristophanes Comicus); ἀωρίαι at an unseasonable time, so late, (Lucian)

1. a turning, e.g. of a horse, (Xenophon Historicus); ἐν στροφαῖσιν ὀμμάτων with rolling of the eyes, (Euripides) 2. a twist, such as wrestlers make to elude their adversary, (Plato Philosophus):—;metaphorically a trick, dodge, (Aristophanes Comicus) 3…
(κυβερνάω, Lat. gubernare, to guide), [in LXX: (תַּחְבֻּלָה) *;] 1. steering, pilotage (Plat.). 2. Metaphorical, government: pl..
with a Substantive, ἔαρ ἐξαπίνας sudden spring, (Thucydides).
[in LXX: Nam.1:10, (מָלֵא), *;] full: with genitive of thing(s), metaphorically, of thoughts and feelings.
ἐπι-γράφω [in LXX for כָּתַב, fig.,] to write upon, inscribe: figuratively, (LXX).
to make to sit, place, [variant datesAnthology Palantina
(προπίπτω), [in LXX: (אֱוִיל) (פָּשַׂק) Sir.9:18 *;] falling forwards, headlong. Metaphorical, precipitate, rash, reck­less: of persons, of things.
1. to destroy utterly, (Odyssey by Homer), 2. Mid., with perfect 2 ἐξόλωλα, to perish utterly, (Sophocles Tragicus)
1. Lat. gubernare, to steer, (Odyssey by Homer), absolute to act as pilot or helmsman, (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. metaphorically to guide, govern, (Pindar)
not-working, idle, (Homer),—; ἀεργοὶ δόμοι idle houses, i. e. where people are idle, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus)—;Cf. attic ἀργός.

1. to cleanse or clean quite, ἀπ. τὴν χεῖρα εἰς τὰ χειρόμακτρα upon the towels, (Xenophon Historicus) 2. to refine from dross, (Strabo Geographus): metaphorically in Pass., ἀποκεκαθάρθαι τὴν φωνήν to be pure in dialect, (Lucian) 3. to clear away, τὰς τραπέζας (Aristophanes Comicus):—;Mid., ἀποκαθήρασθαί τινος to rid oneself of a thing…
ἄ-πιστος, -ον (ἀ- neg., πιστός) [in LXX: *;] (a) of things, incredible: (b) of persons, without faith or trust, unbelieving: specif., of unbelievers as opposite to Christians.

1. Lat. non castigatus, unchastised, undisciplined, unbridled, (Herdotus Historicus), attic, 2. licentious, intemperate, opposite to σώφρων, (Sophocles Tragicus),—; so in adverb, ἀκολάστως ἔχειν (Plato Philosophus); comparative, ἀκολαστοτέρως ἔχειν πρός τι to be too intemperate in a thing, (Xenophon Historicus)
[in LXX: (חָשֹׁךְ), Sir.4:29 *;] sluggish, slothful. SYN.: ἀργός, βραδύς

1. meats carried round, (Xenophon Historicus) 2. a going round, rotatory motion, circuit, revolution, (Aristophanes Comicus), 3. the revolving vault of heaven, (Plato Philosophus) 4. metaphorically, ἐν ταῖς περιφοραῖς in society, (Plutarch)
[in LXX: (נֵרְדְּ)*;] nard; (a) an Indian plant, the Nardostachys nardus jatamansi, used for the preparation of a fragrant ointment; (b) ointment of nard.
1. the body of rowers and sailors, the ship's crew, (Thucydides), 2. service, (Aristophanes Comicus)

1. strength, might, (Iliad by Homer):—;with infinitive, σθ. πολεμίζειν strength to war, (Iliad by Homer); σθ. ὥστε καθελεῖν (Euripides); σθένει by force, (Sophocles Tragicus); λόγῳ τε καὶ σθένει both by right and might, (Sophocles Tragicus); so, ὑπὸ σθένους (Euripides); παντὶ σθένει with all one's might, (Thucydides) 2. strength, might…
1. a sound, but properly of a returned sound, echo, (Homeric Hymns), 2. generally, a ringing sound, (Sophocles Tragicus)
(ἀ- neg., ἐξιχνιάζω, to track out; ἴχνος) [in LXX: (חֵקֶר אַיִן)*;] that cannot be traced out.
[in LXX: (בִּין hi.) (יָרָה hi.), Dan LXX (חָוָה pa.) *;] to show forth, tell, declare, explain: (WH, RV, διασάφησον).
to look at, look upon, mostly with εἰς, (Herdotus Historicus); but with accusative, (Euripides)
συν-κύπτω (Rec. συγκ-), [in LXX: (עָזַב), Sir.12:11 *;] 1. to bend forwards. 2. to be bowed down.
epic imperfect ὄλεκον, ionic ὀλέκεσκον, like ὄλλυμι, to ruin, destroy, kill, (Homer)
easily numbered, few in number, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus): οὐκ ἀριθμητός held in no account, nullo numero habitus, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus)
interj., expressing surprise, indignation, fear (in cl. chiefly in poët.), ah! ha!.
a pirate, Lat. pirata, i. e. one who attacks ships, (Polybius Historicus)

1. to build round, (Demosthenes Orator) 2. to enclose by building round, (Demosthenes Orator):—;Pass. to be built up, walled in, (Thucydides); τὸ περιοικοδομημένον the space built round, the enclosure, Lat. ovile, (Herdotus Historicus)
1. to vomit forth, disgorge, (Odyssey by Homer):—;metaphorically to disgorge ill-gotten gear, (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. absolute to vomit, be sick, (Aristophanes Comicus)

1. with accusative rei, to found as a colony or new settlement, πόλιν (Herdotus Historicus),—; Pass., πόλις οἴκισται (Herdotus Historicus) 2. to people with new settlers, colonise, χώρην (Herdotus Historicus); νήσους (Thucydides):—;Mid. ὅπη γῆς πύργον οἰκιούμεθα in what part of the world we shall make ourselves a fenced home…

1. an opening or introduction to a thing; in Music, a prelude, overture, (Pindar); in poems and speeches, a proem, preface, preamble, introduction, Lat. exordium, (Pindar) 2. metaphorically of any prelude or beginning, φροίμιον χορεύσομαι (Aeschulus Tragicus); μηδέπω ' ν προοιμίοις only just beginning, (Aeschulus Tragicus)…
ἐπι-φαύσκω, [in LXX: (אהל hi.) (הָלַל hi.) *;] to shine forth: figuratively, with dative.
[in LXX: (אֹפֶל), (חָשַׁךְ), *;] in late writers = σκότος, darkness. Metaphorical, (a) of secrecy (opposite to ἐν τ. φωτί): (b) of spiritual darkness: Jn Jn.

1. a muzzle, Lat. capistrum, (Lucian) 2. the nose-band of a horse's bridle, fitted with pipes through which the horses' breath made a whistling sound, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 3. a kind of cup, used as a dice-box, Lat. fritillus, (Aeschines Orator)
μομφή, ῆς, ἡ (μέμφομαι), poët. form of μέμψις, blame, com­plaint.
ἀν-ωφελής, -ές (ἀ- neg., ὄφελος), [in LXX: (יָעַל בִּלְתִּי) (יָעַל לֹא), Wis.1:11 *;] unprofitable: neut. as subst., unprofitableness.

1. a sign or token by which one infers a thing, [variant datesTragica Adespota; λαμπάδος τὸ σύμβολον the token of the beacon-fire, (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;often in plural, of marks on the body, (Euripides); of omens, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 2. a pledge or pawn, on which money was advanced, (Lysias Orator) 3. in plural tallies, Lat…
ἔκ-βασις, -εως, ἡ (ἐκβαίνω), [in LXX: Wis.2:17 *;] 1. a way out (Hom., Xen.). 2. the issue (Menand.).

(μετά + ξύν = σύν), [in LXX: III Ki; Wis.4:10 *;] 1. adv. of place and time; (a) between: ἐν τῷ μ. (s.with χρόνῳ), (b) in late writers, like μετά (adv.), after, afterwards: τὸ μ. σάββατον. 2. Prep. with genitive, between: of place, of persons, as to mutual relation.

1. Dep. to count up, number, reckon, (Xenophon Historicus); κ. τὸ εὐεργέτημα πρός τινα to put it down to his account, (Demosthenes Orator); καταλογιζέσθω μηδεὶς τοῦθ᾽ ὑμῖν ἐν ἀρετῇ let no one impute it to you as a virtue, (Aeschines Orator) 2. to count or reckon among, Lat. annumerare, τοὺς ἀχαρίστους ἐν τοῖς ἀδίκοις (Xenophon Historicus)
προ-γινώσκω [in LXX: Wis.6:13 *;] to know beforehand, foreknow: with accusative of person(s), of the Divine foreknowledge.
adv. [in LXX: Wis.7:15, Sir.14:11 *;] worthily: with genitive (frequently in Inscr.; Deiss., BS, 248; MM, VGT, 51), ἀ. τ. Κυρίου, τ. θεοῦ.
τό (κτίζω), [in LXX: Wis.9:2, Sir.36:20 (17), Sir.38:34, 3Ma.5:11 *;] 1. (cl.) a colony. 2. a created thing, creature.

(φθείρω) [in LXX: (מִשְׁחָת), A א3, Wis.9:15 Ma.7:16 *;] perishable, corruptible: ἄνθρωπος, (opposite to ἄφθαρτος θεός); στέφανος, (opposite to αρτος); σπσρά, (opposite to ἄφθ.); neut., τὸ φ. τοῦτο, pl..

1. a plaything, toy, (Plato Philosophus) 2. in (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus), the Egyptians are called κακὰ παίγνια roguish playmates, 3. a game, a sportive poem, [variant datesAnthology Palantina; of the merry chirp of the cicada, [variant datesAnthology Palantina

compar. of καλός, see: καλῶς καλῶς adv. (καλός), [in LXX for parts and derivatives of יָטַב;] finely, rightly, well: λέγειν, λαλεῖν, as exclamation of approval, κ. ποιεῖν, with dative of person(s) (cl. accusative; WM, § 32, 1 β), with accusative of thing(s), with ptcp., (M, Pr., 131), προϊστάναι (-ασθαι), διακονεῖν, ἀνατρέφεσθαι…
a bite, sting, (Xenophon Historicus): metaphorically, δ. λύπης (Aeschulus Tragicus)

1. hated, abhorred, hateful, (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;with dative hateful or hostile to one, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 2. gloomy, sullen, Lat. tristis, (Aeschulus Tragicus); ὁρᾶν στυγνός gloomy to behold, (Xenophon Historicus);—; στυγνὸς εἴκων yielding sullenly, with an ill grace, (Sophocles Tragicus); neuter as adverb, (Sophocles Tragicus)
ἐκ-μάσσω [in LXX: Sir.12:11, Ep. *;] to wipe off: with accusative.
1. a rising up, (Plato Philosophus) 2. in speaking, recapitulation, (Plato Philosophus)

1. properly the untamed, unconquerable: 2. as Substantive adamant, i. e. the hardest metal, probably steel: metaphorically of any thing unalterable, ἔπος ἐρέω ἀδάμαντι πελάσσας having fixed it firm as adamant, (Oracle quoted in Herdotus Historicus) 3. the diamond, (Theophrastus Philosophus) 4. as adjective, metaphorically…

1. to get quite ready, equip, (Lucian):—;Pass., perfect participle διεσκευασμένοι dressed, (Plutarch): —;Mid. to prepare for oneself, provide, (Thucydides): to equip oneself, (Xenophon Historicus) 2. Mid., διασκευασάμενος τὴν οὐσίαν having disposed of one's property, (Demosthenes Orator)

to join in war, (Thucydides), τινί with one, (Xenophon Historicus)

(accusative -ῶνα, WH), ὁ (Heb. שָׁרוֹן), the plain of Sharon.

[in LXX: (סַל), (דּוּד)*;] a basket, probably of wicker-work, such as were carried by Jews for food.

1. a statement, narrative, (Thucydides) 2. explanation, interpretation, (Plato Philosophus)
τό (κάρα, the head), [in LXX: (גֻּלְגֹּלֶת)*;] a skull.
(ἄργυρος, κόπτω, to beat) [in LXX: (צָרַף) *;] a silversmith.
ὑπο-χωρέω [in LXX: B (-), Sir.13:9, 2Ma.12:12 *;] to go back, retire: before ἐν, before εἰς.
and there, there also: (κ. ἐ., Tr., mg.) (κ. ἐ., T), (κ. ἐ., L) (κ. ἐ., WH) (κ. ἐ., WH).
a plant used for stuffing or padding; and metaphorically " padding, " an expletive, (Aristophanes Comicus)

want of heart, faintheartedness, (Herdotus Historicus), εἰς ἀθυμίαν καθιστάναι τινά (Plato Philosophus); ἀθυμίαν παρέχειν τινί (Xenophon Historicus); ἐν ἀθυμίαι εἶναι (Xenophon Historicus); ἀθυμία ἐμπίπτει τινί (Xenophon Historicus)
a chance, casualty, (Aristotle Philosopher): in bad sense, a mishap, mischance, (Thucydides)
προ-τρέχω [in LXX: (פָּנִים רוּץ), (14) A (דּוּץ), Tob.11:3 (before ἔμπροσθεν), 1Ma.16:21 *;] 1. to run forward. 2. to run on, run in advance: before εἰς τὸ ἔμπροσθεν.
of good size, very large, (Aristophanes Comicus)
ἀπο-τινάσσω [in LXX: A (נָעַר ni.), (נָטַשׁ), La (נָאַר pi.) *;] to shake of.
[in LXX: (בָּעַת pi.) *;] to choke: with accusative, (WH, mg.); imperfect (coniative), of drowning, pass..
a pole, punting-pole, boat-hook, Lat. contus, (Odyssey by Homer), attic: the shaft of a pike, (Lucian)

to fight in single combat, (Euripides); τινι with one, (Herdotus Historicus); of the Athenians at Marathon, μοῦνοι μουνομαχήσαντες τῷ Πέρσῃ having fought single-handed with the Persians, (Herdotus Historicus)
of or for a shepherd, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus): —; ἡ -κή (i.e. τέχνη); (Plato Philosophus)

1. to sling, to use the sling, (Thucydides) 2. to strike by slinging, (Babrius Fabularum Scriptor) 3. to throw as from a sling:—;Pass., (Euripides) 4. to move like a swing, to swing to and fro, (Euripides) from σφενδόνη

to look up from under the brows at, glance at, to look askance at, eye suspiciously or angrily, Lat. limis oculis suspicere, (Plato Philosophus); also ὑπ. ἐλεεινά to cast piteous glances, [variant datesAnthology Palantina:—;Pass. to be looked at with suspicion, (Euripides)

1. indebted, in debt, (Aristophanes Comicus); ὑπ. τινος his debtor, (Plutarch) 2. of property, involved, Lat. obaeratus, (Demosthenes Orator) 3. with genitive, ὑπ. φιλίας bound by ties of friendship, (Plutarch)

1. Pass. to lie together, (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. as Pass. of συντίθημι, to be composed or compounded, ἔκ τινων of certain parts, (Plato Philosophus), 3. of written works, to be composed, (Thucydides), 4. to be contrived, concocted, (Euripides), 5. to be agreed on by two parties, (Thucydides): in participle agreed on, arranged…
chief guard; leader of the body guard
(παγίς), [in LXX: (נָקַשׁ hith.), (יָקֹשׁ pu.)*;] to ensnare: metaphorically, with accusative, ἐν λόγῳ, (not elsewhere).
[in LXX: (לָבַשׁ), Jdth.9:1, Sir.50:11 *;] to put on: with dupl. accusative, (ἐνδύουσι, Rec.). Mid., to put on oneself, be clothed in: with accusative of thing(s).

1. to turn off or aside, τι (Odyssey by Homer): to turn back, (Homeric Hymns):—;Pass., of the day, to decline, get towards evening, (Herdotus Historicus) 2. Pass. to be upset, (Demosthenes Orator) 3. intransitive in Act. to turn aside or off the road, (Xenophon Historicus); πρὸς τὴν ἠῶ ἀποκλίνοντι as one turns to go Eastward…
1. a remembrance, memorial, (Thucydides), 2. a note, memorandum, (Demosthenes Orator):—;in plural memoranda, notes, minutes, Lat. commentarii, (Plato Philosophus)

enclit. part., at all; see: εἴπως, μήπως. μήπως or μή πως (so WH), negative particle, 1. as conjc., lest haply: in final sentences, after verbs of fearing or taking heed, with an ellipse of ptcp.. 2. As interrogative, whether haply. μήπου (WH, μή που), lest anywhere, lest haply.
to weigh down: metaphorically, with accusative of person(s).

ἀπ-άγχω (ἄγχω, to press, strangle), [in LXX: (חָנַק), Tob.3:10 *;] to strangle; mid., to hang oneself.

1. a bean, Lat. faba, (Iliad by Homer) 2. the lot by which public officers were elected at Athens (because those who drew white beans were chosen), ὁ τῷ κυάμῳ λαχών an officer chosen by lot, (Herdotus Historicus); βουλὴ ἡ ἀπὸ τοῦ κυάμου (Thucydides); ἄρχοντας ἀπὸ κυάμου καθιστάναι (Xenophon Historicus)

1. one of many, Lat. unus e multis, i.e. the smallest, least, (Thucydides),—; adverb, δευτέρως καὶ πολλοστῶς in a very small degree, (Aristotle Philosopher) 2. of Time, πολλοστῷ χρόνῳ after a very long time, (Aristophanes Comicus)
a hundred times as much or many, (Xenophon Historicus)
(ἄγκος, a bend), [in LXX for אַצִּיל, חֵיק;] the bent arm.
to cut or carve upon stone, (Herdotus Historicus)
the socket in which the pivot of a door ὁ στρόφιγξ); moved, (Aristophanes Comicus)

1. round, spherical, (Herdotus Historicus), λίθοι στρ. pebbles, (Xenophon Historicus) 2. circular, (Plato Philosophus) 3. round, compactly formed, (Xenophon Historicus) 4. of ships, στρ. ναῦς, στρ. πλοῖον, a merchant- ship, from its round shape, as opposite to the long narrow ship-of-war μακρὰ ναῦς); (Herdotus Historicus), 5…
to yoke together, ζ. κιθάραν to put the cross-bar to the lyre, (Lucian)
(καινός), [in LXX: *;] 1. novelty. 2. freshness, newness: ἐν κ. ζωῆς, ἐν κ. πνεύματος.

(ὅσιος), adv., [in LXX: Wis.6:10 *;] piously, holily: ὁ. καὶ δικαίως κ. ἀμέμπτως.

1. the foremost or upper part of anything: a bust or half-figure, [variant datesAnthology Palantina 2. the forepart of a ship, [variant datesAnthology Palantina
Satan, i. e. an adversary, enemy: name for the Devil, (New Testament) Hebr. word.

1. a broad strap for bearing anything from Root ! τλα, * τλάω, whence also the hero Telamon took his name, compare Ἄτλας 2. a leathern strap or belt, for bearing both shield or sword, (Homer) 3. a broad linen bandage for wounds, (Iliad by Homer); for swathing mummies, (Herdotus Historicus)
(also -α, -ον, as in Wis, l.with), [in LXX: (חֵרֶם), Wis.18:15 *;] destructive, deadly: δίκην, L, txt.

1. one who holds the reins, a driver, charioteer, opposite to παραιβάτης (the warrior by his side), (Iliad by Homer) 2. generally a chariot-driver, as in the games, (Pindar), attic:—;in (Theognis Elegiacus), a rider. 3. metaphorically a guide, governor, (Pindar)
to value in or among, (Demosthenes Orator)
to pour out or off, shed, let fall, (Odyssey by Homer):—;poet. Mid. ἀποχεύομαι, (Euripides)
to bind tight, bind fast, (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;Pass., (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus)
1. Dep. to compute, calculate, (Plutarch) 2. to consider, reflect on, τι (Herdotus Historicus); περί τινος (Thucydides) 3. to reckon on, οὐδεὶς αὑτοῦ θάνατον ἐκλογίζεται (Euripides)
1. commixture, τινος πρός τι (Plato Philosophus) 2. intercourse, (Plutarch)

indecl. (Heb. שַׂלְמוֹן), Salmon: (Σαλά, WH, R, mg.).

to be secretary, (Thucydides), with genitive, γρ. τοῦ συνεδρίου Epigr.
carrying on the back: as Substantive a beast of burthen, (Xenophon Historicus)

one who bears a light shield πέλτη); instead of the heavy ὅπλον, a targeteer, Lat. cetratus, (Euripides), The peltasts held a place between the ὁπλῖται and ψιλοί.
medical treatment: metaphorically a curing, correcting, (Aristotle Philosopher)
Dep. to get for oneself entirely, gain possession of, and in past tenses, to have in full possession, (Sophocles Tragicus)

[in LXX: I Ma.12:1 *;] 1. prop., to work together (with): absol., with dative, dative commod., T, R, txt.. 2. In Hellenistic writers (M, Pr., 65), trans., to cause to work together: with accusative of thing(s), [WH] R, mg..

(πρόβατον) [in LXX (π. πύλη): (צֹאן)*;] of sheep: ἡ π., the sheep-gate.

of cypress-wood, (Odyssey by Homer) from κῦπάρισσος
1. much like ὑπερηνορέων overweening, arrogant, (Iliad by Homer) 2. transitive to treat disdainfully, (Lucian)
ἀφ-υστερέω, -ῶ, [in LXX: (מָנַע), Sir.14:14 *;] 1. as in cl., to be late (Polyb., Sir, l.with). 2. Trans., to keep back: pass..
estrangement, τῆς ξυμμαχίας οὐχ ὁμοία ἡ ἀλλ. its estrangement, its loss, (Thucydides)
contr., -οῦς, -ᾶ, -οῦν (ποπφύρα), [in LXX for אַרְגָּמָן;] purple: as subst., πορφυροῦν (sc. ἱμάτιον).

1. Lat. cubus, a cube: a cubical die, marked on all 6 sides, in plural, dice, (Herdotus Historicus), the Greeks threw with three dice, so that τρὶς ἕξ, three sixes, was the highest throw, (Aeschulus Tragicus); κρίνειν τι ἐν κύβοις to decide it by the dice, by chance, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 2. also of the single pips on the dice…

(διδάσκω), [in LXX: Ma.1:10 *;] given as rendering of Heb. רַבִּי,רַבּוֺן; a teacher: of Jewish teachers, cf.; of John Baptist, of Jesus, and often in Syn., most frequently in voc., as title of address, as, of Jesus by himself, of an apostle, of Christians, of false teachers, (Cremer, 181; DB, i, 609, iii, 294, iv, 691) SYN.: παιδευτής…

Dep.:—; to go or come out with, τινι (Herdotus Historicus)
δια-κωλεύω [in LXX: Jdth.4:7 *;] to hinder, prevent: with accusative.
ἐκ-τένεια, -ας, ἡ (ἐκτενής), [in LXX: Jdth.4:9, 2Ma.14:38, 3Ma.6:41 *;] zeal, intentness, earnestness.
προ-σάββατον, -ου, τό [in LXX: title. א (שַׁבָּת) שַׁבָּת) title., Jdth.8:6 *;] the day before the Sabbath: (L, Tr., txt., πρὸς σ.).
(συντρέχω), [in LXX: Jdth.10:18, 3Ma.3:8 *;] concourse, esp. of a riotous gathering.
a setting straight: successful accomplishment of a thing, success, (Aristotle Philosopher)

1. at what point of time, at what hour, on what day, (Sophocles Tragicus), ὁπ. ἄν at whatever hour or time, (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. in indirect questions, ἢν ὥραν προσήκει ἰέναι, καὶ ὁπ. ἀπιέναι (Aeschines Orator); in answer to a direct question, πηνίκ᾽ ἐστιν τῆς ἡμέρα;—; ὁπηνίκ; what time of day is it? —; what time…
(καλέω) [in LXX: (קָרָא), Jdth.12:10 A, 3Ma.5:14 *;] a calling, call; in NT, always of the Divine call to salvation: (Cremer, 332).

1. to fall under or down, to sink in, (Plutarch) 2. to fall down before any one, with accusative, (Plato Philosophus): —;hence, to be subject to him, fall under his power, (Isocrates Orator); of a flatterer, to cringe to, τινί (Demosthenes Orator); with accusative ὑποπεσὼν τὸν δεσπότην (Aristophanes Comicus) 3. to fall behind another…
1. to laugh approvingly, Lat. arrideo, (Iliad by Homer), attic 2. = ἐπεγγελάω, (Lucian)

(φθόνος), [in LXX: Tob.4:7, 16 AB *;] to envy: with dative (L, txt., Tr., mg., WH, mg., accusative), as in cl..

κατ-ευλογέω, -ῶ, [in LXX: Tob.11:1, 17 *;] to bless fervently.
(οὖσα, fem. part. of εἰμί), [in LXX: Tob.14:13, 3Ma.3:28 *;] substance, property.

(μιαίνω), [in LXX: Wis.14:26, 1Ma.4:43 *;] 1. prop., the act of defiling. 2. = μίασμα.

[in LXX: Da TH Bel AR, 1Ma.6:38 *;] 1. to shake down. 2. Of the hand, to shake or wave as a signal: τ. χεῖρα, τ. χειρί, id. with dative of person(s), before inf..

1. a standing round, a crowd standing round, Lat. corona, (Theophrastus Philosophus), 2. circumstances, a state of affairs, (Polybius Historicus):—;in bad sense, κατὰ τὰς π. in critical times, (Polybius Historicus) 3. outward pomp and circumstance, (Polybius Historicus)
[in LXX: 2Ma.4:31, 3Ma.6:1 *;] 1. to let down, lower. 2. to keep down, restrain: with accusative

1. to join two and two, couple, (Aristotle Philosopher): —;Pass. to be coupled with something else, (Aristotle Philosopher) 2. in Pass. to be coupled, to pair, (Xenophon Historicus)
1. the power of a master over slaves, or the relation of master to slaves, (Aristotle Philosopher) 2. absolute sway, despotism, (Isocrates Orator)

1. liable to give account for one's administration of an office, accountable, responsible, (Herdotus Historicus),—; ὑπεύθυνοι, οἱ, at Athens, magistrates who had to submit their accounts to public auditors λογισταί); (Aristophanes Comicus), 2. with genitive responsible for, ὑπ. ἀρχῆς ἑτέρας quoted in (Demosthenes Orator); of slaves…
to exult over, with dative, (Herdotus Historicus); absolute, καταχαίρων with malignant joy, (Herdotus Historicus)
adv. (φόβος), [in LXX: (פַּחַד), Wis.17:4 *;] without fear: Ju 12.
bent, crooked, curved, of a bow, (Iliad by Homer); of wheels, (Iliad by Homer); of chariots, (Iliad by Homer)
(ὀλίγος + ὤρα, care), [in LXX: (מָאַס)*;] to esteem lightly, think little of: with genitive, (LXX)

to drive against, drive home, ἔγχος (Iliad by Homer); ἐπέρεισε δὲ ἶν᾽ ἀπέλεθρον put vast strength to it, (Homer):—; ἐπ. τὴν φάλαγγά τινι to bring the whole force of the phalanx against, (Plutarch):—;Mid., λαίφη προτόνοις ἐπερειδόμεναι staying their sails on ropes, (Euripides):—;Pass. to lean or bear upon…

(πτοέω) [in LXX: (פַּחַד), Sir א1, 1Ma.3:25 R *;] a fluttering, excitement, caused by any emotion, but esp. by fear, hence, terror: φοβεῖσθαι πτόησιν, to be afraid with (cogn. accusative) or of any terror.
ἐμ-βιβάζω [in LXX: 4 (רָכַב hi.), (דָּרַךְ hi.) *;] 1. to set in, put in. 2. to put on board ship, embark: with accusative of person(s), before εἰς.

1. likely to make one stumble or trip: metaphorically slippery, perilous, dangerous, Lat. lubricus, (Herdotus Historicus),—; σφαλερόν [ ἐστι], with infinitive, it is dangerous to.., (Plato Philosophus), 2. σφάλλομαι); ready to fall, tottering, reeling, staggering, (Aeschulus Tragicus); σφ. σύμμαχοι (Demosthenes Orator)
to drop asleep over, with dative, (Plutarch)
1. Lat. formica, the ant, (Hesiod), 2. a beast of prey in India, (Herdotus Historicus)
1. having no hope of safety, abandoned, profligate, Lat. perditus, (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. active, ἄσωτος γένει bringing ruin on the race, fatal to it, (Aeschulus Tragicus)
[in LXX: (מַרְבַד)*;] a vernacular word, 1 1, a bed-cord (Aristoph., AV., 816; Pr, l.with). 2. In pl., swathings.

1. love, [variant datesTragica Adespota:—; love of a thing, desire for it, τινός (Herdotus Historicus),—;in plural loves, amours, (Euripides); in (Sophocles Tragicus), of passionate joy, compare φρίσσω II. 3. 2. as proper noun the god of love, Eros, Amor, (Sophocles Tragicus)
1. intransitive, of a ship, to run aground or ashore, (Herdotus Historicus) 2. transitive to run (a ship) aground:—;metaphorically to drive headlong, (Euripides)
to kill by hunger, starve, (Plato Philosophus)

1. to be fond of strife, engage in eager rivalry, be contentious, φιλονεικῶν out of contentiousness or party spirit, (Thucydides); φ. πρός τινα (Lysias Orator):—;with accusative, φ. τὸ ἐμὲ εἶναι τὸν ἀποκρινόμενον to be eager that I should be the answerer, (Plato Philosophus); τὰ χείρω φ. to be so obstinate as to choose the worst…

1. unquestioned, impossible to be questioned or refuted, of statements or arguments, (Thucydides); ἀν. ἔχει τὸ ἀνδρεῖον leaves their courage without proof, (Thucydides) 2. of persons, not to be convicted, irreproachable, (Xenophon Historicus)

1. at hand, ready, (Aeschulus Tragicus); of a drawn sword or knife, (Sophocles Tragicus); λίθοις καὶ.. ἀκοντίοις, ὡς ἕκαστός τι πρόχειρον εἶχε (Thucydides); ὃ προχειρότατον ἔχω εἰπεῖν (Demosthenes Orator) 2. πρόχειρόν [ ἐστι] it is easy, with infinitive, (Plato Philosophus), 3. of persons, ready to do, with infinitive…

1. wherein one feels joy, delightsome, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 2. wherein one feels malignant joy, ἐχθροῖς ἐπίχαρτα sufferings that afford triumph to my enemies, (Aeschulus Tragicus); οἱ δικαίως τι πάσχοντες ἐπίχαρτοι to see people justly punished is a satisfaction, (Thucydides)
(- ὀρθός, τέμνω), [in LXX: (יָשַׁר pi.)*;] to cut straight, as a road (τ. ὁδούς, figuratively, Pr, ll with). Metaphorical, τ. λόγον τ. ἀληθείας, (V. Ellic. and CGT, in l; not found elsewhere).
(εὖ, χαρίζομαι), [in LXX for חֵן, *;] 1. = εὔχαρις, winning, gracious, agreeable (Pr, l.with). 2. grateful, thankful.
(contr. fr. -όος; ἁ.- cop., πλόος), [in LXX: *;] simple, single: in a moral sense (DCG, ii, 628 f.), ἀφθαλμός.. ἁπλόος, see: ἁπλοῦς SYN.: ἄδολος, ἄκακος, ἀκέραιος (Tr., Syn., § lvi; Cremer, 107, 639)
(εὖ, σχῆμα), [in LXX: *;] 1. elegant, graceful, comely: τὰ εὐ. ἡμῶν (opposite to τὰ ἀσχ- ἡμ-), in moral sense, seemly, becoming. 2. Also in late Gk., wealthy, influential (RV, of honourable estate).
to praise, laud, extol one, ἐπί τινι for a thing, (Plato Philosophus):—;Pass. to be praised, (Herdotus Historicus)
quick to anger, choleric, (Euripides), —; sharp to punish, of the Areopagus, (Aeschulus Tragicus): τὸ ὀξύθυμον, by crasis τοὐξύθυμον, = ὀξυθυμία, (Euripides)

1. without pain, and so: 2. of persons, insensible to pain, (Aristotle Philosopher) 3. unfeeling, hard-hearted, ruthless, (Sophocles Tragicus); ἀναλγητότερος εἶναι to feel less grieved, (Thucydides): with genitive, ἀν. εἶναί τινος to be insensible to, (Plutarch):—;adverb -τως, unfeelingly, (Sophocles Tragicus) 4. of things, not painful…
a prop, stay, support, Lat. columen, (Sophocles Tragicus):—;in plural the props to keep a boat on shore upright, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus)

1. to set higher, erect, [variant datesAnthology Palantina 2. to set on the other side, carry over, (Plutarch) 3. in Mid. to hold over, so as to protect, [variant datesAnthology Palantina 4. metaphorically, παντὶ θεὸν ὑπερτιθέμεν to set God over all, (Pindar) 5. to communicate a thing to another, ὑπερετίθεα (ionic imperfect for -ετίθην)…

1. of Place, in or at the right place, hence of parts of the body, ἐν καιρίῳ, κατὰ καίριον in a vital part, (Iliad by Homer); also, of wounds, πέπληγμαι καιρίαν πληγήν, καιρίας πληγῆς τυχεῖν (Aeschulus Tragicus); πληγή is sometimes omitted, (Herdotus Historicus):—; adverb -ίως, mortally, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 2. of Time, in season…
to make trial, essay, or proof of a thing or person, with genitive, (Herdotus Historicus), attic:—;so also in Act., ἀποπειρᾶσαι τοῦ Πειραιῶς to make an attempt on the Peiraeeus, (Thucydides)

1. to plan or contrive against, κακὸν πόλει (Tyrtaeus Elegiacus); θάνατόν τινι (Herdotus Historicus):—;with dative pers. only, to plot against, lay snares for, τῇ πόλει (Aeschulus Tragicus); τῷ πλήθει (Aristophanes Comicus);—;absolute, οὑπιβουλεύων the conspirer, (Sophocles Tragicus): —;with accusative rei only, to plan secretly, scheme…
1. a man-woman, hermaphrodite, (Plato Philosophus) 2. a womanish man, effeminate person, (Herdotus Historicus) 3. as adjective common to men and women, [variant datesAnthology Palantina

given to wantonness, wanton, insolent, outrageous, (Plato Philosophus),—; τὸ ὑβριστικόν an insolent disposition, (Xenophon Historicus):—;adverb -κῶς, (Plato Philosophus); comparative -ώτερον, (Demosthenes Orator)
a store, treasure, (Sophocles Tragicus) from θησαυρίζω
neuterplural as adverb, treacherously, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus)
τό (περικαθαίρω, to purify on all sides or completely, Ma.1:29*), [in LXX: (כֹּפֶר)*;] 1. a victim, expiation (Pr, l.with). 2. refuse, rubbish: pl..
1. Dep. to force away:—; Pass. to be forced away or back, (Xenophon Historicus) 2. absolute to use force, (Xenophon Historicus)

1. anything spread or laid out for lying or sitting upon, a mattress, bed, Lat. stragulum, vestis stragula, (Theognis Elegiacus):—;in plural the bedclothes, the coverings of a dinner-couch, (Aristophanes Comicus), 2. a horsecloth, horse-trappings, (Xenophon Historicus)

1. to spend or consume in doing, χρόνον (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. absolute (entry χρόνον); to spend time in a place, (Demosthenes Orator) 3. to waste time by staying in a place, linger there, (Thucydides) 4. to continue in the practice of a thing ἔν τινι (Xenophon Historicus): absolute to dwell upon a point (in speaking)…
(οίνος + πότης, a drinker), poët. and late prose, [in LXX: (יַיִן סָבָא)*;] a wine-drinker, wine-bibber.
