(ἀ- neg., ἦδος, pleasure), [in LXX: Pr 2329 (שִׂיחַ)*;] 1. of things or persons, unpleasantness, odiousness; 2. dislike (Plat.), disagreement: D.

1. a place where people assembled to talk and hear news, a lounge, club-room, (Odyssey by Homer), —;also a council-hall, council, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 2. talk or gossip, such as went on in the λέσχαι, (Euripides):—; in good sense, conversation, discussion, (Herdotus Historicus)
[in LXX: (רָוָה), (שָׁתָה),] causal of μεθύω, to make drunk, intoxicate; pass., to get drunk.
horned, ἔλαφος (Sophocles Tragicus):—;feminine κεραστίς, ίδος, of Io, (Aeschulus Tragicus)

1. of or for the council or the councillors, (Xenophon Historicus) 2. able to advise or deliberate, (Plato Philosophus), 3. as Substantive, βουλευτικόν, in the Athen. theatre, the seats next the orchestra, reserved for the Council, (Aristophanes Comicus) 4. the senatorial order, (Plutarch)
a being fed, feasting, [variant datesAnthology Palantina
[in LXX: (τ. ζημίαν, for עָנַשׁ ni.),] to pay: t. δίκην, to pay penalty.
to be fast asleep, fall asleep, (Herdotus Historicus):—;Pass., perfect participle κατυπνωμένος asleep, (Herdotus Historicus)
to add ornaments to, to decorate after or besides, (Herdotus Historicus); θεὰν ἐπ. to honour, celebrate, (Aristophanes Comicus)
(ζητέω). 1. a seeking, search. 2. a questioning, inquiry, debate: before περί.
to deprive of a thing, (Thucydides):—;Pass. to be deprived of a thing, (Herdotus Historicus), attic
mostly, most often, very often, (Xenophon Historicus)

[in LXX: (מָלֵא) *;] 1. to bring in full measure, hence, to fulfil, accomplish. 2. to persuade, assure or satisfy fully: pass.. 3. to fill: L, mg. (Cl. Ro.,); metaphorically, pass., to be filled with, hence, fully bent on (Ec, l.with).
(ψιθυρίζω, to whisper), [in LXX: (לַחַשׁ) *;] a whispering; (a) of secret slander, (Plut.); (b) of a murmured enchantment, Ec, l.with
(στοῖχος, a row), [in LXX: (כָּשֵׁר) *;] to be in rows, to walk in line. Metaphorical, in late writers, to walk by rule: with dative, to walk by or in (as a rule of life).
the caper-plant, or its fruit, the caper, Lat. capparis, (Aristotle Philosopher) derivation uncertain
τό (φιλέω), [in LXX: (נְשִׁיקָה) *;] a kiss: as a token of Christian brotherhood, φ. ἅγιον, φ. ἀγάπης.
-τος, τό (στίζω, to prick), [in LXX: (נְקֻדָּה) *;] a tattoed mark or brand: τὰ σ. τοῦ Ἰησοῦ.
1. a breastband, girdle, (Lucian) 2. a bundle, bunch, (Plutarch)
Dep. to leap across, τάφρον (Xenophon Historicus)
[in LXX: (פַּג)*;] an unripe fig, which grows in winter and usually falls off in the spring.

to whistle, Lat. stridere, (Iliad by Homer); of a snake, to hiss, (Hesiod):—;Pass. to rush through the air, ἐρροίζητο (3rd singular pluperfect) [variant datesAnthology Palantina

1. near, close to, with genitive or dative, πλησίοι ἀλλήλων or ἀλλήλοισι (Homer):—;absolute near, neighbouring, (Iliad by Homer),—;as Substantive a neighbour, ἰδὼν ἐς πλ. ἄλλον (Iliad by Homer), 2. adverb πλησίον, doric πλα_τίον, = πέλας, near, nigh, hard by, with genitive, (Homer), with dative, (Euripides) 3. with the Art.…
(θρόος, a noise, tumult), [in LXX: (הָמָה *;] in cl., 1. to cry aloud, make an outcry. 2. to utter aloud. 3. In NT (and LXX), pass., to be troubled, as by an alarm: (WH, mg.).
anything flowing, running water, a river, stream, [variant datesTragica Adespota, (Plato Philosophus)
[in LXX: (יָשַׁב)*;] to set beside; act. for mid., to sit down beside: Rec..
to hit one's mark, to be successful, (Demosthenes Orator)
admonition, warning, (Aeschulus Tragicus), τἀμὰ νουθετήματα given to me, (Sophocles Tragicus)
συν-κομίζω (Rec. συγκ-), [in LXX: (עָלָה) *;] 1. to bring together, collect. 2. to take up a body for burial (Soph., Aj., 1048).
to look at, behold, (Mimnermus Lyricus), compare aorist2 προσεῖδον:—;so in Mid., προσορωμένα (Sophocles Tragicus)
to see through, see clearly, (Xenophon Historicus)

1. to scrape, plane, smooth or polish, (Odyssey by Homer): metaphorically, ξῦσαι ἀπὸ γῆρας to scrape off, get rid of old age, (Homeric Hymns):—; Mid., παλτὸν ξύσασθαι to shape oneself a javelin-shaft, (Xenophon Historicus) 2. to make smooth, work delicately, (Iliad by Homer)

of yesterday, τὸ χθιζὸν χρεῖος their yesterday's debt, (Iliad by Homer); ὁ χθ. πόνος yesterday's labour, (Herdotus Historicus); in adverbial sense, with Verbs, χθιζὸς ἔβη he went yesterday, (Iliad by Homer); χθ. ἤλυθες (Odyssey by Homer),—;neuter χθιζόν as adverb = χθές, (Homer); so plural χθιζά, see. πρώιζος.

ἀπο-λούω [in LXX: (רָחַץ)*;] to wash off, wash away; mid., metaphorically, with accusative of thing(s), to wash off oneself: ἀμαρτίας, absol., ἀπελούσασθε, ye washed yourselves clean.
(μέσος), [in LXX: (בֵּין)*;] an arbitrator, mediator: with dupl. genitive of person(s), θεοῦ κ. ἀνθρώπων, with genitive of thing(s), διαθήκης, ὁ δε μ. ἑνὸς οὐκ ἔστιν.
δι-ακούω [in LXX: (שׁמע), (יָד שִׁית hi.)*;] to hear through, hear fully; technically, to hear judicially (as De, l.with; of. Deiss., BS, 230).

1. to milk sheep and goats; βόας (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus): —;Mid., in metaphorically sense, ἀμέλγεσθαι τοὺς ξένους to milk them dry, (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. to draw milk from the animals, ἀμ. γάλα (Herdotus Historicus); Pass., ὄϊες ἀμελγόμεναι γάλα having milk drawn from them, milch- ewes, (Iliad by Homer) 3…
to string on a thing, Pass., (Herdotus Historicus)
άνα-κύπτω [in LXX: (נָשָׂא רֹאשׁ), Dan LXX, Su *;] to lift oneself up; (a) bodily; (b) mentally, to be elated.

to turn up and open hands

[in LXX: (אָסַר)*;] to tie round, bind round: with accusative and dative, pass..
1. a hindrance, impediment, (Euripides) 2. a defence against a thing, precaution, (Thucydides)

1. to bloom, be in flower, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) 2. metaphorically of any thing that forms on the surface, as a salt crust, (Herdotus Historicus); the down on fruit, (Aristophanes Comicus), generally, to be upon the surface, shew itself, appear plainly, (Aristophanes Comicus) 3. to be bright, (Babrius Fabularum Scriptor)

1. laid back, laid on one's back, πέσεν ὕπτιος he fell backwards, opposite to πρηνής, (Iliad by Homer); of a quadruped, ὀρθοῦ ἑστεῶτος καὶ ὑπτίου rearing upright and falling backwards, (Herdotus Historicus) 2. generally with the under side uppermost, χείρ ὑπτία the hollow of the hand, (Plutarch)…

[in LXX: (גָּלַל ni.), (חָלַף hi.),] to roll, roll up: (LXX).

a concubine, mistress, Lat. pellex, opposite to a lawful wife κουριδίη ἄλοχος); (Homer) Prob. from same Root as παλλάς = νεᾶνις.

[in LXX: (זְכוּכִית) *;] 1. (Hdt.) a clear transparent stone. 2. (from Plat. on) glass.

1. left behind, staying behind, (Herdotus Historicus); οἱ ὑπ. those who remained alive, (Herdotus Historicus) 2. of things, ὑπ. τὸ βάραθρον γίγνεται the pit still remains, (Aristophanes Comicus); ὅσα ἦν ὑπ. all that remained to be done, (Thucydides)

glory, renown, especially in war, (Iliad by Homer): of a single person, κῦδος Ἀχαιῶν glory of the Achaians, like Lat. decus, (Homer)

to strike with thunderbolts, (Herdotus Historicus):—; Pass., κεραυνωθείς (Hesiod)

τό [in LXX for מַס, *;] defect, loss, defeat.

Lat. camera, anything with an arched cover, a covered carriage, (Herdotus Historicus)

to urge war against others, (Thucydides), with dative, (Xenophon Historicus)
